title: Design Philosophy

body: - **Local-first, zero-infrastructure** — every byte of telemetry stays on the developer's machine; no Docker, no collector cluster, no cloud backend means the install-to-first-trace loop is one binary launch, not a stack.

- **Single-process modular monolith** — fourteen library crates (seventeen workspace members total: those fourteen + the `pulse-app` binary crate + the `xtask` task-runner crate + the dev-only test-support library crate `test-support`, which no product target links and the engine boot does not wire) are wired by ONE shared engine boot, `pulse_app::engine_boot` (`init_process`, then `start`), which both entry points of the `pulse-app` package call: the Tauri window app (`pulse-app`, `main.rs`) and, since chunk 2026-10-10-console-engine-entry-point, the console program (`andromeda-pulse-engine`, `console.rs`). Neither entry point wires an engine part itself, and the shared boot and the console module name no window framework (pinned by `pulse-app/tests/unit_engine_boot_seam.rs`); `tauri` stays in `pulse-app`'s manifest. Within a program the crates share memory via tokio channels rather than network hops, so ingest→buffer→viz latency is measured in microseconds and the OS sees one engine process per program; since chunk 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door the console program's `door` word also runs as short-lived relay processes that host no engine part (§Infrastructure Patterns → Deployment model; PROVISIONAL — §Occupied Resources → Network ports, the door). Occupied Resources is the canonical workspace-member list; any claim of a count word elsewhere refers back to it.

- **Standards-track at the edges, opinionated in the middle** — OTLP at `:4317`/`:4318`, MCP over stdio, and WASM Component Model plugins are all spec-conformant so external tooling Just Works; internal contracts (TauRPC bridge, Arrow zero-copy hand-off) are tightly opinionated to keep agent-driven development unambiguous.

- **Token-efficient curation as a first-class output** — the snapshot generator is treated as a peer of the visualization surface, not a side feature, because turning local telemetry into LLM context is the differentiator.

- **Capability-scoped extensibility** — WASM Component Model plugins receive only the host imports they declare in WIT, so third-party plugins cannot escalate beyond explicitly granted resources, and the security posture remains auditable.

- **Developer-tool surface** — the visualization shell is a dense, chart-first, low-chrome dashboard targeting developers staring at telemetry for hours; dark-mode is the default color scheme, and the WebGPU canvas + tray icon + OS-notification surfaces are the visual touchpoints arch commits to. Concrete tokens (color, motion, typography, density scale) are owned by the design specialist but must respect this density and color-scheme constraint.

title: Stack and Technologies

body: | Layer | Technology | Role |

| Primary language / runtime | Rust 2024 edition — toolchain pinned to rustc 1.95.0 (`rust-toolchain.toml`); the workspace declares `rust-version = "1.95"` once in `[workspace.package]` (all 17 members inherit it), equal to the pin and set by the resolved dependency graph — 28 packages declare `rust-version = "1.95.0"` (wasmtime 48.0.5 and its internal crates, cranelift 0.135.5, pulley 48.0.5; `cargo metadata --offline`, as measured at chunk `2026-10-04-declared-rust-floor-matches-the-code`), so no toolchain below 1.95.0 builds the product; the workspace's own code needs only rustc ≥ 1.89 (`std::fs::File::lock`, corpus keychain; let-chains 1.88); the xtask test `declared_floor_equals_the_pinned_channel` holds the declared floor equal to the pin at major.minor, so every pinned-toolchain build proves it | Single language across receivers, buffer, viz host, IPC, plugin host, MCP server |
| Desktop shell | Tauri 2.x | Native window + webview, OS bundlers, updater, tray, notifications |
| gRPC server | `tonic` 0.14.x | OTLP/gRPC receiver on `:4317` (with `prost` 0.14 codegen against `opentelemetry-proto`) |
| HTTP server | `axum` 0.8.x on `hyper` 1.x + `tower` | OTLP/HTTP receiver on `:4318` (protobuf and JSON) sharing the Tokio runtime with tonic |
| Async runtime | `tokio` (current stable) | Single multi-threaded runtime serving both OTLP ports and IPC |
| In-process channels | `tokio::sync::mpsc` + `tokio::sync::broadcast` | Ingest→appender hand-off (mpsc, backpressure) and buffer→subscribers fan-out (broadcast) |

| Storage engine | DuckDB 1.5.x via the `duckdb` crate — Cargo.toml requirement `1.10500` (caret, untouched), lockfile-resolved **1.10505.0** as of 2026-08-28 | Embedded columnar OLAP, in-memory ring buffer (5–10 min, configurable) |
| Columnar interchange | Apache Arrow (via `Appender::append_record_batch()` / `stream_arrow()`) | Zero-copy hand-off between OTLP decode → DuckDB → viz/MCP |

| Plugin runtime | `wasmtime` 25+ family with WASM Component Model + WIT — Cargo.toml requirement `"48.0.4"`, lockfile-resolved **48.0.5** as of 2026-10-04 (Cranelift 0.135.5, as measured at `Cargo.lock:`); the bump from 48.0.3 closed RUSTSEC-2026-0325 / -0326 / -0327 with no advisory ignore (the earlier bump from 46.0.3 closed RUSTSEC-2026-0316), and 49.x is out of reach while the toolchain is pinned at 1.95 (49.0.2, the first patched 49.x, needs Rust 1.96) | Capability-scoped third-party extensions loaded from `~/.andromeda-pulse/plugins/` |
| Visualization surface | Webview WebGPU (`<canvas>` + `navigator.gpu`, WGSL) | GPU-accelerated charts inside WebView2 (Windows) and WKWebView (macOS/Linux equivalents) |
| Tauri IPC bridge | TauRPC (`taurpc` crate) | Router-style Rust ↔ webview commands with auto-generated TypeScript bindings |

| MCP server | Hand-rolled serde JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio (`crates/mcp-server/src/jsonrpc.rs`, MCP protocol `2024-11-05`) and, since chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process, the same layer over a Unix-domain socket inside the console engine's process (the door, `pulse-app/src/door.rs`, Unix only; PROVISIONAL — §Occupied Resources → Network ports); `rmcp` linked as a feature-gated anchor dependency — requirement `"3"`, lockfile-resolved 3.1.4 as of 2026-08-29 | 9 named tools on the wire — `query_traces` / `query_metrics` / `query_logs` / `generate_snapshot` (telemetry) + `query_incident_list` / `retrieve_report` / `retrieve_telemetry_slice` / `mark_incident_resolved` (corpus-backed incident/report, chunk #94) + `retrieve_incident_events` (corpus-backed incident lifecycle read-back, chunk `2026-10-02-incident-events-readable-through-mcp`) — gated by `--features mcp-server` as the stdio sidecar and the `rmcp` anchor only: since chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process `pulse-app` links the `mcp-server` crate in every build and the console engine serves the nine through the door with no feature; since chunk 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door a stdio agent reaches them through the console program's word `andromeda-pulse-engine door` (a relay to the door), also with no feature — so `--features mcp-server` gates the stdio sidecar, not every stdio way to the nine (PROVISIONAL — §Occupied Resources → Network ports, the door) |
| OS notifications | `tauri-plugin-notification` 2.x | Native "Snapshot ready" toasts (Notification Center / Action Center / freedesktop) |
| Updater | `tauri-plugin-updater` 2.x with `latest.json` | In-app updates from GitHub Releases |
| Mobile framework | N/A — desktop only (Windows / macOS / Linux) | — |

| Message broker | N/A — one engine process per program (the desktop window app; the console engine `andromeda-pulse-engine`), its parts joined by in-process tokio channels; since chunk 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door the console program's `door` word also runs as short-lived relay processes that host no engine part and join nothing (PROVISIONAL — §Occupied Resources → Network ports, the door) | — |

| AI/ML serving | `llama.cpp` prebuilt binaries (b9305-pinned series) invoked via subprocess (D1 spawn-per-generation); v0.2.0 Epoch 9+; v0.1.0 had no in-process model | L4 interpretation layer — local on-device inference of curated digests, constrained by a committed GBNF (`pulse-app/src/l4-output.gbnf`) passed with `--grammar-file`, running the founder's pick gemma-4-E4B-it-Q4_K_M (selected by `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MODEL_PATH`); CUDA + CPU prebuilt `llama-cli.exe` selected per hardware-profile tier (CUDA build + `-ngl 99` for gpu-primary/gpu-fallback, CPU build + `-ngl 0` for cpu-primary/cpu-fallback — the CPU route founder-retired 2026-10-05 and still routed: 0.3.0 does not implement the retirement, carried to the next version at the 2026-10-09 version close (`.andromeda/residuals.md`); see §Established Decisions [LLM Inference Runtime]); bounded `-st` single-turn + explicit `-n {max_tokens}` + outer wall-clock timeout discipline, plus `-c 8192` / `-rea off` and the model authors' sampling `--temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 64 --min-p 0`. v0.1.0 paste-to-AI snapshot/markdown surface preserved alongside |

| L4 grammar conversion check (test-only) | llama.cpp b9305 (`63248fc3`) `examples/json_schema_to_grammar.py`, vendored byte-identical at `pulse-app/vendor/llama-cpp/` (MIT, its `LICENSE` beside it; stdlib-only Python 3) + a Python 3 interpreter (`python3` or `python`) on every host that runs the workspace tests | `pulse-app/tests/unit_l4_grammar.rs` runs it on `L4_OUTPUT_JSON_SCHEMA` and asserts the committed `L4_OUTPUT_GBNF` equals its output; a missing interpreter FAILS the test, never skips it. Never in the shipped binary; outside cargo-deny's view (security-plan §Dependency Security) |

| Boot-smoke exit witness (harness-only, Linux) | C, the single file `scripts/exit-witness.c`, built by the host's `cc -shared -fPIC -O2` with no dependency beyond the C library (dev-host `cc` read at GCC 16.2.1 20260810, as measured on 2026-10-10; the runner's compiler version was not read) | A shared library bare `scripts/agent-run.sh boot` preloads into the window app's spawn alone (`boot engine` spawns the console engine with no preload, since chunk 2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine) to record which call ended the process (`exit`, `_exit`, `_Exit`, `quick_exit`, `abort` interposed). Built in the ci.yml `boot` job and by the xtask tests, whose seven controls on the built library are Linux only and FAIL on a missing `cc`. Never in the shipped binary; no Cargo dependency, no manifest or lockfile change (chunk 2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-named-from-a-run) |

| A11y regression-detector pin (test-only) | Node: `node` on PATH on every host that runs the workspace tests, running the existing `pulse-app/ui/tests-a11y/regression-detector.mjs`; no npm or Cargo dependency, no manifest or lockfile change (dev host read at v26.8.2, its default, and at 24.21.0, the `mise` install the pre-push check runs under, as measured on 2026-10-10; the runner's Node version was not read) | `pulse-app/tests/a11y_perf_workflow.rs` (`a11y_regression_detector_fails_when_its_baseline_is_absent`) runs the detector with an absent baseline and asserts a non-zero exit and a stderr holding `baseline not found`; a missing `node` FAILS the test, never skips it. Never in the shipped binary (chunk 2026-10-10-no-ci-step-reads-nothing) |

| Gate-script pins (test-only) | `bash` and `awk` on PATH on every host that runs the workspace tests; no Cargo or npm dependency, no manifest or lockfile change (neither tool's version was read on the dev host or the runner) | Four witness tests in `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs` cut the `Enforce coverage thresholds` step's script out of `ci.yml` by the step's name and run it with `bash -e` over constructed `lcov.info` files; six pins in `xtask/src/main.rs` (`empty_input_tests`; five until chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed) run `xtask/ci/quarantine-tracking-check.sh` with `bash` over scratch roots. A missing `bash` or `awk` FAILS the witness and a missing `bash` FAILS the quarantine pins, never skips them. Never in the shipped binary (chunk 2026-10-10-no-gate-stands-while-reading-nothing). Since chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed the `xtask` package has its first integration tests — two binaries in `xtask/tests/` (`agent_run_shell`, 19 tests; `engine_cycle_refusals`, 6) over a shared module `xtask/tests/common/mod.rs` — which run the committed `scripts/agent-run.sh` and the built `harness:engine-cycle` verb with `bash` on real console engines. With the three spawned arms that chunk added to `pulse-app/tests/integration_console_engine.rs` they need, on every host that runs the workspace tests: `bash`, a Linux `/proc`, an advisory file lock under `target/` (`target/test-ports/`) and the engine built in the test profile (a `--workspace` run builds it). At that chunk still no Cargo or npm dependency and no manifest or lockfile change (`tempfile` and `serde_json` were already dependencies of `xtask`; no `libc`). They run in ci.yml's `lint / test`, `mcp-server tests` and `coverage gate` jobs, green on `ci#38079305603`. Since chunk 2026-10-10-shared-telemetry-test-data the port claim is no longer defined in `xtask/tests/common/mod.rs`: that module, the `pulse-app` engine tests and two `xtask` unit tests take `claim_port` / `PortClaim` from the workspace's dev-only member `test-support` (`test_support::ports`), so the advisory-lock need under `target/test-ports/` also holds for the four in-process arms of `pulse-app/tests/integration_engine_boot.rs`, those two unit tests and the member's own port tests. That is the first manifest and lockfile change these tests brought: `xtask`, `pulse-app` and `buffer` name `test-support` under `[dev-dependencies]` and `Cargo.lock` gained one workspace entry — still no registry package and no npm dependency, `deny.toml` unchanged. One more test-only `xtask` pin module, `test_support_edges` (five tests), reads the workspace manifests as text, as `license_check` and `rust_floor` do, and needs no host tool; it holds the dev-only edge of §Cross-cutting Patterns → Module dependency direction. Since chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process three more test binaries of `pulse-app/tests/` (`unit_door`, `unit_observability_allowlist_door`, `integration_door`) need Unix-domain sockets under a path shorter than 108 bytes on every host that runs the workspace tests, and one arm, `another_account_is_refused_at_each_of_three_layers` of `integration_door`, runs its one client as `python3 -c …` under `sudo -n -u nobody` and under `sudo -n`, so that arm needs `python3` and a passwordless `sudo`. **A stated exception to this row's FAILS-never-skips rule:** where `sudo -n true` fails — the dev host, in every run — the arm prints its skip sentence and passes, because that host has no second account to drive; the skip never stands as a pass in CI, where the `lint-test` step `Door refuses another account` (§Infrastructure Patterns → CI/CD approach) reads the arm's own output and fails on a skip, an empty output or a failed arm. No Cargo or npm dependency and `Cargo.lock` byte-identical at that chunk. Since chunk 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door one more test binary, `unit_door_bridge`, needs Unix-domain sockets (it reaches a socket at a path of 107 bytes, and makes a path of 108 bytes by hard-linking a socket bound at a short path), and a second arm of `integration_door`, `another_account_through_the_bridge_receives_nothing`, runs a copy of the built `andromeda-pulse-engine` as `door` under `sudo -n -u nobody` and under `sudo -n`, so it needs a passwordless `sudo` (not `python3`); it too prints its own skip sentence and passes where `sudo -n true` fails, and the `lint-test` step reads both arms' sentences and fails on either skip. No Cargo or npm dependency and `Cargo.lock` byte-identical at that chunk. PROVISIONAL — §Occupied Resources → Network ports, the door |

| Xlib thread initialisation (Linux, product start path) | The host's Xlib, `libX11.so.6`, reached at run time through the already-direct `libc` dependency: `dlopen` (`RTLD_NOW`), `dlsym` for `XInitThreads`, one call through an `unsafe extern "C" fn() -> c_int`; the handle is never closed. No Cargo dependency, no manifest or lockfile change; `tao` stays 0.35.0 | `pulse_app::xlib_threads::init()` is the SECOND statement of `main()` (`pulse-app/src/main.rs`), directly after `render_posture::apply_linux_default()`, which stays the first, and before the tokio runtime builds any thread. It returns one closed value, unused and unlogged: `Initialised` · `LibraryNotFound` · `SymbolNotFound` · `Refused` (the call returned 0) · `NotApplicable` (not Linux); every arm but the first is inert and the start goes on. It reads and sets no environment variable, emits no log record, starts no thread and takes no input from outside the binary; four `unsafe` blocks, each under a `// SAFETY:` comment. One call site, pinned with its place in `main` by `pulse-app/tests/unit_xlib_threads.rs`. Why: the app uses Xlib from two threads — GTK's main thread and the device-event thread `tao` 0.35.0 starts on X11, whose one `XInitThreads` call is not on the start path (0.35.3 and 0.37.1 the same) — and an Xlib older than 1.8 does not initialise its thread support when it loads (the `ubuntu-22.04` runner's `libx11-6 1.7.5-1ubuntu0.3`; the dev host's 1.8.13 does). Without the call a reply is lost inside the app, Xlib raises an I/O error on a healthy connection and GDK's handler calls `_exit(1)` in the app's first second: 12 of 16 runner boots on `ci#38019133294` and `ci#38022477393`, 0 of 24 on `ci#38026637514` attempts 1 to 3, as measured at chunk 2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-closed (the step inside Xlib that loses the reply was not traced). It leaves with the window (the route entry `Window retired`) |
| Push notifications | N/A — OS-native local toasts only, no FCM/APNS/web push | — |

| Secret / key storage | `keyring` 3.x with the explicit platform feature set (`apple-native` / `windows-native` / `sync-secret-service` / `crypto-rust`) + `blake3` KDF for the fallback | OS credential store holding the corpus AES-256-GCM cell key (macOS Keychain / Linux Secret Service / Windows Credential Manager), with an opt-in `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_CORPUS_PASSPHRASE` BLAKE3-derived fallback. **The feature set is load-bearing** — keyring 3.x declares no `default` feature, so a bare `keyring = "3"` links no backend and silently yields a per-process key |
| Error handling | `thiserror` 2.x (modules) + `anyhow` 1.x (boundaries) | Module-internal enums; boundary catch-all at Tauri commands and `main.rs` |
| Validation | `serde` + smart enum types + `TryFrom<u16>` | Validation surface is small (enum settings, port ranges, file paths); OTLP validated by `prost`/`tonic` decode |
| Module boundary enforcement | Cargo workspace, one crate per module | Compile-time `[dependencies]` graph + `pub`/`pub(crate)` visibility |
| Build / package manager | Cargo (workspace) | One workspace, multiple library crates, one binary crate |
| CI task runner | `cargo-xtask` | Release / sign / notarize as Rust binaries inside the same workspace |

| Release pipeline | `tauri-action` GitHub Action + Tauri 2 native bundlers | Builds `.msi` / `.dmg` / `.AppImage` / `.deb` distribution artifacts (macOS `.app` bundle is wrapped into the `.dmg` rather than published standalone) and uploads `latest.json` per release |
| Code signing | Azure Key Vault (Windows EV) + Apple Developer ID (macOS notarization) | Trusted-publisher signing for all distributed bundles |
| Distribution channels | GitHub Releases (primary) + Homebrew tap + Scoop manifest | Three channels driven from the same workflow |
| Code quality (lint/typecheck) | `cargo fmt` + `cargo clippy` (Rust); TauRPC-generated `.d.ts` + `tsc --noEmit` (webview) | Lint and typecheck on every CI run; clippy lints fail the build |

| GUI verification harness (dev-only) | `@crabnebula/tauri-driver` 2.x + `webdriverio` 9.x (npm devDependencies in `pulse-app/ui`) | Headful WebDriver drive of the **assembled 17-stage path** (launch → boot-geometry → traces-empty → traces-populate → traces-scroll → native-menu-suppressed → connection-status → storm-incident → findings-window → report-window → report-copy → investigate → empty-states → dashboard-toggle → dashboard-close → widget-close → signpost-repeat; grew from 7 at `2026-08-23-integration-ux-e2e-test`, 7 → 13 at `2026-08-23-headful-leg-extension`, 13 → 15 at `2026-08-24-headful-mechanics-probe-race-disposition`, where `widget-close` stopped being terminal — `signpost-repeat` follows it deliberately, restoring the widget to prove the close signpost fires on EVERY close — 15 → 16 at `2026-08-27-report-window-copy-affordance`, whose `report-copy` presses the report's real Copy control and reads its settled `data-copy-state` plus the live-region text, DOM-only by construction like its `report-window` / `findings-window` neighbours, and 16 → 17 at `2026-08-30-diagnostics-un-muting-harness-truth-sweep`, whose `boot-geometry` reads the compact widget's outer position/size + current monitor via the driver and re-derives the app's OWN snap formula in the Rust verdict — `wx == mx + mw − round(480.0 × scale) − 24 && wy == my + 24` for the TopRight default — DOM-only, no press, the geometry-truth half the declined-on-measurement `setWindowRect` probe could not give) in the live Tauri window, driven by `cargo xtask webview-drive [--expect-absent <STAGE>] [--no-inject]` (each stage id is `--expect-absent`-eligible; CLI shape unchanged), under the deterministic-L4 gate the driver sets into the spawned app's environment; each stage asserts against the app's own obs log and/or the driver's DOM report, and `--no-inject --expect-absent <STAGE>` is the code-driven RED mutation arm. Telemetry enters only over real OTLP via `crates/ingest/examples/inject_demo` (no in-process bypass). **The injector's CLI contract, formalized 2026-08-25, extended 2026-08-28 and 2026-10-10:** with NO arguments it emits the finite ~600-batch 100 %-error storm on an identical BUDGET — batch count, span count, error count and durations unchanged — but **NOT byte-identically since 2026-08-28**: each run draws a `fresh_run_salt()` into `trace_id`/`span_id`, so span identity is deliberately per-run and two runs never collide on the `spans` primary key. The BUDGET is what the harness depends on (see the `PULSE_INJECTOR` entry), and the clause's historical verification was a COUNT equality (3540 = 3540), never a byte comparison. `--sustained` runs UNBOUNDED at a moderate error rate, `--minutes=N` bounds a run, `--error-pct=0..100` overrides the degrading service's rate (range-checked), `--replay` pins the salt to a fixed constant so a restart deliberately re-emits the previous run's identities (the retrying-exporter shape `smoke:gap-resume` arm A drives), and an unknown argument is REJECTED with exit 2 rather than ignored. Since chunk 2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine the endpoint port follows `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_GRPC_PORT` (`http://127.0.0.1:{port}`, 4317 when unset): a set value that is not a port from 1 to 65535, a blank one included, is REJECTED with exit 2 and nothing sent, never defaulted. Sustained mode retries a transient export failure with a backoff and a consecutive-failure ceiling, so backpressure does not end a run but a dead receiver still does — a finite storm exits and the 60 s traces window then ages out, which is the false-negative the mode exists to remove. The win32 native driver arrives via the napi optional dep `@crabnebula/tauri-driver-win32-x64-msvc` (no `cargo install tauri-driver`, no Rust dependency), and the host `msedgedriver` — which must match the installed WebView2 Runtime — is located via `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MSEDGEDRIVER_PATH` and never committed. Dev-only: devDeps only, no runtime/bundle impact |

title: Established Decisions

body: - **[Platform] Tauri 2 desktop shell**: chosen over Electron because bundle size is 5–10× smaller (~10–20 MB vs 100 MB+), the security model is capability-scoped, and a Rust backend means the receiver, buffer, and UI bridge live in one process with no Node bridge tax.

- **[Primary Language] Rust 2024 edition (toolchain pinned 1.95.0; declared `rust-version = "1.95"`, equal to the pin and set by the dependency graph; the workspace's own code needs rustc ≥ 1.89)**: matches the high-performance OTel-receiver trend (Rotel benchmarks: 75% less memory, 50% less CPU than the Go Collector) and means one language end-to-end through ingest, buffer, viz host, plugin host, and MCP server.

- **[Backend Framework — OTLP receiver] `tonic` 0.14.x + `axum` 0.8.x on shared `hyper` 1.x + `tower`**: a single Tokio runtime serves both `:4317` gRPC and `:4318` HTTP without two unrelated substrates; axum's middleware/extractor ergonomics outweigh the ~30 transitive deps for a 12-module monolith. Alternatives (raw hyper, poem+tonic, actix+tonic) either lost on ergonomics or fought Tauri's `tokio::main` integration. **Caveat to reconcile before locking versions**: `tonic` 0.14 vs `opentelemetry-otlp` 0.31 (which still pins `tonic` 0.13 in some feature combinations) — read both `Cargo.toml`s before tagging.

- **[Database] DuckDB embedded via the `duckdb` crate — requirement `1.10500` (caret) in Cargo.toml, lockfile-resolved 1.10505.0 as of 2026-08-28 (DuckDB 1.5.x bundled), in-memory ring buffer**: columnar+SQL+Arrow trifecta is exactly what aggregating spans/metrics by service/time-bucket needs at 10k spans/sec. SQLite was rejected because aggregating 10k spans/sec into per-service p99 series in row-store SQL turns the query into the bottleneck. DataFusion remains a documented swap-out only if DuckDB's C++ FFI complicates Tauri cross-compile.

- **[ORM / Migrations] None — direct SQL via `duckdb` crate's `Connection` and `Appender`**: ring-buffer schema is small, lifecycle is "create on startup" + periodic `DELETE WHERE ts < cutoff`, and Arrow zero-copy ingest sidesteps any ORM marshalling tax.

- **[In-Process Channel Architecture] `tokio::sync::mpsc` + `tokio::sync::broadcast`**: mpsc for the OTLP-ingest → DuckDB-appender hand-off (built-in backpressure absorbs receiver bursts); broadcast for fan-out from buffer to live UI subscribers (compact widget, full dashboard, tray icon, MCP server can all subscribe to the same span stream). `crossbeam-channel` was rejected because mixing tokio mpsc with crossbeam adds bridging complexity for a pure-tokio stack.

- **[Plugin Runtime] WASM Component Model via `wasmtime` 25+ (requirement `"48.0.4"`, lockfile-resolved 48.0.5 as of 2026-10-04) with WIT interfaces**: capability-based sandboxing (no syscalls, file, or socket access unless explicitly granted) and type-safe host imports match the standards path. Extism was considered for easier multi-language guest support, but Component Model is the standards-track choice the input.md explicitly calls out and aligns with Bytecode Alliance LTS.

- **[WebGPU Visualization Surface] Webview WebGPU (`<canvas>` + `navigator.gpu`)**: WGSL shaders run unchanged across WebView2 (Windows) and WKWebView (macOS); IPC pushes Arrow data into the canvas. Native `wgpu` 25+ surface was rejected for v1 because Tauri 2 native-overlay flickering is documented (issue #9220), and "ship on three OSes with one codebase" beats "avoid theoretical browser GC pauses." **Documented upgrade path**: native `wgpu` 25+ surface for the compact widget if browser GC jank becomes a measured problem (hybrid Option C).

- **[Fault Identity — what makes two faults ONE fault] Two layers, decided independently: L1 fingerprint normalization is TOKEN-LEADING; L2 incident identity is COALESCE-PER-CUE-IDENTITY**. **L1** — stacktrace normalization strips a path token only when the absolute marker STARTS a token (position 0, or preceded by a non-path byte); both the Unix `/` arm and the Windows drive-letter arm carry that precondition (`crates/buffer/src/fingerprint.rs::is_token_boundary`). Absolute paths are stripped for host-stability, while **relative path structure is identity-significant** — `src/a.rs` and `src/b/c.rs` are DISTINCT fingerprints. Rationale: host-stability is what absolute-path stripping buys; stripping relative structure serves nothing and destroys identity resolution, and for a diagnostic tool over-coalescing hides distinct faults. Blast radius: the fingerprint value reaches the appender, the consumer, the storm-observer adapter and boot wiring, and — since `2026-08-17-incident-fingerprint-producer-repaired` — onward through the attention cue, the digest cue ref and the incident producer into `Incident.fingerprint` (persisted to the corpus, read by the `fingerprint_match` retrieval arm and the digest assembler). Since `2026-08-26-interpretation-brief-completeness` the L1 fingerprint DOES reach a rendered surface — threaded as a citable evidence id into the L4 prompt (`citable_evidence_ids`, deduped order-stable from `digest.attention_cues[].fingerprint`) and, via the `evidence_refs.fingerprint_hashes` union at the producer, into the MCP `retrieve_telemetry_slice.fingerprint_refs` response and the Diagnostic Report's Evidence section; the `Incident.fingerprint` FIELD itself still has no viz / MCP / UI consumer (the webview `IncidentRecord` view drops it and `PreviouslySeenMatch` omits it), and `span_events.fingerprint` is still never SELECTed. **L2** — incidents coalesce on the cue tuple `(kind, scope, scope_id)`, which for storms is effectively per-service; a storm carrying a different fingerprint on a service that already has an open incident is absorbed BY DESIGN. Fingerprint is absent from that key on the ground that survives: every downstream surface is already N-safe (the per-service constellation join reduces by max tier over all matching active incidents; the digest assembler reads `list_active` only as a boolean), so a second concurrent incident would change no rendering and no L4 behaviour — it would only add rows. Per-fingerprint dedupe is therefore **possible-but-declined** rather than unavailable: the cue now carries a real fingerprint, so this decision is REVISITABLE by a future entry, and until one takes it the predicate stays as written. **REJECTED**: keying on `L4Output.fingerprint` — model-authored, and a constant under the deterministic runner, so per-fingerprint dedupe would be a no-op in exactly the mode used for reproducible e2e verification. **SHIPPED 2026-08-17** (was DEFERRED — the documented path if incident-per-identity is ever wanted): threading a real `ExceptionFingerprint` through `AttentionCue` → `DigestCueRef` → the producer. `AttentionCue.fingerprint` and `DigestCueRef.fingerprint` (`Option<String>`, `#[serde(default)]`, full 32-char lowercase hex; `None` for baseline-derived families, which detect a statistical condition rather than a specific fault) now carry the L1 value to the incident site. **Producer repaired**: `Incident.fingerprint` is contracted (`crates/triage/src/contract.rs`) and consumed (digest retrieval / assembler) as a lowercase-hex grouping hash, and is now PRODUCED from the threaded L1 fingerprint via the crate-internal `triage::contract::hex_lower` — the SAME encoder the assembler applies to Q3 rows, deliberately not the 4-byte `pattern::storm::fingerprint_to_hex_prefix` (8 chars, bounded-cardinality tracing only; a prefix here could never match). The corpus-retrieval `fingerprint_match` arm is therefore FED, not starved — its do-not-simplify-it-away guard now rests on the arm being live rather than on a contracted-but-starved mismatch. This is TEXT, not identity: the tuple `(kind, scope, scope_id)`, the coalesce predicate, severity, priority tier and the evidence union are unchanged, and a deduped incident keeps its creation title — coherent because `kind` is part of the identity key. S3 stays the weakest shape. The remainder rides the L4 MODEL, not the framing: the model-replacement chunk 2026-10-05-l4-runs-on-a-small-current-model-chosen-by-measurement re-ran the same shapes and grader on candidate models under v2.5 and confirmed Qwen3.5-2B-Q4_K_M at `PASS · rank1 37/40` against a bar of 36 (held-out 19/20), through a `--grammar-file` GBNF with per-model authors' sampling, as measured at that chunk (`evidence/confirmation.md`), while the shipped model was still Llama-3.2-3B; the pattern-discrimination entry then chose the model — the founder's pick, gemma-4-E4B-it-Q4_K_M, over the QAT build (2026-10-05; chunk 2026-10-05-l4-model-chosen-by-pattern-discrimination, `evidence/table.md`) — and chunk 2026-10-05-l4-runs-the-founder-s-pick-with-its-authors-settings ships it (founder rulings 2026-10-05). **The scope obligation's reading** (chunk 2026-10-06-l4-first-hypothesis-names-the-triggering-service; as measured at its `evidence/reading.md`): the shipped gemma-4-E4B-it-Q4_K_M through llama-cli CUDA `-ngl 99`, one pre-registered reading fired once on 2026-10-07 and never re-run, re-ordered or re-thresholded, 240 of 240 generations parsed, n = 10 per shape; the grader is the dev probe's `identifies` label over the first hypothesis statement only (the cue's `scope_id` as a whole word, neither neighbour in `[a-z0-9_-]`, AND a retry token; negation is not read, a space-separated sibling passes, `retried` is not a token); the bar is `both` ≥ 36/40 over the ordinary shapes S1–S4 and ≥ 19/20 over the sibling shapes S7 + S8 (a retry storm scoped to `conductor` beside a `conductor-canary` services row, S8 with two corpus lines naming the canary). It read `shipped` 40/40 · 20/20, the v2.5 baseline `ns` 38/40 · 20/20, and the harness-only line-bearing renders `L` and `LI` 40/40 · 20/20 each: every arm met the bar, the selection is `shipped`, the verdict PASS, and the regression guard (the sentence is reverted if `shipped` reads below `ns` on either half) HOLDS. What the reading does not show stands beside it: the baseline arm met the bar too, so the probe had no known-positive for the miss Conductor's fourth series hit (the storm attributed to the hyphenated sibling in 1 of 3 end-to-end drives); the sentence's measured effect is two generations on one ordinary shape (S3), and whether it fixes that case was unmeasured at that chunk; the next chunk measured it on replayed product prompts, where `shipped`, which carries the sentence, read 9 of 20 `both` on one prompt of three — the sentence alone does not fix it. **The canary-history readings and the corpus-selection remedy** (chunk 2026-10-07-l4-probe-reproduces-the-canary-history-miss; as measured at its `evidence/reading-reproduction.md`, `reading-replay.md`, `reading-remedy.md` and `reading-third.md`; the shipped gemma-4-E4B-it-Q4_K_M through llama-cli b9305, the same `identifies` grader, each reading pre-registered and run once on 2026-10-07). *Synthetic shapes:* `shipped` over S7–S16, n = 20 a shape, read 199 of 200 `both` (one `signal_only`, on S16) — NOT REPRODUCED, a finding and never a pass; the corpus block alone, in the eight variations read (S9–S16), does not carry the miss. *Replay:* three prompts the product itself composed in a new Conductor run, captured at the model-binary handle by the operator's pass-through (no key read; held outside every repository, never committed, the operator deleting them after that chunk's wrap) and replayed through the dev probe, read REPRODUCED on the second drive's prompt (d2), where `shipped` missed the service in 11 of 20 (d1 1 of 20, d3 0 of 20); no captured drive missed live. The known-positive is therefore a REAL prompt, never a synthetic shape. *Remedy:* four candidate edits of the corpus block read on d2, n = 20 (`CR` appends one static restating line after the last corpus line · `CO` puts the triggering service's own lines first · `CC` keeps the first two lines · `CX` keeps the own lines and removes the others, the header and its note going too when none is left): `shipped` 11 `both`, `CR` 16, `CO` 19, `CC` 14, `CX` 20, every guard cell 20 of 20; the pre-registered order `CR`, `CO`, `CC`, `CX` SELECTED `CO`, and `CX` also met the bar. A further reading outside the plan, selecting nothing, n = 40 a cell, read d1 `shipped` 36 `both`, `CX` 40; d3 `shipped` 36, `CO` 40, `CX` 40; d2 `CO` 39, `CX` 40 — service misses over the three prompts `CO` 5 of 120 (it composes as `shipped` on d1) and `CX` 0 of 120. **The founder chose `CX`** (2026-10-07 20:08 local, by dialog, relayed by the pc overseer) on that reading's counts; the order's selection of `CO` stands as measured beside it, and `CX` is what ships: `triage::digest::retrieval::select_corpus_matches` takes `triggering_scope: Option<&str>` (before `limit`; still re-exported through `triage::contract`), and its one production caller, `assemble`, passes the triggering cue's `scope_id`. With `Some(scope)` the scope arm keeps a candidate only when its `scope_id` equals that scope AND is an active scope; the fingerprint arm is unchanged, so a corpus row matching a fingerprint of the window from another scope is still selected; the narrowing runs before the five-line cap and only ever removes; `None` selects as before. For a digest whose triggering cue carries a `scope_id`, the `CORPUS MATCHES:` block therefore holds that service's own incidents and the fingerprint arm's matches and no other active service's, and is absent when none is left; `render_payload`, the framing note, the `TRIGGER:` line, the cap and `DIGEST_CORPUS_RETRIEVAL_LIMIT` are unchanged. This is selection of prompt context, not identity — the tuple, the coalesce predicate and the title grounding are unchanged. The product narrows BEFORE the cap where the measured arm edited an already capped block; the two part only when an own match stands sixth or later by age, a case no shape and no capture holds, and on the three captures the product's selection composes byte for byte what the `CX` arm composed (`evidence/product-path-equality.md`). What the readings do not show stands beside them: `CX` is not shown to be the whole remedy — on d3, 13 of 40 first hypotheses still name the sibling beside the right service (14 under `shipped`); one own line there carries a model-authored title that names the sibling, and `CX` keeps it by rule; a line of another service stays when its fingerprint is live in the window, a case no capture held and no arm read; and the counts are replays of captured prompts — no generation ran on the tree that ships, so Conductor's sixth series is the first live reading. The probe keeps NO durable known-positive: the one shape derived from a captured prompt, S17, read clean under `shipped` (1 miss of 20), so once the captures are deleted the replay, remedy and third readings cannot be run again, and nothing in the tree fails without the remedy and passes with it under a real model. *(Decision rationale + the external-harness switching cost: see `architecture-amendments.md` § Decision-history 2026-08-16.)*

- **[Corpus Write Arbitration — which of two writers to the same incident row wins] Monotonic last-writer guard at the `CorpusWriter` choke point**: incident status writes are arbitrated by a bound `AND updated_unix_nano <= ?2` predicate appended to the existing `incidents` UPDATE, with a second bound `SELECT 1 FROM incidents WHERE id = ?1` classifying the zero-row result. `CorpusWriter::update_incident_status` and `IncidentPersistence::update_incident_status` therefore return `Result<IncidentWriteOutcome, _>` (`Applied` | `DeclinedStale`): a write whose payload is OLDER than the stored row is **DECLINED, not failed** — losing to a fresher writer is an expected outcome, and encoding it as an `Error` would make "log it as a failure" the default at every call site. `Error::QueryFailed` continues to mean the row does not exist. The predicate works because every registry mutator bumps `updated_at_unix_nano` to `now` (`mark_resolved` / `mark_read` / `attach_resolution_summary` / `attach_interpretation_summary`), so a stale snapshot necessarily carries a smaller value. **Placement is the corpus layer, not the `triage` trait**, because it is the ONLY choke point all SEVEN production writers traverse: six share `IncidentPersistence` (the persist cycle, the auto-resolve observer, `incidents.acknowledge`, `incidents.mark_resolved`, and both `inference_runtime` L4 writers) while the seventh — the cross-process `andromeda-pulse-mcp` sidecar at `crates/mcp-server/src/tools.rs` — calls `CorpusWriter` directly and bypasses that trait entirely. Since chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process that same `tools.rs` write (`dispatch_mark_incident_resolved` → `update_incident_status`) has a second carrier: the console engine's door, in the engine's own process, over the engine's own `Arc<dyn CorpusWriter>`, refused with `-32001` before the dispatcher is called unless the write switch `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DOOR_RESOLVE` reads on — so the seventh writer is no longer cross-process only, it still traverses this choke point, and the guard, its existence probe and `Applied` / `DeclinedStale` are unchanged (`the_door_resolves_an_incident_and_says_it_was_a_write`, `pulse-app/tests/integration_engine_boot.rs`, reads the row `resolved` through the engine's own `CorpusWriter`; PROVISIONAL — §Occupied Resources → Network ports, the door). The placement costs no new crate edge (`mcp-server → corpus` and `pulse-app → corpus` already exist) and no DDL. **REJECTED — a status-only predicate** (`status != 'resolved'`): disproved by measurement, since `attach_resolution_summary` REQUIRES `status == Resolved` and is the documented final write, so such a guard would break it. **REJECTED — delta-persistence** (persist only changed rows): larger, needs new dirty-tracking state with crash-loss semantics, and does nothing for the cross-process path, which is not a snapshot problem. `triage::contract::IncidentWriteOutcome` is a deliberate PARALLEL type rather than a re-export — `triage` sits below `corpus` in the dependency DAG, so the `pulse-app` adapter maps between the two. **Residual CLOSED 2026-08-29** (chunk `2026-08-29-app-registry-reconciliation`): this entry previously recorded an accepted residual — the guard made the CORPUS correct but not the app, so after an external MCP resolve the running app showed the incident active until restart and its persist cycle declined that row every cycle. That is no longer true. The 60 s incident persist cycle now RECONCILES first: it reads the durable active-incident **ids** for the workspace through `triage::contract::DurableActiveIncidents::active_incident_ids` (a narrow read port declared in `triage`, implemented at the `pulse-app` binary boundary over the SAME `Arc<dyn CorpusWriter>` the write path uses, so no new crate edge and no payload decoded in `triage`), resolves any registry row absent from that set via the existing `IncidentRegistry::mark_resolved` transition, and only then runs its write loop — so the row it just reconciled is never re-offered. A durable-read `Err` reconciles NOTHING (treating it as an empty set would match every registry row and resolve the whole active list) and warns on `triage.incident.persist.error` with `persist_kind = "incident_reconcile"`; the outcome is counted once per cycle as `reconciled_count` on `triage.incident.persist`. `load_active_incidents` remains a boot-only caller, and the monotonic predicate, its existence probe and the `Applied` / `DeclinedStale` semantics above are unchanged. Measured live: a real `andromeda-pulse-mcp` subprocess resolved a row and the running app dropped it within two persist cycles with NO restart (`reconciled_count` 1 / `declined_count` 0, against 0 / 2 under a mutation with reconciliation removed). The reconciler deliberately emits no `IncidentLifecycleEvent`: `pulse://stream/incidents` has producers but no consumer, so a send would be dead plumbing — the webview learns of the change through its existing ~1 s `incidents.list_active` poll.

- **[License] `MIT OR Apache-2.0`, stated in every manifest that carries a license**: the project ships under the SPDX expression `MIT OR Apache-2.0`, copyright holder Turbolet85 (founder 2026-09-29, the repository public since that day; the shape the sibling Conductor project landed at `cdb7082`). Both texts sit at the repository root and are stored LF: `LICENSE-MIT` (`Copyright (c) 2026 Turbolet85`) and `LICENSE-APACHE` (the Apache License 2.0 verbatim, its appendix template line left as the standard text). The Cargo value is set ONCE, at `Cargo.toml [workspace.package] license`; every workspace member inherits it through `license.workspace = true` and none overrides it. The npm manifest `pulse-app/ui/package.json` and its lockfile root entry (`packages[""]`) carry the same expression. The two channel manifests `update-channels.yml` generates use their channel's native either-of syntax: Homebrew `license any_of: ["MIT", "Apache-2.0"]`, Scoop `"license": "MIT|Apache-2.0"`. The Tauri bundles carry no license key of their own: `tauri.conf.json` sets no `bundle.license`, which defaults to the Cargo value (tauri-utils 2.9.0). cargo-deny license-checks the workspace's own crates as well as its dependencies (security-plan §Dependency Security → CI integration). The test-only `xtask` module `license_check` pins the two texts, the Cargo value and its inheritance, the npm pair and the channel syntax, each surface mutation-checked at chunk 2026-09-30-dual-license. Out of this decision: per-source-file headers, a NOTICE bundle, the `authors` field.

title: Conventions

body: - **Workspace API style — internal Rust↔webview**: TauRPC routers, one router per module crate (`ingest`, `buffer`, `viz`, `ui-bridge`, `snapshot`, `curation`, `triage`, `workspace-detector`, `plugins`, `mcp-server`, `corpus`, `security`); no manual TypeScript re-declaration of command signatures. Frontend consumes only TauRPC-generated `.ts` bindings.

- **External wire — OTLP receiver**: OpenTelemetry spec exactly. `:4317` accepts gRPC over `opentelemetry-proto`; `:4318` accepts HTTP/protobuf at `/v1/traces`, `/v1/metrics`, `/v1/logs` (HTTP/JSON encoding optional). No URL versioning prefix beyond what the OTLP spec defines.

- **External wire — MCP server**: JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio per MCP spec; tool methods are `query_traces`, `query_metrics`, `query_logs`, `generate_snapshot`, `query_incident_list`, `retrieve_report`, `retrieve_telemetry_slice`, `mark_incident_resolved` (these 4 added chunk #94), `retrieve_incident_events` (added chunk `2026-10-02-incident-events-readable-through-mcp`). "Over stdio per MCP spec" is the sidecar's wire; since chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process the same nine tool methods have a second wire, the console engine's door — line-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 over the Unix-domain socket `run/door/sock`, methods `initialize` · `tools/list` · `tools/call` · `ping` (§Standard Contracts → Engine door; PROVISIONAL — §Occupied Resources → Network ports). Since chunk 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door that wire is also reached over stdio through the relay `andromeda-pulse-engine door`, one connection per request; "over stdio per MCP spec" stays the sidecar's wire.

- **Error response schema (Tauri IPC)**: every `#[taurpc::procedure]` returns `Result<T, AppError>` where `AppError` is a `serde`-friendly enum with stable variants (`Validation { field, reason }`, `NotFound { resource }`, `Internal { message }`, `Plugin { plugin_id, message }`, `Storage { message }`, `Ingest { message }`). Module-internal code uses `thiserror`-derived enums and converts at the bridge via `From` impls. `main.rs` and any non-IPC top-level uses `anyhow::Result`.

- **Error response schema (OTLP receiver)**: per OpenTelemetry HTTP spec — non-2xx responses carry `Status` proto in body for HTTP/protobuf, or HTTP/JSON for HTTP/JSON; gRPC errors use standard `tonic::Status` codes.
- **Error response schema (MCP)**: standard JSON-RPC 2.0 error object with stable `code` (numeric), `message` (string), and optional `data`; MCP-spec error codes are honored.

- **File naming**: Rust files are `snake_case.rs`; one library crate per module under `crates/<module-name>/`; binary crate is `pulse-app/`. WIT interface files are `kebab-case.wit`. Webview source files follow the design specialist's convention (out of scope here).

- **Variable / function naming**: Rust `snake_case` for functions/variables/modules, `UpperCamelCase` for types/traits/enums, `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE` for constants — standard `cargo clippy` `style` group enforced in CI.

- **Endpoint naming**: OTLP endpoints are spec-fixed (`/v1/traces`, `/v1/metrics`, `/v1/logs`). Tauri IPC procedures use one of two authorized shapes: (a) top-level bare `snake_case` verbs for the cross-cutting envelope (`app_info`, `health`, `ready`, `get_settings`, `update_settings`); (b) `<router>.<verb>` dotted namespaces for per-crate routers (e.g., `traces.query`, `snapshot.generate`, `plugins.list`, `mcp.start`, `workspace.detect`). Both segments are `snake_case`. Occupied Resources is the canonical procedure list; the Convention defines the shape, not the enumeration.

- **Database entity naming**: DuckDB tables use plural `snake_case` matching the OTLP entity they hold (reserved set in Occupied Resources: `spans`, `span_events`, `metrics_points`, `log_records`, `log_templates` — every reserved table has a producer since chunk `2026-08-30-diagnostics-un-muting-harness-truth-sweep` deleted the three producer-less CREATEs); columns are `snake_case`; ring-buffer cutoff is enforced via a periodic `DELETE FROM <table> WHERE ts < now() - INTERVAL '<retention> minutes'` task sweeping only live tables. Occupied Resources is the canonical table-name list; the Convention defines the shape, not the enumeration.

- **Primary key convention**: spans use the OTLP-native 16-byte `trace_id` + 8-byte `span_id` as composite identity (no surrogate); **metric points use `(metric_name, ts_unix_nano, resource_hash, seq)`** and **log records use `(ts_unix_nano, resource_hash, severity_number, seq)`** — in BOTH cases the OTLP-native columns alone cannot separate two rows one resource emits in the same nanosecond. An OTLP LogRecord carries **no spec-defined unique id and no `name` column**, so its three native columns cannot separate two records at the same severity (an ordinary `INFO` burst); `metrics_points` carries a **scrubbed `labels` column** (`VARCHAR NOT NULL DEFAULT ''`, chunk `2026-08-23-metrics-points-labels`) that is deliberately OUTSIDE the key, so two data points of one metric differing only by their label set — the ordinary shape of any dimensioned metric — remain identical on every KEY column and are separated by `seq` alone; labels carry the dimension for read-back, never identity. (Before that chunk the table stored no attributes column at all, so the pair was indistinguishable in the stored row as well.) And since the metric name is span-masked at ingestion (`security::scrubber::mask_secret_spans`, chunk `2026-09-30-span-level-redaction`), two DISTINCT names that differ only inside a masked span mask to one text and collide there (a single-token credential-shaped name still masks whole; a multi-word name keeps its non-secret words). **No UUID or random surrogate keys are introduced** — `seq` is the one declared exception, now spanning BOTH tables: an internal disambiguating ordinal, allocated one block per batch from a per-table buffer-global counter (`BufferState::reserve_log_seq_block` / `BufferState::reserve_metric_seq_block` — separate counters, because one shared counter would couple two tables' allocation for no gain), and deliberately never an observable (absent from `BufferStateSnapshot`, `buffer.tick`, the `viz` `SELECT_LOGS` / `SELECT_METRICS` / `COUNT_METRICS` column lists, the `metrics.*` IPC response, and the MCP response shape). A per-batch ordinal on the `span_events.event_index` model is NOT sufficient for either table and was rejected: `event_index` is safe only because its key carries `(trace_id, span_id)`, a unique parent that scopes it, and neither `log_records` nor `metrics_points` has such a parent — a per-batch reset leaves two same-nanosecond rows in different export batches both at index 0. *(Measured 2026-08-22 and again 2026-08-23: the Arrow Appender enforces these keys at `flush()`, and a colliding pair fails the ENTIRE batch — chunks `2026-08-22-log-records-identity` and `2026-08-23-metrics-points-identity`, the latter measured live at `rows_ingested` 0 pre-fix → 5 post-fix.)*

- **Timestamp handling**: all DuckDB timestamp columns are `TIMESTAMPTZ` (DuckDB native, microsecond precision, UTC-stored); incoming OTLP nanosecond timestamps are stored as `TIMESTAMPTZ` (microsecond truncation accepted) plus a sibling `BIGINT` column `ts_unix_nano` when nanosecond precision is required for spec round-tripping.
- **Nullable patterns**: nullable columns are reserved for OTLP-spec-optional fields (e.g., `parent_span_id`, optional resource attributes); required spec fields are `NOT NULL`.

- **Module visibility discipline**: each crate exposes only its public contract via `pub`; cross-crate utilities use `pub(crate)`; no `pub use` re-exports across crate boundaries except in the explicit contract module of each crate.
- **Feature flags**: Cargo features are `kebab-case` (`mcp-server`, `otap-ingest`); default features are minimal (no `mcp-server`, no `otap-ingest`).

- **Configuration units**: durations in user-facing config are seconds with explicit units in field names (`retention_seconds`); ports are `u16` with `TryFrom<u16>` validating non-privileged-or-explicitly-allowed ranges.

title: Standard Contracts

body: - **Tauri IPC introspection — `app_info` command**: every TauRPC router exposes a top-level `app_info` returning the application identity envelope.

```json
  {
    "name": "andromeda-pulse",
    "version": "0.1.0",
    "rust_version": "1.95",
    "tauri_version": "2.x",
    "features": ["mcp-server"],
    "build_profile": "release"
  }
  ```
- **Tauri IPC liveness — `health` command**: returns liveness state of the in-process subsystems.

When degraded, `status` becomes `"degraded"` and any failing subsystem string becomes the failure reason (e.g., `"otlp_grpc_receiver": "bind_failed: address in use"`); HTTP-style status is implicit via the IPC `Result` (a hard failure returns `Err(AppError::Internal { ... })`).
- **Tauri IPC readiness — `ready` command**: returns whether the app is ready to ingest and serve queries.

```json
  {
    "ready": true,
    "checked_at": "2026-05-02T12:34:56Z",
    "checks": {
      "duckdb_connection": "ok",
      "ingest_mpsc_capacity_pct": 0,
      "broadcast_subscribers": 2,
      "plugins_loaded": 0,
      "mcp_server_enabled": false,
      "rows_ingested": 12000,
      "buffer_used_seconds": 120,
      "retention_seconds": 600
    }
  }
  ```
When not ready, `ready` is `false` and any failing check is the offending reason string (e.g., `"duckdb_connection": "init_in_progress"`).

- **OTLP receiver — spec-conformant**: `:4317` gRPC implements the `TraceService`, `MetricsService`, `LogsService` from `opentelemetry-proto`; `:4318` HTTP exposes `POST /v1/traces`, `POST /v1/metrics`, `POST /v1/logs` accepting `Content-Type: application/x-protobuf` (and `application/json` per spec). No project-specific envelope.

- **MCP server — spec-conformant**: standard MCP `tools/list` returns `query_traces`, `query_metrics`, `query_logs`, `generate_snapshot`, `query_incident_list`, `retrieve_report`, `retrieve_telemetry_slice`, `mark_incident_resolved` (these 4 added chunk #94), `retrieve_incident_events` (added chunk `2026-10-02-incident-events-readable-through-mcp`: input `{incident_id: integer}`, `additionalProperties: false`; response `{incident_id, events: [{event_kind, occurred_unix_nano}], total, truncated}`, oldest first, bounded at `INCIDENT_EVENTS_READ_LIMIT` = 256 with `truncated` set past it; `event_kind` coerced on egress to the closed `triage::contract::incident_event_kinds()` set, any other value reading `unknown`; an unknown id → JSON-RPC -32603 `incident not found`); standard `tools/call` invokes them with JSON-RPC 2.0 framing over stdio — the sidecar's carrier; the same nine are also invoked through the console engine's door (the next entry). Since chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process every `tools/list` entry carries a boolean member `write`, true for `mark_incident_resolved` alone (`tools_list_manifest()`, `crates/mcp-server/src/jsonrpc.rs`), in the sidecar's own answer too — the one change the sidecar's output took at that chunk. The manifest's `additionalProperties: false` is declared and not enforced by the sidecar: the tools' argument structs read past an undeclared member (as measured at that chunk, read in the source); the door refuses one itself. Capabilities, prompts, resources, sampling sections follow the MCP spec defaults.

- **Engine door — the tools inside the engine's process** (chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process; the form an outside reader depends on — Conductor reads the engine through it): **Connect** — a Unix-domain stream socket at `run/door/sock` under the data dir of a running `andromeda-pulse-engine run`, as the engine's own account. **Admission** — on every accepted connection the peer's account is read from the kernel and must equal the engine's effective account; any other account, root included, and a peer whose account cannot be read, sees the connection closed with no byte written. **Call** — one JSON-RPC 2.0 object per line, UTF-8, at most 65 536 bytes; a request with no `id` is not answered and runs nothing. Methods: `initialize` (the sidecar's `jsonrpc::initialize_result()` unchanged — `serverInfo.name` reads `andromeda-pulse-mcp`, protocol `2024-11-05`) · `tools/list` · `tools/call` · `ping`. `tools/call` carries `params.name` and `params.arguments` and runs one of the nine tools of the entry above through `mcp_server::tools::call_tool` over the engine's own handles — a read connection of the door's own taken from the engine's buffer connection, the engine's `Arc<dyn CorpusWriter>` and its `incident_workspace_key`; the door opens no database and no corpus, reads no `run/workspace-key` and prepares no SQL. `arguments` must be an object whose every member the tool's `inputSchema.properties` declares, else `-32602` before any tool runs. **The one write** — `mark_incident_resolved` answers `-32001` unless `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DOOR_RESOLVE` reads on; `tools/list` names it either way, marked `write`. **Answer** — one line, `result` as the tool returns it, at most 1 048 576 bytes; a longer answer is not cut, the caller gets `-32003`. **Bounds** — a request line over 65 536 bytes: `-32600`, the connection closed · a call over 5 s: `-32002`, and the door interrupts its own read connection · a connection with no complete line for 30 s, or a caller that does not read its answer, is closed · at most 8 connections, a ninth closed at accept · one tool call at a time. **Errors** — the JSON-RPC error object with a fixed message, never the tool's own text: `-32700` parse error · `-32600` request too large · `-32601` unknown tool / method not found · `-32602` invalid arguments · `-32603` tool failed · `-32001` the write is switched off · `-32002` timed out · `-32003` answer too large. So "no such incident" and a fault both read `-32603`. **Records** — `app.boot.door`, `door.call`, `door.refused`, closed labels only (obs-plan §6 and §8 hold their fields). Not shown: that the interrupt ends a real running query (no query of that chunk runs long enough). **Stdio** (since chunk 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door) — a caller with no socket client reaches the door by starting `andromeda-pulse-engine door` as the engine's own account. The relay resolves the data dir as `run` does (`engine_boot::resolve_data_dir()`) and canonicalizes the data dir and `{data dir}/run/door/sock` both sides; a socket that does not resolve, resolves outside the data dir, or has a path of 108 bytes or more is unreachable. Each standard-input line that is not whitespace alone takes a connection of its own, in order: the line is sent with its `\n` (an unterminated last line gets one), the write side shut, the whole answer read until the door closes, and only then written to standard output unchanged — the `tools/list` line through the relay equals a direct socket read byte for byte. A line over 65 536 bytes is sent as its first 65 537 bytes with no terminator and the rest of it discarded, never sent. The relay parses nothing, writes no answer of its own, retries nothing and has no time bound of its own; it writes no record and no file. Standard input ending is exit 0; a connect, write, shutdown or read failure on the socket, or a failed write of standard output, is exit 1 with the one fixed standard-error line `andromeda-pulse-engine door: the door cannot be reached` and nothing on standard output from the failed connection; off Unix the word prints that line and exits 1 at once. The door treats the relay as any caller: the account check, one `door.call` per answered request, a request with no `id` answered and recorded with nothing, no idle refusal (one connection per request). Another account through the relay receives no byte: on Linux a refused connection reads `EPIPE` or `ECONNRESET` at the client, so the relay exits 1 with the fixed line (as measured on `ci#38227488889`). The door's own form above is unchanged. Console program only, Unix only, in every build. PROVISIONAL — §Occupied Resources → Network ports, the door.
- **Common response envelope (Tauri IPC paginated lists)**: list-returning IPC commands wrap results in:

```json
  {
    "items": [],
    "total": 0,
    "next_cursor": null
  }
  ```
Cursor is an opaque string; absent (`null`) means "no more results."

- **Real-time push contract**: live span/metric streams to the webview use Tauri 2 IPC `Channel` API with binary Arrow IPC payloads (no JSON-stringify tax); event names are `pulse://stream/spans`, `pulse://stream/metrics`, `pulse://stream/logs`, `pulse://stream/snapshot-progress`, `pulse://stream/plugin-events`. SSE/WebSocket are not used because the consumer is in-process.

- **Capability record — the form another project reads**: `docs/capability-record.json` (`schema_version` 1; header `product` · `version` · `as_of` · `supersedes` · `legend`; `capabilities`, 82 entries P-001…P-082 in id order, each `id` · `title` · `disposition` · optional `note`) is the one current record of the capability ids. The accepted set is every entry whose `disposition` is the string `claimed`; an entry whose `disposition` is `retired` says with what in `surfaces` (closed words `window` · `model` · `desktop` · `workspace` · `training-export` · `corpus-encryption`) and by which working-route entry in `removed_by` (entry titles). Those three fields — `disposition`, `surfaces`, `removed_by` — are what the external harness (Conductor) derives its accepted set from; nothing else in the file is needed for it. A change of the form of those three fields is a change another repository reads, and is made known to it. The record is validated by `cargo xtask verify:capability-matrix` (§Occupied Resources → xtask CLI surfaces) and supersedes `docs/v0_2_0/pulse-capability-spec.md`, `docs/v0_2_0/capability-verification-matrix.json` and `andromeda-pulse-0.3.0/verification-matrix.json`, which stand unchanged until the working route retires or re-homes them.

The bind address is not configurable: the engine config holds two validated PORTS and `start` builds `127.0.0.1:{port}` itself (`loopback`, `pulse-app/src/engine_boot.rs`), so no caller can ask for a non-loopback bind; a rejected port variable records the bind as failed (`reason = "invalid_port"`) and starts no receiver. What listens is read from a spawned console engine's own socket list under `/proc` (since chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed): `pulse-app/tests/integration_console_engine.rs` asserts by set equality, in both census arms, that the listeners are exactly the two receivers on `127.0.0.1` and, since chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process, the one `unix` listener of the next bullet, and that under a rejected gRPC port variable the bind record reads `invalid_port`, that receiver is not started and the HTTP receiver and the door listen (until that chunk the census read the two receivers and no socket beyond them, the HTTP receiver alone under a rejected gRPC port). Read on the console program; the window app's socket list was not read.
  - The door — one Unix-domain stream socket, no TCP port (chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process): the console program `andromeda-pulse-engine run` holds a third listener, at the canonical `{data dir}/run/door/sock` (mode 0600, inside `run/door/`, mode 0700; §Filesystem locations), seated by `engine_boot::start` for `Program::Console` alone (`door::open`, `pulse-app/src/door.rs`) after the buffer and the corpus exist. The window app `pulse-app` opens no door and writes no door record; on a system that is not Unix the socket code is compiled out and no door is seated. A door that cannot bind — the closed outcomes `path_too_long` · `in_use` · `occupied` · `bind_failed` on the `app.boot.door` record — leaves the engine running with no door. Its form is §Standard Contracts → Engine door. **PROVISIONAL — a boundary widening, one item:** the endpoint, the owner check, the reach of the nine tools and of the one write, the write-switch variable and the workflow step that runs a client as a second account are the operator's answers (the pc overseer: at that chunk's P4 dialog, 2026-10-10, and the operator's reading of 2026-10-11 at its wrap); the founder's own word is owed on the surface itself, and nothing of it is ratified. Since chunk 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door the same item also covers the console program's third word `door` — the stdio relay to this socket (one connection per request; no file, listener, pid file, variable or binary of its own; an unreachable door is exit 1 with one fixed standard-error line) — and the second arm of the workflow step that runs a client as a second account: the operator's answers at that chunk's P4 (the pc overseer, 2026-10-12) and at its operator pass, and the operator's answer as the founder's delegate at its wrap; the founder's own word is still owed and nothing of it is ratified. Every other statement of the door in this document rests on this one.
  - `:24317` / `:24318` — harness-only defaults of `cargo xtask harness:engine-cycle` (chunk 2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine): the loopback ports it hands the console engine's two receivers for its own run through `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_GRPC_PORT` / `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_HTTP_PORT`. The verb refuses 4317 and 4318 in either flag (`shared-port`), so a cycle never binds the product defaults, and since chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed it refuses to start when either of its ports already accepts a connection (`port-taken`). Since that chunk the pair is also bound on every `cargo xtask pre-push:linux` run, whose sixth stage runs a cycle on these defaults and stops `cannot-evaluate` / `engine-port-taken` on a taken port before starting anything — the operator's reading (the pc overseer, 2026-10-10), PROVISIONAL, the founder's own word owed. No port is added to the product.
  - `:20000`–`:31999`, 24317 and 24318 left out — test-only loopback ports (chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed): a test that hands a port to an engine, or reads one after its listener is gone, uses a number CLAIMED from this range — held under an advisory file lock in `target/test-ports/` and shown bindable when claimed — never bound to port 0, read and released. Since chunk 2026-10-10-shared-telemetry-test-data the claim has one definition, `test_support::ports::claim_port` / `PortClaim` (`crates/test-support/src/ports.rs`; a panic when no port can be claimed), taken by seven test binaries since chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process (six before it): the five port-using binaries `agent_run_shell`, `engine_cycle_refusals`, `integration_console_engine`, `integration_door` (the fifth, since that chunk: its spawned engines' two ports) and `integration_engine_boot` (its in-process arms hand the engine two claimed ports each, held for the arm's life; four arms at chunk 2026-10-10-shared-telemetry-test-data), the `xtask` unit-test binary (one test each in `harness_ready.rs` and `engine_cycle.rs`, one claim each) and the member's own four tests. No test in `integration_engine_boot.rs`, `xtask/src/harness_ready.rs` or `xtask/src/engine_cycle.rs` binds port 0 and releases it any more; the 23 binds of port 0 that keep their listener are untouched. As measured at chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed, on the tree that still picked by bind-and-release one of seven hand runs of the three binaries that then claimed failed one arm on a port another process held, and after the claims 14 of 14 hand runs were green; at chunk 2026-10-10-shared-telemetry-test-data seven of seven hand runs of the four binaries were green (counts, not exclusions). 4317 and 4318 are bound by no test and no gate entry. No port is added to the product.

Each target carries its OWN exact obs allowlist leaf — a bare `metric` key exists carrying only `value`/`unit`/`module`, so a leaf-less `metric.*` target keeps `value` and has every label silently redacted. **P-025 measures the constellation DOT hue, not a Halo State Pulse canvas**: that canvas has no production render site (measured 2026-08-21), while the severity→hue semantic is live via `severityToHueFraction` on the dot (chunk 2026-08-21-delegated-timing-observables)

- **Tauri IPC events (broadcast channels)**: `pulse://stream/spans`, `pulse://stream/metrics`, `pulse://stream/logs`, `pulse://stream/snapshot-progress`, `pulse://stream/plugin-events` (deferred — no runtime emitter as of chunk #74; pending plugin invocation telemetry chunk), `pulse://stream/connection-state` (chunk #59), `pulse://stream/attention-cues` (chunk #62), `pulse://stream/restart-events` (chunk #63), `pulse://stream/service-lifecycle` (chunk #67), `pulse://stream/incidents` (chunk #78; **producer-only** — operator ruling 2026-08-30: producers exist but no consumer subscribes, the webview learns of incident changes through its ~1 s `incidents.list_active` poll; recorded rather than removed so a future consumer finds the topic reserved), `pulse://stream/cadence-events` (chunk #80 — cadence coordinator L6-visibility topic, `crates/triage/src/cadence/broadcast.rs:`), `pulse://stream/digests` (chunk #81), `pulse://stream/model-status` (chunk #82), `pulse://stream/config-events` (chunk #96). **Cross-window UI-coordination events** (a distinct class from the `pulse://stream/*` Rust→webview broadcast channels above — first-party webview↔webview frontend events via `@tauri-apps/api/event` emit/listen, gated by `core:event` in `pulse:default`, carrying no telemetry): `findings:dismissed` / `report:open` (`{incidentId}`) / `report:closed` (chunk 2026-07-10-incidents-floating-window-disclosure — the `findings` + `report` floating windows coordinate dismiss / open-report / restore-focus across windows).

- **Process / service identity**:
  - Tauri app bundle identifier: `com.andromeda.pulse`
  - **Dev-build binary (what `cargo build` emits): `target/{profile}/pulse-app` / `pulse-app.exe`** — Cargo's `[[bin]] name = "pulse-app"` governs every local build, so this is the path a harness, smoke command or plan invocation must name. **Bundled binary name (what the Tauri bundler produces for distribution): `andromeda-pulse` (Linux/macOS), `andromeda-pulse.exe` (Windows).** The two are NOT interchangeable and `target/{profile}/andromeda-pulse` exists on no host — recorded 2026-08-26 after a chunk plan's smoke command named exactly that path (one measured instance; the immediately preceding chunk's plan named `target/debug/pulse-app.exe` correctly, so the confusion is invited by this registry entry rather than systemic). The CORRECT `target/{profile}/andromeda-pulse*` paths are two, each a declared `[[bin]]` name: the console program `target/{profile}/andromeda-pulse-engine` (the `pulse-app` package's second `[[bin]]`, since chunk 2026-10-10-console-engine-entry-point; the package sets `default-run = "pulse-app"`, so `target/{profile}/pulse-app` stays the window app's path and the one bare `agent-run.sh boot` builds and spawns; since chunk 2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine `agent-run.sh boot engine` builds and spawns `target/release/andromeda-pulse-engine run` by path, so the harness names two binaries, one per program) and the sidecar below. `target/{profile}/andromeda-pulse` itself still exists on no host.

  - Console engine binary: `andromeda-pulse-engine` — the second `[[bin]]` of the `pulse-app` package (`pulse-app/src/bin/andromeda-pulse-engine.rs`; chunk 2026-10-10-console-engine-entry-point). Its `main` hands its arguments to `pulse_app::console::main`: a closed three-word command line (usage `usage: andromeda-pulse-engine <run|version|door>`; the third word since chunk 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door) — `run` boots the two receivers, the buffer, the detectors and the corpus through the shared `pulse_app::engine_boot` with no window, no display and no model runner — and, since chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process, the door, which `engine_boot::start` seats for `Program::Console` alone and nowhere else (`door::open`, then `tokio::spawn(door.serve())`; neither entry point changed; PROVISIONAL — §Network ports, the door) — and stays up until SIGTERM or SIGINT (recorded as `app.exit` with class `signal`, the signal re-raised; no event loop, no `stop` command); `version` prints one line and exits 0; `door` is the stdio relay (`pulse_app::door_bridge::main`) — a client of a running console engine's `run/door/sock`, started by a stdio agent, which builds no tokio runtime, calls neither `engine_boot::init_process` nor `engine_boot::start`, and adds no listener, port, file, pid file, log record, variable or binary; it exits 0 when standard input ends and 1 with the one fixed standard-error line `andromeda-pulse-engine door: the door cannot be reached` when the door cannot be reached (at once off Unix; §Standard Contracts → Engine door, Stdio; PROVISIONAL — §Network ports, the door); any other command line prints usage on stderr and exits 2, creating nothing. The product binaries are three: `pulse-app` (the window app), `andromeda-pulse-engine` (the console program), `andromeda-pulse-mcp` (the stdio sidecar). The credential service id `com.andromeda.pulse` is written in one place for both engine programs, `engine_boot::os_key_backend()`. Not shown: the binary inside a distribution bundle (what `tauri build` does with a second `[[bin]]` is not measured), or run as a background service.
  - MCP sidecar binary (when feature enabled): `andromeda-pulse-mcp`

- **Cargo workspace crate names**: `ingest`, `buffer`, `viz`, `ui-bridge`, `snapshot`, `curation`, `triage`, `workspace-detector`, `plugins`, `mcp-server`, `corpus`, `security`, `interpretation`, `config-watcher`, `pulse-app`, `xtask`, `test-support` — these seventeen names are reserved at the workspace level and cannot be reused by scopes. `test-support` (the member `crates/test-support`, `publish = false`, since chunk 2026-10-10-shared-telemetry-test-data) is test support and never product: a library crate with two modules, `otlp` (the telemetry test factories) and `ports` (the test port claim, §Network ports), taken as a dev-dependency only — `buffer`, `pulse-app` and `xtask` name it under `[dev-dependencies]`, it depends on `ingest` alone, and no product target links it (§Cross-cutting Patterns → Module dependency direction).

- **DuckDB database / schema names**:
  - In-memory database identity: `pulse_buffer` (single in-memory `:memory:` DuckDB connection, schema `main`)
