since chunk 2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-named-from-a-run the step has two neighbours in the `boot` job, its own lines unchanged — `Build the exit witness` before it, after the release build (`cc -shared -fPIC -O2` builds `scripts/exit-witness.c` into `$RUNNER_TEMP` and names it through `$GITHUB_ENV` as `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_EXIT_WITNESS_LIB`; no `LD_PRELOAD` in the step), and `Boot series (equal source)` after it and before `ci-gates` (`if: always()`, a plain `run: cargo xtask harness:boot-series --count 7`, no soft-fail key), each held by its own workflow test in the same file, three in all; they share `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR`, which every job exports to `$GITHUB_ENV` from a step right after harden-runner — `runner.*` is unavailable in workflow- and job-level `env:` (chunk 2026-09-29-p-025-hue-shift-observable-made-gradable). `boot`'s readiness poll runs `cargo xtask harness:ready` since chunk 2026-10-09-boot-smoke-s-early-exit-found-and-closed (same threaded `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_PIDFILE` / `_LOGFILE`, same `HARNESS_STATUS_TIMEOUT`, default 10 s; asked `--program window` by bare `boot` and `--program console` by `boot engine` in the sh script since chunk 2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine), so it reports ready only on the `running-healthy` status verdict for the program asked plus both receivers reading `accepting` — a connection accepted on each OTLP port and this run's own bound record for it in the log family (`harness:ready`'s entry, above; chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed). A second caller of the sh script since that chunk: `cargo xtask harness:engine-cycle` runs `boot engine`, `status engine` and `cleanup` (its own entry, above). A third since chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed: the sixth stage of `cargo xtask pre-push:linux` runs `cleanup` once on its stage data dir, with the two cycle port variables beside the stage child set, when its engine cycle left a port accepting or its engine alive (its own entry, below). On a failed readiness poll `boot` reports how the app ended — `app ended: {record}` from the exit record, or `app still running (pid N) but never reported healthy`, followed, when the last readiness verdict held a `refusing` label, by `the receivers never both accepted: OTLP gRPC 127.0.0.1:{port}, OTLP HTTP 127.0.0.1:{port}`, and, when it held a `foreign` label, by `a receiver port accepts but this run's log holds no bound record for it: OTLP gRPC 127.0.0.1:{port}, OTLP HTTP 127.0.0.1:{port}` (the sh script alone, since chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed; both lines can print) — and runs `bash "$0" cleanup`; `agent-run.ps1 boot` mirrors the poll and the `refusing` line through `Invoke-Ready` (parsed by `pwsh` with 0 parse errors, never run) and was not edited at that chunk: its readiness branch matches `refusing` alone and prints no `foreign` line. `cargo xtask smoke:hue-shift` — the P-025 scenario leg implemented at `xtask/src/hue_shift.rs` (chunk 2026-09-29-p-025-hue-shift-observable-made-gradable; registered per the same formalized-CLI-contract rule): drives a finite storm against the release binary and grades the emitted `metric.constellation.hue_update_ms` samples, the rise against `interpretation.incident.created` and the fall against the first `triage.incident.auto_resolve.tick` with `resolved_count ≥ 1`, each on anchor error ≤ 1000 ms. Contract: exit 0 PASS · 1 FAIL · 2 INCONCLUSIVE (a precondition unmet, e.g. no incident formed); artifact under `target/hue-shift/`. Dev-host only — not wired into CI. `cargo xtask smoke:discovery` — the P-027 scenario leg implemented at `xtask/src/discovery.rs` (chunk 2026-09-30-p-027-discovery-bound; registered per the same formalized-CLI-contract rule, reusing `xtask/src/external_resolve.rs`'s direct-binary helpers): boots the release binary on a fresh data dir, waits (≤ 60 s) for a `services.list_with_states.request` record, then starts `inject_demo --sustained --error-pct=0`, and grades the first `metric.constellation.discovery_ms` record at or after the first `duckdb.append {table_name: spans}` (the first sighting) within a 30 s observe window — PASS iff the interval ≤ 5000 ms, the sample's own anchor (`timestamp − duration_ms`) lies ≤ 1000 ms from that append, and the log holds 0 `app.panic.fatal` and 0 ERROR. Contract: exit 0 PASS · 1 FAIL · 2 INCONCLUSIVE (no spans append, the webview not polling before it, a window below 21 s, or a data dir already holding a log family); artifact under `target/discovery/`. Dev-host only — not wired into CI. `cargo xtask smoke:gap-resume` (`xtask/src/gap_resume.rs`, chunk 2026-08-28-ingest-consumer-initiating-freeze) and `cargo xtask smoke:external-resolve` (`xtask/src/external_resolve.rs`, chunk 2026-08-29-app-registry-reconciliation) — the two remaining sibling scenario legs, dev-host only and not wired into CI: gap-resume drives seed → gap → resume and takes its verdict from the shipped `ingest_progress::evaluate`, in three arms (the default gap arm, `--sustained`, `--reconnect-only`), each proving its own precondition; external-resolve resolves an incident through a real `andromeda-pulse-mcp` subprocess and grades on `reconciled_count` ≥ 1 with `declined_count` 0 (INCONCLUSIVE when no incident formed or the resolve did not apply). `cargo xtask pre-push:linux` — the native Linux pre-push verb implemented at `xtask/src/pre_push.rs` (chunk 2026-09-29-ci-wall-time-and-round-trips; it runs on the Linux dev host itself since chunk 2026-10-09-pre-push-check-native-on-linux, which removed the hop to a second operating system and its copy of the repository; registered per the same formalized-CLI-contract rule). Contract: exit 0 green · 1 red · 2 cannot-evaluate; one pretty-JSON verdict on stdout `{verdict, reason, head, tree, stages[{name, ok, ms}], missing[]}` — six members, pinned by set equality, none carrying a value of an environment variable or a path — plus a twin at `target/pre-push/report.json`. Reasons, complete: `all-stages-ok` · `not-linux` · `pins-unreadable` · `home-unset` · `provisioning-missing` · `run-dir-unusable` · `tree-unreadable` · `stage-failed:{stage}` · `restore-failed:bindings` · `engine-port-taken` · `engine-cycle-unevaluated` — eleven (nine until chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed; the two it added both read `cannot-evaluate`). Linux host only: any other system reads `cannot-evaluate` / `not-linux`. A run goes, in order: the host guard → its two pins, read from the repo — the `rust-toolchain.toml` channel and ci.yml's `node-version` major (either unreadable is `pins-unreadable`) → `HOME` (unset or empty is `home-unset`) → the provisioning probes → the per-run area → `head` and `tree` → the stages. Every probe and stage child is spawned with a CLEARED environment plus exactly `HOME` · `PATH` (`{HOME}/.cargo/bin`, then the directory of the first `node` file found in an absolute directory of the verb's own PATH — left out when there is none — then `/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin`) · `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` (`target/pre-push/run/data`, absolute) · for the `npm` stage only `PUPPETEER_CACHE_DIR` (`target/pre-push/run/puppeteer`, absolute) · for the three git calls that compute `head` and `tree` only `GIT_INDEX_FILE` (`target/pre-push/run/index`); the session bus address, the runtime dir and the display variables are not in the set (pinned by set equality), so no stage reaches an OS credential store. One child is given more since chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed: the single `cleanup` child the sixth stage runs when its engine cycle left a port accepting or its engine alive also carries `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_GRPC_PORT` / `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_HTTP_PORT` (24317 / 24318), so its probe never touches 4317 or 4318; the cycle that stage starts builds its own children's cleared set (`harness:engine-cycle`'s entry, above), which holds no session bus address and no runtime dir either. A missing piece reads `cannot-evaluate` / `provisioning-missing`, named in `missing[]`, never green: `rust:{channel}` (the pinned channel absent from `rustup toolchain list`), `rust:clippy` and `cargo-nextest` (probed with `cargo +{channel} … --version` only when the channel is listed — a `cargo +{channel}` call against an absent channel could install it), `node:{pin} (found {version})` (the `node --version` major against the pin; `none` when no `node` answered, `unreadable` when the output is not a short version token), `tool:npm`, `tool:git`, `tool:cc`, `tool:python3` (`python3`, else `python`, printing `Python 3`); the verb installs nothing and prints no install command. The per-run area `target/pre-push/run/` (`data/`, `puppeteer/`, the temporary index) is the verb's own, removed and created again once the provisioning check has passed (a failure is `run-dir-unusable`), so a `provisioning-missing` run rewrites only the report twin; the verb touches nothing else under `target/pre-push/` and never `~/.cache/puppeteer`. `head` and `tree` (HEAD's sha and the tree id of HEAD plus the working tree) are computed through the temporary `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, the real index untouched (a failed git read is `tree-unreadable`). It then runs, in the working tree, `script-modes` · `source-lint` (`cargo xtask check:english-sources`; since chunk 2026-10-01-real-model-incident-surfacing) · `npm` · `clippy` · `test` · `ci-gates` in order — six stages, each stage's output on stderr — stopping at the first failure. The `test` stage rewrites the tracked `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts`, and the verb puts that file back as it found it whichever way the stage ended (a file absent before is removed again; a restore that fails is red, `restore-failed:bindings`); the restore runs when the stage's command returns, not on a signal, so a verb killed in the middle of `test` leaves the bindings rewritten. The sixth stage (`ci-gates`) reads a real console engine cycle since chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed, in place of a seed log of three records the stage wrote itself. In order: the stage data dir is removed and created again; either cycle port (24317, 24318) already accepting stops the run `cannot-evaluate` / `engine-port-taken` with nothing started; `cargo xtask harness:engine-cycle --data-dir {that dir}` runs under the stage child set; then both ports and the pid of that data dir's pid file are read — one still accepting or alive, and the script's `cleanup` runs once on that data dir and the stage is red (`stage-failed:ci-gates`) whatever the cycle returned; else a cycle exit of 2 is `cannot-evaluate` / `engine-cycle-unevaluated`, an exit of 0 hands the stage to `cargo xtask ci-gates` over the same data dir, and any other exit is red. Stage names, their order and the six verdict members are unchanged; a stage that stops `cannot-evaluate` is listed `"ok": false`. The cycle's engine writes its corpus-key lock file to the temp dir, its child set holding no runtime dir (§Filesystem locations). As measured on the warm dev host with the engine already built in release (that chunk's `evidence/gate-readings.md` and `evidence/operator-pass.md`): four green runs of the verb at 107.04, 108.13, 109.07 and 110.44 s, the sixth stage 18.8 to 19.0 s over a log family of 335 records each time; no cold release build was timed, and a taken port on 24317 / 24318 and the teardown after a cycle that left an engine were not read live — the decision is pinned (seven pins), the teardown call by one pin against a real process. It starts no `pulse-app`. Until that chunk the verb bound no port and started no program; since it the sixth stage, and no other, starts the console engine `andromeda-pulse-engine` and binds loopback 24317 and 24318 (never 4317 or 4318). That change is the operator's reading (the pc overseer, 2026-10-10), PROVISIONAL — a boundary widening on which the founder's own word is owed. Since chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process the engine that stage starts — like every engine `harness:engine-cycle` starts — also opens the door's Unix-domain listener at `run/door/sock` inside its own data dir (the stage's socket path is 82 bytes by that chunk's research computation, not re-measured); the same PROVISIONAL item covers it (the operator's reading of 2026-10-11), no verb, script word, status or verdict shape changed, and `check:engine-log` passes over a log holding one `app.boot.door` record. The verb reads `HOME` and `PATH` from its own environment by value, to build the stage environment, and prints or writes neither (§Environment variables). Its Node is whichever `node` stands first on the caller's PATH: on the dev host Node 24 is a user-level `mise` install (v24.21.0 with npm 11.19.0, as measured on the dev host at chunk 2026-10-09-pre-push-check-native-on-linux's `evidence/node-24-install.md`) beside the host's default Node 26, so a green run is started with the Node 24 directory first on PATH, and a run started without it reads `cannot-evaluate`, never green. Dev-host only — not wired into CI. `cargo xtask perf:budget --data-dir <DIR> --require <arm,arm>` — the perf-budget grader implemented at `xtask/src/perf_budget.rs` (chunk 2026-09-30-perf-budget-gate-reads-real-samples; registered per the same formalized-CLI-contract rule): grades `<DIR>/logs/agent-latest.jsonl*` — every family member, concatenated — against the obs-plan §10 budgets: frame `fields.duration_ms` p99 ≤ 33.0 ms, memory `fields.value` max ≤ 512 000 000, snapshot `fields.duration_ms` p99 ≤ 500.0 ms, p99 by nearest rank (the ⌈0.99·n⌉-th smallest). A graded field that is not a JSON number is Unreadable and fails the gate whether or not its arm is required; a memory sample of 0 counts but is not informative. Contract: one line per arm, then `perf-budget: PASS|FAIL|NEUTRAL`; exit 0 PASS · 1 FAIL (an arm over budget, an Unreadable arm, or a `--require`d arm with no sample) · 2 cannot-evaluate (an unknown arm name, no log family under `<DIR>/logs`, or every arm empty with none required); never PASS over empty input. An empty frame arm names its cause, derived by `xtask::perf_budget::frame_cause` from the same log's `ui.webgpu.adapter` records (none → `no adapter record in this log`; any `obtained` → `adapter obtained but no frame recorded`; else → `no WebGPU adapter ({the distinct outcomes, sorted, comma-joined})`): an unrequired one prints `frame: cannot-evaluate: 0 samples, {cause}`, a `--require`d one `frame NEUTRAL — {cause} (required) FAIL` (chunk 2026-09-30-perf-instruments-measure-their-budgets). Wired in ci.yml's lint-test Linux as `--require memory,snapshot` over the `perf_budget_samples` producer log. `cargo xtask perf:load-profiles` alone runs the same grader in-process with no arm required; `cargo xtask check:engine-log` calls it in-process for the memory arm alone, as required (`perf_budget::grade_arm`, chunk 2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine); `cargo xtask ci-gates` runs no grader and prints no perf-budget, frame or heartbeat line since chunk 2026-10-10-no-gate-stands-while-reading-nothing (its own entry follows); the `xtask/ci/perf-slo-check.{sh,ps1}` scripts the two once called are deleted. `cargo xtask ci-gates` — the obs-log reading gate implemented at `xtask/src/ci_gates.rs` (chunk 2026-10-10-no-gate-stands-while-reading-nothing; registered per the same rule). It reads the app's log family `agent-latest.jsonl*` under the resolved log dir in two arms: zero-spans (the family holds at least one record; a non-empty line is a record whether or not it parses) and zero-panic (no `app.panic.fatal` record at level ERROR). Contract: exit 0 PASS with exactly `ci-gates: zero-spans PASS ({n} log records across {k} file(s))` and `ci-gates: zero-panic PASS` · 1 FAIL — members holding zero records (`::error::ci-gates: zero-spans FAIL (log files present but contain no events)`), or a panic record (the zero-spans PASS line, then `::error::ci-gates: zero-panic FAIL: app.panic.fatal at {member file name}:{line}`) · 2 cannot-evaluate — the log dir absent or holding no family member (`::error::ci-gates: cannot-evaluate (no agent-latest.jsonl* file in the log dir)`); never a pass over an absent family (before that chunk: exit 0 with four NEUTRAL lines). A member that cannot be read is skipped with `ci-gates: skipping {file name} (unreadable)`; `::error::` lines go to stderr, the rest to stdout; the output holds closed labels, counts, a member's file name and a line number, never a record's text or a path. It adds no environment variable, port, TauRPC procedure or capability. Run by ci.yml's `boot` job after the smoke and the series, and by `pre-push:linux`'s sixth stage over the log family of the real console engine cycle that stage just ran, in the same data dir and only when the cycle exited 0 (until chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed, over a seed log the stage wrote itself). `cargo xtask quarantine-tracking` — the quarantine convention gate, the script pair `xtask/ci/quarantine-tracking-check.{sh,ps1}` (contract registered at the same chunk). It scans the `.rs` files under five search dirs — `crates`, `pulse-app/src`, `pulse-app/tests`, `xtask/src` and, since chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed, `xtask/tests` (four until then; the `.sh` and the `.ps1` mirror both take the entry) — for a line-anchored `#[ignore]` and fails one with no GitHub issue URL in its surrounding window. Contract: a missing search dir → exit 1 with `::error::quarantine-tracking-check: search dir {dir} is missing` per missing dir, relative to the root · a scan of zero `.rs` files → exit 1 · an untracked `#[ignore]` → exit 1 · otherwise exit 0 with `quarantine-tracking-check: PASS (0 quarantine(s) across {N} file(s))`, or `PASS ({k} quarantine(s) tracked via GitHub issue URL across {N} file(s))`; no NEUTRAL arm, never a pass over an absent or empty input (before that chunk both read NEUTRAL, exit 0). The `.sh` is held by six pins that run it with `bash` over scratch roots (five until chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed, which added one for `xtask/tests`); the `.ps1` mirror was parsed by `pwsh` with 0 parse errors and never run, its `xtask/tests` entry included. Run by ci.yml's `lint-test` job. `cargo xtask perf:frame-sample` — the dev-host frame-budget gate implemented at `xtask/src/perf_frame.rs` (same chunk and rule): Windows only; boots `target/release/pulse-app.exe` on a fresh TempDir with `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` and `WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS` (a SwiftShader WebGPU flag set) in the app CHILD's environment only, waits ≤ 60 s for a first frame sample, feeds `target/release/examples/inject_demo.exe --sustained` for 30 s, stops the app by pid and confirms :4317/:4318 released, then grades the frame arm as required. Contract: exit 0 PASS · 1 FAIL (0 frame samples once the app is healthy, or p99 > 33 ms) · 2 INCONCLUSIVE (not Windows, a release binary missing, :4317/:4318 already accepting, or the app never healthy); artifact under `target/perf-frame/<UTC stamp>/`; a 0-sample run prints `perf:frame-sample: frame: 0 samples — {cause}` from the same derivation. Dev-host only — not wired into CI: the hosted Windows runner produced 0 frame samples under the same flag set with the app healthy (`ci#36723465727`; operator decision 2026-09-30). `cargo xtask verify:capability-matrix` — the capability record's gate, implemented at `xtask/src/capability_record.rs` (chunk 2026-10-10-capability-record-re-based; registered per the same formalized-CLI-contract rule; `evaluate` reads both files, `judge` is the pure verdict; one caller, the verb in `xtask/src/main.rs`): reads two fixed in-repo paths held as constants, `docs/capability-record.json` and `andromeda-pulse-0.4.0/working-route.md`, with no path argument and no environment variable. Contract: exit 0 clean · 1 findings · 2 cannot-evaluate (the record absent, unreadable, not JSON or without a `capabilities` array; the route absent or unreadable); one line `verify:capability-matrix: {clean|violations} ({n} ids: {c} claimed, {r} retired, {k} violation(s))`, the counts read from the record, or `verify:capability-matrix: cannot-evaluate ({reason})`; one JSON event line (target `xtask.verify_capability_matrix`) and the report twin `target/capability-matrix/report.json`, both carrying `state` · `capability_count` · `claimed_count` · `retired_count` · `violation_count` · `reason`, the twin adding `violations` and `generated_at`. Findings: the id set not exactly P-001…P-082 once each; a `disposition` that is neither `claimed` nor `retired`; a `legend` not equal to the module's three closed sets; a claimed entry without a carrying requirement in P-083…P-129 (or a `note` saying why none carries it), without a scenario beyond `source-evidence`, with an unknown scenario kind or verification mode, a file ref that does not exist, a `contains` anchor not found, or an `external` / `manual` / `by-construction` scenario with no `note`; a retired entry carrying a `scenarios`, `verification_mode` or `carried_by` key, an empty or unknown `surfaces`, a `removed_by` or `kept_half_owner` title no working-route entry carries, or a `guard` that is absent, of an unknown state, or without the list its state requires; a record with no claimed id. A route entry's title is its line without a leading `[marker] ` stamp, up to the first ` — `. It validates no proof of a retired id. Runs as a `run:` step of ci.yml's `lint-test` job after `capability-widening-check`. It reads a file the wrap writes: a route-resolve that renames, retires or splits an entry the record names reddens it until the record is corrected. Before that chunk it read `docs/v0_2_0/capability-verification-matrix.json` (P-001…P-060) and exited 0 or 1, an absent file falling into the generic error exit.

- **Tauri capability identifiers (reserved at arch level)**: `pulse:default`, `pulse:tray`, `pulse:notification`, `pulse:updater`, `pulse:plugin-fs`, `pulse:clipboard` — concrete capability JSON files live in `pulse-app/capabilities/`.
- **Updater channel**: `latest.json` published to GitHub Releases under the canonical repository; updater public key is shipped baked into the Tauri config.

- **Bundle artifact names** (per release): `andromeda-pulse_<version>_x64-setup.msi`, `andromeda-pulse_<version>_x64.dmg`, `andromeda-pulse_<version>_aarch64.dmg`, `andromeda-pulse_<version>_amd64.AppImage`, `andromeda-pulse_<version>_amd64.deb`.
- **Docker volumes**: N/A — no Docker.

title: Infrastructure Patterns

body: Contracts: .andromeda/registries/architecture-contracts.toml — ask registry.py contracts; read one contracts/architecture/{key}.md; never whole.

title: Cross-cutting Patterns

body: - **Config management**: layered with explicit precedence (highest wins) — process env vars (`ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*`) > user `~/.andromeda-pulse/config.toml` > built-in defaults. No external secrets manager (this is a local OSS desktop app); code-signing secrets live only in GitHub Actions encrypted secrets and Azure Key Vault.

- **Self-observation discipline**: `opentelemetry-stdout` (or file exporter targeting `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/`) is the only exporter the product itself uses for its own telemetry; the OTLP network exporter is never pointed at the product's own `:4317`/`:4318` ports. Any future "outbound observer" variable must be explicitly distinct from the inbound receiver port variables.

- **Feature-gate hygiene**: `--features mcp-server` and `--features otap-ingest` (and any future flags) are off by default; flag-specific dependencies (`rmcp`, OTAP-specific crates) only enter the build graph when the feature is enabled, preserving the small-binary baseline. That holds for `rmcp`; the workspace crate `mcp-server` is not flag-specific since chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process — `pulse-app` names it as a plain dependency and links it in every build (the console engine's door calls its dispatch), and the `mcp-server` feature only forwards `mcp-server-crate/mcp-server`; `Cargo.lock` and `deny.toml` did not change.

- **Cross-bridge data shape**: any type that crosses the TauRPC bridge or appears in an MCP tool response must be `serde::Serialize`; this is enforced at compile time by the bridge derive macros. Internal-only types are not constrained.

- **OS notification policy**: native OS notifications (via `tauri-plugin-notification`, gated by capability `pulse:notification`) fire on completion of `pulse://stream/snapshot-progress` and on updater state transitions; no other subsystem emits notifications without an explicit decision. User opt-out is a single boolean `notifications_enabled` in `~/.andromeda-pulse/config.toml` (default `true`); when disabled, the snapshot generator and updater still complete their work but suppress the toast. Notification text shape and per-locale strings are owned by the design specialist.

- **Tray icon policy**: a single tray icon (gated by capability `pulse:tray`) is the always-on surface that signals app-running state and offers a minimal action menu — at minimum: open/focus the main window, show ingest summary (current spans/sec, retention used), toggle MCP server (only when `--features mcp-server` is built and the `mcp-server` crate is loaded), generate snapshot (invokes `snapshot.generate`), quit. Tray click on the icon focuses or restores the main window; closing the main window minimizes to tray rather than terminating the process (process termination requires the explicit Quit menu item or OS-level kill). Tray icon glyphs and per-locale menu labels are owned by the design specialist; menu accessibility (keyboard navigation, screen-reader labels) is owned by the a11y specialist.

- **Webview IPC capability policy**: the main webview window runs under capability `pulse:default`. Tauri capabilities are **negative-default** — nothing the capability does not grant is reachable — but the granularity is the IPC LAYER, **not** the individual TauRPC procedure: TauRPC dispatches every router method through ONE invoke handler (`taurpc::create_ipc_handler`), which `core:default` admits, so `pulse-app/capabilities/` holds **no per-procedure entries** (measured 2026-08-21: `default.json` grants `core:default` + seven `core:window:*` + `updater:default`, and three procedures were added with the file untouched while `xtask capability-drift` stayed clean). Adding a TauRPC procedure therefore requires a router registration in the owning crate, an entry in Occupied Resources, and its `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` pin in `xtask/src/main.rs` — which the `capability-drift` gate diffs against BOTH the worktree bindings AND, since chunk 2026-08-30-staged-bindings-assertion, the git-INDEX copy of `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` (the gate additionally asserts the staged `pulse-app/capabilities/*.json` grants against `staged_gate::EXPECTED_GRANTS` and folds any non-clean staged outcome into the same failure exit, so a pin edit must be STAGED together with the regenerated bindings or the gate reds) — **not** a capability-JSON edit. What DOES require an explicit per-feature capability addition with a stated rationale is a Tauri **core API** surface: filesystem, shell, dialog and http are not granted to `pulse:default`, and each `core:window:*` permission a frameless-window affordance needs (`allow-start-dragging`, `allow-close`, `allow-set-size`, …) is granted individually — those ARE silently rejected at runtime when missing. The updater capability `pulse:updater` is bound to the `tauri-plugin-updater` flow that consumes `latest.json` from GitHub Releases and is not exposed to webview JavaScript.

- **Module dependency direction**: dependencies in `Cargo.toml` flow toward the `pulse-app` binary; no library crate depends on the binary crate; no library crate depends on a sibling unless its declared contract requires it. One carve-out, since chunk 2026-10-10-shared-telemetry-test-data: a dev-only edge from a member to `test-support` is allowed, and only that — PROVISIONAL (the operator's word, the pc overseer, 2026-10-10, kept at that chunk's wrap as the operator's reading; the founder's own word is owed; not the founder's word). It is pinned by a committed test, the test-only `xtask` module `test_support_edges`: it reddens if any member names `test-support` outside its `[dev-dependencies]`, or if `test-support` depends on anything but `ingest`, whose types it builds. As built, `buffer`, `pulse-app` and `xtask` name it under `[dev-dependencies]`; `ingest` does not name it. The graph the product is built from forms a DAG with `pulse-app` as the only root; no product target links `test-support`.

- **Test-time telemetry injection**: end-to-end tests inject synthetic spans/metrics/logs by speaking OTLP to the running receiver on `:4317` (gRPC) or `:4318` (HTTP) — the same surface external SDKs use. No in-process test-mode bypass, no separate "test ingest" feature flag, no mock-channel back-door. Tests that need a non-default port resolve it via `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_GRPC_PORT` / `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_HTTP_PORT`. Tests that need to inspect buffer state read it back through the TauRPC `traces.*` / `metrics.*` / `logs.*` query routers. The console program mounts no TauRPC router: a test of it still injects over real OTLP (gRPC to the bound receiver) and reads state back from the program's own log records on a spawned run, or from the `EngineHandles` that `engine_boot::start` returns in an in-process arm, or, since chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process, through the door (`pulse-app/tests/integration_door.rs` sends a log record over real OTLP and reads it back with a `query_logs` call on `run/door/sock`) — a product surface, not a test-mode bypass: injection is still OTLP only; the query routers remain the read-back path for the window app.

- **Development Style**: agent-driven. Downstream specialist plans (tests, obs, setup-project) should branch their research toward agent-driven development workflows (deterministic harness invocations, machine-parseable outputs, schema-stable contracts, `cargo xtask` task surfaces).

title: Project Intent

body: - **Product type**: cross-platform desktop application (Windows / macOS / Linux) shipped as native bundles, and — since chunk 2026-10-10-console-engine-entry-point — a second program over the same engine: the console program `andromeda-pulse-engine`, driven by a closed three-word command line (`run` | `version` | `door`) with no window and no display — `door` (since chunk 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door; PROVISIONAL — §Occupied Resources → Network ports, the door) a stdio relay to the running engine's door that hosts no engine part. Not a web app, not a microservice fleet. What the console program is not yet: a background service, a bundled release artifact, or a place where an incident forms without the deterministic gate set.
- **Scale intent**: startup. Single-machine, single-user; no tenancy, no orchestration, no clustering.

- **Growth model**: modular monolith (twelve Rust crates wired by one shared engine boot into two programs of the `pulse-app` package — the Tauri window app and the console engine `andromeda-pulse-engine`) with a WASM Component Model plugin extension layer for third-party additions. Internal modules are the unit of growth for first-party functionality; WASM components are the unit of growth for community/third-party functionality.

- **How new functionality is added**:
  - First-party features: new scopes via `/andromeda-scope-arch`, which generally adds either (a) a new Cargo crate to the workspace following the established crate-per-module pattern, or (b) new TauRPC routers/queries/snapshot strategies inside an existing crate. The twelve reserved crate names cannot be re-purposed.
  - Third-party features: WASM Component Model plugins dropped into `~/.andromeda-pulse/plugins/`, exposing functionality through host-imported WIT interfaces with capability-scoped access.

- **Template patterns**: each library crate follows the same shape — a public contract module (the only `pub` surface), `pub(crate)` internals, `thiserror`-derived error enum, and (where applicable) a TauRPC-router module mounted by `pulse-app`. Plugin authors follow the WIT-interface template under `crates/plugins/wit/` and the example plugins under `plugins-examples/`.

title: Inherited Defaults

body: - Language / runtime: Rust 2024 edition (toolchain pinned 1.95.0; declared `rust-version = "1.95"`, equal to the pin and set by the resolved dependency graph, held equal by the xtask test `declared_floor_equals_the_pinned_channel`; the workspace's own code needs rustc ≥ 1.89), single Tokio multi-threaded runtime.
- Desktop shell: Tauri 2.x with TauRPC IPC bridge.

- Backend framework (in-process receivers): `tonic` 0.14.x (gRPC, `:4317`) + `axum` 0.8.x on `hyper` 1.x + `tower` (HTTP, `:4318`). Open question carried from Established Decisions: if `opentelemetry-otlp` 0.31's transitive pin on `tonic` 0.13 cannot be resolved at lock time, the fallback is to downgrade Stack to `tonic` 0.13.x (matching `opentelemetry-otlp`) rather than fork or wait for upstream; the Stack/Decisions/Defaults rows are then re-pinned in the same iteration.
- Database: DuckDB 1.5.x via the `duckdb` crate — requirement `1.10500` (caret), lockfile-resolved 1.10505.0 as of 2026-08-28 — in-memory ring buffer (5–10 min retention, configurable).
- ORM / migrations: none — direct SQL via `duckdb` crate `Connection` + `Appender`; schema created on startup.
- Columnar interchange: Apache Arrow zero-copy via `Appender::append_record_batch()` / `stream_arrow()`.
- Channels: `tokio::sync::mpsc` for ingest→appender, `tokio::sync::broadcast` for buffer→subscribers.

- API style — internal IPC: TauRPC routers, one per crate, with two authorized procedure shapes — top-level bare `snake_case` verbs for the cross-cutting envelope (`app_info`, `health`, `ready`, `get_settings`, `update_settings`) and `<router>.<verb>` dotted namespaces for per-crate routers (`traces.query`, `snapshot.generate`, `plugins.list`, etc.). See Conventions for the shape rule and Occupied Resources for the canonical procedure list.
- API style — external OTLP: spec-fixed (`/v1/traces`, `/v1/metrics`, `/v1/logs` on `:4318`; gRPC services on `:4317`).

- API style — external MCP: JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio, implemented by the hand-rolled `crates/mcp-server/src/jsonrpc.rs` layer — since chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process linked by `pulse-app` in every build and also serving the console engine's door over `run/door/sock`; `--features mcp-server` gates the stdio sidecar and the `rmcp` anchor, no longer the layer; since chunk 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door a stdio caller also reaches the layer, through the door, by starting `andromeda-pulse-engine door` with no feature (PROVISIONAL — §Occupied Resources → Network ports, the door); `rmcp` rides as the feature-gated anchor dependency at requirement `"3"`, lockfile-resolved 3.1.4 as of 2026-08-29 (the old 1.5.0-vs-0.3.x open question is CLOSED by measurement — chunk `2026-08-29-advisory-backlog`).

- Plugin runtime: `wasmtime` 25+ Component Model with WIT interfaces (requirement `"48.0.4"`, lockfile-resolved 48.0.5 as of 2026-10-04), capability-scoped. The Tauri-side capability `pulse:plugin-fs` gates the host's read of `~/.andromeda-pulse/plugins/` for module discovery and is independent of the per-guest WIT capability grants (which never include host filesystem unless a plugin's WIT explicitly imports a fs interface).
- Visualization: webview WebGPU (`<canvas>` + `navigator.gpu`, WGSL).

- LLM inference runtime: `llama.cpp` prebuilt CUDA + CPU binaries (b9305-pinned series) invoked via subprocess (D1 spawn-per-generation), behind the `LlmInferenceRunner` trait (chunk #82 surface); constrained generation via the committed GBNF `--grammar-file` (`L4_OUTPUT_GBNF`, the b9305 converter's output for the shipped schema), running gemma-4-E4B-it-Q4_K_M with `--temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 64 --min-p 0`; CUDA/CPU binary per hardware-profile tier (`-ngl 99` GPU / `-ngl 0` CPU — the CPU route founder-retired 2026-10-05 and still routed, the retirement carried unimplemented to the next version at the 2026-10-09 version close); bounded single-turn `-st` + `-n {max_tokens}` + outer wall-clock timeout, plus `-c 8192` / `-rea off`. Three documented sibling-impl swap paths through the trait (`llama-server` D2 / in-process `llama-cpp-2` / `candle`). *(Superseded the Pre-D1 `mistralrs = "=0.8.0"` choice — see `architecture-amendments.md`.)*
- Error handling: `thiserror` 2.x in modules, `anyhow` 1.x at boundaries, `serde`-friendly `AppError` enum at the IPC bridge.
- Validation: `serde` + smart enum types + `TryFrom<u16>`; no validation library by default.
- Module boundaries: Cargo workspace, one crate per module, dependency-graph enforcement.
- Build: Cargo + `cargo-xtask` for release/sign/notarize tasks.
- Deployment: `tauri-action` GitHub Action + Tauri 2 native bundlers + Tauri updater plugin (`latest.json`).
- Distribution: GitHub Releases (primary) + Homebrew tap + Scoop manifest.
- Code signing: Azure Key Vault (Windows EV) + Apple Developer ID (macOS notarization).
- Config precedence: env vars > `~/.andromeda-pulse/config.toml` > built-in defaults.
- Development Style: agent-driven.

title: Existing Scopes

body: - **`pulse-v0_2_0-route`** — Pulse v0.2.0 evolution scope. Defined at `docs/v0_2_0/pulse-v0_2_0-route.md`. Active scope drives Epoch 9 (Foundation v0.2.0) work: chunks #57 (widget real-data binding) → #58 (curation crate extraction) → #59 (connection state machine) → #60 (triage crate scaffold + attention cue contract types) → subsequent v0.2.0 chunks (#61+ streaming baseline trackers / #62 attention cue emitter / #63 restart event detector / etc.). Registered 2026-05-16 per chunk #60 substrate landing (session 74 wrap commit `589225f`). Supporting documents: `docs/v0_2_0/pulse-capability-spec.md` (capability spec P-001 through P-060+), `docs/v0_2_0/pulse-distillation-architecture.md` (L1-L4 layered pipeline), `docs/v0_2_0/pulse-vision-and-backlog.md` (product framing + backlog).

title: Build system

body: **Build system.**
- Cargo workspace; package manager is `cargo`.
- Lint: `cargo fmt --check` + `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`.
- Typecheck: implicit in `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`; webview TypeScript bindings emitted by TauRPC are typechecked with `tsc --noEmit`.
- Build: `cargo tauri build` (invoked by `tauri-action`); release profile is workspace default with `lto = "thin"`, `codegen-units = 1`, `strip = true` for distribution bundles.

title: Deployment model

body: **Deployment model.**
- Public OSS desktop app distributed through GitHub Releases; "deployment" is the release pipeline, not server hosting.
- No Docker, no Kubernetes, no serverless, no docker-compose.

- Runtime topology on the user's machine: the engine runs as one of two programs — the Tauri process hosting all fourteen library crates and the embedded webview, or (since chunk 2026-10-10-console-engine-entry-point) the console program `andromeda-pulse-engine run`, one process hosting the same engine with no webview, no window and no model runner, ended by SIGTERM or SIGINT. Both engine programs default to the same data dir, the same two ports and the same pid file path. Not built: a background-service form of the console program, a `stop` command, a release bundle that carries it. Since chunk 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door, short-lived `andromeda-pulse-engine door` processes too — the stdio relay a stdio agent starts, one per agent session, a client of the running console engine's door that hosts no engine part (no tokio runtime, neither boot function, no file, pid file or log record; PROVISIONAL — architecture §Occupied Resources → Network ports, the door). Plus one optional `andromeda-pulse-mcp` sidecar process (only when `--features mcp-server` is enabled at build time and `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED=true` at runtime).

title: CI/CD approach

body: **CI/CD approach.**
- Platform: GitHub Actions.

- `ci.yml` runs on every PR and push to main as six independent jobs, each on `ubuntu-22.04` with no matrix and no `needs:` edge, so a round lasts as long as its longest job: `lint-test` (`cargo fmt --check` → `cargo clippy ... -D warnings` → the xtask gates → `cargo xtask test` → since chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process `Door refuses another account`, a plain `run` step directly after it with no `if:`, no `continue-on-error` and no upload: it runs `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci --no-tests=fail --success-output immediate -E 'binary(integration_door) & (test(=another_account_is_refused_at_each_of_three_layers) | test(=another_account_through_the_bridge_receives_nothing))'` (two arms since chunk 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door; one until it) with its output kept in `$RUNNER_TEMP/door-other-account.txt`, and exits non-zero unless nextest exited 0, the file is not empty, it holds `door other-account arm: directory refused, socket mode refused, account check refused`, and it holds `door bridge other-account arm: no byte reached another account through the bridge, the account check refused` (else `::error::the bridge other-account arm did not read the account check refusing`) — so either arm's skip fails the step; the step's own text holds no `sudo` — two things run as another account, `nobody` and root: the three-layer arm's one client and the relay arm's copy of the built `andromeda-pulse-engine`, run as `door`; pinned by the pins and `bash -e` witnesses in `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs`, among them `door_other_account_step_fails_a_bridge_arm_that_skipped`; as measured on `ci#38097928056` (a `pull_request` run on the pushed tip `2e4ee5ec`): `verdict: green · checks 7/7`, the step success, `nobody` refused by the kernel at the 0700 directory and at the 0600 socket, root held by neither mode and closed by the door's account check at all three layers; and as measured on `ci#38227488889` (a `pull_request` run on the pushed tip `2595b5cc`): `verdict: green · checks 7/7`, the step success with both sentences, the relay's four other-account readings (`nobody` and root, at the modes as made and with the outer layers opened) each exit 1 with 0 bytes on stdout; PROVISIONAL — architecture §Occupied Resources → Network ports, the door —, then `perf:slo-load`, `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile perf-samples --no-tests=fail` (the `pulse-app/tests/perf_budget_samples.rs` producer, excluded from the default nextest filter; the flag since chunk 2026-10-10-no-gate-stands-while-reading-nothing, when every nextest invocation of the workflow began to fail on a selection that matches no test), `cargo xtask perf:budget --data-dir target/tmp/perf-budget-samples --require memory,snapshot`, and an `if: always()` `logs-perf-samples-{os}` upload) · `mcp-test` (nextest with `--features mcp-server`) · `a11y` (`cargo xtask test:a11y`) · `boot` (the mcp-feature release build → `Build the exit witness`, where `cc` builds `scripts/exit-witness.c` into `$RUNNER_TEMP` and names it through `$GITHUB_ENV` as `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_EXIT_WITNESS_LIB` → the agent-harness boot smoke, its lines unchanged → `Boot series (equal source)`, a plain `run: cargo xtask harness:boot-series --count 7` under `if: always()` with no soft-fail key → `cargo xtask ci-gates` → since chunk 2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine `Console engine cycle`, a plain `run: cargo xtask harness:engine-cycle --data-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/andromeda-pulse-engine-data"` under `if: always()` with no soft-fail key, on a data dir other than the job's own; since chunk 2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-named-from-a-run one run of the job reads eight boots, a boot that ended by itself fails the job — its settle verdict reads `ended`, or, since chunk 2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-closed, it took no settle verdict and its exit record is an end the app made itself (any record but the boot verb's own `signal 15 (TERM)` / `signal 9 (KILL)`) — `ci-gates` is skipped when the smoke or the series fails and the upload still runs; the two steps are pinned by three workflow tests in `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs`. As measured on `ci#38019133294` (attempt 1, the merge commit `ab6a1ae6ef0d`): red in `boot` alone, seven of eight boots ended by themselves, the three that carry a witness label reading `exit-call`, the series step 4 min 27 s; the run after it, `ci#38022477393` (attempt 1, the merge commit `71ce5340f2ad`), read five of eight, 12 of 16 over the two runs. The cause was closed at chunk 2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-closed: the app used Xlib from two threads without initialising Xlib's thread support, which the runner's Xlib 1.7.5 does not do at load, and `pulse_app::xlib_threads::init()` now runs second in `main()` (§Stack and Technologies). As measured on `ci#38026637514` (pull_request, the pushed tip `4e61553b`, the merge commit `69c81cb339a9`): success on attempts 1, 2 and 3 — attempt 1 all six jobs, attempts 2 and 3 the `boot` job alone — each attempt 8 of 8 boots settled and `boot-series.json` `all-settled` with `settled` 7; 24 boots, 0 self-ended. The series stays a gating step, and a self-end in it is a new reading to bring to the operator, not an expected red. Since chunk 2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine the job has a second upload, `Upload engine logs artifact` after `Upload boot logs artifact` (`if: always()`, `logs-engine-${{ runner.os }}`, the cycle data dir's `logs/`, `if-no-files-found: error`, `retention-days: 14`): the console engine's own log is graded on every run of the job whatever its earlier steps returned and kept under its own name, and four more workflow tests in the same file pin the cycle step and the upload. As measured on `ci#38065768197` (pull_request, the pushed tip `b32e979f`): green, checks 7 of 7, the cycle step `success`) · `supply-chain` (`cargo audit` as a plain `run:` step since chunk 2026-10-09-supply-chain-job-same-on-push-and-pull-request — no action, no token, nothing published, so it ends the same on a pull-request run and on a push run; exit 0 clean · 1 a vulnerability · 2 could not evaluate, on the runner image's own `cargo-audit`, which no step installs; pinned by the self-lint test `ci_workflow_audit_step_is_a_plain_run_step`; its `cargo auditable build --workspace --release` is a release-build smoke) · `coverage`. The trigger block (`pull_request`, and `push` on `main`) is pinned as it stands by `ci_workflow_triggers_are_pull_request_and_push_on_main`. A `pull_request` run builds the pull request's merge ref, not the pushed tip: as measured on `ci#37979648967`, the boot job fetched and checked out `refs/remotes/pull/40/merge` — `88d5ed30`, whose parents are `main`'s tip `178ebac5` and the pushed tip `e2931127` — so every pull-request reading of a build branch is a reading of that branch merged with `main`, its log's `git.commit.sha` names the merge commit, and "equal source" across such runs means the branch tip AND `main`'s tip both unchanged. On that run the merged tree was equal to the pushed tip's (0 files differ), which holds only while `main` holds nothing the branch lacks (chunk 2026-10-09-boot-smoke-s-early-exit-found-and-closed). No CI job compiles or tests on Windows or macOS since chunk 2026-10-09-ci-on-linux-alone: the three-system matrices of `lint-test` and `a11y` and the macOS/Windows `release` job left, and the frame budget stays the dev-host `perf:frame-sample`. The workspace release build keeps two CI witnesses, `supply-chain`'s `cargo auditable build --workspace --release` and `boot`'s `cargo build --workspace --release --features mcp-server`, pinned by the self-lint test `ci_workflow_keeps_the_linux_release_build_witnesses`; `ci_workflow_runs_on_linux_only` pins that the workflow names no other system, matrix value or system condition. Rust caches are budgeted against the 10 GB repository cap: `lint-test` and `boot` own target caches keyed `lint-test-{os}` / `boot-Linux` and save on failure too; `mcp-test` and `a11y` restore `lint-test-{os}` read-only and `supply-chain` restores `boot-Linux` read-only; `coverage` caches the registry only (chunk 2026-09-29-ci-wall-time-and-round-trips). `{os}` resolves to `Linux` alone, and no job writes `release-{os}` or a Windows or macOS `lint-test-{os}` key any more. Measured after chunk 2026-09-29-ci-wall-time-and-round-trips: 8 entries, 10 605 172 169 of the 10 737 418 240 B cap (≈ 1.2 % headroom — a watch until the next `Cargo.lock`-driven `lint-test` re-save sheds its release dependencies). Re-read after the `release` key gained `cache-on-failure` (`ci#36765040464`, chunk 2026-09-30-perf-instruments-measure-their-budgets): byte-identical, 8 entries, 132 246 071 B (1.23 %) headroom, no key evicted — still a watch. Re-read at chunk 2026-10-09-ci-on-linux-alone (2026-10-09T15:13:15Z): 10 entries, 12 208 662 121 B, which is 1 471 243 881 B over the cap; six entries (8 531 028 085 B) sit on keys no job writes any more (`release-Windows`, `lint-test-Windows`, `lint-test-macOS` and `release-macOS` on `refs/heads/main`; `lint-test-Windows` and `release-Windows` on `refs/pull/39/merge`), and the four that stay (`boot-Linux`, `lint-test-Linux`, `coverage`, the gitleaks cache) sum 3 677 634 036 B. Re-read at chunk 2026-10-09-supply-chain-job-same-on-push-and-pull-request (2026-10-09T17:49:51Z): 10 entries, 12 208 662 121 B, the same count and bytes; no entry evicted and none created. "Keys no job writes" holds for the build branch's workflow only: `main`'s own workflow keeps its seven jobs and three-system matrix until the version reaches it, and the push run of 2026-10-09 on `main` (`ci#37964887106`) restored the four orphaned entries on `refs/heads/main`, whose `last_accessed` moved from 13:05Z to 17:15Z; the two on `refs/pull/39/merge` still read 08:24Z. So least-recently-used names those two alone, and the listing does not test whether GitHub evicts the six first.

- `release.yml` runs on tag push (`v*`): `tauri-action` builds `.msi` / `.dmg` / `.AppImage` / `.deb` per OS in matrix (macOS `.app` bundle is built then wrapped into `.dmg`, not published standalone); signs Windows artifacts via Azure Key Vault EV cert; notarizes macOS artifacts via Apple Developer ID; uploads bundles + `latest.json` to GitHub Releases.
- `update-channels.yml` runs on completion of `release.yml`: updates Homebrew tap and Scoop manifest with new version + sha256.
- All shared CI logic that needs Rust lives in the `xtask` crate so contributors can run identical commands locally with `cargo xtask <task>`.

title: architecture.md — Amendments
body:
# architecture.md — Amendments

Append-only history of amendments to `architecture.md`. **The body holds only current truth; this sidecar holds the
change history** (also in git). Two kinds of entry:

- **Registry-closure** — arch-registry acknowledgments (this was the in-body `§Architecture Registry Updates`
  section under v2): code that landed via `/andromeda-implement` chunks before arch could update `§Occupied
  Resources`. The items themselves are current truth in `§Occupied Resources`; these entries record when/why/where
  each was added. Each `Marker:` path under `.andromeda/runs/` holds the full original amendment record.
- **Decision-history** — the evolution narrative behind an `§Established Decisions` entry, kept out of the body so
  the body states only the current decision + its current constraints.

title: Decision-history
body: ## Decision-history

title: 2026-05-25 — LLM inference runtime: mistralrs → llama.cpp subprocess (D1), session 144 validation
body:
### 2026-05-25 — LLM inference runtime: mistralrs → llama.cpp subprocess (D1), session 144 validation
**Section:** LLM inference runtime decision (L4).
**Change:** the L4 runtime was `mistralrs = "=0.8.0"` in-process (chunk #82/#83 Pre-D1 decision, chosen for its native JSON-constrained generation); now prebuilt `llama.cpp` (build b9305) invoked as a **subprocess** (D1 spawn-per-generation). The body carries the defense-in-depth bounds discipline `-n {max_tokens}` + `-st` + an outer wall-clock timeout. Only the concrete impl swapped (`MistralRsInference` → `LlamaCliInference`); `pub trait LlmInferenceRunner: Send + Sync` is unchanged. Rejected alternatives stay documented sibling-impl swap paths through that trait: in-process `llama-cpp-2` bindings (`=0.1.146` exposes `json_schema_to_grammar()` and fits the trait via `spawn_blocking`) and `candle` (the original chunk #82 escape hatch).
**Why:** `mistralrs` CPU inference is broken on Windows MSVC hosts (upstream issue #1134, open across 0.7.0 → 0.8.1+): sampling threads deadlock with zero token output. `llama.cpp` on the same GGUF and host generated cleanly — 122.3 tok/sec under `--json-schema-file` GBNF constraint with complete schema-conformant JSON (28.2 tok/sec CPU, 231.2 tok/sec unconstrained CUDA). `llama-cpp-2` was rejected for its Windows build-toolchain cost (`libclang` + `cmake` + MSVC), not justified for v0.2.0. Two runaway generations from missing bounds motivated the bounds discipline. The trait was designed to anticipate exactly this staged swap as the bus-factor mitigation pattern.
**Ref:** NOT DERIVED

**Why:** the workspace-key registration follows the 2026-06-29 `window-geometry.json` registration precedent. The at-rest correction records measured truth: a second process could not decrypt its predecessor's rows and the OS credential store held zero entries. title: 2026-09-29-ci-wall-time-and-round-trips — seven-job CI, the pre-push verb, the boot end-status recorder
body:
## 2026-09-29-ci-wall-time-and-round-trips — seven-job CI, the pre-push verb, the boot end-status recorder
**Section:** §Infrastructure Patterns → CI/CD approach · §Occupied Resources → xtask CLI surfaces · §Occupied Resources → Filesystem locations
**Change:**
- CI/CD: was "matrix over Linux/macOS/Windows; fmt → clippy → xtask test → `cargo build --workspace` (release profile smoke)"; now seven independent jobs — `lint-test` (3-OS matrix; `perf:slo-load` on Linux) · `release` (macOS/Windows) · `mcp-test` (Linux) · `a11y` (3-OS) · `boot` (Linux: mcp-feature release build, boot smoke, `ci-gates`) · `supply-chain` (its auditable build is the Linux release smoke) · `coverage`. Rust caches budgeted against the 10 GB cap: `lint-test` / `boot` own the `lint-test-{os}` / `boot-Linux` target caches and save on failure; `release`, `mcp-test`, `a11y`, `supply-chain` restore read-only; `coverage` caches the registry only.
- xtask CLI surfaces: `cargo xtask pre-push:linux` registered (exit 0 green · 1 red · 2 cannot-evaluate; one JSON verdict `{verdict, reason, head, tree, stages[], missing[], remediation, cache}` + `target/pre-push/report.json`; Windows host, WSL `Ubuntu` via `env -i`; pins read from the repo; missing provisioning → `cannot-evaluate` with one apt line; tree-id-verified clone sync; stages `script-modes` · `npm` · `clippy` · `test` · `ci-gates`; no port, no `pulse-app`, no new env var; cross-project fragility: Node 24 from the Viola repo's distro install). `smoke:gap-resume` (three arms) and `smoke:external-resolve` (`reconciled_count` verdict) registered beside `smoke:hue-shift`, dev-host only. `harness:status` JSON gains `ended` (the `run/andromeda-pulse.exit` record, `exit N` / `signal N (NAME)`, ≤ 48 printable ASCII, only when not `running-healthy`, null under ps1); arms and exit codes unchanged. `agent-run.sh boot` runs the app under a waiting subshell writing `run/andromeda-pulse.{spawn,exit}`, takes the app pid from the spawn record (none in 5 s → exit 1), and its failure path prints `app ended: {record}` (was: the spawn pid IS the app, and a `wait` named the signal); `agent-run.ps1` does not mirror the recorder; the boot smoke is the `boot` job's step.
- Filesystem: `run/andromeda-pulse.spawn` + `run/andromeda-pulse.exit` registered as harness-written (never the product binary); the pidfile passage's provisional pid now comes from the spawn record.
**Why:** CI wall time was the build loop's bottleneck (warm 44.8 min); after a seven-job split and a fix to xtask's child-cargo environment the warm round measured 25.5 min. The recorder exists because an app that dies after `boot: ready` is an orphan whose end status nothing else can read; it is the Linux boot watch's instrument. A proposed §Stack row for the WSL distro was rejected as registry over-reach — the fragility rides the verb's registration.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-09-29T21-44-34Z-wrap/

title: 2026-10-04-corpus-key-creation-is-race-free — locked corpus-key creation; the lock file is the second data-dir escape
body:
## 2026-10-04-corpus-key-creation-is-race-free — locked corpus-key creation; the lock file is the second data-dir escape
**Section:** §Occupied Resources → Corpus SQLite → At-rest posture · §Occupied Resources → Filesystem locations (new "Out-of-data-dir lock file (corpus-key creation)" bullet; the training-export sink bullet)
**Change:**
- At-rest posture: concurrent first creation converges on one key — `OsKeychainBackend::fetch_from_os_store` is a locked create-or-read (exclusive `std::fs::File::lock` on the entry's lock file, then get → only on `NoEntry` generate → set → read back → return the read-back key → unlock); no unlocked generate-and-set path remains. Measured: 8 re-exec processes → 1 distinct key (8 distinct, 7 not stored on the prior code). A lock failure maps to `KeychainError::Unavailable` / `Failed` → `Error::KeyringUnavailable`, degrading like an unreachable store.
- Filesystem locations: registers `andromeda-pulse-corpus-key-{h16}.lock` (first 16 hex of BLAKE3 over service ‖ 0x00 ‖ account) — per-user, content-free, mode 0600, never deleted, written by the app and the MCP sidecar through `Corpus::open`; in `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` on Linux, else `std::env::temp_dir()`; a set-but-unusable `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` fails closed. Four residuals stated in the body (XDG disagreement, shared-`/tmp` denial, passphrase degrade, no lock timeout).
- The training-export sink was "the ONE deliberate exception" to data-dir confinement; now "one of TWO", the other being the lock file.
**Why:** concurrent first-run processes each minted a key and the last write won, so a losing process's rows were undecryptable to its peers. The lock is keyed on the credential entry, not the data dir, because racing processes may resolve different data dirs. A boundary widening the founder ratified live on 2026-10-04 (relayed by the overseer), confirmed by the operator at this wrap.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-10-04T09-16-41Z-wrap/

title: 2026-10-04-linux-launch-stays-up-on-nvidia-wayland — the Linux NVIDIA launch-posture default registered
body:
## 2026-10-04-linux-launch-stays-up-on-nvidia-wayland — the Linux NVIDIA launch-posture default registered
**Section:** §Occupied Resources → Environment variables (a new `__NV_DISABLE_EXPLICIT_SYNC` entry; the `WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS` entry)
**Change:** registered `__NV_DISABLE_EXPLICIT_SYNC` — a SYSTEM variable read only by NVIDIA's driver, not an `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*` input: on Linux the product presence-reads it and, when absent, sets it to `1` from `render_posture::apply_linux_default()`, the first statement of `main()`, ahead of the tokio multi-thread runtime build (`unsafe set_var` under a single-thread SAFETY precondition); the value is never parsed or logged; a preset value (empty included) is honoured, never overwritten; macOS / Windows untouched; NVIDIA-scoped by construction, no detection probe; WebKitGTK children inherit it; reported once per boot on `app.boot.render.posture {posture, lever}`; residual — a host presetting `0` dies as before. The `WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS` entry keeps its harness-only status and its out-of-product-config ban, now stating that this Linux default is the product's one sanctioned launch-posture env default and licenses no WebView2 or other GPU flag in product code or `tauri.conf.json`.
**Why:** the default Linux launch died ~2.0 s into boot on NVIDIA + native Wayland (GDK `Error 71` → `_exit(1)`, 3/3) and stayed up 60 s with this default applied, measured on one host; the four surviving levers shared one factor, removing NVIDIA's EGL explicit-sync path. A boundary widening the founder ratified live on 2026-10-04 (remedy option 1; the DMA-BUF-renderer lever and a detection probe rejected), recorded as such at this wrap by the overseer.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-10-04T12-30-22Z-wrap/

**Section:** §Occupied Resources → `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC`
**Change:** The entry now states that the incident title is cue-grounded in EVERY mode, this one included.
- The producer prefixes the triggering cue kind's closed ASCII cause label (`triage::contract::cue_cause_label` — `Error-rate spike` · `Latency regression` · `Restart event` · `Service went silent` · `Retry storm` · `Reflection trend`) onto the model title BEFORE the scrub.

- Under this mode a storm incident reads `Retry storm: Deterministic verification incident` on the report header, Findings rows, MCP `query_incident_list` / `retrieve_report` and the digest's CORPUS MATCHES lines.
- Rows written before the chunk stay unprefixed (no migration).
- The canned rank-1 hypothesis names a retry storm for every incident, so only the title discriminates the cause in this mode.
**Why:** The model can drop the triggering cause (Conductor's d3 interpretation named no retry for a retry-storm-born incident), and the product had no deterministic field naming it. The founder ruled on 2026-10-04 (relayed by the overseer): ship the deterministic cause, in the title, at the producer, with existing rows left unprefixed. ## 2026-10-05-l4-runs-the-founder-s-pick-with-its-authors-settings — L4 output constrained by a committed GBNF via --grammar-file, with the authors' sampling
**Section:** §Established Decisions → [LLM Inference Runtime — L4 interpretation layer] (the constraint mechanism, the argv, the prefill-trap note) · §Stack and Technologies (AI/ML serving row) · §Inherited Defaults (LLM inference runtime line)
**Change:** Was "native JSON-schema-constrained GBNF sampling (`--json-schema-file`)"; now a committed GBNF, `pulse-app/src/l4-output.gbnf` (`L4_OUTPUT_GBNF`, 44 rules), passed per spawn with `--grammar-file` and never `--json-schema-file`. The grammar is the b9305 `json_schema_to_grammar.py` output for `L4_OUTPUT_JSON_SCHEMA`, byte for byte, pinned by `pulse-app/tests/unit_l4_grammar.rs`, which runs the converter vendored at `pulse-app/vendor/llama-cpp/`. `grammar_for_schema` maps any other schema to `InferenceFailed { grammar_schema_mismatch }` before anything is written or spawned, and a per-spawn RAII temp file in `std::env::temp_dir()` carries the grammar. After `-n` the argv carries the shipped model's published sampling `--temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 64 --min-p 0` (`LLAMA_CLI_TEMP` / `_TOP_P` / `_TOP_K` / `_MIN_P`), then `--grammar-file {path}`; `-p {prompt}` is last and the only OTLP-derived operand. The b9305 grammar-prefill trap now stands as the reason the product passes `--grammar-file`, re-measured on the product (chunk-base argv 4/4 `json_parse_failed`).
**Why:** A boundary widening (the subprocess boundary gains the `--grammar-file` crossing and four sampling operands), ratified by the founder's own word — at phase (inputs#I1 ruling 1) and live at this wrap's escalation on 2026-10-05, the grammar crossing and all four sampling operands, relayed verbatim by the overseer. The json-schema form cannot run gemma4 on b9305: an output-format grammar is prefilled and fails at sampler init, a user grammar never is.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-10-05T15-18-57Z-wrap/

## 2026-10-09-ci-on-linux-alone — CI/CD approach: six jobs on Linux alone; the `release` job and both matrices leave
**Section:** §Infrastructure Patterns → CI/CD approach (the key file `registries/contracts/architecture/ci-cd-approach.md`) · §Occupied Resources → xtask CLI surfaces (`check:english-sources`)
**Change:**
- CI/CD approach, the `ci.yml` bullet. Was: seven independent jobs, `lint-test` and `a11y` on a Linux/macOS/Windows matrix, a macOS/Windows `release` job owning `release-{os}` with `cache-on-failure`, three perf steps "on Linux". Now: six jobs (`lint-test` · `mcp-test` · `a11y` · `boot` · `supply-chain` · `coverage`), each on `ubuntu-22.04`, no matrix, no `needs:` edge; the perf steps are unconditional; no CI job compiles or tests on Windows or macOS.
- The workspace release build keeps two CI witnesses, `supply-chain`'s `cargo auditable build --workspace --release` and `boot`'s `cargo build --workspace --release --features mcp-server`, pinned by `ci_workflow_keeps_the_linux_release_build_witnesses`; `ci_workflow_runs_on_linux_only` pins that the workflow names no other system.
- Cache keys: `lint-test-{os}` (owned by `lint-test`, restored read-only by `mcp-test` and `a11y`), `boot-Linux` (owned by `boot`, restored read-only by `supply-chain`), `coverage` (registry only). `{os}` resolves to `Linux` alone; no job writes `release-{os}` or a Windows or macOS `lint-test-{os}` key.
- A third dated cache reading beside the two of 2026-09-29/30: 2026-10-09T15:13:15Z, 10 entries, 12 208 662 121 B, which is 1 471 243 881 B over the 10 737 418 240 B cap; six entries (8 531 028 085 B) sit on keys with no writer; the four that stay sum 3 677 634 036 B.
- xtask CLI surfaces: the `check:english-sources` step is wired in `lint-test` on `ubuntu-22.04` (was "on all three OSes").
**Why:** Chunk 2026-10-09-ci-on-linux-alone removed the Windows and macOS runners from the `ci` workflow, the CI clause of P-113. The reading records the cache as measured and names no remedy: the wrap deletes nothing outside the tree, and who owns the six entries is a route matter.
**Kept:** The two dated cache measurements of 2026-09-29/30 with their "a watch" wording; the `release.yml` and `update-channels.yml` bullets (both workflows are unchanged); the dated Windows-runner facts in the xtask entry.

title: 2026-10-09-boot-smoke-s-early-exit-found-and-closed — two harness verdict verbs registered; boot polls readiness
body:
## 2026-10-09-boot-smoke-s-early-exit-found-and-closed — two harness verdict verbs registered; boot polls readiness
**Section:** §Occupied Resources → xtask CLI surfaces (`cargo xtask harness:status`; `cargo xtask harness:ready`, new; `cargo xtask harness:settled`, new; `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1}`) · → Filesystem locations (`run/andromeda-pulse.pid`; `run/andromeda-pulse.spawn` + `run/andromeda-pulse.exit`) · → Environment variables (`ANDROMEDA_PULSE_PIDFILE`, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LOGFILE`)
**Change:**
- `cargo xtask harness:ready` registered: object `{verdict, pid, ended, otlp_grpc, otlp_http}`; arms `ready` (exit 0) / `not-ready` (1) / `ended` (1) / `cannot-evaluate` (2); `ready` is the `harness:status` verdict `running-healthy` AND a TCP connection accepted on `127.0.0.1` at both resolved OTLP ports (defaults 4317 / 4318), one second per attempt; labels `accepting` | `refusing`; `ended` needs a pid; a port variable outside 1 to 65535 is `cannot-evaluate`.
- `cargo xtask harness:settled [--timeout-seconds N]` registered (default 30, below 8 refused, 200 ms poll): `settled` (exit 0: a navigation record for each of the four window labels and a live pid) / `ended` (1) / `not-settled` (1) / `cannot-evaluate` (2); object `{verdict, pid, ended, app_exit_record, windows_settled, display, session_bus}`, also written to `logs/harness-settled.json` when `logs/` exists. `not-settled` is pinned and never read live; the non-Unix socket branch was not compiled on the dev host.
- `boot` polls `harness:ready`. Was: "Callers are exactly the two harness legs (the boot poll + the `status` verb)" of `harness:status`; now the `status` verb is its one script caller. A failed poll prints `app ended:` or `app still running …`, and `the receivers never both accepted: …` only when the last verdict held a `refusing` label. The ps1 verb mirrors it through `Invoke-Ready`: parsed, never run.
- The pid file and the exit record gain two xtask readers; both variables are also threaded into the `harness:ready` child.
- The waiting subshell's `/dev/null` streams are its own; the app's stdout and stderr go to `logs/boot.log`.
**Why:** the chunk closed the readiness gap: `boot` had reported ready before the receivers bound. The registry enumerates xtask verbs, so a new verb registers.
**Kept:** the script line citations on the two variable entries (the citation sweep proved them); `harness:status`'s object, arms and exit codes.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-10-09T19-51-29Z-wrap/

**Change:** The row describes a verb that runs on the Linux dev host itself; was "the WSL Linux pre-push verb … Windows host only", every call going through `wsl.exe` into a distro clone. Now:
- Linux alone; any other system reads `cannot-evaluate` / `not-linux`.
- The verdict document has six members, `{verdict, reason, head, tree, stages[{name, ok, ms}], missing[]}`, pinned by set equality, none carrying an environment value or a path; was eight, with `remediation` and `cache{bytes, cap, cleaned}`.
- Reasons, complete: `all-stages-ok` · `not-linux` · `pins-unreadable` · `home-unset` · `provisioning-missing` · `run-dir-unusable` · `tree-unreadable` · `stage-failed:{stage}` · `restore-failed:bindings`; `sync-mismatch` is gone.
- Order of a run: host guard → two pins from the repo (the Rust channel, ci.yml's Node major) → `HOME` → provisioning probes → per-run area → `head` and `tree` → six stages in the working tree, output on stderr.
- Every probe and stage child: a cleared environment plus `HOME`, `PATH`, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR`, `PUPPETEER_CACHE_DIR` (the `npm` stage only), `GIT_INDEX_FILE` (the tree-id git calls only); no session bus, runtime dir or display variable.
- `missing[]` names: `rust:{channel}`, `rust:clippy`, `cargo-nextest` (the last two probed only when the channel is listed), `node:{pin} (found {version})` with `none` / `unreadable`, `tool:npm`, `tool:git`, `tool:cc`, `tool:python3`. The apt-list pin and the one `sudo apt-get install` line are gone; the verb installs nothing.
- The per-run area `target/pre-push/run/` is reset once provisioning has passed, so a `provisioning-missing` run rewrites only the report twin. The clone, its 40 GiB cap and the binary-patch sync are gone.
- The `test` stage's rewrite of the tracked bindings is put back as found; `restore-failed:bindings` when it cannot; the restore does not run on a signal.
- "reads no new env var" is retired: the verb reads `HOME` and `PATH` by value and prints or writes neither.
- Node is the first `node` on the caller's PATH; on the dev host a user-level `mise` Node 24 (v24.21.0, npm 11.19.0, as measured there) beside the default Node 26. The other project's Node install is no longer read.
**Why:** The chunk rebuilt the verb natively and measured it green on the dev host twice. The reset-after-provisioning order, the `home-unset` reason and the `missing[]` names are implement's deviations, accepted for these rows by the operator (the pc overseer, 2026-10-10).

Such a boot's entry keeps `verdict`, `app_exit_record`, `windows_settled` null and carries `ended` and `exit_witness` read from its own data dir: the pid from `run/andromeda-pulse.spawn`, the record through `harness_status::{end_file, read_ended}`, the label through `harness_witness::label` (two production callers now, was one). **Section:** §Occupied Resources → Process / service identity (Console engine binary) · §Project Intent → Product type · §Design Philosophy (Single-process modular monolith) · §Stack and Technologies (Message broker row) · §Established Decisions [Mobile / Message Broker / Push Notifications] · §Infrastructure Patterns → Deployment model (key file)
**Change:** The console program's command line was a closed two-word grammar (`run` | `version`); it is now three words, usage `usage: andromeda-pulse-engine <run|version|door>`. `door` is the stdio relay (`pulse_app::door_bridge::main`): a client of a running console engine's `run/door/sock`, started by a stdio agent, which builds no tokio runtime, calls neither `engine_boot::init_process` nor `engine_boot::start`, and adds no listener, port, file, pid file, log record, variable or binary; exit 0 when standard input ends, exit 1 with the one fixed standard-error line `andromeda-pulse-engine door: the door cannot be reached` when the door cannot be reached (at once off Unix); any other command line still prints usage and exits 2, creating nothing; the product binaries stay three. "The OS sees one process per program" and "each product program is a single process" now read one ENGINE process per program, the console program's `door` word also running as short-lived relay processes that host no engine part. The deployment topology names those processes, one per agent session, beside the optional sidecar, which stays as written.
**Why:** The chunk added the word as the stdio way to the door. It is a boundary widening, one item with the door: the form, the word and its exits are the operator's answers at the chunk's P4 and operator pass (the pc overseer, 2026-10-12), and the operator's answer as the founder's delegate at this wrap's widening halt, which also chose the one-engine-process wording for the three process-count sites — PROVISIONAL, the founder's own word owed.

## 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door — a stdio way to the door: the Engine door's Stdio clause and stdio no longer the sidecar's alone
**Section:** §Standard Contracts → Engine door · §Occupied Resources → MCP stdio surface · → Engine door surface · §Established Decisions [MCP Server Surface] · [API Style — MCP Server Surface 3] · §Conventions → External wire — MCP server · §Stack and Technologies (MCP server row) · §Inherited Defaults → API style — external MCP
**Change:** The Engine door gains a **Stdio** clause: a caller with no socket client starts `andromeda-pulse-engine door` as the engine's own account; the data dir resolves as `run` resolves it, the data dir and `{data dir}/run/door/sock` canonicalized both sides, a socket that does not resolve, leaves the data dir or has a path of 108 bytes or more unreachable; each non-blank standard-input line takes a connection of its own, in order — sent with its `\n`, the write side shut, the whole answer read and only then written out unchanged (the `tools/list` line equals a direct read byte for byte); a line over 65 536 bytes is sent as its first 65 537 bytes unterminated and its rest discarded; the relay parses nothing, answers nothing of its own, retries nothing, has no time bound and writes no record or file; exit 0 / exit 1 with the fixed line; the door treats it as any caller (account check, one `door.call` per answered request, a request with no `id` answered and recorded with nothing, no idle refusal); another account through it receives no byte (EPIPE / ECONNRESET on Linux, exit 1, as measured on `ci#38227488889`). The door's own form is unchanged. Was "The MCP stdio surface above stays the sidecar's"; now stdio is no longer the sidecar's alone: the MCP stdio surface also carries the door's methods over the relay (Unix only, no feature), the envelope over the relay is the door's with its codes and bounds, `--features mcp-server` gates the sidecar and not every stdio way to the nine, and the ways in besides telemetry stay two — the relay enters through the door.
**Why:** The Engine door is the form Conductor reads, so the stdio way is stated in it; the socket form did not move. The stdio way is part of the door's one PROVISIONAL item (the operator's answers at P4 and at this wrap's halt as the founder's delegate), the founder's own word owed.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-10-12T09-33-13Z-wrap/

Was "the arm's one client … is the only thing run as another account"; now two things are: that client and the relay arm's copy of the built `andromeda-pulse-engine`, run as `door` under `sudo -n -u nobody` and `sudo -n`. As measured on `ci#38227488889`: green 7/7, the relay's four other-account readings each exit 1 with 0 bytes on stdout. The test-only Stack row adds `unit_door_bridge` (Unix sockets; a 107-byte path reached, a 108-byte one made by hard link) and the relay arm's need for a passwordless `sudo`, skipping like the first arm. The directory tree lists `pulse-app/src/door_bridge.rs`.
**Why:** The relay's owner-only property is read on the hosted runner by a second arm in the existing step (the operator's P4 answer, proof (b)). The step and the word are the operator's answers, PROVISIONAL with the door, confirmed at this wrap's halt as the founder's delegate; the founder's own word owed.

title: 2026-05-25 — LLM inference runtime: mistralrs → llama.cpp subprocess (D1), session 144 validation
body:
### 2026-05-25 — LLM inference runtime: mistralrs → llama.cpp subprocess (D1), session 144 validation
The v0.2.0 chunk #82/#83 Pre-D1 decision originally chose `mistralrs = "=0.8.0"` for its native first-class
JSON-constrained generation surface. Empirical validation in session 144 (2026-05-25) invalidated that choice on
the CPU code path: `mistralrs` CPU inference is broken on Windows MSVC hosts per upstream issue
[EricLBuehler/mistral.rs#1134](https://github.com/EricLBuehler/mistral.rs/issues/1134) ("Endless inferencing with
cpu", OPEN since 2025-02-12, spans 0.7.0 → 0.8.1+) — load completes, "Dummy run completed" logs, then sampling
worker threads deadlock in futex/sched_yield spin with zero token output. A cross-check using prebuilt `llama.cpp`
(build b9305) against the EXACT same GGUF on the EXACT same host (Ryzen 9 5950X / RTX 3090) generated tokens
cleanly: 28.2 tok/sec CPU, 231.2 tok/sec unconstrained CUDA (`-ngl 99`), 122.3 tok/sec under `--json-schema-file`
GBNF constraint with complete schema-conformant JSON in ~4.3s — versus 60+ minutes of mistralrs CPU saturation
producing zero tokens. The runtime was therefore swapped from in-process `mistralrs` to `llama.cpp` invoked as a
**subprocess** (D1 spawn-per-generation). Rejected alternatives, both still documented sibling-impl swap paths
through the unchanged `LlmInferenceRunner` trait: in-process `llama-cpp-2` bindings (Windows `libclang` + `cmake` +
MSVC build-toolchain cost — the spike confirmed `llama-cpp-2 = "=0.1.146"` exposes `json_schema_to_grammar()` and
fits the trait via `spawn_blocking`, but the build stack cost was not justified for v0.2.0); `candle` (the original
chunk #82 escape hatch). Two runaway generations during the spike (both from missing bounds) motivated the
defense-in-depth `-n {max_tokens}` + `-st` + outer wall-clock-timeout discipline now in the body. The chunk #82
`pub trait LlmInferenceRunner: Send + Sync` was specifically designed to anticipate this staged swap as the
bus-factor mitigation pattern — only the concrete impl swapped (`MistralRsInference` → `LlamaCliInference`).
