title: 2026-08-16-fault-identity-semantics-decided — Fault identity decided at both layers
body:
## 2026-08-16-fault-identity-semantics-decided — Fault identity decided at both layers
**Section:** §Established Decisions
**Change:** New entry **[Fault Identity — what makes two faults ONE fault]** recording both decided semantics: L1 fingerprint normalization is TOKEN-LEADING (an absolute marker must START a token; relative path structure stays identity-significant, so `src/a.rs` and `src/b/c.rs` are distinct fingerprints), and L2 incident identity is COALESCE-PER-CUE-IDENTITY on `(kind, scope, scope_id)`. The entry also carries both rejected alternatives, the deferred `AttentionCue` threading path, and the known `Incident.fingerprint` producer defect that leaves the corpus-retrieval `fingerprint_match` arm correct-per-contract but starved.
**Why:** Operator-decided at the chunk's /andromeda-phase P4 review, both recommendations accepted. Before this amendment arch carried NO fault-identity, fingerprint or incident-coalescing entry at all (verified: zero grep hits), so a later chunk reading arch alone could legitimately have re-keyed coalescing on `L4Output.fingerprint` or re-greedied the normalizer — both of which this chunk measured as wrong. **Decision-history:** L1's docs and its pre-existing test had encoded absolute-only all along; only the implementation was greedy (`is_absolute_path_start` fired on any `/`, and because `is_path_char` admits `/`, the skip swallowed the rest of the token). **Switching cost recorded:** the external Conductor verification harness had just aligned to the greedy behaviour — its P-017 spec clause, its `FingerprintVariant` tests and `scenarios/fingerprint-storm.toml` — and re-aligns a third time, executed in that repo; Conductor is read-only from here and is cited, never copied. Purely additive: no existing arch wording was retired, so no duplicate-occurrence amendment follows.

title: 2026-08-17-incident-fingerprint-producer-repaired — [Fault Identity]: deferral SHIPPED, producer repaired, retrieval arm FED
body:
## 2026-08-17-incident-fingerprint-producer-repaired — [Fault Identity]: deferral SHIPPED, producer repaired, retrieval arm FED

**Section:** §Established Decisions → [Fault Identity — what makes two faults ONE fault]
**Change:** Four clauses of the entry restated to shipped reality, all within its single bullet (verified: `fingerprint` occurs on exactly one line of this document, so there is no second site restating the retired wording).
1. The **DEFERRED** `AttentionCue` → `DigestCueRef` → producer threading is now **SHIPPED 2026-08-17** — both carriers named (`Option<String>`, `#[serde(default)]`, full 32-char lowercase hex; `None` for baseline-derived families).
2. The **"Known producer defect, owned elsewhere"** paragraph becomes **"Producer repaired"**: `Incident.fingerprint` is produced from the threaded L1 fingerprint via the crate-internal `triage::contract::hex_lower` — the same encoder the assembler applies to Q3 rows, explicitly NOT the 4-byte `fingerprint_to_hex_prefix`. The corpus-retrieval `fingerprint_match` arm is **FED**, not STARVED; its do-not-simplify guard now rests on the arm being live.
3. The **L1 blast-radius** sentence no longer says "confined to storm grouping": the value now flows onward into `Incident.fingerprint` (persisted, read by the retrieval arm and assembler). No viz / MCP / UI consumer exists — the field reaches no rendered surface — and `span_events.fingerprint` is still never SELECTed.
4. The **L2 coalesce-key rationale** is restated on the ground that survives. "Because the cue does not carry one" became false, so the key now rests on every downstream surface already being N-safe. Per-fingerprint dedupe is **possible-but-declined** and the decision REVISITABLE; the predicate itself is unchanged.

**Why:** chunk `2026-08-17-incident-fingerprint-producer-repaired` shipped the exact threading this entry had recorded as the deferred path, and fed the arm the entry described as starved. Report §Changes → Symbols/APIs lands both new fields; §Spec-master edits names both amendments as due; §Decisions & corrections records that the same two now-false L2 reasons were corrected in-code at `pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs` in the same chunk. title: 2026-08-23-ingestion-scrub-coverage — three reserved DuckDB tables recorded as declared-but-never-written
body:
## 2026-08-23-ingestion-scrub-coverage — three reserved DuckDB tables recorded as declared-but-never-written

**Section:** §Occupied Resources → DuckDB database / schema names → Reserved tables (primary) · §Conventions → Database entity naming (restating site)

**Change:** The reserved-table enumeration no longer reads as seven live write targets. `append_record_batch_to_table` is the only DuckDB write path in `crates/buffer` and fires for exactly FOUR — `spans`, `metrics_points`, `log_records`, `span_events`. **`resources`, `instrumentation_scopes` and `span_links` have no producer**: all three are declared in `crates/buffer/src/schema.rs` and swept by `crates/buffer/src/retention.rs`, so three of the seven retention DELETEs sweep permanently-empty tables. The §Conventions restatement, which listed the same seven names unqualified AND asserted the periodic `DELETE FROM <table>` cutoff task, was qualified in the same pass. Recorded consequences: none of the three can carry host data, so none can leak nor be scrubbed (security-plan §Logging records the same fact from the PII side, where only `instrumentation_scopes` was in frame because it is the only one of the three with a client-controlled text column), and a claim keyed on "the reserved tables" must not be read as "the written tables".

**Why:** chunk `2026-08-23-ingestion-scrub-coverage` measured `instrumentation_scopes` producer-less while establishing its own target set (the route entry and security-plan both said five columns; four are live), and the adjacent sweep found `resources` and `span_links` in the same state. Applied AS MEASURED per the 2026-08-15 playbook rule: the impl half — either a producer lands or the dead schema and its dead DELETEs are retired — is too large to ride this chunk and is owned by the working-route entry "Diagnostics un-muting + harness-truth sweep" (CARRY added at this wrap). This entry records the measurement, not the cleanup.

title: Infrastructure Patterns
body:
## Infrastructure Patterns

**Build system.**
- Cargo workspace; package manager is `cargo`.
- Lint: `cargo fmt --check` + `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`.
- Typecheck: implicit in `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`; webview TypeScript bindings emitted by TauRPC are typechecked with `tsc --noEmit`.
- Build: `cargo tauri build` (invoked by `tauri-action`); release profile is workspace default with `lto = "thin"`, `codegen-units = 1`, `strip = true` for distribution bundles.

**Deployment model.**
- Public OSS desktop app distributed through GitHub Releases; "deployment" is the release pipeline, not server hosting.
- No Docker, no Kubernetes, no serverless, no docker-compose.
- Runtime topology on the user's machine: one Tauri process hosting all fourteen library crates and the embedded webview; one optional `andromeda-pulse-mcp` sidecar process (only when `--features mcp-server` is enabled at build time and `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED=true` at runtime).

**Project directory structure.**

```
andromeda-pulse/
├── Cargo.toml                      # workspace manifest
├── Cargo.lock
├── rust-toolchain.toml             # pin rustc 1.95.0
├── .github/
│   └── workflows/
│       ├── release.yml             # tauri-action: build + sign + notarize + publish
│       ├── ci.yml                  # fmt + clippy + cargo-xtask test
│       └── update-channels.yml     # Homebrew tap + Scoop manifest jobs
├── crates/
│   ├── ingest/                     # OTLP receivers (tonic + axum)
│   │   ├── Cargo.toml
│   │   └── src/
│   ├── buffer/                     # DuckDB ring buffer + Arrow appender
│   │   ├── Cargo.toml
│   │   └── src/
│   ├── viz/                        # query layer feeding webview WebGPU charts
│   │   ├── Cargo.toml
│   │   └── src/

│   │   ├── Cargo.toml

│   │   ├── Cargo.toml

```

**CI/CD approach.**
- Platform: GitHub Actions.
- `ci.yml` runs on every PR and push to main as seven independent jobs, so a round lasts as long as its longest job: `lint-test` (matrix Linux/macOS/Windows: `cargo fmt --check` → `cargo clippy ... -D warnings` → the xtask gates → `cargo xtask test`, plus on Linux `perf:slo-load`, then `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile perf-samples` (the `pulse-app/tests/perf_budget_samples.rs` producer, excluded from the default nextest filter), `cargo xtask perf:budget --data-dir target/tmp/perf-budget-samples --require memory,snapshot`, and an `if: always()` `logs-perf-samples-{os}` upload) · `release` (macOS/Windows: `cargo build --workspace --release`; no frame boot step — the frame budget is the dev-host `perf:frame-sample`) · `mcp-test` (Linux: nextest with `--features mcp-server`) · `a11y` (matrix: `cargo xtask test:a11y`) · `boot` (Linux: the mcp-feature release build, the agent-harness boot smoke, then `cargo xtask ci-gates`) · `supply-chain` (its `cargo auditable build --workspace --release` is the Linux release smoke) · `coverage`. Rust caches are budgeted against the 10 GB repository cap: `lint-test` and `boot` own target caches keyed `lint-test-{os}` / `boot-Linux` and save on failure too; `release` owns `release-{os}` (macOS, Windows; since chunk 2026-09-30-perf-budget-gate-reads-real-samples — a `lint-test` re-save after a `Cargo.lock` change drops the release dependencies, which left the job cold) and saves on failure too (`cache-on-failure: true`, chunk 2026-09-30-perf-instruments-measure-their-budgets — a red release round had saved nothing, so the next rebuilt cold); `mcp-test`, `a11y` and `supply-chain` restore one read-only; `coverage` caches the registry only (chunk 2026-09-29-ci-wall-time-and-round-trips). Measured after that chunk: 8 entries, 10 605 172 169 of the 10 737 418 240 B cap (≈ 1.2 % headroom — a watch until the next `Cargo.lock`-driven `lint-test` re-save sheds its release dependencies). Re-read after the `release` key gained `cache-on-failure` (`ci#36765040464`, chunk 2026-09-30-perf-instruments-measure-their-budgets): byte-identical, 8 entries, 132 246 071 B (1.23 %) headroom, no key evicted — still a watch.
- `release.yml` runs on tag push (`v*`): `tauri-action` builds `.msi` / `.dmg` / `.AppImage` / `.deb` per OS in matrix (macOS `.app` bundle is built then wrapped into `.dmg`, not published standalone); signs Windows artifacts via Azure Key Vault EV cert; notarizes macOS artifacts via Apple Developer ID; uploads bundles + `latest.json` to GitHub Releases.
- `update-channels.yml` runs on completion of `release.yml`: updates Homebrew tap and Scoop manifest with new version + sha256.
- All shared CI logic that needs Rust lives in the `xtask` crate so contributors can run identical commands locally with `cargo xtask <task>`.

title: security-plan
Security Plan — andromeda-pulse

body:
_Generated by `/andromeda-security`. This file is the single source of truth
for all security requirements. Read by downstream skills (design / tests /
obs / a11y per D26 cross-cutting), route (per D25 bootstrap phasing),
setup-project (materializes `@` imports + secure defaults per D22),
security-pass (per-phase enrichment), and combine + `/implement` (via phase loop)._

_Do not edit during phase loop runs (security-pass / combine / `/implement`).
Manual edits between runs are fine._

_This body holds ONLY current truth. Amendment history — the externalized Security Decisions Log plus superseded guidance (e.g., the pre-pivot `opentelemetry-stdout` self-observation references) — lives in the sibling `security-plan-amendments.md` (append-only changelog)._

_**Stack adaptability:** This plan is for a **local-first Tauri 2 desktop app** and, since chunk `2026-10-10-console-engine-entry-point`, a console program (`andromeda-pulse-engine`) over the same engine boot that names no window framework. Web/API anti-patterns are adapted: there is no public API surface, no user auth, no cloud DB. Loopback OTLP receivers + WASM plugin sandbox + code-signing supply chain are the dominant surfaces._

title: Threat Model Summary

body: _[ALL tiers — VERBATIM copy from threat-assessment.md]_
**Security tier:** `Minimal (0)`

_Justification: This is a local-first, zero-infrastructure single-user desktop app (Design Philosophy + Project Intent) with no user accounts, no persistent user data store (in-memory DuckDB ring buffer with 5–10 min retention), no internet-exposed network surface (OTLP receivers bound to `127.0.0.1` only per Occupied Resources), and no compliance-regulated data classifications. Standard tier is not warranted because there is no public API, no user authentication surface, and no multi-tenant data; Hardened tier is not warranted because no payment, health, or compliance-regulated data is present._
**Data classification:**

- **Type:** user-content (telemetry payloads — traces, metrics, logs)
  - **Where:** OTLP receivers (`ingest` crate on `:4317`/`:4318`), DuckDB in-memory ring buffer (`buffer` crate, schema `pulse_buffer.main`, tables `spans`, `span_events`, `metrics_points`, `log_records` — the producer-less `span_links` / `resources` / `instrumentation_scopes` CREATEs were deleted at chunk 2026-08-30-diagnostics-un-muting-harness-truth-sweep), broadcast fan-out to viz/MCP, and curated snapshot markdown files written to `~/.andromeda-pulse/snapshots/`.
  - **Volume:** transient (5–10 min in-memory ring buffer, configurable via `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_RETENTION_SECONDS`); aggregate within retention window (10k spans/sec target). Snapshots persist to disk under the per-platform data dir.
  - **Sensitivity note:** Telemetry can contain incidentally captured secrets, IDs, URLs, error messages, and SQL fragments from the host application being instrumented. OTLP attributes are user-controlled content.

- **Type:** config (user settings)
  - **Where:** `~/.andromeda-pulse/config.toml`, env vars `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*`. Surface is small: enum settings, port ranges, file paths, retention seconds, log level, MCP enabled flag, plugin dir.
  - **Volume:** per-user (single-user local app).

- **Type:** config (signing/release credentials — out of app runtime)
  - **Where:** GitHub Actions encrypted secrets and Azure Key Vault. Apple Developer ID for notarization. Updater public key is baked into the Tauri config.
  - **Volume:** N/A at runtime (build/release pipeline only); the binary ships only the public verification key.

- **Type:** user-content (third-party WASM plugin binaries)
  - **Where:** `~/.andromeda-pulse/plugins/` loaded by `wasmtime` Component Model host (`plugins` crate). Capability-scoped per WIT imports. Signed-plugin verification deferred post-v1.
  - **Volume:** per-user; arbitrary number.

- **Type:** user-content (persistent incident corpus — post-#68 substrate)
  - **Where:** `~/.andromeda-pulse/corpus/corpus.db` SQLite database (`corpus` crate). Holds 5 tables (6 → 5 at chunk 2026-08-30-diagnostics-un-muting-harness-truth-sweep — `baseline_state` DROPPED as dead schema via the SCHEMA_VERSION 1→2 ladder migration; its writer had moved to the file-based `baseline_persistence` path at chunk #72): `service_registry` (lifecycle state machine per chunk #71), `pipeline_metrics` (incl. storm-detector state per chunk #71 + Drain template-mining persistence per chunk #69), `incidents` + `incident_events` + `digest_archive` (Phase 7+ surfaces). All cell-level encrypted via AES-256-GCM. The 32-byte key comes from the OS credential store primary (`MacosKeychain` / `LinuxSecretService` / `WindowsDpapi` via the `keyring` crate, declared with the explicit platform feature set) OR the opt-in passphrase-fallback-with-warning posture per chunk #73 P-049 (`BackendKind::PassphraseFallback`). Both branches are reached as of 2026-08-15-corpus-key-persistence: the key persists across processes (measured — a second boot decrypted its predecessor's rows with 0 `decryption_failed`), concurrent first-run processes converge on one key through the locked create-or-read (measured at 2026-10-04-corpus-key-creation-is-race-free — 8 processes, 1 distinct key), and the fallback emits its once-per-boot WARN when configured and the store is unreachable or the corpus-key lock dir is unusable (see §Secret Management → Runtime).
  - **Volume:** per-user persistent; bounded by retention/compaction (pipeline_metrics rolls off per chunk #69 cadence).
  - **Sensitivity note:** Corpus stores PII-scrubbed projections of telemetry per chunk #72 uniform-scrubber coverage (OTLP attribute values pass through `security::scrubber::mask_secret_spans` — span-level masking gated by `scrub_attribute`'s verdict, since 2026-09-30-span-level-redaction — at every CORPUS write path before write — the corpus projections are covered; the DuckDB ring buffer's five client-controlled cells are covered too since 2026-08-23 — four columns, plus `metrics_points.labels` since 2026-08-23-metrics-points-labels — see §Security Anti-Patterns → Logging, which also records the ring buffer as still unencrypted). At-rest confidentiality protected by AES-256-GCM cell encryption; integrity by GCM authentication tag. Pre-chunk-#70 flat-file `baseline-corpus.bin` artifact is eliminated; no plaintext runtime state survives on disk.

- **Type:** none — credentials / PII / payment / health
  - **Where:** N/A. No user accounts, no payment SDK, no identity provider, no health-domain framing.
**Attack surface:**

- **Vector:** public API (network-bound on loopback only)
  - **Entry point:** OTLP/gRPC on `:4317` and OTLP/HTTP on `:4318`, both bound `127.0.0.1` only. Routes `POST /v1/traces`, `POST /v1/metrics`, `POST /v1/logs`. Wire formats: protobuf via `prost`/`tonic` decode, plus HTTP/JSON.
  - **Trust boundary:** `prost`/`tonic` protobuf decode validates wire shape. Loopback-only binding means any local process (including unprivileged user processes, container sidecars, browser tabs via DNS rebinding considerations) can post telemetry. No auth declared at this surface.

- **Vector:** IPC (Tauri TauRPC bridge — webview ↔ Rust)
  - **Entry point:** Procedures: top-level `app_info`, `health`, `ready`, `get_settings`, `update_settings`; routers `traces.*`, `metrics.*`, `logs.*`, `snapshot.{generate,list_recent,copy_to_clipboard}`, `plugins.{list,reload,invoke}`, `mcp.{status,start,stop}` (feature-gated), `workspace.{detect,list}`. Real-time push events `pulse://stream/*` via Tauri IPC `Channel` API with binary Arrow IPC payloads.
  - **Trust boundary:** Tauri 2 capability gating admits the webview to the IPC LAYER as a whole — `pulse:default` does not enumerate individual procedures (TauRPC dispatches every router method through one invoke handler; measured 2026-08-21). Per-procedure coverage therefore rests on argument-level validation plus the `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` drift gate, not on the capability layer. Errors crossing the bridge are forced to `Serialize`-able `AppError` enum variants. Validation surface relies on `serde` deserialization plus `TryFrom<u16>` for ports/enums.

- **Vector:** plugin host (WASM Component Model)
  - **Entry point:** `~/.andromeda-pulse/plugins/` filesystem load by `wasmtime` 25+ via `plugins` crate; `plugins.invoke` IPC dispatches into a guest. Capability `pulse:plugin-fs` gates host's read of the plugin dir.
  - **Trust boundary:** Capability-scoped sandboxing — guests receive only host imports declared in their WIT. No syscalls, file, or socket access unless explicitly granted in WIT. Signed-plugin verification deferred post-v1.

- **Vector:** MCP stdio surface (feature-gated)
  - **Entry point:** `andromeda-pulse-mcp` sidecar — hand-rolled serde JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdin/stdout (`crates/mcp-server/src/jsonrpc.rs`; `rmcp` is a feature-gated anchor import, not the protocol layer — measured chunk `2026-08-29-advisory-backlog`): `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `notifications/*`. Tools: 9 — `query_traces`, `query_metrics`, `query_logs`, `generate_snapshot` (telemetry) + `query_incident_list`, `retrieve_report`, `retrieve_telemetry_slice`, `mark_incident_resolved` (corpus-backed, chunk #94) + `retrieve_incident_events` (corpus-backed, read-only, chunk `2026-10-02-incident-events-readable-through-mcp`: returns only a coerced closed event-kind label + a timestamp per event, bounded at 256). The sidecar is only present when `--features mcp-server` AND `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED=true`; that double gate is the sidecar's alone — since chunk `2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process` the same nine tools are also reachable through the console engine's door (the next vector), seated for `Program::Console` in `engine_boot::start` behind neither gate: `pulse-app` links `mcp-server` in every build (the dependency is no longer `optional`; the feature reads `mcp-server = ["mcp-server-crate/mcp-server"]` and `rmcp` still enters only under it). The sidecar itself is unchanged, except that its `tools/list` answer carries a boolean `write` on every tool. **Stdio is no longer the sidecar's alone:** since chunk `2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door` a stdio agent reaches the same nine tools through `andromeda-pulse-engine door`, the relay to the console engine's door, behind neither gate of the double gate; its caller is checked by the door's account check, not by this vector's trust boundary (the next vector; PROVISIONAL there). **Stdio is no longer its only input:** since chunk 2026-08-14-workspace-key-alignment the sidecar also reads `<data_dir>/run/workspace-key` at `init_incident_context`, falling back to `data_dir` on any absent or invalid value.
  - **Trust boundary:** Stdio caller is whatever process the user launched the sidecar from (typically an LLM client). No network exposure. JSON-RPC framing per MCP spec. The published-key read is validated per §Input Validation (bounded, UTF-8, control-char rejected) and consumed only as an opaque filter string.

- **Vector:** the console engine's door (a Unix-domain socket; chunk `2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process`)
  - **Entry point:** the Unix-domain stream socket `{data dir}/run/door/sock` (mode 0600, inside `run/door/`, mode 0700), opened by `andromeda-pulse-engine run` alone — the window app opens none, and off Unix none is seated. JSON-RPC 2.0, one request per line: `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `ping`. `tools/call` serves the sidecar's nine tools in the engine's own process, over the engine's buffer read connection, its `CorpusWriter` and its `incident_workspace_key`. One write, `mark_incident_resolved`, behind the `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DOOR_RESOLVE` switch. Conductor is the named reader. Since chunk `2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door` a stdio agent reaches the door through `andromeda-pulse-engine door`, a short-lived relay it starts (one per agent session) — a client of `run/door/sock`, one connection per request line, with no listener, port, file, pid file, variable or log record of its own; the door treats it as any caller (the account check; one `door.call` per answered request; a request with no `id` answered and recorded with nothing; no idle refusal). It is a way through the door, not a third way in. Until the route entry `Stdio sidecar retired` lands, the engine has two ways in besides telemetry: this door and the stdio sidecar.
  - **Trust boundary:** own host only — no TCP port and no network listener is added. The caller must be the engine's own account by the kernel's peer credential (§Authentication & Authorization): any other account, root included, is closed with no byte written. The directory's and the socket's modes are outer layers that hold an unprivileged account and do not hold root. Requests are bounded and refused with fixed messages (§Input Validation). **PROVISIONAL — a boundary widening, one item:** the endpoint, the owner check, the reach of the nine tools and of the one write, the write-switch variable and the workflow step that runs a client as a second account are the operator's answers (the pc overseer: at that chunk's P4 dialog, 2026-10-10, and the operator's reading of 2026-10-11 at its wrap); the founder's own word is owed on the surface itself, and nothing of it is ratified. Since chunk `2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door` the same item also covers the console program's third word `door` (the stdio relay) and the step's second arm: the operator's answers at that chunk's P4 (the pc overseer, 2026-10-12) and at its operator pass, and the operator's answer as the founder's delegate at its wrap; the founder's own word is still owed. Every other statement of the door in this plan rests on this one.

- **Vector:** filesystem reads (config + workspace detection)
  - **Entry point:** `config.toml` under per-platform data dir; env-var-overridable paths (`ANDROMEDA_PULSE_CONFIG_PATH`, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR`, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_PLUGIN_DIR`); workspace-detector crate inspects host project context (`workspace.detect`, `workspace.list`); `<data_dir>/run/workspace-key`, written by whichever engine program boots — the window app or the console program `andromeda-pulse-engine`, through the shared engine boot — and read by the sidecar (chunk 2026-08-14-workspace-key-alignment).
  - **Trust boundary:** arch declares only `serde` + smart enum types + `TryFrom<u16>`. For the published workspace key the discipline IS declared (§Input Validation): canonicalize-and-confine on write, bounded + UTF-8 + control-char-rejecting read, and the value used only as an opaque filter string, never as a path.

- **Vector:** in-app updater
  - **Entry point:** `tauri-plugin-updater` 2.x consuming `latest.json` from GitHub Releases.
  - **Trust boundary:** Updater public key baked into Tauri config; updater capability `pulse:updater` is bound to the plugin flow and "is not exposed to webview JavaScript."

- **Vector:** OS notification / tray surfaces
  - **Entry point:** `tauri-plugin-notification` (capability `pulse:notification`); tray icon (capability `pulse:tray`). Outbound user-facing only.
  - **Trust boundary:** Outbound surfaces; not an input vector. Capability-gated.

- **Vector:** CLI input (env vars + binary launch)
  - **Entry point:** Reserved env vars `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*`, `RUST_LOG`, plus the system `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` (Linux; the corpus-key lock dir, read by all three product binaries — `pulse-app`, `andromeda-pulse-engine`, `andromeda-pulse-mcp` — through `Corpus::open`, since chunk `2026-10-04-corpus-key-creation-is-race-free`), and the system `__NV_DISABLE_EXPLICIT_SYNC` (Linux; presence-read at the head of the window app's `main()` in `pulse-app/src/main.rs` and set to `1` by it when absent, since chunk `2026-10-04-linux-launch-stays-up-on-nvidia-wayland`). Since chunk `2026-10-10-console-engine-entry-point` also the command line of the console program `andromeda-pulse-engine` (`run`, `version` or, since chunk `2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door`, `door`; PROVISIONAL — the door's vector).
  - **Trust boundary:** `serde` + `TryFrom<u16>` for ports; the console program's command line is a closed three-word grammar (the third word, `door`, since chunk `2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door`, PROVISIONAL with the door's item) — any other command line prints usage on stderr and exits 2, creating nothing (§Input Validation); an MCP feature-flag env-var mismatch logs a warning rather than failing. `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is trimmed, then — when set — must be absolute, `canonicalize()` and be a directory, else lock-dir resolution FAILS CLOSED (never a fallback); it is deliberately not confined under the data dir (founder-ratified 2026-10-04; §Security Anti-Patterns → Input). Product-consumed path env vars are trim + traversal-rejected + length-bounded (4096) + `canonicalize()`d + asserted regular-file, with confinement OPT-IN via `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_ALLOW_ROOT` for the three L4 vars (fail-closed when that root is set but unresolvable); the harness-only carve-out — tool-locator vars, the `agent-run.{sh,ps1}` `.spawn` / `.exit` boot-recorder state files, the harness-written files under `logs/` (`harness-settled.json`, `xvfb.log` and, since chunk `2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-named-from-a-run`, `exit-witness.jsonl`, `boot-series.json` and the `series/boot-{ordinal}/` per-boot copies), the xtask-only presence read of `DISPLAY` / `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` / `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` (chunk `2026-10-09-boot-smoke-s-early-exit-found-and-closed`), the `pre-push:linux` xtask verb's by-value read of `HOME` / `PATH` with its per-run area under `target/pre-push/run/` (chunk `2026-10-09-pre-push-check-native-on-linux`), and, since chunk `2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine`, the console-engine harness (the `engine` word of `agent-run.sh boot` / `status`, sh only, a closed word set; the `--program window|console` flag of `harness:status` / `harness:ready`; the `harness:engine-cycle` xtask verb's by-value read of `HOME` / `PATH` with its cleared child environment and its per-cycle data dir under `target/engine-cycle/`; the dev example `inject_demo`'s read of `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_GRPC_PORT`), none product-consumed — stands per §Security Anti-Patterns → Input. Beside the carve-out since chunk `2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed`, its classification PROVISIONAL (the operator's reading, the pc overseer, 2026-10-10; the founder's own word owed): the sixth stage of `pre-push:linux` starts the console engine `andromeda-pulse-engine` and binds loopback 24317 / 24318, never 4317 or 4318. The exit-witness arm of chunk `2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-named-from-a-run` sits beside the carve-out too, with its classification PROVISIONAL (the operator's reading, awaiting the founder's own word): bare `agent-run.sh boot`, the window program's boot, reads `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_EXIT_WITNESS_LIB` (sh only; trim + regular-file check, fail closed) and loads the named library into the window app's process on its spawn line through `LD_PRELOAD` (since chunk `2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine` the script has a second spawn line, the console engine's under `boot engine`, which never reads the variable and carries no preload, and `harness:engine-cycle` passes the variable on by value to its children only when its own environment holds it), `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_EXIT_WITNESS_FILE` being read by that library alone and both variables removed from the process environment at load; the `harness:boot-series` xtask verb reads `PATH` by value and sets `XDG_DATA_HOME` / `XDG_CACHE_HOME` on each of its boots and, since chunk `2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-closed`, reads a boot's own spawn record, exit record and witness file through the existing bounded readers when that boot took no settle verdict — part of the same PROVISIONAL item as the witness record, not a second one. No `pulse-app` code reads any of them, and the witness library is the one harness member that runs inside the app's process. `__NV_DISABLE_EXPLICIT_SYNC` is presence-only — never parsed, never logged; a preset value is honoured, never overwritten; the window app alone writes the process environment, and only before any thread exists, and WebKitGTK's child processes inherit the value (founder-ratified widening 2026-10-04). Residual: a host that presets `0` keeps the NVIDIA + Wayland launch death, by design. `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DOOR_RESOLVE` (chunk `2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process`) is a closed on/off switch read by both programs through `EngineConfig::from_env` and used by the console program's door alone; a value outside the set fails closed to off (`rejected`) and is never logged (§Input Validation; PROVISIONAL — the door's vector above). Since that chunk every console engine the harness starts also opens the door's socket inside its own data dir (§Security Anti-Patterns → Input).

- **Vector:** webview content (host-side)
  - **Entry point:** WebView2 (Windows) / WKWebView (macOS/Linux). WebGPU canvas rendered from Arrow data. Webview source under `pulse-app/ui/`.
  - **Trust boundary:** Tauri capability model (`pulse:default`) gates IPC procedures; no `fs`, `shell`, `dialog`, `http` core APIs granted. WGSL shaders are first-party.

- **Vector:** none — public internet API, OAuth flow, webhook, file upload from internet
  - All N/A. Local-only desktop app; no inbound internet exposure.
**Auth model:**
- **Approach:** none
- **Provider:** N/A

- **Scope:** N/A for user accounts — Tauri capability-based authorization (`pulse:default`) is the trust model; the OS user owns the app. Loopback-only OTLP binding is the de facto authorization boundary. Beside them since chunk `2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process`: the console engine's door admits only the engine's own OS account, by the kernel's peer credential on its Unix socket (§Authentication & Authorization; PROVISIONAL — Attack surface, the door's vector).
**Infrastructure:**

- **Hosting:** local-only — public OSS desktop app distributed via GitHub Releases; runs on the user's Windows/macOS/Linux machine as one of three product binaries: the window app `pulse-app` (the Tauri process); the console program `andromeda-pulse-engine` (since chunk `2026-10-10-console-engine-entry-point`: the same engine boot — the two loopback receivers, the buffer, the detectors, the corpus and, on Unix since chunk `2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process`, one Unix-domain listener at the canonical `{data dir}/run/door/sock`, the door, which the window app does not seat — with no window framework, no webview, no TauRPC bridge and no plugin host, driven by `run` or `version`, ended by SIGTERM or SIGINT, and since chunk `2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door` by a third word, `door`, which boots no engine and relays a stdio agent's lines to the door of an engine already running on the same data dir — the word lives in this binary, so the product binaries stay three); and the stdio sidecar `andromeda-pulse-mcp`. How the console program is distributed, and a background-service form of it, are not built.
- **Database:** embedded — DuckDB 1.5.x via `duckdb` crate, in-memory `:memory:` connection (`pulse_buffer`), no persistent disk database.

- **Networking:** local only — OTLP receivers bound `127.0.0.1` only; the stdio sidecar opens no socket; since chunk `2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process` the console engine also serves the nine tools over a Unix-domain socket inside the data dir (`run/door/sock`) — own host only, no TCP or network listener added; updater is outbound HTTPS to GitHub Releases; no inbound internet exposure.

- **CI/CD:** GitHub Actions — `ci.yml` (fmt + clippy + xtask test + workspace build; six jobs on `ubuntu-22.04` alone since chunk 2026-10-09-ci-on-linux-alone); `release.yml` (`tauri-action` builds `.msi`/`.dmg`/`.AppImage`/`.deb`, signs Windows via Azure Key Vault EV, notarizes macOS via Apple Developer ID, uploads bundles + `latest.json` to GitHub Releases); `update-channels.yml` (Homebrew tap + Scoop manifest). Code-signing secrets live in GitHub Actions encrypted secrets and Azure Key Vault.
**Compliance triggers:**

None — no compliance-regulated data detected. No payment SDK → no PCI DSS. No user accounts / no PII collection by the app itself; telemetry stays on the local machine within v1 → no GDPR-as-controller posture. No health-domain framing → no HIPAA. No children's-product framing → no COPPA.

This tier is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for how much security rigor downstream
skills (security-pass per phase + cross-cutting reads from design / tests /
obs / a11y) should apply.

title: Authentication & Authorization

body: _N/A (deliberate) — auth approach = "none" (no user accounts, no token issuance, no per-user scope). Tauri 2 capability gating (`pulse:default`, `pulse:tray`, `pulse:notification`, `pulse:updater`, `pulse:plugin-fs`) substitutes for runtime authorization; covered under §API Security + §Security Anti-Patterns._

**One caller-identity mechanism exists since chunk `2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process`: the door's owner check.** There are still no user accounts, no token issuance, no session and no per-user scope. On every connection the console engine's door accepts, the peer's account is read from the kernel (`tokio::net::UnixStream::peer_cred`) and compared in one function (`door::admits`) with the engine's own effective account (`door::own_account`, `libc::geteuid`); any other account, root included, and a peer whose account cannot be read, is closed with no byte written (fail closed; one `door.refused` record, reason `other_account`). The 0700 directory and the 0600 socket are outer layers: they refuse an unprivileged account at the kernel and do not hold root, which the account check alone refuses — as measured on `ci#38097928056`, where `nobody` was refused by the kernel (errno 13) at the directory and at the socket, and root passed both and was closed by the door at all three layers. No secret, credential, key or auth library is involved (`tokio` and `libc` only); authorization of the one write is the `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DOOR_RESOLVE` switch (§Input Validation). Read on the hosted runner alone: the dev host has no second account to drive. Since chunk `2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door` a stdio caller through `andromeda-pulse-engine door` is admitted or refused by the same owner check as any peer; the relay adds no identity mechanism, secret or library (`std` Unix sockets). Run by another account it receives no byte: on Linux a connection the door refuses reads `EPIPE` or `ECONNRESET` at the client, so the relay ends exit 1 with its fixed line and nothing on stdout — as measured on `ci#38227488889`, four readings (`nobody` and root, at the modes as made and with `run/door/` 0755 and the socket 0666), each exit 1 with 0 bytes on stdout; the arm asserted 3 `door.refused {other_account, other}` records (root as made, `nobody` opened, root opened; `nobody` as made is stopped by the directory mode), records held in no kept artifact. PROVISIONAL — §Threat Model Summary → Attack surface, the door's vector.

title: Input Validation

body: _[ALL tiers]_

**Boundary:** validate at ALL system boundaries — wherever untrusted data
enters the system. The dominant boundaries here are the loopback OTLP receivers, the TauRPC bridge, the WASM plugin host, the MCP stdio surface, the console engine's door socket (since chunk `2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process`), the console program's command line, and env-var/config-file inputs.
| Boundary | What to validate | How (stack-specific) |

| OTLP/gRPC `:4317` (`ingest` crate `TraceServiceServer` / `MetricsServiceServer` / `LogsServiceServer`) | Wire shape via `prost` 0.14 decode; explicit decode size cap; post-decode invariants (`span_id` is 8 bytes, `trace_id` is 16 bytes, attribute keys/values bounded) | `tonic` 0.14.x — `.max_decoding_message_size(8 * 1024 * 1024)` set on each generated `*ServiceServer` builder per the `tonic` 0.14 server config. `prost` only validates wire format; the `ingest` crate runs post-decode bounds checks before handing batches to `buffer::Appender`. |

| OTLP/HTTP `:4318` (`ingest` crate `axum` 0.8.x routes `POST /v1/traces`, `POST /v1/metrics`, `POST /v1/logs`) | Body byte cap (raw protobuf/JSON bypasses the 2 MB extractor default per JFrog axum-core advisory); `Host` header allowlist; CORS deny-by-default | `axum` `DefaultBodyLimit::max(8 * 1024 * 1024)` attached at router build OR `tower_http::limit::RequestBodyLimitLayer`. `Host` header check via custom middleware (see §API Security). `tower_http::cors::CorsLayer::new()` with no `allow_origin` calls. |

| TauRPC bridge (`ui-bridge` crate routers — top-level `app_info`/`health`/`ready`/`get_settings`/`update_settings` plus `traces.*`, `metrics.*`, `logs.*`, `snapshot.*`, `plugins.*`, `mcp.*`, `workspace.*`, `telemetry.frontend.*`) | `serde` deserialization on every `#[taurpc::procedure]` argument; smart enum types for any settings field; `TryFrom<u16>` for ports per Conventions | `serde` derive on argument structs; Convention-mandated `AppError::Validation { field, reason }` enum variant returned on rejection. Capability gating is negative-default at the IPC LAYER, not per procedure (TauRPC uses one invoke handler), so the per-procedure enforcement is the validated argument struct plus the `xtask` `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` drift gate. The three `telemetry.frontend.*` delegated-timing procedures validate via `validate_duration_ms`, `validate_discovered_count` (bound 10_000) and the closed `HueSeverityTier` enum, each rejection unit-tested by name (2026-08-21). `telemetry.frontend.record_webgpu_adapter` (chunk 2026-09-30-perf-instruments-measure-their-budgets — a Boundary widening the founder ratified at P4 2026-09-30, verbatim «Да, делай») validates `outcome` as the closed serde `snake_case` enum `WebgpuAdapterOutcome` (`obtained`|`no_navigator_gpu`|`adapter_null`|`adapter_request_rejected`|`device_request_failed`; an unknown value is rejected at deserialization, pinned by name) and coerces `window_label` through `coerce_window_label` (4 labels + `unknown`; coerces, never rejects); pinned in `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` (44). |

| Plugin host inputs (`plugins` crate `plugins.invoke` TauRPC procedure + WASM module bytes loaded from `~/.andromeda-pulse/plugins/`) | Plugin file path is canonicalized and asserted to be inside the resolved plugin dir; per-plugin `wasmtime::ResourceLimiter` caps memory (e.g., 64 MB), tables, instances; `Config::epoch_interruption(true)` for call timeouts; wasi-http header field-size bounded by the `MAX_WASM_HTTP_FIELDS_SIZE_BYTES` const in `crates/plugins/src/engine.rs` per April 2026 advisory CVE-2026-27572 (NOT a `wasmtime::Config` method — enforcement attaches via the wasi-http context, `WasiHttpCtxBuilder::max_field_size`, when wasi-http imports land at chunk #46+) | `wasmtime` 25+ `Config` builder; `std` both-sides-`canonicalize()` + resolved-plugin-dir confinement on the `workspace_detector::contract::publish_workspace_key` precedent (`strict-path` DROPPED from the graph at chunk `2026-08-29-advisory-backlog`; see §Code Patterns anti-patterns); guest WIT imports declare exact capability surface. |

| DuckDB query parameters (`viz` crate `traces.*`/`metrics.*`/`logs.*` query handlers; MCP `query_traces`/`query_metrics`/`query_logs` tools) | Service name, span name, attribute key, time-range filter, limit/offset bound; reject identifier interpolation entirely | `duckdb` crate prepared statements with `Connection::prepare` + parameter binding via `?` placeholders. NEVER `format!("SELECT … WHERE service_name = '{}'")` per the dominant 2026 DuckDB CVE pattern (Dagster GHSA-mjw2-v2hm-wj34, Vanna CVE-2024-5827, dagster-duckdb CVE-2026-41490 — see §Code Patterns). Table/column names are spec-fixed in Occupied Resources; user input never names a table. |

| Configuration values — `~/.andromeda-pulse/config.toml` | Field shape via `serde` derive; port range via `TryFrom<u16>` (non-privileged unless explicitly allowed); retention seconds bounded; log level enum; plugin dir path canonicalization | `serde` + `TryFrom<u16>` per Established Decisions Validation Library entry. Fall back to `garde` 0.20+ only if a future scope adds cross-field validation per the documented upgrade path. |

| Persisted window geometry — `<data_dir>/window-geometry.json` (read at boot for remembered-position restore; written on window-move) | Integer x/y per window label via `serde` deserialization to `Position { x: i32, y: i32 }`; a missing/corrupt file falls back to the default (centered/snap) without panic via `unwrap_or_default`; atomic `.tmp`+rename on write | `serde` + `serde_json` per the Validation Library entry. Rust-owned self-written file (not external untrusted input), but the bounded integer struct + graceful default keep a corrupt file non-fatal; no coordinate values are logged (§Logging). Chunk 2026-06-29-window-geometry-movable-shell, P-061. |

| Published workspace key — `<data_dir>/run/workspace-key` (written at boot by whichever engine program runs — the window app `pulse-app` or the console program `andromeda-pulse-engine` — through the one shared `engine_boot::publish_workspace_key_for_sidecar`, at the same path; read CROSS-PROCESS by the `andromeda-pulse-mcp` sidecar) | Read bounded to `MAX_WORKSPACE_KEY_BYTES` (4096); UTF-8 checked; trailing newline trimmed; empty and control-character values rejected — any failure yields `None` and the reader falls back to `data_dir`. Write path canonicalizes `data_dir` + `run/` and refuses if `run/` escapes the data dir, then atomic `.tmp`+rename | `workspace_detector::contract::{publish_workspace_key, read_published_workspace_key}`. Rust-owned self-written file, but read by a SEPARATE process, so validated as untrusted on the read side. **The value is consumed only as an opaque filter string — never opened, joined, or otherwise used as a path**, so its content cannot reach the filesystem (CWE-22 closed by construction). Only the basename is logged (§Logging). Chunk 2026-08-14-workspace-key-alignment. |

| CLI / env var inputs (`ANDROMEDA_PULSE_CONFIG_PATH`, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR`, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_GRPC_PORT`, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_HTTP_PORT`, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_RETENTION_SECONDS`, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LOG_LEVEL`, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED`, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC`, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_CORPUS_PASSPHRASE`, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_BASELINE_BOOTSTRAP_SECONDS`, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_HARDWARE_PROFILE`, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_PLUGIN_DIR`, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DOOR_RESOLVE`, `RUST_LOG`, the system `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` on Linux — the corpus-key lock dir, since chunk `2026-10-04-corpus-key-creation-is-race-free` — and the system `__NV_DISABLE_EXPLICIT_SYNC` on Linux — presence-read and product-set, since chunk `2026-10-04-linux-launch-stays-up-on-nvidia-wayland`) | Path env vars: canonicalize and verify they resolve under the user's home or an explicit override base; ports: `TryFrom<u16>`; retention: bounded (e.g., 60–86400 seconds); log level: enum parse; mcp_enabled: bool with the existing graceful-degrade warning when feature not built; l4_deterministic: bool via bounded truthy-parse (`1|true|yes`, default false; no unbounded string), with two readers since chunk `2026-10-10-console-engine-entry-point` — the window app `pulse-app` (truthy seats the canned runner, else the llama-cli runner) and the console program `andromeda-pulse-engine` (truthy seats the canned runner; unset seats NOTHING: no interpretation subscriber and no L4 heartbeat is spawned, cues and digests are still produced, no incident forms, and the WARN `app.boot.engine` record says so with `interpretation = none`, `reason = deterministic_gate_unset`); the console program reads, through the shared `engine_boot` code and under the rules this row states, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR`, the two OTLP port variables, the retention variable, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LOG_LEVEL` / `RUST_LOG`, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_CORPUS_PASSPHRASE`, the system `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` and the variables `Thresholds::from_env` reads, and none of the three L4 path variables, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_ALLOW_ROOT`, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_HARDWARE_PROFILE`, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_PIDFILE` or `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LOGFILE` (pinned by source text in `pulse-app/tests/unit_engine_boot_seam.rs`); the two port variables yield validated PORTS only — the bind host is not an input in either program: `engine_boot::start` builds `127.0.0.1:{port}` itself, and a rejected port records the bind as failed (`reason = "invalid_port"`) and starts no receiver; corpus_passphrase: bounded parse on read (non-empty, ≤ 1024 bytes; unset / empty / over-long ⇒ not-configured, keeping the fallback opt-in), consumed ONLY as KDF input — never canonicalized, never used as a path, never logged (it is secret-class per §Secret Management); baseline_bootstrap_seconds: bounded `u64` parse, whitespace-trimmed, non-zero and strictly below `WINDOW_DURATION_SECONDS` (86400) — unset / empty / unparseable / zero / out-of-range ⇒ the 3600s default, never a panic and never a silent adoption of an unintended bound; not a path, never canonicalized, carries no user data (chunk 2026-08-16-baseline-family-reachability); hardware_profile (`crates/interpretation/src/hardware.rs::parse_profile_override`, read once per `HardwareProfileDetector::new()`): `trim` + lowercase, then a closed match over the four profile labels in snake or kebab case (`gpu_primary` · `gpu_fallback` · `cpu_primary` · `cpu_fallback`) — any other value is rejected to real detection with one WARN on `interpretation.hardware.detect`, never a panic; not a path, never canonicalized, the value never logged (only the resolved profile label); registered 2026-10-04 as registry completeness, the input unchanged; nv_disable_explicit_sync (`__NV_DISABLE_EXPLICIT_SYNC`, a system NVIDIA-driver variable, Linux only): PRESENCE-read (`var_os(..).is_some()`) — the value is never parsed, never validated (nothing to validate: only its presence decides) and never logged; when absent the product SETS it to `1` (`pulse_app::render_posture::apply_linux_default`, the first statement of the window app's `main()` in `pulse-app/src/main.rs`, before any thread exists; the console program's `main` only hands its arguments to `pulse_app::console::main`, and its files name no render posture (pinned by source text) — `unsafe { std::env::set_var }` under a single-thread `// SAFETY:` precondition); a preset value of any kind (empty included) is honoured, never overwritten; macOS / Windows: not acted on; only the variable NAME reaches the log (`app.boot.render.posture`). A boundary widening the founder ratified live on 2026-10-04; residual: a host that presets `0` keeps the NVIDIA + Wayland launch death, by design | `std` both-sides-canonicalize on the `workspace_detector::contract::publish_workspace_key` precedent for ALL **product-binary** `*_PATH` / `*_DIR` env vars — the single product path primitive since chunk `2026-08-29-advisory-backlog`: `strict-path` was evaluated and DECLINED at the chunk-`2026-08-26` P4 review (zero `.rs` users repo-wide, unmeasured Windows `\\?\` behaviour, and a security guard is the worst place for a library's first use) and then DROPPED from the dependency graph at the 2026-08-29 chunk, so the former strict-path/`std` split has one surviving arm. `serde` + `TryFrom<u16>` for the rest. **Corpus-key lock dir (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, Linux; product-consumed, `crates/corpus/src/keychain.rs::resolve_lock_dir`):** trimmed; unset or blank ⇒ `std::env::temp_dir()` (canonicalized, asserted a directory); set ⇒ must be absolute, `canonicalize()` and be a directory, else FAIL CLOSED (`KeychainError::Unavailable`, never a fallback); deliberately NOT confined under the data dir — a founder-ratified widening (2026-10-04), see §Security Anti-Patterns → Input; consumed only as the directory of the content-free lock file, never logged. **Harness-only path boundary (not product-consumed, so outside the canonicalize-and-confine rule per §Security Anti-Patterns → Input):** `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MSEDGEDRIVER_PATH` — read solely by `xtask::webview_drive::resolve_msedgedriver`, validated by whitespace-trim + `is_file()`, unset / not-a-file ⇒ clean SKIP (exit 0, prints the fetch recipe) rather than a panic or hard fail; the resolved value is never logged (only the variable NAME and the fetch URL appear in the skip message). It resolves an out-of-repo tool that must match the installed WebView2 Runtime, so confinement under the data dir is inapplicable by design (chunk 2026-08-23-webview-self-verify). A second harness-only reader, `xtask::harness_ready` (chunk `2026-10-09-boot-smoke-s-early-exit-found-and-closed`; not product-consumed): the system `DISPLAY`, `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` and `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` are read by xtask alone to probe the display and the session bus — a display only in its local forms `:N` / `:N.S`, probed as the X socket of that number; a bus address only as `unix:path=`, else the `bus` socket under the runtime dir, probed by a Unix-socket connect; a `%`-escaped bus path reads `unknown` rather than being probed undecoded; the output is one closed label per target (`reachable` · `gone` · `unset` · `unknown`) and no value of the three is printed or written. That xtask read of `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is separate from the product's fail-closed lock-dir rule in this row, which is unchanged. `harness:ready` also reads `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_GRPC_PORT` / `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_HTTP_PORT` (defaults 4317 / 4318): a value that is not 1 to 65535 reads `cannot-evaluate`; since chunk `2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed` it probes both resolved ports and then reads the log family once as JSON lines (a line that is no JSON is skipped), and each receiver member of its verdict is one of three closed labels — `accepting` (a loopback connection accepted on the resolved port AND, after the last `app.boot.engine` record, an INFO record of that receiver's bind target, `app.boot.otlp.grpc.bind` / `app.boot.otlp.http.bind`, whose `bind_address` is `127.0.0.1:` and that port), `foreign` (the connection accepted and no such record: a failed-bind ERROR record, a record for another port or for the other receiver, a record before the last boot record, or no boot record at all), `refusing` (no connection accepted) — `ready` needing the status verdict `running-healthy` and both receivers `accepting`, for both programs; labels alone leave the verb, no record text, address or path; a `harness:settled --timeout-seconds` below 8 reads `cannot-evaluate`. A third harness-only reader, `cargo xtask pre-push:linux` (`xtask/src/pre_push.rs`, chunk `2026-10-09-pre-push-check-native-on-linux`; not product-consumed): the system `HOME` and `PATH` are read by xtask alone, by value, to build the environment of its stage children, and neither is printed or written — `HOME` unset or empty reads `cannot-evaluate` / `home-unset`; a non-absolute `PATH` entry is skipped in the search for `node`; its two pins come from the repository (the Rust channel from `rust-toolchain.toml`, the Node major from ci.yml), either unreadable reading `pins-unreadable`; a missing required tool or an unmet pin reads `cannot-evaluate` / `provisioning-missing` and is named in `missing[]`, never green; the Node version it found is printed only as a short version token, else `none` / `unreadable`. Every probe and stage child gets a cleared environment plus a pinned set (§Security Anti-Patterns → Input), and the verdict document carries no value of an environment variable and no path. Since chunk `2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed` its sixth stage runs a real console engine cycle on the fixed harness-only ports 24317 / 24318 (never 4317 / 4318): a cycle port already accepting reads `cannot-evaluate` / `engine-port-taken` before anything starts, a cycle that could not be evaluated reads `cannot-evaluate` / `engine-cycle-unevaluated`, and after the cycle the stage reads both ports and the pid file of its stage data dir and ends what it started; the one `cleanup` child of that teardown carries the two cycle port variables beyond the pinned set; the closed reasons are eleven, and the verdict's six members still carry no value of an environment variable and no path. The classification of that stage is PROVISIONAL (§Security Anti-Patterns → Input). A fourth harness-only boundary, the exit-witness arm (chunk `2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-named-from-a-run`; no `pulse-app` code reads any of it; its classification is PROVISIONAL, §Security Anti-Patterns → Input): `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_EXIT_WITNESS_LIB` is read and validated by bare `scripts/agent-run.sh boot`, the window program's boot, alone among the script's paths (sh only; `boot engine` never reads it and sets no preload, since chunk `2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine`) — trim + a regular-file check: unset or blank spawns the app as before, set and not a regular file reads `boot: exit witness library not found` and exits 1 before the pre-build (fail closed, not a skip), the value never printed; `cargo xtask harness:engine-cycle` reads the variable by value only to pass it on to its children when present, never printing or writing it (same chunk); a regular file is loaded into the window app's process on its spawn line through `LD_PRELOAD`, with `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_EXIT_WITNESS_FILE` = `{data dir}/logs/exit-witness.jsonl` set beside it and read by the library alone, which opens it for append, removes both variables from the process environment and checks nothing more of the path; the witness reader behind `harness:settled`'s `exit_witness` member and, since chunk `2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-closed`, behind `harness:boot-series`'s per-boot `exit_witness` takes at most 64 lines of at most 4096 printable-ASCII bytes with one of three kinds and a `u32` pid, anything else reading `unreadable`, never a partial record, and only one closed label leaves it; `cargo xtask harness:boot-series --count N` reads `cannot-evaluate` on a count outside 1 to 16, a non-Linux host, no data dir or one that already holds `series/`, or no `xvfb-run` on `PATH` (read by value only for that search, never printed), sets `XDG_DATA_HOME` / `XDG_CACHE_HOME` on each of its boots, reads — since the same chunk, for a boot that took no settle verdict and for the smoke's top data dir when it holds no `logs/harness-settled.json` — that boot's spawn record through `read_pid`, its exit record through `read_ended`'s 48-byte grammar and its witness file through that bounded reader, both listed values passing `bounded_label` (part of the same PROVISIONAL item as the witness record), and its verdict document carries no value of an environment variable and no path. A fifth harness-only boundary, the console-engine harness (chunk `2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine`; not product-consumed, no file under `pulse-app/src` changed; §Security Anti-Patterns → Input): `scripts/agent-run.sh` `boot` / `status` take one optional word from a closed set — none is the window app, `engine` the console engine, any other word prints usage and exits 2 before a directory is made (sh only — the `.ps1` script has no such word; pinned since chunk `2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed` by committed shell-level tests in `xtask/tests/agent_run_shell.rs`: bare `boot` resolves the window program, `status engine` and bare `status` read the program asked for, and any other word after `boot` or `status` is usage, exit 2 and no data dir — the word-arm clause of test-plan §1 `harness-cleanup-verdict-and-boot-spawn-shell-coverage`, closed there); `cargo xtask harness:status` / `harness:ready` take `--program window|console`, a clap value enum, and their `program` member is one of three closed labels (`window` · `console` · `unknown`) read from the last `app.boot.engine` record of the log family, a run of the other program or of none reading `wrong-program`; `cargo xtask harness:engine-settled --timeout-seconds N` reads `cannot-evaluate` below 20, and `cargo xtask check:engine-log` takes no argument — both resolve their paths as `harness:status` does, and no line of the check holds a record's text or a path (pinned); `cargo xtask harness:engine-cycle [--data-dir DIR] [--grpc-port N] [--http-port N]` parses its ports as `u16` and is refused before anything starts — `cannot-evaluate`, exit 2, one closed label on stderr — on `not-linux`, `shared-port` (4317 or 4318 in either flag), `data-dir-holds-a-log-family`, `port-taken` (either cycle port already accepting a loopback connection — since chunk `2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed`; read after the three before it and before the `HOME` read, so 4317 and 4318 are refused before any port is probed; nothing built or started, no data dir made), `home-unset`, `path-unset`, `data-dir-unusable`, `injector-build-failed` — eight closed labels; it reads `HOME` and `PATH` by value only to build its children's environment, printing and writing neither, and its verdict carries no value of an environment variable and no path; the dev example `inject_demo` (never shipped) reads `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_GRPC_PORT` through `resolve_port` — unset is 4317, and a set value that is not a port from 1 to 65535, a blank one included, exits 2 with nothing sent and a message that never repeats the value, the host fixed at `127.0.0.1` (`harness:ready` still reads a blank value as the default). **PRODUCT-CONSUMED path boundary — GUARDED since chunk `2026-08-26-l4-runtime-security-residuals`:** `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MODEL_PATH` · `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LLAMA_CUDA_BIN_PATH` · `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LLAMA_CPU_BIN_PATH`, all read by the shipped window app `pulse-app` alone (the console program reads none of them) via `pulse-app/src/llamacli_inference.rs::validate_path_input`. **Always-on:** trim + reject-empty · reject a `..` traversal component BEFORE canonicalizing (canonicalization erases `..`, so a post-check can never observe it) · reject over `MAX_PATH_INPUT_BYTES` (4096) · `canonicalize()` · assert regular-file. **Confinement is OPT-IN** via `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_ALLOW_ROOT` (below); when a root resolves, the canonicalized candidate must live under the canonicalized root — **both sides canonicalized**, because on Windows `canonicalize()` returns a `\\?\` extended-length prefix and comparing a prefixed child against a bare root fails regardless of the true relationship. These do NOT fall under the harness-only carve-out (they reach the product); see §Security Anti-Patterns → Input for the NARROWED exception that remains. — **`ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_ALLOW_ROOT`** (added 2026-08-26): the opt-in confinement root itself. Bounded trimmed parse — unset / empty ⇒ not-configured, so paths resolve unconfined and one WARN per boot announces it; set-but-traversal-bearing / over-long / non-canonicalizable / not-a-directory ⇒ **FAIL CLOSED**, rejecting every candidate rather than degrading silently to unconfined, because a typo must not disable the guard the operator explicitly asked for. Never panics, never blocks boot — a rejection degrades to `ModelStatus::Error` → `ModelNotConfigured`. Not secret-class; env-layer only. Also read at build time only: `ANDROMEDA_LLAMA3_TOKENIZER_PATH` (`crates/triage/build.rs`, offline tokenizer override; note the `ANDROMEDA_LLAMA3_` prefix). Per Occupied Resources, mismatched MCP feature flag must continue to log at `warn` and proceed (do not regress this graceful-degrade behavior). — **`ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DOOR_RESOLVE`** (chunk `2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process`): the write switch of the console engine's door, a closed set parsed by `ResolveWrite::from_value` — unset or `on` ⇒ on; `off` ⇒ off; any other value, one that is not UTF-8 included ⇒ off and read `rejected` (FAIL CLOSED; the boot record `app.boot.door` is then WARN). Not a path, never canonicalized; the value is never logged, only the closed label `resolve_write` = `on` | `off` | `rejected`. Read by `EngineConfig::from_env` (field `door_resolve`), which BOTH programs call: the console program reads and uses it, the window app reads it and uses nothing of it. Env-layer only. PROVISIONAL — §Threat Model Summary → Attack surface, the door's vector. |

| Console program command line — `andromeda-pulse-engine run` / `andromeda-pulse-engine version` / `andromeda-pulse-engine door` (the second `[[bin]]` of the `pulse-app` package; chunk `2026-10-10-console-engine-entry-point`; `door` since chunk `2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door`) | A closed three-word grammar: `run` boots the engine and stays up until signalled; `version` prints one line and exits 0; `door` is the stdio relay to a running engine's door (below); no word, an unknown word, a second word or a word that is not Unicode prints `usage: andromeda-pulse-engine <run\|version\|door>` on stderr and exits 2, creating nothing (no data-dir entry, no log record). No word takes a value, a path or an address, and no `stop` command exists. `run` and `version` were classified a bounded input, not a boundary widening, by the operator (the pc overseer, 2026-10-10): the requirement itself rules a console program driven by commands (P-086, approved by the founder with the route on 2026-10-09), and those two words are its first closed members; a later command that takes a value, a path or a network address is a new question each time. **`door` is not covered by that reading: it is a boundary widening, PROVISIONAL with the door's one item** (the operator's answers at that chunk's P4 and wrap; §Threat Model Summary → Attack surface, the door's vector). `door` builds no runtime and calls neither `engine_boot::init_process` nor `engine_boot::start`; it resolves the data dir through `engine_boot::resolve_data_dir` (the `run` path's variables and no other), canonicalizes the data dir and `{data dir}/run/door/sock` both sides, and treats a socket that does not resolve, resolves outside the data dir or has a path of 108 bytes or more as unreachable; it reads standard input by line bounded at `door::MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` + 1 — an over-bound line is sent as its first bound + 1 bytes with no terminator and its rest discarded, never sent; a line of whitespace alone opens nothing — parses no request, and sends each line on a connection of its own to the door, which applies every bound and the account check. An unreachable door, or a failed socket or standard-output operation, is exit 1 with one fixed standard-error line and nothing on standard output. It adds no env var, flag, value, listener, port, file, pid file or log record. | `std` only: `pulse_app::console::parse` maps the arguments to the closed `Command` enum (a word that is not Unicode is refused, never a panic); pinned by `pulse-app/tests/unit_console_commands.rs` and the spawned-binary arms of `pulse-app/tests/integration_console_engine.rs` (exit codes, an empty data dir); the relay by `pulse-app/tests/unit_door_bridge.rs` and the spawned relay arms of `pulse-app/tests/integration_door.rs`. |

| L4 inference argv prompt (`pulse-app/src/llamacli_inference.rs`, `generate_constrained` → `build_llama_cli_args`; the `-p` operand, assembled by `crates/interpretation/src/prompt.rs` from a first-party template with OTLP-derived content confined to `digest.payload_summary` + `project_context` + — since chunk `2026-08-26-interpretation-brief-completeness` — the `<CITABLE_EVIDENCE_IDS>` section (deduped order-stable `digest.attention_cues[].fingerprint` ids: blake3 full-hex, non-PII by construction, bounded by the cue set)) | `validate_prompt_bounded` before the `Command` is built: byte ceiling `MAX_PROMPT_BYTES` (16384) plus rejection of NUL and the remaining C0/C1 controls — **with `\n`, `\r` and `\t` deliberately whitelisted**, because the prompt is multi-line markdown by construction and a naive `char::is_control()` predicate would reject every legitimate prompt and silently disable L4. Over-long ⇒ reject, never truncate (silent truncation corrupts model input); the digest is skipped instead | `std` — a pure bounded-parse helper returning a bounded `PromptRejection` whose `label()` is the only thing that reaches the log. The ceiling is DERIVED, not invented — and re-based on the live post-citable-section measurement (chunk `2026-08-26-interpretation-brief-completeness`): real-model `interpretation.prompt.assemble` records measured 6715..=6830 bytes on the 2026-08-26 sustained leg, and the 2026-08-27 damper-chunk legs added a reflection prompt at 6,932 B (sparse-digest v2.2 legs ran 6,386–6,387 B), and the 2026-10-04 v2.4 composition (the dev probe's synthetic S4 retry storm with one corpus match, TRIGGER line + corpus framing note + framing instruction; chunk `2026-10-04-l4-interpretation-names-its-triggering-cue`, `--dry-run`) measured 7,185 B, and the 2026-10-05 v2.5 composition of the same synthetic S4 (the framing instruction reworded, +220 B; chunk `2026-10-04-l4-rank-1-hypothesis-names-the-retry-on-every-storm-shape`, `--dry-run`, primary builder only — the fallback and reflection compositions carry the same +220 B and were unmeasured at v2.5) measured 7,405 B, and the 2026-10-05 pattern-discrimination composition (the dev probe's synthetic A6: a cueless digest carrying three resolved corpus matches of one fingerprint, today's render, through the product's unchanged `render_payload` → `build_primary_tier_prompt` → `validate_prompt_bounded`; chunk `2026-10-05-l4-model-chosen-by-pattern-discrimination`, `--dry-run`, primary builder only) measured 7,575 B, and the 2026-10-07 v2.6 composition of the same synthetic A6 (the framing instruction's added scope sentence: +249 B on every composition, the 248 B sentence and its joining space; chunk `2026-10-06-l4-first-hypothesis-names-the-triggering-service`, `--dry-run`, primary builder only) measured 7,824 B; that chunk also took the first readings of the other two tiers, on an EMPTY digest only — primary 7,011 B, fallback 7,200 B (its sanity pin asserts under 8,000 B), reflection 7,549 B — and its real-model reading's largest product composition was 7,693 B (the synthetic S8, a retry storm with two corpus matches), as measured at that chunk (`evidence/prompt-sizes.md` and its report), and chunk `2026-10-07-l4-probe-reproduces-the-canary-history-miss` (`--dry-run`, 391 + 15 cells; as measured at its `evidence/prompt-sizes.md`) measured 8,059 B on a prompt the product itself composed in a live run (the third captured drive's, five corpus lines, at `f70be92` — the first size measured on a product-composed live prompt), 8,067 B on the composition of the synthetic S14 / S15 with their five corpus lines (the probe's baseline arm `nb`: the block as composed before the corpus selection was narrowed to the triggering scope), 8,059 B as the largest the product composes over the synthetic shapes with that narrowing (S9), and 8,293 B as the largest harness cell (the probe's candidate arm `R3R2` on S9, never a product composition) — session measurement notes, never bounds — so the ceiling sits ~2.03× above the 8,067 B observed maximum (8,317 B ≈ 8.1 KiB headroom) and below the Windows `CreateProcess` 32767 command-line limit — the guard fires before the OS does, turning an opaque spawn failure into a bounded category. Rejection is surfaced on the existing `interpretation.inference.error` leaf carrying no prompt text, excerpt, or offending substring (chunk 2026-08-26-l4-runtime-security-residuals); since chunk `2026-08-27-idle-observer-generation-damper` the same leaf also carries the two formerly-SILENT `InferenceError::InferenceFailed` sites (`llamacli_inference.rs` child-wait io-error → `io_error`; stdout UTF-8 decode → `stdout_utf8_invalid`) as bounded categories — no output bytes, no prompt text (the stdout-decode failure is model OUTPUT, so the no-output-bytes guarantee is the load-bearing half). **Every other operand is first-party** (chunk `2026-10-05-l4-runs-the-founder-s-pick-with-its-authors-settings`; the widening founder-ratified live 2026-10-05): `--grammar-file {path}` names a per-spawn temp file in `std::env::temp_dir()` holding the committed `L4_OUTPUT_GBNF`, chosen by `grammar_for_schema`, which refuses any schema but `L4_OUTPUT_JSON_SCHEMA` (`grammar_schema_mismatch` on the same leaf, nothing written or spawned); `--temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 64 --min-p 0` are compile-time constants; `-p` stays the ONE OTLP-derived operand and the last. **A harness-only second reader of the same bound** (chunk `2026-10-07-l4-probe-reproduces-the-canary-history-miss`; a Boundary widening the founder answered on 2026-10-07 — by dialog at 13:13 local, relayed verbatim by the pc overseer, that the builder reads the digest itself; and at 13:49 local his pick of the operator's pass-through as the vehicle, in a question stating that the captures never enter a repository, relayed by the pc overseer): the dev probe's replay input (`pulse-app/examples/l4_decision_probe/replay.rs`, `--replay LABEL=DIR`; an example binary, never shipped) reads a captured product prompt from a run-time path OUTSIDE the tree and passes it unchanged as the probe's `-p` operand, admitted only as regular files of at most 64 KiB and valid UTF-8, a capture directory inside the work tree and outside `target/` refused, through the same `validate_prompt_bounded`, with the recorded argv equal to the probe's own and the first cue line's `scope_id` equal to `--replay-scope`; nothing of a prompt is printed or stored (closed labels, sizes and counts; pinned), no captured prompt text is committed, no corpus key is read and no corpus opened, and the operator deletes the captures after that chunk's wrap. The product's argv is unchanged: no operand added |

| MCP stdio inputs (`mcp-server` crate — all 9 tools dispatched by name: `query_traces`/`query_metrics`/`query_logs`/`generate_snapshot` + the chunk #94 corpus-backed `query_incident_list`/`retrieve_report`/`retrieve_telemetry_slice`/`mark_incident_resolved` + the chunk `2026-10-02-incident-events-readable-through-mcp` `retrieve_incident_events`, whose `{incident_id: integer}` input deserializes through the serde `IncidentIdArgs` with `additionalProperties: false` and whose corpus read is a prepared `?1`/`?2` statement bounded at `INCIDENT_EVENTS_READ_LIMIT` = 256, never selecting `payload`) | Hand-rolled serde JSON-RPC 2.0 framing (`crates/mcp-server/src/jsonrpc.rs`, MCP protocol `2024-11-05`, name-dispatch via `tools.rs::dispatch_tool`; `rmcp` present only as the feature-gated anchor import `use rmcp as _;` — measured chunk `2026-08-29-advisory-backlog`); tool argument structs via `serde`; query parameters routed through the same DuckDB prepared-statement boundary above | `rmcp` pinned `"3"` (lockfile-resolved 3.1.4) — the former 0.3.x-pending-reconciliation instruction is RETIRED, the reconciliation CLOSED by measurement at chunk `2026-08-29-advisory-backlog`; `setup-project` installs `rmcp = "3"` and carries no open question. Tool argument structs use `serde`; the `query_*` tools share the `viz` crate's prepared-statement code path. Snapshot tool output is not sanitized for LLM-side prompt injection — see §Code Patterns anti-patterns and §Logging redaction notes. **INTENDED vs MEASURED — an undeclared argument member (as measured at chunk `2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process`, read in the source):** the tool manifest declares `additionalProperties: false` on every tool, and that declaration is NOT enforced on the sidecar — the argument structs (`QueryTracesArgs`, `QueryMetricsArgs`, `QueryLogsArgs`, `GenerateSnapshotArgs`, `IncidentIdArgs`) carry no `deny_unknown_fields` and read past an unknown member, and `dispatch_query_incident_list` parses no arguments at all. Consequence: the sidecar accepts a call carrying an undeclared member; the member is dropped by `serde` and reaches no query, no path and no log. Only the console engine's door refuses one (the next row). No fix is built: the sidecar leaves at the route entry `Stdio sidecar retired`, minted at that chunk's wrap, and that entry owns this gap (the operator's word, the pc overseer, 2026-10-11). Since that chunk the name dispatch is `call_tool` (it returns `ToolAnswer` and writes no log record); `dispatch_tool` keeps its signature and its three records by calling it, and `call_tool` has a second caller, the door's `door::EngineTools`; `tools/list` gives every tool a boolean `write`, true for `mark_incident_resolved` alone, on both carriers. |

| The console engine's door (`pulse-app/src/door.rs`, chunk `2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process` — the Unix-domain stream socket `{data dir}/run/door/sock`, seated by `andromeda-pulse-engine run` alone through `engine_boot::start` for `Program::Console`; the window app seats none and writes no door record; compiled out off Unix). PROVISIONAL — §Threat Model Summary → Attack surface, the door's vector | **The endpoint:** `run/door/` created mode 0700 before the bind, the socket mode 0600; the path canonicalized, refused when it leaves the data dir, bound at its canonical path, which must be shorter than 108 bytes; closed outcomes `listening` · `path_too_long` · `in_use` · `occupied` · `bind_failed` — any but `listening` leaves the engine running with no door; a socket file an earlier run left is replaced only when it is a socket and a connect to it is refused. **The caller:** the peer-account check on every accepted connection (§Authentication & Authorization). **The request:** JSON-RPC 2.0, one request per line; the closed methods `initialize` · `tools/list` · `tools/call` · `ping`; the closed nine-tool set; `arguments` an object whose every member the tool's `inputSchema.properties` declares (`declared_only`: `-32602` before any tool runs), then the tools' serde structs and the shared prepared-statement path. **Bounds:** a request line of at most 65 536 bytes (longer: `-32600`, the connection closed) · an answer of at most 1 048 576 bytes (never cut: `-32003`) · a call of at most 5 s (`-32002`, then an interrupt of the door's own read connection) · a connection idle for 30 s, or a caller that does not read its answer, closed · at most 8 connections · one tool call at a time. **The write:** `mark_incident_resolved` refused with `-32001` before the dispatcher is called unless the switch `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DOOR_RESOLVE` is on. Every refusal carries a fixed message and never the tool's own error text | `std` + `tokio` Unix sockets + `libc::geteuid`; the envelope functions of `crates/mcp-server/src/jsonrpc.rs`; `mcp_server::tools::call_tool` over `door::EngineTools`. The door opens no database and no corpus, reads no `run/workspace-key` and prepares no SQL (that chunk's gate probe, a grep of `door.rs` for those forms, reads 0). Proven in `pulse-app/tests/unit_door.rs`, the five door arms of `integration_engine_boot.rs` and, on a spawned engine, `integration_door.rs`. Not shown: that the interrupt after a timed-out call ends a real running query (owner: the route entry `Door admission lifecycle and bounds`). Stated limits: the socket file outlives the engine and is replaced at the next boot; with no buffer connection every tool call answers `-32603`, the corpus tools included. |

| Tauri IPC `Channel` API streaming payloads (`pulse://stream/spans`, `pulse://stream/metrics`, `pulse://stream/logs`, `pulse://stream/snapshot-progress`, `pulse://stream/plugin-events`) | Outbound only; payloads are first-party Arrow IPC produced by `viz`/`buffer` crates. If a future plugin returns Arrow IPC bytes, treat as untrusted with a size cap before re-emitting. | Arrow IPC payload size cap enforced in the producing crate before `Channel::send`; per security-research §Apache Arrow Rust, the GHSA-m5xw-hwxw-fq3j R-language CVE does not affect arrow-rs but plugin-sourced Arrow IPC must still be size-bounded. |
(See `## Security Anti-Patterns` § Input for input-validation bans.)

title: Data Protection

body: _[Minimal-tier-retained — the bullet `HTTPS enforced` + `no sensitive data stored` template hint does NOT apply: this section is load-bearing for the distribution channel (Tauri updater Minisign verification, Azure Key Vault HSM custody for Windows EV + Apple Developer ID + updater Minisign keypair, per-medium at-rest posture for ring buffer / snapshots / config / logs / plugins). DO NOT trim during right-sizing. A Standard-tier upgrade would add: backup encryption posture, log-chain tamper evidence, KMS rotation logs, full SBOM / sigstore intermediate-build signing.]_
**In transit:**
- **TLS:** N/A for inbound — OTLP receivers bind `127.0.0.1` only and do not terminate TLS. The `tonic` 0.14.x and `axum` 0.8.x servers run plaintext loopback.
