No PCI DSS (no payment SDK), no GDPR-as-controller (telemetry stays on user's machine; user owns the data dir), no HIPAA (no health-domain framing), no COPPA (no children's-product framing). Caveat carried from Phase 1: telemetry from the host application being instrumented may incidentally contain PII or secrets — addressed under §Logging & Monitoring snapshot/clipboard/MCP hygiene rather than as a compliance obligation on this app.]_

title: Security Anti-Patterns (NEVER do these)

body: _[ALL tiers — single source of truth for all security bans]_

title: Authentication

body: _[User-auth bans omitted — there are no user accounts (auth approach=none). Capability-system bans below cover the Tauri authorization model that substitutes for runtime auth.]_
The door's owner check has four bans (chunk `2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process`; PROVISIONAL with the door — §Threat Model Summary → Attack surface, the door's vector):
- NEVER write a byte to a door peer before its account is read from the kernel and found equal to the engine's own effective account.
- NEVER admit root, or a peer whose account cannot be read.
- NEVER widen `run/door/` beyond mode 0700 or `run/door/sock` beyond mode 0600.
- NEVER treat those two modes as the control against root — they do not hold it (as measured on `ci#38097928056`); the account check does.

title: Input

body: - NEVER trust `Content-Length` or trailers as a substitute for `axum::extract::DefaultBodyLimit` / `tower_http::limit::RequestBodyLimitLayer` on the OTLP HTTP `:4318` routes — the JFrog axum-core advisory documents this as the root cause of unbounded request DoS.

- NEVER `format!("SELECT … WHERE service_name = '{}'", user_input)` against the `duckdb` crate `Connection`; ALWAYS use `Connection::prepare` with `?` placeholders and `Statement::execute([&param])` parameter binding — the Dagster GHSA-mjw2-v2hm-wj34, Vanna CVE-2024-5827, dagster-duckdb CVE-2026-41490 cluster proves this is the dominant 2026 DuckDB vuln class. DuckDB explicitly warns: "Treat SQL in DuckDB like code in Bash or Python and do not execute SQL from untrusted sources without proper sandboxing."

- NEVER skip post-`prost`-decode invariant checks on OTLP payloads — `prost` only validates wire format; `span_id` is 8 bytes, `trace_id` is 16 bytes, attribute keys aren't 1 GB, etc. must be checked in the `ingest` crate before handing to `buffer::Appender` per security-research §prost.

- NEVER read a **product-binary** `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*_PATH` / `*_DIR` env var without `std::path::Path::canonicalize()` + an assertion that the canonical path starts under the resolved per-platform data dir (or under the explicit override base if `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` is set). **Carve-out — harness/xtask-only tool-locator vars:** a path var that is NOT consumed by the production binary and resolves an EXTERNAL tool which by design lives outside the data dir (`ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MSEDGEDRIVER_PATH`; the pre-existing `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_PIDFILE` / `_LOGFILE` are the same class) is guarded instead by a trim + `is_file()` existence check with a clean skip on absence. Confinement is inapplicable there — the tool is deliberately out-of-tree — and the var never reaches the shipped binary, so the CWE-22 surface it would otherwise widen does not exist. The carve-out is scoped to exactly that: harness-only, not-production-consumed, existence-guarded. **A sibling harness-only class — boot-recorder STATE FILES, not env vars:** `run/andromeda-pulse.spawn` (the app pid) and `run/andromeda-pulse.exit` (the app's one-line end, `exit N` / `signal N (NAME)`) are written by the `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1}` boot waiting wrapper — sh since chunk 2026-09-29-ci-wall-time-and-round-trips, ps1 (`exit N`, ASCII, no BOM) since chunk 2026-09-30-perf-budget-gate-reads-real-samples — and read only by the harness: `boot` polls the spawn record ≤ 5 s and exits 1 without it, and `cargo xtask harness:status` reads the exit record through `read_ended`'s bounded grammar (one line, ≤ 48 printable ASCII chars, anything else read as no record); since chunk `2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-closed` `cargo xtask harness:boot-series` reads both as well, for a boot that took no settle verdict — the pid from the spawn record through `read_pid` (not from the pid file, which the boot verb's cleanup removes on a failed boot), the exit record through the same grammar — a read that belongs to the exit-witness arm below and shares its PROVISIONAL classification (its item (d)). The production binary never reads either file, so the canonicalize-and-confine rule has nothing to guard there. **The same class since chunk `2026-10-09-boot-smoke-s-early-exit-found-and-closed` (classified routine harness evidence, not a boundary widening — the pc overseer's own classification as operator, founder-delegated, given at that chunk's plan and kept at its wrap card, 2026-10-09; not the founder's word):** (a) readers — `boot` polls `cargo xtask harness:ready` in place of `harness:status` (the ps1 mirror parsed, never run), and `harness:ready` and `harness:settled` read the exit record through the same `read_ended` grammar, as their bounded `ended` field; (b) two harness-WRITTEN files under the data dir's `logs/`, never read by the product — `logs/harness-settled.json` (the settle verdict, written by `harness:settled` when that `logs/` dir already exists: closed labels, a pid, a 0-to-4 count and the bounded exit record; no value of any environment variable and no path; its field set is pinned) and `logs/xvfb.log` (the display server's own error output, written by `xvfb-run -e` in the CI smoke step — third-party text that passes no scrubber; read whole five times at that chunk, four empty and one holding keymap-compiler warnings, none holding telemetry; the operator's standing stop: if it is seen to carry anything of a watched service's telemetry, stop and say so). Both ride the boot job's `logs-boot-Linux` artifact, which holds further harness-written files since chunk `2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-named-from-a-run` (the exit-witness arm, below); `run/` is still not uploaded; (c) three SYSTEM variables read by xtask alone, by presence, labels only — `DISPLAY`, `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`, `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` — to label the display and the session bus `reachable` · `gone` · `unset` · `unknown`; no value of the three is printed or written, and the product binary's reads are unchanged. **The same class since chunk `2026-10-09-pre-push-check-native-on-linux` (read as routine harness evidence, not a boundary widening — the pc overseer's own reading as operator, given in that chunk's wrap directive, 2026-10-10; not the founder's word):** `cargo xtask pre-push:linux` (`xtask/src/pre_push.rs`; an xtask verb, never product-consumed; it evaluates on Linux alone) (a) reads the system `HOME` and `PATH` from its own environment BY VALUE, only to build the environment of the children it spawns, and prints or writes neither — `HOME` unset or empty reads `cannot-evaluate` / `home-unset`, and the search of `PATH` for the first `node` file takes absolute directories only; (b) spawns every probe and stage child with a CLEARED environment plus exactly `HOME`, `PATH` (`{HOME}/.cargo/bin`, the found `node` directory when there is one, `/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin`), `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` (`target/pre-push/run/data`, absolute), `PUPPETEER_CACHE_DIR` for the `npm` stage only (`target/pre-push/run/puppeteer`; read by no product code) and `GIT_INDEX_FILE` for the three git calls that compute `head` and `tree` — the session bus address, the runtime dir and the display variables are outside the set, pinned by set equality, so no stage reaches an OS credential store; (c) writes only its per-run area `target/pre-push/run/` (removed and created again once its provisioning check has passed) and the report twin `target/pre-push/report.json`, whose six members carry no value of an environment variable and no path (the member set is pinned; the Node version it may name is a bounded version token, else `none` / `unreadable`); it installs nothing and prints no install command, and its stages' output goes to stderr as the tools' own text, passing no scrubber. **Outside that reading since chunk `2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed` — classification PROVISIONAL (a boundary widening; the operator's reading, the pc overseer, 2026-10-10, given at that chunk's plan dialog and kept in its wrap directive; the founder's own word is owed; not the founder's word):** the verb's sixth stage starts the console engine `andromeda-pulse-engine` and binds loopback 24317 and 24318. In order: it removes and creates again the stage data dir; it stops `cannot-evaluate` / `engine-port-taken`, with nothing started, when either cycle port already accepts; it runs `cargo xtask harness:engine-cycle --data-dir {that dir}` under the unchanged stage child set; then it reads both ports and the pid of that data dir's pid file — one still accepting or alive, and the script's `cleanup` runs once and the stage is red whatever the cycle returned; a cycle exit of 2 is `cannot-evaluate` / `engine-cycle-unevaluated`; an exit of 0 hands the stage to `cargo xtask ci-gates` over the same data dir. Three statements of the paragraph above change with it: item (b)'s exact set has one exception, the single `cleanup` child, which also carries `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_GRPC_PORT` / `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_HTTP_PORT` (24317 / 24318) so that its probe never touches 4317 or 4318; item (c)'s "writes only its per-run area" does not cover what the stage's engine writes — the content-free corpus-key lock file goes to the system temp dir, the cycle's child set holding no runtime dir — and the cycle's stderr prints the data dir through the boot verb's ready line; and the reading of 2026-10-09 that heads the paragraph does not reach this stage. Nothing product-consumed is added — no `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*` name, no product port, no file under `pulse-app/src` — and 4317 and 4318 are never touched. Not read live: a taken port on 24317 / 24318, and the teardown after a cycle that left an engine (the decision is pinned, the teardown call by one pin against a real process; test-plan §1 `pre-push-engine-cycle-stage-glue-coverage`). **The same class since chunk `2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine` (read as routine harness evidence, not a boundary widening — the pc overseer's own reading as operator, given at that chunk's plan dialog, 2026-10-10: none of it runs inside the product process or adds a product input, and the engine log upload is the same class as the boot job's log already kept; not the founder's word):** (a) the boot-recorder state files gain a writer and two readers — `agent-run.sh boot engine` spawns `target/release/andromeda-pulse-engine run` by path under the same waiting wrapper and writes the spawn record and the exit record as for the window app; `cargo xtask check:engine-log` reads the exit record through `read_ended`, and it and `cargo xtask harness:engine-settled` resolve their paths as `harness:status` does; the script's new input is one optional word from a closed set (none · `engine`; any other is usage, exit 2), and `harness:status` / `harness:ready` take `--program window|console`, their `program` member one of three closed labels; since chunk `2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed` `harness:ready` also reads, from the log family it already read, the receivers' bind records that stand after the last `app.boot.engine` record, and lets out one of three closed labels per receiver (`accepting` · `foreign` · `refusing`), while `agent-run.sh boot` prints one more failure line on `foreign`, carrying the two loopback ports and nothing else, and `agent-run.ps1`, not edited, still matches `refusing` alone — that read is routine harness evidence too, on the operator's own reading at that chunk's route-resolve card (the pc overseer, 2026-10-10: a harness verb reading further record kinds from a log family it already reads; not the founder's word); (b) `cargo xtask harness:engine-cycle` (an xtask verb, never product-consumed; it evaluates on Linux alone) reads the system `HOME` and `PATH` from its own environment BY VALUE, only to build its children's environment, and prints or writes neither, and spawns every child with a CLEARED environment plus exactly `HOME`, `PATH`, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR`, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_GRPC_PORT`, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_HTTP_PORT` (24317 / 24318 by default; 4317 and 4318 refused), `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_RETENTION_SECONDS` = 60, `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_CORPUS_PASSPHRASE` (32 hex characters made per run from two `RandomState` hashers, never printed or written) and `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_EXIT_WITNESS_LIB` only when its own environment holds it — the session bus address, the runtime dir and the display variables are outside the set, pinned by set equality; (c) the verb itself writes only its per-cycle data dir, by default `target/engine-cycle/{UTC second}/` (`logs/` with the engine's log family, `boot.log` and `build.log`; `run/`; `corpus/`), git-ignored, nothing removed after a cycle, while the engine it starts also writes the content-free corpus-key lock file `andromeda-pulse-corpus-key-{h16}.lock` to the system temp dir — the child set holds no runtime dir, so the engine takes the `std::env::temp_dir()` branch of the lock-dir rule, and, handed a passphrase and no session bus, the passphrase fallback after opening that file; the placement is pinned on a spawned engine since chunk `2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed`, and the file is never removed (§Data Protection → At rest records the shared temp-dir case as a residual); its eight-member verdict carries no value of an environment variable and no path (the member set is pinned), while its stderr passes through the boot verb's own `boot: ready (PID=…, data_dir=…)` line, which prints the data dir; (d) the `boot` job's `Console engine cycle` step runs it on a data dir of its own, and `Upload engine logs artifact` uploads that dir's whole `logs/` as `logs-engine-Linux` (14 days, failing on no file, the upload action at the sha the workflow already pins): the engine's log family, which is its allowlisted record, plus `boot.log` and `build.log`, and `build.log` holds cargo's `Compiling` lines with the runner's checkout paths, passing no scrubber, as the boot upload's does. The class covers both harness files, `boot.log` and `build.log`, as it does in the boot job's upload — the operator's own reading, given at that chunk's wrap card (the pc overseer, 2026-10-10; not the founder's word); the reading at the plan dialog had named the engine's own log family alone; (e) the dev example `inject_demo` (never shipped) reads `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_GRPC_PORT` to pick its port, the host fixed at `127.0.0.1`, a value that is no port refused with exit 2 and never repeated. **The exit-witness arm (chunk `2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-named-from-a-run`) — classification PROVISIONAL: the operator's reading of 2026-10-10 (the pc overseer: routine harness evidence, the app's exit record), awaiting the founder's own word at the epoch boundary; it is not the founder's word. It differs from every member above in one respect: it is harness code that runs INSIDE the app's process, so the class's standing reason (the variable never reaches the shipped binary) holds for the binary's own code only. The operator's standing stop: every kept witness file is read whole, and a line holding anything beyond its shape stops the reading.** (a) `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_EXIT_WITNESS_LIB` is read and validated by bare `scripts/agent-run.sh boot`, the window program's boot, alone among the script's paths (sh only; `agent-run.ps1` unchanged; since chunk `2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine` the script holds a second spawn line, the console engine's under `boot engine`, which never reads the variable, sets no preload and neither removes nor creates the witness file), trimmed: unset or blank spawns the app as before; a regular file puts `LD_PRELOAD` = that file and `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_EXIT_WITNESS_FILE` = `{data dir}/logs/exit-witness.jsonl` on the window app's spawn command, neither exported, so the pre-build and every other verb run without them; set and not a regular file reads `boot: exit witness library not found`, exit 1, before the pre-build — FAIL CLOSED, not the class's clean skip on absence; the value is never printed; the arm still ships with no committed shell-level test — it is clause (d) of test-plan §1 `harness-cleanup-verdict-and-boot-spawn-shell-coverage`, a row whose `cleanup`, `boot` failure-reason and word-arm clauses closed at chunk `2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed` and which stays open on its clauses (c), (d) and (e). One more harness member reads the variable since chunk `2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine`: `cargo xtask harness:engine-cycle` reads it by value from its own environment, only to pass it on into its children's cleared environment when present, prints and writes nothing of it, reports `logs/exit-witness.jsonl` of the cycle's data dir as the closed label `witness_file` = `absent` | `present`, and reads `fail` on `present` (three cycles run with the variable set read `absent`). The library still runs inside the window app's process only, never the console engine's. That reader is named here because it reads this item's variable; no classification of its own is made for it. (b) The library, `scripts/exit-witness.c` (first-party C, no dependency beyond the C library; built by `cc -shared -fPIC -O2`, in CI into `$RUNNER_TEMP` and named through `$GITHUB_ENV`, with no `LD_PRELOAD` in that step): it interposes `exit`, `_exit`, `_Exit`, `quick_exit`, `abort`; at load it opens the file its variable names for append, close-on-exec, and removes `LD_PRELOAD` and that variable from the process environment, so no process the app starts loads it (held by a control in the workspace suite and its known positive); with the variable unset it does nothing, and with the file not openable it removes the two variables and stays inert; it applies no check of its own to that path, which the boot verb sets. No `pulse-app` code reads either variable (0 lines in `pulse-app/src` and `crates`) and no file of the shipped binary changed. (c) The kept files, all harness-written under `logs/`, never read by the product, riding `logs-boot-Linux`: `exit-witness.jsonl` (three closed line shapes `loaded` / `end` / `runtime-exit`, each one write of at most 4096 bytes — pids, a thread id, a process name, the call, its code, `errno`, at most 23 frames as module basename, exported symbol and hex offset, names reduced to printable ASCII without `"` and `\`; it passes no scrubber; one bounded reader takes it, at most 64 lines of at most 4096 printable-ASCII bytes, and lets one closed label out — `unset` · `unreadable` · `loaded` · `exit-call` · `runtime-exit` · `no-record` — to its two callers: `harness:settled`, as the settle verdict's eighth member `exit_witness`, and, since chunk `2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-closed`, `harness:boot-series`, as the `exit_witness` of a boot that took no settle verdict (item (d)); the reader's bound and the label set are unchanged), `boot-series.json` (closed labels of at most 48 printable-ASCII bytes, ordinals, counts, the bounded exit record) and the `series/boot-{ordinal}/` copies of each series boot's log family, `boot.log`, `harness-settled.json`, `xvfb.log` and `exit-witness.jsonl`. As measured on `ci#38019133294`: eight witness files, 15 lines, each read whole, 0 lines beyond the shape; all eight `xvfb.log` 0 B. (d) `cargo xtask harness:boot-series --count N` (an xtask verb, never product-consumed): a count outside 1 to 16, a non-Linux host, no data dir or one that already holds `series/`, or no `xvfb-run` on `PATH` reads `cannot-evaluate`; it reads `PATH` by value only to find `xvfb-run` and never prints it; it sets `XDG_DATA_HOME` / `XDG_CACHE_HOME` to empty directories inside each boot's own data dir and removes `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_PIDFILE` / `_LOGFILE` from each boot's environment. Since chunk `2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-closed` it also reads, for a series boot that took no settle verdict and for the smoke's own top data dir when that holds no `logs/harness-settled.json`, what the boot left in its own data dir, through the readers already there: the pid from `run/andromeda-pulse.spawn` (`read_pid`), the exit record from `run/andromeda-pulse.exit` (`read_ended`'s grammar) and the witness file through the bounded reader of item (c). It lists that exit record and that one closed label as the boot's `ended` and `exit_witness` in `boot-series.json`, both under the 48-byte printable-ASCII bound, and counts the boot `ended` unless the record is the boot verb's own `signal 15 (TERM)` / `signal 9 (KILL)`. No member, label, kept file or witness line kind was added, and nothing new is read from inside the app's process. This second reader is part of the same PROVISIONAL item as the witness record itself: one thing awaits the founder's own word, not two (the operator's word at the wrap, the pc overseer, 2026-10-10). A limit: the read is pinned per arm and was read on a real process by a local leg; it never ran on a runner. Its verdict carries no value of an environment variable and no path; the series' own data dirs are not uploaded, and `run/` is still not uploaded. **Carve-out — the corpus-key lock dir (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`), product-read, deliberately unconfined (chunk `2026-10-04-corpus-key-creation-is-race-free`; a boundary widening the founder ratified live on 2026-10-04):** all three product binaries (`pulse-app`, `andromeda-pulse-engine`, `andromeda-pulse-mcp`) read the system `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` (Linux) through `Corpus::open` only to locate the content-free corpus-key lock file. It is trimmed; when set it must be absolute, `canonicalize()` and be a directory, else lock-dir resolution FAILS CLOSED (`KeychainError::Unavailable`) and never falls back to the temp dir; unset or blank ⇒ `std::env::temp_dir()`, itself canonicalized and asserted a directory. Data-dir confinement is omitted by design: the lock is keyed on the one per-user credential entry, which racing processes share whatever data dir they resolve, and the per-user runtime dir lives outside the data dir. With the `~/Downloads` training-export sink and the per-spawn L4 grammar temp file in `std::env::temp_dir()` (since chunk #84), it is one of the THREE product-written locations outside the data dir. Residuals (no confining mechanism): processes disagreeing on `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` lock different files; the Linux `/tmp` fallback admits a local pre-create denial (fail closed, no exposure); no lock timeout. **The second-account step, a harness record (chunk `2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process`) — classification PROVISIONAL, part of the door's one item (§Threat Model Summary → Attack surface, the door's vector):** the `lint-test` job's step `Door refuses another account` — a plain `run` step directly after `cargo xtask test`, with no `if:`, no `continue-on-error` and no upload — runs two arms of `pulse-app/tests/integration_door.rs` — `another_account_is_refused_at_each_of_three_layers` and, since chunk `2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door`, `another_account_through_the_bridge_receives_nothing` (one selection, the same flags) — and passes only when nextest exits 0, its kept output is not empty and holds BOTH arms' sentences (the three-layer sentence and `door bridge other-account arm: no byte reached another account through the bridge, the account check refused`). The step's own text holds no `sudo`; two things run as another account, root included, each against the socket of an engine the test itself spawned: the three-layer arm's one client (`python3 -c …`, run under `sudo -n -u nobody` and under `sudo -n`) and the relay arm's copy of the built `andromeda-pulse-engine`, run as `sudo -n [-u nobody] env ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR={data dir} {copy} door` (the data dir and `run/` opened to 0755, the copy in the arm's own temp dir). Where `sudo -n true` fails each arm prints its skip sentence and passes (the dev host, in every run), and either skip sentence fails the CI step. Test-only; no product binary reads or runs any of it. **Every harness-started console engine opens the door since that chunk:** `agent-run.sh boot engine`, `cargo xtask harness:engine-cycle`, the `Console engine cycle` CI step and the sixth stage of `cargo xtask pre-push:linux` each start an engine that now also holds a Unix-domain listener at `run/door/sock` (directory 0700, socket 0600) inside that cycle's or stage's own data dir, beside the two loopback ports; the harness verbs read what they read before, `check:engine-log` passes over a log holding one `app.boot.door` record per boot, and the socket file is not removed when the engine ends. The sixth stage's PROVISIONAL item (above) covers the socket too (the operator's reading of 2026-10-11); "writes only its per-cycle data dir" stays true, the socket being inside it.

- **The test port claim — test-only, stated as built, no class reading made for it** (chunk `2026-10-10-shared-telemetry-test-data`): the claim has ONE home, `test_support::ports::claim_port` / `PortClaim` in `crates/test-support/src/ports.rs` — the workspace member `test-support` (`publish = false`), named by `buffer`, `pulse-app` and `xtask` under `[dev-dependencies]` only and depending on `ingest` alone, both held by the `xtask` test module `test_support_edges`, so no product target links it. A claim is a number from 20000 to 31999 with 24317 and 24318 left out, held under an advisory lock (`File::try_lock`) on the empty file `target/test-ports/{number}` for the life of the claim and shown bindable at the claim; the file is never unlinked, and a test panics when no port can be claimed. The directory is found from the crate's compile-time manifest directory, two levels under the repository root: no environment variable is read at run time and none is added. Test-written, never product-written and never product-read: no new place on disk (`target/test-ports/` stood before, architecture §Occupied Resources → Filesystem locations), no new port range, no new listening socket, no line of product source changed. The dev-only edge it rides is architecture's carve-out of §Cross-cutting Patterns → Module dependency direction, PROVISIONAL there.

**NARROWED EXCEPTION — three product-consumed path vars are guarded, with confinement opt-in (guard landed 2026-08-26, chunk `2026-08-26-l4-runtime-security-residuals`; exception first recorded 2026-08-26 at chunk `2026-08-25-demo-injector-formalized-api-surface-retire`).** The sentence that stood here previously — "Everything the product reads stays under the categorical rule" — was FALSE, and had been since chunk #84. `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MODEL_PATH` · `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LLAMA_CUDA_BIN_PATH` · `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LLAMA_CPU_BIN_PATH` are read by a SHIPPED binary — the window app `pulse-app` alone among the three product binaries: the console program `andromeda-pulse-engine` reads none of them and no `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_ALLOW_ROOT`, constructs no `LlamaCliInference` and emits no `interpretation.model.*` record (pinned by source text in `pulse-app/tests/unit_engine_boot_seam.rs`), so the residual consequence stated here does not reach it — (`pulse-app/src/llamacli_inference.rs`, `read_env_path` → `canonicalize_path` at construction), so the harness-only carve-out above does NOT reach them. **What they DO enforce:** trim + reject-empty, `canonicalize()`, and an assert that the resolved path is a REGULAR FILE (a directory or symlink-to-directory is rejected) — the half of the CWE-22 defense that resolves `..` and symlink chains. **What they ADDITIONALLY enforce since the guard landed:** a `..` traversal component is rejected BEFORE canonicalization (canonicalization erases `..`, so a post-check could never observe it), a raw value over `MAX_PATH_INPUT_BYTES` (4096) is rejected, and — when `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_ALLOW_ROOT` resolves to a directory — the canonicalized candidate must live under the canonicalized root, both sides canonicalized per the `publish_workspace_key` precedent. A root that is SET but unresolvable **fails closed**, rejecting every candidate. **What is still deliberately OMITTED:** the categorical data-dir confinement assert of the ban above. Confinement is OPT-IN, not defaulted, with the rationale stated in code at `canonicalize_path` and unchanged in substance — the GGUF model and the prebuilt `llama-cli.exe` live outside the data dir by design and their distribution is an explicitly OPEN arch caveat, so a data-dir default would reject every configuration that has ever run L4 on this project. **Consequence, stated plainly and now scoped:** on a host that does NOT set `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_ALLOW_ROOT`, an attacker who can set these env vars can still point the product at an arbitrary on-disk file — reading it as a model, or EXECUTING it as the inference binary. What changed is that this is no longer a silent convention: the unconfined posture is announced once per boot at WARN on `interpretation.model.allow_root`, and an enforcement mechanism is available to any host that wants it. That is a meaningful escalation over the msedgedriver carve-out, whose var never reaches the shipped binary. It is bounded by the same trust boundary as the rest of this tier (local single-user desktop; an attacker who can set the victim's environment has other paths), which is why it was accepted rather than blocking — but it is an accepted risk, not an absent one. **Owner: DISCHARGED** — the working-route entry *"L4 runtime security residuals"* landed as chunk `2026-08-26-l4-runtime-security-residuals`. The sibling argv-prompt residual it also owned is **CLOSED**: the digest-derived, OTLP-sourced `-p` value now passes `validate_prompt_bounded` at its single production caller before `build_llama_cli_args` is invoked (see the L4-argv row in §Input Validation). What remains is the scoped consequence above — opt-in confinement, announced when off — not a pending obligation. This is a CWE-22 (Path Traversal) class defense; specific 2025–2026 CVE anchors (e.g., zip crate CVE-2025-29787, RustFS CVE-2025-68705) involve crates not in this project's dependency graph but document the same symlink-chain / TOCTOU traversal class that `tauri-plugin-fs`-style file APIs and any user-overridable path env-var construct are equally exposed to. The canonicalize-and-confine primitive used HERE — and now project-wide — is `std` both-sides-canonicalize on the `workspace_detector::contract::publish_workspace_key` precedent. `strict-path` was evaluated and declined for this boundary at the chunk-`2026-08-26` P4 review (zero `.rs` users repo-wide; unmeasured Windows `\\?\` behaviour; a security guard is the worst place for a library's first use) and DROPPED from the dependency graph entirely at chunk `2026-08-29-advisory-backlog` — the "intended primitive for the other product path boundaries" clause that stood here is retired with it.

- NEVER call `tonic::transport::Server::builder()...add_service(generated_server)` without `.max_decoding_message_size(8 * 1024 * 1024)` set on each `*ServiceServer` builder — `tonic` historically accepted 1 GB+ unary requests by default per security-research §tonic.
- NEVER trust plugin-returned Arrow IPC bytes without a size cap before re-emitting on the Tauri `Channel` API.

title: Data Protection

body: - NEVER add a non-Cranelift `wasmtime` feature flag on x86_64 builds without re-checking the April 2026 advisory cluster — Cranelift backend on x86_64 was the unaffected configuration for the two Critical sandbox escapes (CVE-2026-34941, CVE-2026-35195). A future "use the experimental Winch backend" change would re-introduce the exposure per security-research §wasmtime 25+.

- NEVER override the `tauri-plugin-updater` 2.x signature verification — Minisign Ed25519 verification cannot be disabled per security-research §tauri-plugin-updater, and any wrapper code must not attempt to bypass it.

- NEVER ship the Tauri updater Minisign **private** key in the repo or in any build artifact — only the public key belongs in `tauri.conf.json` per security-research §Tauri 2 Updater Signature Verification.

- NEVER store the Windows EV signing cert outside Azure Key Vault HSM — per security-research §Azure Key Vault OIDC, only DigiCert or GlobalSign HSM-RSA CAs are supported and the key must never leave the HSM.

- NEVER enable DuckDB encryption at rest on the in-memory ring buffer — CVE-2025-64429 is documented against the encryption feature; the in-memory `:memory:` connection avoids the entire surface and an unnecessary feature flip would re-introduce it.

title: API

body: - NEVER use `tower_http::cors::CorsLayer::permissive()` or `allow_origin(Any)` on the OTLP HTTP `:4318` router — default-deny is the correct posture per security-research §CORS deny-by-default.

- NEVER skip the Host-header allowlist middleware on `:4318` — DNS rebinding is the documented attack against localhost OTLP/HTTP receivers per security-research §Host header validation (Coder Agent API CVE 2025-09-19, CVE-2025-66414 against MCP TypeScript SDK Dec 2025); "localhost is not a security boundary" is the explicit lesson.

- NEVER add a TauRPC procedure to a router crate without its `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` pin in `xtask/src/main.rs` AND a validated argument struct — the `xtask capability-drift` check is the enforcement mechanism and fails CI on an unpinned procedure — and, since chunk `2026-08-30-staged-bindings-assertion`, on any STAGED-index disagreement (bindings vs `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES`, capability grants vs `staged_gate::EXPECTED_GRANTS` in both directions, an unpinned `pulse-app/capabilities/*.json`, or a staged deletion of either subject). (Per-procedure `pulse-app/capabilities/` entries do NOT exist in this project: TauRPC dispatches all methods through one invoke handler, measured 2026-08-21.) NEVER grant a Tauri CORE API (`fs` / `shell` / `dialog` / `http`) or a `core:window:*` permission without an explicit per-feature capability addition with a stated rationale — THOSE are silently rejected at runtime when missing, which becomes a hard-to-diagnose dead-affordance bug (and, since the same chunk, a left-REVOKED or silently-ADDED grant is also caught mechanically by the staged-grants assertion — silent runtime rejection is no longer the sole stated enforcement).

- NEVER grant Tauri core APIs (`fs`, `shell`, `dialog`, `http`) to `pulse:default` without an explicit per-feature capability addition with stated rationale per Cross-cutting Patterns Webview IPC capability policy.
- NEVER expose `pulse:updater` to webview JavaScript per Cross-cutting Patterns Webview IPC capability policy — the updater capability is bound to the `tauri-plugin-updater` flow only.

- NEVER widen `pulse:notification` (`tauri-plugin-notification`) or `pulse:tray` (tray icon) beyond outbound-only emit calls per Threat Model Summary "OS notification / tray surfaces" trust-boundary classification — both are outbound user-facing surfaces, not input vectors. Granting webview-side input handlers (e.g., notification action callbacks that re-enter Rust with arbitrary string payloads, tray menu items wired to invoke arbitrary IPC) converts an outbound surface into a phishing / IPC-abuse vector. The capability JSON for both MUST list only the outbound emit subset; any incoming-event handler MUST go through a separately-named capability with stated rationale.

- NEVER widen `pulse:plugin-fs` beyond the host's read of the resolved plugin dir per Threat Model Summary "plugin host (WASM Component Model)" entry-point classification — the capability gates the `plugins` crate's filesystem load of `~/.andromeda-pulse/plugins/` and MUST NOT be exposed to webview JavaScript, MUST NOT be granted write/delete/execute scope, and MUST NOT be retargeted away from the canonicalized plugin dir resolved per the §Input env-var canonicalization ban. Webview exposure converts an internal plugin-loader capability into an unconstrained filesystem-read primitive against the user's plugin dir; write/execute widening converts it into a plugin-supply-chain compromise vector that bypasses the deferred-post-v1 signed-plugin verification.

- NEVER bind the OTLP receivers to `0.0.0.0` or any non-`127.0.0.1` interface — the loopback-only binding is the de facto authorization boundary per Phase 1 Sec 3 reasoning; binding to `0.0.0.0` invalidates the entire Minimal-tier risk model.

- NEVER instrument the product's own telemetry with an OTLP network exporter pointed at the product's own `:4317`/`:4318` ports per Cross-cutting Patterns Self-observation discipline — creates an infinite loop and bypasses the loopback authorization model.

title: Secrets

body: - NEVER commit `.env`, `*.p12`, `*.pem`, `*.cer`, `*.key`, or `~/.tauri/*.key` files to git — `.gitignore` enforces; gitleaks CI step verifies.
- NEVER store the Azure Key Vault service principal as a long-lived GitHub Actions secret — use GitHub OIDC federation per security-research §Azure Key Vault OIDC.

- NEVER reference third-party GitHub Actions by `@v2` / floating tag — pin by 40-char commit SHA per security-research §Pin GitHub Actions by SHA + Dependabot. The tj-actions/changed-files CVE-2025-30066 (23k repos) demonstrated the retroactive-tag-rewrite attack class.

- NEVER grant `permissions: { contents: write }` at the workflow level — set workflow-level to `contents: read` and elevate per-job to `write` only on the publish step per security-research §Minimum GITHUB_TOKEN permissions.
- NEVER place Azure Key Vault credentials, Apple Developer ID credentials, or Tauri updater Minisign private key outside the GitHub Environment named `production-release` with manual approval gate.

title: Logging

body: **Uniform scrubber coverage (post-chunk-#72 reality, corrected as measured 2026-08-22):** The PII scrubber (`crates/security/src/scrubber.rs`, chunk #68 substrate — since chunk `2026-09-30-span-level-redaction` reached through `security::scrubber::mask_secret_spans` at every boundary but one, `scrub_attribute` staying its detection verdict) is invoked at the persistence boundaries enumerated below — not single-site as the pre-#72 plan body implied. **The catalog carries EIGHT categories** since chunk `2026-08-22-pii-scrubber-recall`: JWT · bearer · api_key · secret_kv · **provider_key** · email · credit_card · ssn. The eighth (`provider_key`) closes the BARE-CREDENTIAL recall gap — the four credential arms before it are all key-name-anchored, so a standalone `sk_live_…` / `sk-proj-…` / `ghp_…` / `AKIA…` token matched nothing and reached stored fields verbatim (measured RED before the fix on both `log_records.body` and `span_events.exception_message`). It is anchored-prefix + length-floor by design, ordered after the keyed arms so `api_key=` keeps its own category and before `credit_card` so a digit-heavy key is not mis-labelled; the module's stated posture is recall over precision for seven of the eight arms, bounded by a false-positive corpus that keeps ordinary high-entropy identifiers Allowed. **The `credit_card` arm is precision-gated** since chunk `2026-09-29-scrubber-path-false-positive` (founder ratification 2026-09-30, "Luhn on windows"): its regex finds a candidate run of ASCII digit groups joined by single ` ` / `-` (`\b[0-9]+(?:[ \-][0-9]+)*\b`), and the arm matches only when some window of consecutive WHOLE groups carrying 13–19 digits passes Luhn — which every issued card number does (ISO/IEC 7812). It replaced the checksum-free `\b(?:\d[ \-]?){13,19}\b`. Windows never split a group, because Luhn at arbitrary offsets would pass most long digit runs by chance. This closes the measured harness-basename false positive: a date-time stamp such as `rm-20260923-093840` in a path, a `workspace=` key or the digest's `PROJECT:` line, and a 19-digit nanosecond timestamp, now return `Allowed` (as measured at `crates/security/src/scrubber.rs::scrubber_allows_non_card_digit_runs`, mutation-checked in both directions). **Accepted recall trade:** a Luhn-invalid (mistyped) card number, or one fused inside a longer single digit group, is no longer redacted. **Span-level masking replaces whole-value replacement** since chunk `2026-09-30-span-level-redaction` (a Boundary widening, founder ratification at P4 2026-10-01, «Ок давай по типу правила»): `mask_secret_spans` masks each secret where it sits and keeps the rest of the value byte-identical, so one card number no longer blanks a whole digest. The extent is CLASS-AWARE — keyed arms (`bearer`, `api_key`, `secret_kv`) mask from the key word to the end of the line holding the match end; bare arms (`jwt`, `provider_key`, `email`, `ssn`) mask the whole whitespace-delimited token; `credit_card` masks the Luhn-qualifying digit-group run; overlapping or touching spans merge under the earliest arm in catalog order. That extent is what keeps never-weaken: a multi-word value after `password:` and a base64 bearer tail past `+` / `/` (both outside their arm's regex match) are masked to the end of their line. Detection is unchanged — `scrub_attribute`'s verdict gates the mask (equality pinned over the recall and false-positive corpora and two proptests), a flagged value with no locatable span masks whole (fail closed), and a single-token secret masks exactly as whole-value replacement did. Masking re-runs to a bounded fixpoint (at most 4 extra passes), because a mask can expose a match its neighbour hid (a Luhn-valid digit run fused to a key word becomes a card candidate once the key is masked — as measured at the chunk's mutation m4, a proptest shrinking to exactly that case). Whole-value replacement survives at ONE site: `metrics_points.labels` (`encode_labels`, the only production `scrub_attribute` caller — see the third scrub shape below).

**INTENDED posture:** any attribute value crossing into persistent storage (corpus.db) OR the self-observation log sink (`agent-latest.jsonl`) passes through `mask_secret_spans()` first — gated by `scrub_attribute()`'s `ScrubbedValue::Allowed(_)` / `ScrubbedValue::Redacted` verdict and masking only the matched spans — except `metrics_points.labels`, which takes the `scrub_attribute()` verdict whole-value per label.

**MEASURED reality (2026-08-23) — the intended posture HOLDS for every client-controlled ring-buffer column that a producer can reach.** Coverage spans: the OTLP appender's DuckDB writes for **`log_records.body`** (via `extract_log_body`) and **`exception_message` / `exception_stacktrace` on both `span_events` and `log_records`**; the Drain template + corpus persist path (template content + variable bindings); ServiceRegistry corpus persist; RetryStormState corpus persist (`crates/triage/src/pattern/persistence.rs::StormStateSnapshot::scrubbed_clone`); the incident-summary corpus write boundary — since chunk `2026-08-26-interpretation-brief-completeness`, `Incident.resolution_summary_text` holds a scrubbed JSON projection of the parsed `L4Output` written at THREE paths (incident creation, dedupe re-generation refresh, and the resolution-summary final write — `scrubbed_l4_json` in `pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs`); since chunk `2026-09-30-span-level-redaction` each STRING LEAF of the projection is span-masked before it is serialized — never the serialized text, where `secret_kv`'s `\S+` would run across compact-JSON delimiters — so the summary stays parseable and a redaction no longer collapses it to a category marker or sends the report to the pending notice (the training export's `interpretation` egress masks the same JSON per leaf); since chunk `2026-08-23-ingestion-scrub-coverage` — the four client-controlled columns that previously reached storage unscrubbed: **`spans.service_name` · `span_events.name` · `metrics_points.metric_name` · `log_records.severity_text`**; and — since chunk `2026-08-23-metrics-points-labels` — a FIFTH persisted client-controlled cell, **`metrics_points.labels`** (a `VARCHAR NOT NULL DEFAULT ''` column holding a data point's attribute set, scrubbed at its write boundary). The covered set is therefore **five** persisted client-controlled cells.

`service_name` is scrubbed inside `extract_service_name` (`crates/buffer/src/appender.rs`) rather than at the column push, because that one `pub(crate)` fn is the choke point for THREE consumers — the `spans` column, the storm `FingerprintObserver`, and the baseline `SpanObserver` tap — and scrubbing only the column would leave two raw paths into `triage` AND desynchronise DuckDB's service identity from the baseline registry the per-service joins key on. The tap drives ONE `SpanObserver`, a `CompositeSpanObserver` fanning each span out to three observers in order — baseline, restart, and (since chunk `2026-09-30-p-027-discovery-bound`) the first-sighting `DiscoveryObserverAdapter`, which registers a baseline-admitted service in the lifecycle `ServiceRegistry` at its first span — so the tap's scrubbed name now also keys that registry directly, where before only `tick_all` inserted it (from the baseline's own map, keyed by the same scrubbed name). The choke point's consumers stay THREE; what grew is the tap's downstream fan-out, and the desync argument now covers the lifecycle registry as well: a raw tap would put an unscrubbed identity into both registries. The other three scrub at their push sites through `scrub_otlp_field`. Treatment is uniform across all four **columns** (and the three persisted service keys) — span-masked since chunk `2026-09-30-span-level-redaction`, so a single-token credential-shaped name masks exactly as before while a multi-word name keeps its non-secret words (`checkout owner@x.com` → `checkout [REDACTED:email]`) — decided against the alternatives (a collision-safe discriminator mints a stable derived identifier of the secret; leaving `metric_name` raw leaves the gap open) — `metrics_points.metric_name` is the only target inside a PRIMARY KEY. **The collision that treatment implied is CLOSED** (chunk `2026-08-23-metrics-points-identity`): the key gained a `seq` ordinal, so two DISTINCT credential-shaped names redacting identically at the same `ts_unix_nano` + `resource_hash` no longer collide — both rows persist, and no batch fails. The rejected alternative stands — the discriminator is content-INDEPENDENT (a per-table monotonic counter, never derived from the secret), so no stable identifier of the credential is minted. **Residual, and the reason this is not a pure win:** two names that differ only inside a masked span still mask to ONE text, so those rows land indistinguishable from each other (under span masking a name's non-secret words survive, so names differing outside the masked span stay distinct). Redaction holds and there is no new leak — but the whole-batch ERROR was the only signal that a credential-shaped collision had occurred at all, and closing it removes that signal. Scrubbing `metric_name` remains mandatory; reverting it to raw is still the rejected alternative.

**A THIRD scrub SHAPE exists, and it is not optional** (chunk `2026-08-23-metrics-points-labels`). Beside the choke-point form (`extract_service_name`, one fn feeding three consumers) and the push-site form (`scrub_otlp_field` on a bare column value), `metrics_points.labels` scrubs the **JOINED `key=value` form, UNIONED with the bare value** — either match redacts. The joined form is load-bearing, not defensive: `scrub_attribute` takes a single `&str`, and TWO of the eight catalog arms are key-name-anchored — `secret_kv` (`(?i)(password|passwd|secret|token)[\s=:]+\S+`) and `api_key` (`(?i)(api[_\-]?key|access[_\-]?token|secret[_\-]?key|auth[_\-]?token)[\s=:]+[\w\-]{12,}`). A label `{password: "hunter2"}` presents only `hunter2` to a value-only scrub and matches **nothing**, so the entire keyed class would be stored verbatim while only bare-shape values (the eighth arm) were caught. No catalog arm is `^`/`$`-anchored, so joining with `=` is a superset in practice for the `\b`-anchored arms too; the union is what keeps that true if an anchored arm is ever added. **Label KEYS are stored verbatim** — only the VALUE becomes `[REDACTED:{category}]`, reconstructed as `{key}=[REDACTED:{category}]` from the key already held. **Failure mode of this treatment, accepted:** over-redaction when the KEY alone trips a match (`password=1` redacts a benign value), per the key-anchored arms' recall-over-precision posture (only the `credit_card` arm is precision-gated; see the catalog paragraph above). Because the key survives, two distinct keys can never collapse into one placeholder — the redaction-collision class chunk `2026-08-23-metrics-points-identity` closed is **not** reintroduced. Verified by mutation check: neutralising the label scrub stores `password=hunter2` verbatim.

**Two different fives — do not conflate them.** The five-column enumeration this section previously carried was measurably wrong in COUNT: **that** five was four live columns plus one vacuous. The CURRENT five is a genuine live count — the four columns above plus `metrics_points.labels`. The vacuous member's substrate no longer exists: the producer-less `instrumentation_scopes` (and `resources` / `span_links`) CREATEs were DELETED at chunk `2026-08-30-diagnostics-un-muting-harness-truth-sweep` — every remaining ring-buffer table has a producer, so "the reserved tables" and "the written tables" now denote the same set, and no scrub target can be vacuous by construction (arch §Occupied Resources owns the schema enumeration).

**`incident_events` lifecycle writes are a deliberate NO-SCRUB boundary** (chunk `2026-08-30-diagnostics-un-muting-harness-truth-sweep`; writer census and vocabulary as measured at chunk `2026-10-02-incident-events-readable-through-mcp`): `event_kind` comes from the closed four-kind vocabulary `triage::contract::incident_event_kinds()` = `created`, `active`, `acknowledged`, `resolved` — one shared definition written by the producer and read by the sidecar, never client text — and every row carries an EMPTY `cell_encrypt`-ed payload. TWO production writer paths reach the table: the producer's creation event (`pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs::create_incident_from_l4_output` writes `INCIDENT_EVENT_CREATED` through `IncidentPersistence::save_incident_event` → `CorpusWriter::save_incident_event`), and `CorpusWriter::update_incident_status`, which records one row per status VALUE-change inside the guarded-update transaction and is the choke point every status writer reaches, the cross-process MCP sidecar's `mark_incident_resolved` included and, since chunk `2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process`, the same tool called through the console engine's door in the engine's own process (through `dispatch_mark_incident_resolved` over the engine's `CorpusWriter`, only when the write switch is on; PROVISIONAL — §Threat Model Summary → Attack surface, the door's vector). Both carry a bounded literal, so nothing client-controlled crosses this boundary and no scrub is attached; attaching one would scrub a constant. The table's one production READER is the `retrieve_incident_events` tool (`CorpusWriter::load_incident_events`), served by the sidecar and, since that chunk, by the door through `call_tool`, whose `door.call` record carries no answer: it never selects `payload`, coerces `event_kind` on egress to the closed vocabulary (anything else reads `unknown`), returns only that label plus `occurred_unix_nano`, and its response body is never logged (stderr and file-sink canary absence measured).

**`ui.ipc.rejection` is a deliberate NO-SCRUB log boundary** (chunk `2026-08-30-acl-rejection-logging`): the capability-rejected-IPC record §Logging & Monitoring "What to log" mandates — a WARN emitted once per rejection event (never per invoke, off any hot path) behind its OWN exact allowlist leaf `{error_category, window_label, payload_bytes}`. Nothing client-controlled or free-text crosses it: `error_category` is the closed `IpcRejectionCategory` enum (`acl_rejected`|`other`, classified webview-side from the rejection value), `window_label` is bounded by `coerce_window_label` (4-label set + `unknown`; coerces, never rejects — an out-of-set label lands coerced, wire-proven), and `payload_bytes` is a `u32` bounded by `validate_payload_bytes`. The copied markdown, the command string and the raw rejection text are deliberately EXCLUDED — wire-measured at markdown 0× across 6,033 revoked-run log lines with exactly one WARN per rejection. NO bare `ui` allowlist key exists (measured), so the exact leaf is what keeps the three fields unredacted; pinned ×4 in `pulse-app/tests/unit_observability_allowlist_ipc_rejection.rs` incl. the fallback discriminator and banned-field checks.

**`ui.webgpu.adapter` is a deliberate NO-SCRUB log boundary** (chunk `2026-09-30-perf-instruments-measure-their-budgets`; a Boundary widening the founder ratified at P4 2026-09-30, verbatim «Да, делай»): one webview-originated record per canvas-mount WebGPU adapter request (never per frame, off any hot path) — INFO on `obtained`, WARN otherwise — behind its OWN exact allowlist leaf `{outcome, window_label}` beside `ui.ipc.rejection`. Nothing client-controlled or free-text crosses it: `outcome` is the closed `WebgpuAdapterOutcome` enum (`obtained`|`no_navigator_gpu`|`adapter_null`|`adapter_request_rejected`|`device_request_failed`, classified webview-side; an unknown value is rejected at deserialization) and `window_label` is bounded by `coerce_window_label` (4-label set + `unknown`; coerces, never rejects). The raw adapter / rejection error text is deliberately EXCLUDED. Still no bare `ui` key; pinned ×3 in `pulse-app/tests/unit_observability_allowlist_webgpu_adapter.rs` (field set both directions, a non-allowlisted field redacted, the no-`ui`-fallback discriminator). Its live witness for the `obtained` arm is the dev-host `perf:frame-sample` leg (2 `obtained` records, fields unredacted). Since chunk `2026-10-09-boot-smoke-s-early-exit-found-and-closed` the CI boot job's smoke step runs `cargo xtask harness:settled` after `boot` and before `status` and `cleanup`, so the smoke reads the app past its adapter request on every run that reaches the settle verdict; as measured on one run (`ci#37979648967`): the app lived 5.494 s from its first record to its `app.exit`, and its log holds 2 `ui.webgpu.adapter` records, both `outcome: no_navigator_gpu`. Under the step's former order the record was there on some runs only (the app lived 0.57 s to 1.40 s before `cleanup`; four of seven boot-job logs of 2026-10-09 held it, both fields rendered, as measured at chunk `2026-10-09-supply-chain-job-same-on-push-and-pull-request`).

**`app.exit` is a deliberate NO-SCRUB log boundary** (chunk `2026-10-01-conductor-return`): one product-originated record per process end — exactly one, by a process-wide once-flag and by construction (the emitter drops the sink's only `WorkerGuard` after writing) — behind its OWN exact allowlist leaf `{exit_class, exit_code, exit_code_known, signal}` beside `app.panic.fatal`. Nothing client-controlled or free-text crosses it: `exit_class` and `signal` are closed labels (`event_loop`|`outside_event_loop`|`signal` · `none`|`sigterm`|`sigint`), `exit_code` an `i32` (0 when unknown) and `exit_code_known` a bool; a panic payload, an error `Display`, a native message and every path are deliberately EXCLUDED. No bare `app` key; pinned ×4 in `pulse-app/tests/unit_observability_allowlist_app_exit.rs` (mutation-checked), and the re-exec arms of `pulse-app/tests/integration_exit_cause_record.rs` read 0 full data-dir paths and 0 planted canary across each child's whole log family. Its stated failure mode is the set of ends it cannot see, by construction: SIGKILL, `_exit`, Windows `TerminateProcess`, a Rust `std::process::exit` on Windows (`ExitProcess` runs no `atexit` — as measured at that chunk) and failures before the sink exists (stderr / `boot.log` only).

**`app.boot.door`, `door.call` and `door.refused` are deliberate NO-SCRUB log boundaries** (chunk `2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process`), each behind its OWN exact allowlist leaf; no bare `door` key and no bare `app` key exists. `app.boot.door` — `{state, resolve_write}` (`listening` | `path_too_long` | `in_use` | `occupied` | `bind_failed` · `on` | `off` | `rejected`), once per boot of a program that seats the door, INFO when `listening` with the switch not `rejected`, WARN otherwise. `door.call` — `{method, tool, outcome, write, result_type, result_count, answer_bytes, duration_ms}` (`method` and `tool` closed sets, anything else reading `other` / `none`; `outcome` one of nine closed labels), once per request that is answered, written BEFORE the answer line so an applied write always has its record even when the caller is gone, INFO for `ok`, WARN otherwise. `door.refused` — `{reason, peer}` (`other_account` | `too_many_connections` | `request_too_large` | `idle` · `owner` | `other`), WARN. Nothing client-controlled crosses them: no argument, no answer, no path (the socket's included), no account id and no error's text; none is written at ERROR. Pinned in `pulse-app/tests/unit_observability_allowlist_door.rs` (exact resolve, field-set equality in both directions, `for_target("door")` none) and by the spawned arms of `pulse-app/tests/integration_door.rs` (a marker sent as telemetry and read back through a door call stands 0 times in the log family; no full data-dir path). Stated limits: a tool called through the door also writes the tools' own library records into the console engine's log (`viz.query.traces` · `viz.query.metrics` · `viz.query.logs` · `viz.query`, and for `generate_snapshot` `metric.snapshot.token_count_ms` · `snapshot.token.count.validate`) — which of them a real call wrote was not enumerated from a log; a caller that does not read its answer leaves an `idle` refusal beside the call record; "no such incident" and a real fault both record `tool_error`. No scrub or redaction shape changed at that chunk.

**Residual, unchanged by this chunk:** the DuckDB ring buffer itself remains **unencrypted** — the corpus AES-256-GCM posture does not cover it — so the control here is redaction at the write boundary, not confidentiality at rest (enabling DuckDB at-rest encryption stays banned per §Security Anti-Patterns → Data Protection, CVE-2025-64429). `span_events.exception_type` remains a separate, deliberate exclusion ("class identifier, not user content") — a decision, not a gap. The 8-category catalog was unchanged by that chunk (`2026-08-23-ingestion-scrub-coverage`): no arm added, reordered, or retuned. The `credit_card` arm's match predicate was later retuned at chunk `2026-09-29-scrubber-path-false-positive`, with category count and order unchanged. Verified RED-before / GREEN-after on the real OTLP path, with a mutation check confirming the pins discriminate and a live wire run recording `redactions_applied` 0 → 4 and zero canary occurrences across 21,846 log lines. The owning working-route entry is **closed**.

Audit finding 1.B (single-site scrubber framing in pre-#72 plan body) is closed by the coverage above. The five NEVER bullets below ARE the rules the scrubber enforces at runtime wherever it is invoked.

- NEVER log raw OTLP attribute values, span/log/metric content payloads, snapshot file contents, clipboard contents, or MCP tool response bodies — they may contain incidentally captured secrets from the instrumented host application. **Verification status of the snapshot/clipboard arm (recorded 2026-08-30-dead-lib-src-test-migration):** unlike the wire-measured `ui.ipc.rejection`, L4-path and OTLP-scrub arms of this section, the `snapshot.generate` / `snapshot.copy_to_clipboard` resolver arm has NO executed test carrier and never did — its canary (`generate_does_not_log_snapshot_or_clipboard_or_workspace_path_canaries`) was dead under `[lib] test = false` and was DELETED at that chunk because any test binary linking the resolver aborts at load (`STATUS_ENTRYPOINT_NOT_FOUND` via the tauri clipboard/notification import chain). Executed coverage 0→0 — the rule stands, its verification is OWED via the `tauri::test::mock_builder()` lift (blocked by the Wry-typed `AppHandle<Wry>` OnceLock in `SnapshotApiImpl`); owner: test-plan §1 `snapshot-resolver-level-coverage`.

- NEVER log a full product-consumed filesystem path — basename of the canonicalized path only. Covers the plugin dir, the three L4 model/binary path vars, the `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_ALLOW_ROOT` root, the console engine's door socket path `{data dir}/run/door/sock` (chunk `2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process`: no door record carries it or any path — `app.boot.door` reports the endpoint as a closed `state` label only, and the spawned arms of `pulse-app/tests/integration_door.rs` read no full data-dir path in the log family), and the corpus-key lock dir / lock-file path (chunk `2026-10-04-corpus-key-creation-is-race-free`: no `tracing::` site was added; a lock-dir, open or lock failure surfaces only as the unit `KeychainError::Unavailable` / `Failed` → `KeyringUnavailable` on the existing `corpus.open.error` / `mcp.boot.corpus.init` records, carrying no path and no OS error text), and the per-spawn L4 grammar temp file passed as `--grammar-file` (`andromeda-pulse-llama-grammar-{pid}-{nanos}.gbnf` in `std::env::temp_dir()`; never logged at all — 0 occurrences of `andromeda-pulse-llama-grammar` and 0 full GGUF paths in the GREEN real-model leg's log, chunk `2026-10-05-l4-runs-the-founder-s-pick-with-its-authors-settings`): the L4 records emit `path_basename` / `root_basename` plus the env-var NAME (safe — only `*_SECRET` / `*_TOKEN` / `*_KEY` / `*_PASSPHRASE` names redact), and an argv-prompt rejection carries a bounded category with no prompt text, excerpt, or offending substring. Measured at the wire (chunk `2026-08-26-l4-runtime-security-residuals`): the model path's containing directory appears 0× across 11,251 log lines while the basename appears once; the full root path 0×. **The rule is now CATEGORICAL** (chunk `2026-08-30-diagnostics-un-muting-harness-truth-sweep`): the two boot records that stood as the known carried exception — `app.boot.tracing.init` and `app.boot.pid` — now emit `log_dir_basename` / `path_basename` / `run_dir_basename` / `data_dir_basename` via `pulse_app::observability::log_basename`, their allowlist leaves renamed to match, and the boot smoke measured 0 full paths on the un-muted set.
- NEVER log DuckDB query parameter values — log query identifier + parameter count instead.

- NEVER expose stack traces, Rust struct names, file paths, or library versions in `AppError::Internal { message }` content surfaced to the webview — sanitize at the `From<thiserror::Error> for AppError` impl.
- NEVER expose internal hostnames or IPs in OTLP error responses or MCP error objects.

title: Code Patterns

body: - NEVER use `tokio::process::Command::new(...).arg(user_input)` against any string sourced from an OTLP attribute, MCP tool argument, or workspace-detector output — the MCP STDIO command-injection cluster (CVE-2025-49596 MCP Inspector, CVE-2025-54994, CVE-2025-54136 Cursor, CVE-2026-22252 LibreChat) demonstrates this is a live 2025–2026 class. **ONE product path passes OTLP-derived text to argv and is admitted only through a bound** (chunk `2026-08-26-l4-runtime-security-residuals`): the L4 `-p` prompt, gated by `validate_prompt_bounded` — 16384-byte ceiling + NUL/C0/C1 rejection with `\n`, `\r`, `\t` whitelisted, since the prompt is multi-line markdown by construction and a naive `is_control()` predicate would reject every legitimate prompt and silently disable L4. The ceiling is measured, not guessed — re-based live at chunk `2026-08-26-interpretation-brief-completeness`: ~2.03× the observed maximum — 8,067 B, the 2026-10-07 dev-probe composition of the synthetic S14 / S15 with their five corpus lines (the baseline arm `nb`: the block as composed before the corpus selection was narrowed to the triggering scope; chunk `2026-10-07-l4-probe-reproduces-the-canary-history-miss`), beside 8,059 B, the first size measured on a prompt the product itself composed in a live run (the third captured drive's, five corpus lines); before it 7,824 B, the 2026-10-07 v2.6 dev-probe composition of the synthetic A6 (a cueless digest carrying three resolved corpus matches of one fingerprint, today's render, with the framing instruction's added scope sentence, +249 B; chunk `2026-10-06-l4-first-hypothesis-names-the-triggering-service`; primary builder only); before it 7,575 B, the 2026-10-05 pattern-discrimination composition of the same A6 at v2.5; before that 7,405 B, the 2026-10-05 v2.5 dev-probe composition (synthetic S4: a retry storm with one corpus match, carrying the TRIGGER line, the corpus framing note and the reworded framing instruction; primary builder only — fallback and reflection carry the same +220 B and were unmeasured at v2.5; their first readings, at v2.6 on an empty digest only, are fallback 7,200 B and reflection 7,549 B beside primary 7,011 B); before that 7,185 B, the 2026-10-04 v2.4 composition of the same shape; before that 6,932 B, the 2026-08-27 reflection prompt (the 2026-08-26 sustained v2.2 range was 6715..=6830 B with the citable-evidence-ids section; measurement notes, never bounds) — and below the Windows `CreateProcess` 32767 limit so the guard fires before the OS. Note what the bound does and does NOT do — the OTLP-derived substring is already PII-scrubbed upstream by `Digest::scrubbed_clone`, so this is a SHAPE-and-LENGTH control against the banned argv construct, not a confidentiality fix. The argv's other operands are first-party (chunk `2026-10-05-l4-runs-the-founder-s-pick-with-its-authors-settings`; founder-ratified live 2026-10-05): the `--grammar-file` path names a per-spawn temp file holding the committed GBNF, and `--temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 64 --min-p 0` are compile-time constants — none carries OTLP-derived text, so `-p` stays the one path this ban admits. A second, NON-product argv path exists in the dev probe (an example binary, never shipped; chunk `2026-10-07-l4-probe-reproduces-the-canary-history-miss`, a Boundary widening the founder answered on 2026-10-07): `--replay` passes a captured product prompt, read from a run-time path outside the tree, unchanged as the probe's `-p` operand, through the same `validate_prompt_bounded` and its own file checks (§Input Validation, the L4 argv row); the product count stays ONE.

- NEVER load a plugin from a path that wasn't canonicalized and asserted to be inside the resolved plugin dir — pair with the §Input ban above; this defends against `~/.andromeda-pulse/plugins/../../etc/...` walks via `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_PLUGIN_DIR`.

- NEVER spawn the `andromeda-pulse-mcp` sidecar without verifying both the compile-time `--features mcp-server` build flag AND the runtime `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED=true` env var — single-gate is a regression of the architecture's declared double-gate per Established Decisions MCP Server Surface.

- NEVER serialize an `anyhow::Error` directly across the TauRPC bridge — must convert to the `serde`-friendly `AppError` enum first per Conventions Error response schema (Tauri IPC). Direct serialization either fails to compile (no `Serialize` impl) or, if hand-implemented, leaks the full error chain to the webview.
- NEVER use `serde_json::from_slice::<T>(buf)` on a buffer that hasn't been size-bounded by the `axum` `DefaultBodyLimit` layer — covers the OTLP HTTP/JSON path on `:4318`.

- NEVER use the `wasmtime` `Linker` to expose host functions outside the WIT contract for a given guest — bypasses the architecture's capability-scoped sandbox per Established Decisions Plugin Runtime.

title: Universal

body: - NEVER let the rust-toolchain drift below 1.85.0 — Edition 2024 cannot parse without it per security-research §Rust 2024 edition; the security-positive defaults (`unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn`, `unsafe extern`, `static mut` reference denial, tightened `if let` temporary scopes) require 1.85+. That 1.85.0 is the Edition-2024 minimum, not the build floor: the workspace declares `rust-version = "1.95"`, equal to the pinned 1.95.0 channel and set by the resolved dependency graph (wasmtime / cranelift / pulley declare 1.95.0), and the xtask test `declared_floor_equals_the_pinned_channel` holds the declared floor equal to the pin.

- NEVER ship a release without resolving the `tonic` 0.14 vs `opentelemetry-otlp` 0.31 / `tonic` 0.13 duplicate per Established Decisions caveat — `cargo deny check bans` is the enforcement mechanism per security-research §cargo-deny.

- NEVER log, or run any code that needs thread-locals, from a C `atexit` handler or a signal handler on the thread that is ending the process — under glibc the exiting thread's TLS destructors run BEFORE `atexit` handlers, and a `LocalKey::with` panic inside an `extern "C"` handler aborts the process. The `libc` FFI exit surface (`pulse-app/src/observability.rs`, chunk `2026-10-01-conductor-return`; Edition 2024 `unsafe` discipline) hands the record to a thread spawned at install (`pulse-exit-reporter`, a bounded ≤ 2 s wait), and the Unix signal path records from a runtime task — never from the async-signal context — then restores `SIG_DFL` and re-raises the SAME signal, so the process still ends BY that signal (never by an exit code standing in for it; the harness records `signal N`).
