**Wireframe notes:** Compact widget is a fixed quarter-screen size; custom frameless titlebar includes app icon (small), title text in `font-body`, settings gear icon (aperture glyph), and platform-specific window controls (traffic-light buttons on macOS, standard buttons on Windows / Linux). Canvas fills the remaining viewport; the footer band is a read-only status display.

title: Wireframe — Full dashboard (Traces primary screen)

body:
```
+------------------------------------------------+
| [⚙] andromeda-pulse Traces [Logs] [⋯]  [━⊟◯] |  <- header (height space-lg, padding space-md)
| [telescope icon] Investigate  [aperture icon]  |     custom titlebar + tab nav (model TBD)
+------------------------------------------------+
|                                                |
| [Service constellation map with Halo pulses]  |  <- hero / signature section
|                                                |     (color-inset canvas bg, radius-md,
|                                                |      padding space-md, border subtle)
|                                                |     Signature: per-service Halo dots
+------------------------------------------------+
|  Trace ID         Service    Latency   Error  |  <- primary content (data table)
|  ─────────────────────────────────────────     |     (header bg color-base, rows hover
|  5a9e2d1f3c...    auth-svc   145ms    ✓       |      color-primary at 10% opacity,
|  7b4c8e9a2f...    api-gate   203ms    ✗       |      cell padding space-sm, font-data)
|  3d6f1a8c5e...    cache      52ms     ✓       |
+------------------------------------------------+
| Time range: [picker] | Service: [filter]      |  <- footer (height space-sm,
+------------------------------------------------+     color-text-tertiary, font-label)
```

**Wireframe notes:** Full dashboard is resizable; default 2/3 to full-screen width. The Traces primary screen is a **flex column bounded to the shell's `main` height** (`calc(100vh − titlebar 32px − tabnav 40px − footer var(--spacing-lg))`, `overflow:hidden`), so the **whole dashboard shows no outer page scrollbar at any window size** — only the table's own region scrolls. Two **fixed** (`flex-shrink:0`) regions stack on top: the constellation map hero (the severity-hue constellation dots; the per-dot Halo State Pulse glow is deferred — §Component) and, directly above the table, a right-aligned **`Errors only` filter toolbar** (an `aria-pressed` toggle; the default order is anomaly-first, erroring rows hoisted to the top). Below them the **sortable data table flex-fills the remainder** (`flex:1 / min-height:0 / overflow-y:auto`, custom dark-track + Earth-Blue-thumb scrollbar) with a **sticky opaque `color-base` thead** — rows scroll internally *under* the fixed hero + toolbar + header. (Internal-scroll + bounded route: P-082; Errors-only toolbar above the table: P-068.) **The hero is a landmark region** (2026-08-23-a11y-verification): a `<section>` carrying the STABLE literal accessible name `"Telemetry traces chart"` — deliberately static, since a landmark whose name tracks the data churns the screen-reader rotor — described by a visually-hidden aggregate summary element (`data-testid="constellation-summary"`) wired as its `aria-describedby` target, carrying lifecycle counts + a findings tally only (no service name enters the accessible tree). `role="status"` on that element is deliberately NOT applied. The ASCII above is an illustrative sketch: its footer row + per-dot label detail lag current truth (footer is now the plain-language connection-status line, P-070; the hero dots carry always-on per-dot name + severity-token labels, P-069) — see the amendment sidecar handoff note.

title: Component — Custom titlebar (desktop-webview specific)

body: **Layout:**
- Flex row, `height: space-lg`, `padding: 0 space-sm`, `gap: space-sm`.
- Background: `color-base`.
- Drag region: full width except buttons (Tauri 2 `data-tauri-drag-region` attribute on titlebar container).
- Flex segments: `[app-icon + title | grow | settings-button | window-controls]`.
**Components:**
- **App icon:** small custom glyph (aperture or constellation-grid), `color-primary`, clickable → focus main window.
- **Title:** `font-label` weight, `color-text-primary`, `"andromeda-pulse"` (compact widget) or `"andromeda-pulse — {view}"` (full dashboard).
- **Settings button:** aperture glyph icon, `color-text-secondary`, hover → `color-text-primary` over `duration-fast` ease-out, click → Settings modal.

- **Window controls (Windows / Linux):** three buttons (minimize, maximize, close) on the right side; `color-text-secondary`, hover state darkens background to `color-raised-2`. macOS uses traffic-light buttons (red, yellow, green) on the left side via the OS chrome convention.
**Border:** bottom 1px subtle border (`Border Progression Subtle` token).

title: Component — Halo State Pulse canvas (hero / signature)

data.head: ### Component — Halo State Pulse canvas (hero / signature)

body: > **MEASURED 2026-08-21 (chunk 2026-08-21-delegated-timing-observables) — this canvas does NOT render. DEFERRED 2026-08-29 (operator ruling, chunk 2026-08-29-halo-state-pulse-signature-deferred): the signature glow layer is deferred to the next version — neither built in 0.3.0 nor deleted from this spec.** Three independent probes at HEAD found no production render site on desktop-webview (re-verified at HEAD 2026-08-29): `<HaloCanvas` over `pulse-app/ui/src` (non-test) returns zero hits, and `Halo|halo` over `dashboard/Dashboard.tsx` and `widget/CompactWidget.tsx` returns zero hits — every non-test reference is a `vi.mock` factory or a comment. What IS live is the constellation DOT hue: `severity-to-halo.ts::severityToHueFraction(tier: PriorityTier | null)` feeding `ConstellationDot.priorityTier`, driven by **cumulative incident severity** (tiers none/curious/suggested/autonomous) — NOT by error rate, which the chunk-#31-era model used and design-system-amendments 2026-05-29 superseded. P-025's timing observable (`metric.constellation.hue_update_ms`) measures that real surface. The build-or-retire product decision the 2026-08-21 note pinned on the "Halo State Pulse canvas disposition" route entry is RESOLVED as defer: the render half rides `.andromeda/residuals.md` (target 0.4.0); the design sketch that gathered in `andromeda-pulse-0.4.0-incubator/signature-orb/` was removed on 2026-10-09 on the founder's word, so the deferred design has no sketch outside this spec. The desktop-native (tray) halo below was NOT probed by that chunk and does not inherit this measurement — it is deferred on its own ground (nothing renders it in 0.3.0 either; see §Surface: desktop-native). This section's spec is the deferred design record. The ASCII sketches keep their halo labels; this status note governs.
**Layout:**
- Container: `position: relative`, `width: 100%`, `height: 100%` (compact widget) or fixed hero height (full dashboard).
- Background: `color-inset`.
- Border: 1px subtle border with `radius-md`.
- Padding: `space-md`.
- `<canvas>` element fills the container; `devicePixelRatio` scaling is handled by React + the browser.
**Canvas rendering (WebGPU):**
- Render loop at 60 FPS via `requestAnimationFrame`.

- For each service in the constellation (from `traces.query` result):
  - Render a service dot at the constellation position (computed from service topology via the viz crate).
  - Overlay a circular halo glow (WebGPU fragment shader) implementing the Brand Identity signature spec: pulse frequency clamped from `throughput_hz / 1000`, blur radius envelope per pulse cycle, hue LCH-interpolated from `color-primary` (Earth Blue) → `color-accent` (Alert Burgundy) by **cumulative incident severity** (design-system-amendments 2026-05-29; the earlier error-rate driver is superseded), opacity envelope per pulse cycle.
- **Fallback (if WebGPU unavailable):** the `<canvas>` shows a `font-body` message in `color-text-tertiary` ("WebGPU not supported in this context").

- **Reduced motion (`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`):** the halo becomes a static glow (no pulsing rhythm), but hue still updates per cumulative incident severity. Per design-system Motion accessibility section. (This rule attaches to whichever surface actually renders — today the constellation dot.)
**Signature element details:**
- On compact widget: a unified single halo around an aggregated badge (e.g., "24 services, avg 1.2% error").
- On full dashboard Traces view: per-service halos on each constellation dot.

- Motion is data-driven (not decorative) — activity state drives the breathing period and cumulative incident severity drives hue (design-system-amendments 2026-05-29). Both bullets above are deferred to the next version per the status note at the top of this section.

title: Component — Primary navigation (desktop-webview)

body: **IA model:**
- Compact widget: settings via the gear icon (modal); no other navigation. Esc minimizes to tray.
- Full dashboard: tab-based or sidebar navigation (model TBD — design commits to both being valid; tabs require less chrome on narrow windows, sidebar scales better for 3–4 views).
**Tab / sidebar structure (either model):**
- **Traces** — per-service trace samples, constellation map.
- **Metrics** — time-series throughput + latency, per-service aggregates.
- **Logs** — log records, severity filtering.
- **Snapshots** — generated snapshot list, view / copy actions.
- **Settings** — theme, widget snap position, retention, MCP toggle.
**Active state indicator:**
- Tab: underline or background change to `color-raised-2`, text `color-text-primary`.
- Sidebar (if used): left border in `color-primary` weight, background `color-raised-1`.
**Keyboard navigation:** Tab through tabs / sidebar items; Enter / Space to activate; Escape to exit Settings modal.

title: Component — Trace data table (primary content block)

data.head: ### Component — Trace data table (primary content block)

body: **Layout:**
- Grid: native `<table>` markup (thead + tbody + rows; first-party component — no shadcn, per the corrected Tooling context).
- Header row: `background: color-base`, `color: color-text-primary`, `font-weight: 600`, `font: font-label`.
- Data rows: transparent background (parent surface shows through); 1px bottom border subtle.
- Padding: each cell `padding: space-sm`.
- Hover state: row background fades to `color-primary` at 10% opacity — no transition (instant per `0.35` expression).
**Columns (sample):**
- **Trace ID:** `font-code` monospace, `color-text-primary`, selectable for copy.
- **Service:** `font-body`, `color-text-primary`.
- **Latency:** `font-data` (monospace tabular numerals), `color-text-secondary`, right-aligned.
- **Error:** `font-label`, status glyph (✓ in `color-feedback-success`, ✗ in `color-accent`).

**Sorting:** column headers clickable; click cycles through ascending → descending → unsorted (visual feedback: text bold, small caret in `color-primary`). The default (unsorted) order is anomaly-first — erroring rows hoisted to the top (P-068).

**Filter toolbar (above the table):** a right-aligned `Errors only` toggle (`aria-pressed`) sits in its own toolbar row directly above the table, narrowing to `error_count > 0` rows; the constellation hero + this toolbar stay fixed above the scrolling table (P-068 / P-082).

**Internal scroll region:** the table sits in its own bounded scroll region (`flex:1 / min-height:0 / overflow-y:auto`, custom scrollbar per §Anti-Patterns Per-Surface Bans) with a **sticky opaque `color-base` thead**, so rows scroll internally while the hero + toolbar + header stay fixed and the dashboard never grows an outer page scrollbar — the route is bounded to the shell's `main` height (P-082).

**Keyboard / focus (2026-08-23-a11y-verification):** the table body is a **roving-tabindex row list** — each `<tr class="trace-row">` carries `tabIndex` `0` when active and `-1` otherwise, so the table contributes exactly ONE tab stop. Tab enters at the active row; Up/Down move between rows; Home/End jump to first/last; Enter runs that row's Investigate; Esc returns focus to the `Errors only` toggle. The focused row shows the `--border-focus` ring via `:focus-visible`, and moving focus scrolls the table's OWN region (never the page). The in-row Investigate button is `tabIndex={-1}` — it keeps its accessible name and click behaviour but is no longer a separate tab stop (a11y-plan §11 grid-lite carve-out). Row focus survives the live re-poll (P-081). Traversal is row-level, not 2-D cell-level: a read-only 4-column table with one action per row does not warrant a grid.

**Pagination / virtualization:** TBD by downstream; the table's own scroll region (above) handles overflow, and the telescope-icon "investigate" action triggers a detail view (not in-table inline expansion) — reachable by click, or by Enter on the keyboard-focused row.

title: Component — Empty / error state (desktop-webview data views)

data.head: ### Component — Empty / error state (desktop-webview data views)

body: **Applies to:** the Metrics / Logs / Snapshots data views — rendered in the primary content region in place of the chart / table / list when there is no data or a query fails. A single shared `EmptyState` component backs all three so the data views read as one system.

**Layout:** centered column in the primary content region — a decorative Observatory glyph (telescope, 24px, `aria-hidden`) above a message (`font-body` 14px) and an optional actionable hint; `gap: space-sm`, `padding: space-xl`. No focusable element (read-only, affordance-exempt).

**Empty (no data):** message + hint in `color-text-secondary` (a11y SC 1.4.3 — body-size text needs ≥4.5:1; NOT `color-text-tertiary`, 4.2:1 large-text-only). The hint names the OTLP receiver ports (`:4318` / `:4317`, in `font-code`) — e.g. "No metrics received yet" / "Point an OTLP metrics exporter at :4318 / :4317". Shown only on a settled zero-data load (never flashed while loading; hidden once populated).

**Error (query failure):** a distinct variant checked BEFORE the empty branch — a static message ("Couldn't load {metrics|logs}", never the raw `AppError`) with NO exporter hint, so a failure never masquerades as "no data". `color-text-secondary`; `color-accent` (Alert Burgundy) remains available for an optional error icon / border per the "never color alone" discipline.

title: Component — Investigation modal (supporting moment)

body: **Trigger:** clicking the titlebar "Investigate" button (telescope icon), clicking a trace row, or pressing **Enter on the keyboard-focused row** — the in-row telescope button is no longer reachable by Tab (`tabIndex={-1}`; see §Component — Trace data table).

**Motion:** Investigation Capture Collapse (design-system Motion supporting moment) — scale + opacity ease-out into a centered snapshot object. Within the `0.35` webview expression budget (exempt from the 200ms hard limit per design-system Motion).

**Layout:** centered modal over a semi-opaque backdrop (high `z-index`); inner card `background: color-raised-3`, 1px subtle border, `radius-lg`, `padding: space-md`, capped to ~80% of viewport with scrollable overflow. Title "Investigate {trace-id}" (`font-heading`, `color-text-primary`); content is the structured trace detail (span tree, attributes, events) in a scroll region; top-right `✕` close. Exact control styling owned by the implementation route.

title: Component — Settings modal (form)

body: **Trigger:** clicking the aperture icon in the titlebar or selecting the "Settings" tab.
**Motion:** modal open / close eases over `duration-standard`, within the `0.35` webview expression budget.
**Layout:** same overlay + card structure as the Investigation modal (`padding: space-md`); form sections stacked vertically with `gap: space-lg`.
**Form controls:**
- **Theme selector:** radio buttons or dropdown (dark / light / auto). Labels in `font-body`.

- **Widget snap position:** grid of FOUR radio buttons (top-left / top-right / bottom-left / bottom-right, default top-right), with a visual preview of the widget position on screen — the shipped `WidgetPosition` enum is corner-only (corrected as measured 2026-08-30 against `crates/ui-bridge/src/contract.rs`, test-pinned; not the nine-value corners+edges+center grid earlier drafts assumed).
- **Retention seconds:** numeric input, range 300–600, label + helper text in `font-label`.
- **MCP server toggle:** checkbox (visible only when the `mcp-server` Cargo feature is built), label "Enable MCP Server", helper text "Exposes query tools to Claude Code and other MCP clients."

**Input + button styling:** inputs `color-inset` background, 1px subtle border, `radius-sm`, `padding: space-sm`; focused → `color-primary` border + 20%-opacity focus ring (Border Progression Focus); error → `color-accent` border + helper text (`font-label`). Submit row: primary (Save) `color-primary` background / `color-base` text, secondary (Cancel) alongside. Exact control styling owned by the implementation route.

title: Component — Footer (read-only status bar)

body: **Compact widget:**
- Layout: flex row, `justify-content: space-between`, `height: space-sm`, `padding: 0 space-md`, transparent background.
- Left: "Ingest: {spans/sec}" in `font-data`, `color-text-tertiary`.
- Right: "Error: {%}" in `font-data`, `color-text-tertiary` (or `color-accent` if error % exceeds threshold, e.g., 5%).
- Border-top: 1px subtle border.
**Full dashboard:**
- Layout: flex row, `height: space-sm`, `padding: 0 space-md`, `gap: space-md`.
- Left: time-range picker (e.g., "Last 5m") — styled as a button with dropdown caret.
- Center: service filter (e.g., "All services" or selected service name) — styled as a button with dropdown caret.
- Right: ingest rate and error % (read-only, `font-label`, `color-text-tertiary`).

- Connection status (dashboard-only, P-070 — `ConnectionStatusLine`): a plain-language read-only line stating connected-source count ("Receiving from {N} services"), spans/s, and buffer fill ("buffer {used} min / {window} min") — human words in `font-body`, numerics in the `font-code` Data role (tabular-nums), `color-text-primary`. The compact widget stays aggregate-glance (no worded line). Live-updates via a 1s poll; the connected count reuses the P-067 live-recency gate.
- Border-top: 1px subtle border.

title: IA notes

body: **Navigation model:**
- Compact widget is the primary glance surface — minimalist chrome, always-on-top, snap-to-corner per Settings (four corners, default top-right). Esc minimizes the widget to the system tray.
- Full dashboard is reached by expanding the compact widget via the Settings toggle or a keyboard shortcut (TBD by downstream — design suggests `Cmd+Shift+P` / `Ctrl+Shift+P`).

- Both surfaces share the same underlying data feeds (TauRPC `traces.*`, `metrics.*`, `logs.*` routers). (They were also specified to share one Halo State Pulse WebGPU rendering; that layer is deferred to the next version on both — see §Component.)
**Responsive behavior:**
- Compact widget: fixed quarter-screen size — no CSS media-query breakpoints (user-resizable, but the layout does not reflow). Minimum recommended size stays readable on a 13-inch laptop display.

- Full dashboard: resizable with no hard breakpoints. The tabs-or-sidebar navigation model may adapt to available width downstream (e.g., tabs collapse to a hamburger menu at narrow widths); both models remain valid.
**Deep-link convention:**
- Compact widget: no deep links (glance-only surface).
- Full dashboard: routable views per tab/sidebar entry (`/traces`, `/metrics`, `/logs`, `/snapshots`, `/settings`). Hash routes vs. query params is a TanStack Router decision downstream.
**Keyboard shortcuts (TBD by downstream):**
- `Cmd+K` / `Ctrl+K`: command palette (if implemented) or global search.
- `Cmd+Shift+P` / `Ctrl+Shift+P`: toggle compact widget ↔ full dashboard.
- `Esc`: minimize widget or close modal.
**Multi-surface coordination:**

- Compact widget canvas + full dashboard Traces view + tray icon (desktop-native) were specified to render the same WebGPU Halo State Pulse visualization for cross-surface consistency; the whole layer is DEFERRED to the next version (webview halves measured non-rendering 2026-08-21, tray never probed and deferred on its own ground — see §Component and §Surface: desktop-native Signature placement). The data feed is shared via Tauri 2 broadcast channels (`pulse://stream/spans`, `pulse://stream/metrics`).

title: Surface: desktop-native

body: **Tooling context:** Framework Tauri 2.x (native window management, tray via `tauri-plugin-notification`, custom menu via Tauri's menu builder). OS-native UI (no React webview at this surface).
**Expression level (this surface):** 0.2 (minimal motion — icon state changes, traffic-light color transitions, badge emergence only). Tray menu is OS-native; no custom chrome animation.

**Signature placement (DEFERRED to the next version — operator ruling 2026-08-29; this layer was never probed by the 2026-08-21 webview measurement and defers ON ITS OWN GROUND — nothing renders it in 0.3.0):** "Halo State Pulse" is SPECIFIED to render as a unified animated glow around the aggregated service-count badge in the tray icon area:

1. **Tray icon glyph** — monochrome SVG template image (platform-dependent size). Shape: a stylized constellation star or pulsar with a circular outline (aperture metaphor). The OS handles template-image tinting.

2. **Halo State Pulse (secondary composited layer)** — WebGPU canvas in a small click-through overlay window positioned behind / around the tray icon glyph, rendering the unified halo per the Brand Identity spec. SVG-filter fallback substitutes when WebGPU is unavailable in the tray context, honoring the visual equivalence criteria from design-system Surface: desktop-native (blur radius envelope, LCH fidelity ≥95%, opacity envelope).

title: Primary screens

body: - **Tray icon** — always-visible status glyph; its Halo State Pulse unified-badge layer (encoding aggregated service health and ingest volume) is deferred to the next version — see §Signature placement.
- **Tray menu** — flat hierarchy menu triggered by right-click on the tray icon. Actions: open / focus main window, generate snapshot, toggle MCP server (when feature is built), open settings, quit.

- **Notifications (OS-native)** — toasts fired on snapshot generation completion, MCP server state changes, updater state transitions, and the window-close-to-tray signpost (P-063; fires on every close-to-tray while `notifications_enabled` is true).

title: Wireframe — Tray icon

body:
```
   [  ★  ]   <- single monochrome SVG glyph (aperture / constellation star)
   ══════    <- unified halo (WebGPU canvas or SVG-filter fallback)
              composited around the glyph, pulsing at throughput Hz,
              hue-shifting per error rate (color-primary ↔ color-accent)
```

**Notes:** The tray icon SVG itself is static (no animation in the SVG); all motion and colour encoding live in the secondary Halo State Pulse layer (WebGPU canvas or SVG filter). This separation lets the OS render the glyph at its native size and position while the halo is a semi-transparent composited layer. On macOS, the glyph uses the template-image flag (the OS auto-tints the SVG fill with the current menu-bar color scheme). On Windows and Linux, the same SVG is rendered with the system status-bar tint.

title: Wireframe — Tray menu (right-click context)

body:
```
Open andromeda-pulse                        <- primary action (focuses compact widget)
──────────────────────────────────────────
Ingest: 2.4k/s | Error: 1.2% | 8m used     <- read-only summary line (font-label, color-text-tertiary)
──────────────────────────────────────────
Generate Snapshot                           <- action (invokes snapshot.generate TauRPC)
[✓] Toggle MCP Server                      <- checkbox toggle (visible when mcp-server feature built)
Open Settings                               <- action (focuses Settings panel in app)
──────────────────────────────────────────
Quit                                        <- action (terminates the process)
```

**Notes:** Menu items are OS-native (system font, system colors, standard button ordering). Dividers are OS-native separators. The summary line is read-only (no click handler); it updates live as telemetry flows in (via TauRPC `health` / `ready` polling on a short interval, or via IPC event subscription on `pulse://stream/spans`).

title: Component — Tray icon (desktop-native specific)

body: **Design:**
- Single monochrome SVG glyph (aperture or constellation-star motif). Platform size conventions are honored automatically by the OS tray API.
- Color on macOS: template-image flag set, OS auto-tints to menu-bar color (typically white on dark, black on light).
- Color on Windows / Linux: SVG fill defaults to `color-text-primary`; system tint is applied where the platform's tray protocol supports it.
**SVG construction:**
- ViewBox sized for crisp rendering at small platform sizes.

- Simple line-based design (no complex fills, all strokes) for clarity at small sizes:
  - Outer circle (stroke 1px).
  - Inner star or aperture cross (4–6 strokes forming a simple glyph).
  - No gradients, no shadows, no embellishment.

**Halo State Pulse (secondary layer) — DEFERRED to the next version (see §Signature placement above); the deferred spec, preserved as-worded incl. its error-rate hue driver (this layer was never reconciled to the severity driver and defers as specified):**

- **Option A (WebGPU, preferred):** a separate transparent, click-through, always-on-top window hosting a small `<canvas>` element rendering the Halo State Pulse via the same WebGPU shader used on desktop-webview. Pulsing frequency, blur radius envelope, LCH hue shift, and opacity envelope all per the Brand Identity signature spec. Positioned to overlap the tray icon glyph (platform-specific positioning via Tauri 2 window APIs).

- **Option B (SVG-filter fallback):** inline SVG with CSS `filter: blur(...)` and CSS animations matching the WebGPU output. Hue shift via `<feColorMatrix>` interpolating between `color-primary` and `color-accent` per error rate. Visual equivalence ≥95% per design-system Surface: desktop-native criteria.
**State variants:**
- **Healthy (low error rate):** halo glows `color-primary`, pulsing smoothly at throughput frequency.
- **Degraded:** halo shifts toward an intermediate LCH hue, pulsing rate increases with error magnitude.
- **Unhealthy (high error rate):** halo glows `color-accent`, pulsing at the maximum clamped frequency — urgent visual signal without visual noise.
- **Silent (zero throughput):** halo dims to the low end of the opacity envelope, pulsing rate drops to the minimum (a faint, ambient signal).
**Reduced motion (`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`):** halo becomes a static glow (no pulsing animation), but hue still updates per error rate.

title: Component — Tray menu (OS-native)

body: **Structure:**
- Flat hierarchy, no nested submenus.
- Top item: "Open andromeda-pulse" or "Focus window" — single action, targets the compact widget.
- Divider.
- Summary line (read-only): `font-label`, `color-text-tertiary`. Updates live (suggested polling interval 1–2 seconds).
- Divider.
- Action items: "Generate Snapshot", "[✓] Toggle MCP Server" (when feature built), "Open Settings".
- Divider.
- Bottom item: "Quit" — terminates the entire process.
**Implementation details:**
- Built via Tauri 2 `tauri::menu::Menu` builder (native OS menu API per platform).
- Menu item selection fires Tauri IPC commands (e.g., `snapshot.generate`, `mcp.start` / `mcp.stop`).
- Summary line is a menu item with no click handler (read-only label on macOS / Windows, dimmed text on Linux).
- Keyboard navigation: arrow keys cycle through items, Return / Space selects, Escape closes the menu.
**Tone (menu labels):**
- Action labels use the observational, contemplative voice (matching brand personality).
- "Generate Snapshot" — not "Export Data" or "Save Report".
- "Toggle MCP Server" — not "Enable AI Integration" or "Start LLM Mode".
- "Open Settings" — not "Preferences" or "Config".

title: Component — Notifications (OS-native)

body: **Trigger events:**
1. Snapshot generation completion (via `snapshot.generate` TauRPC command).
2. MCP server status change (start / stop, when feature is built).
3. Update available (Tauri updater plugin fires the notification when a new release is detected).

4. Window-close to tray (the predictable-close signpost): fires on EVERY close that sends the app to the tray — the compact-widget ✕; the dashboard ✕ merely collapses to the widget and never signposts — gated on `notifications_enabled` alone, with no once-per-process latch (measured at HEAD: `should_show_close_signpost`, `pulse-app/src/window.rs`; the P-063 intent F3 wording as corrected by P-066). A clear "still running in the tray — right-click the tray icon to quit" indication so close→hide-to-tray is predictable.
**Notification format:**
- Title: terse (1–2 words). Examples: "Snapshot ready", "MCP Server started", "Update available".
- Body: 2 lines max, descriptive but compact. Examples: "2.5k tokens, 42 spans", "Ready to accept Claude Code connections".
- Icon: app icon at the OS-conventional notification size.
- Action button (when OS supports): "View" (opens snapshot viewer in app) or "Copy to Clipboard" (direct action without opening app).
**Implementation:**
- Via Tauri 2 `tauri-plugin-notification` (native Notification Center on macOS, Action Center on Windows, freedesktop notifications on Linux).
- User opt-out: `notifications_enabled` boolean in `~/.andromeda-pulse/config.toml` (default true). When disabled, snapshot generation and updater still complete but suppress the toast.
**Reduced motion:** notification emergence is instant (no fade-in animation per the `0.2` expression level).

title: Component — File picker (snapshot export, when invoked from native)

data.head: ### Component — File picker (snapshot export, when invoked from native)

body: **Trigger:** TBD — may be triggered by "View Snapshot" action in the app or via the tray menu.
**Implementation:**
- Native OS file picker dialog (`NSOpenPanel` on macOS, `IFileDialog` on Windows, `zenity` on Linux).
- Never a custom file browser inside the app UI.
- Default directory: `~/.andromeda-pulse/snapshots/`.
- File filter: markdown (`.md`) or plaintext (`.txt`).

title: IA notes

body: **Navigation model (tray surface only):**
- Single entry point: tray icon click (left-click) focuses / restores the compact widget; right-click opens the menu.

- Menu actions are limited to "open app", "generate snapshot", "toggle MCP", "open settings", "quit". Deep navigation into app views (Traces, Metrics, etc.) happens inside the app window, not via the tray menu.
**Keyboard shortcuts (tray level):**
- Tray menu: arrow keys navigate, Return selects, Escape closes. No global hotkeys at the tray level (e.g., `Ctrl+Shift+P` does NOT toggle tray menu visibility).
**Cross-surface coordination:**

- Tray icon Halo State Pulse and compact widget Halo State Pulse were specified to be fed by the same real-time data stream (`pulse://stream/spans` broadcast channel), rendering the unified halo at the same frequency and hue — a deferred-layer consistency requirement that ships WITH the layer (both halves deferred to the next version).

- Full dashboard Traces view was specified to render per-service halos (separate from the tray's unified halo) with all three surfaces sharing one Halo State Pulse shader; the WHOLE layer is deferred to the next version (webview half measured non-rendering 2026-08-21 — see §Component; the tray's own layer, never probed, defers on its own ground — see §Signature placement).
**Platform-specific notes:**
**macOS:**
- Tray icon uses the `NSStatusItem` API; the template-image flag makes the SVG scale and tint automatically.
- Menu uses `NSMenu` + `NSMenuItem`; standard platform look-and-feel.
- Button ordering (when a confirmation dialog appears): Cancel left, Confirm right.
- Notification Center integration via `NSUserNotification` / `UNNotificationCenter`.
- Cmd+Q to quit is respected by Tauri 2 by default.
**Windows:**
- Tray icon uses the `NotifyIcon` API; high-DPI support required (125%, 150%, 200% via `devicePixelRatio` scaling or multi-resolution SVG).
- Menu uses `ContextMenuStrip`; system look-and-feel.
- Button ordering (when a confirmation dialog appears): Confirm left, Cancel right.
- Action Center integration via Windows Toast.
**Linux:**
- Tray icon uses AppIndicator or StatusNotifier protocol (Tauri 2 abstracts both).
- Menu uses GTK+ menu integration; respects system theme (light / dark adaptation).
- Button ordering (when a confirmation dialog appears): standard Linux convention.
- Notification support via freedesktop notifications (`libnotify`).
- XDG desktop integration for autostart (TBD by downstream if Settings includes a "Launch on startup" toggle).
- Support both X11 and Wayland tray protocols (Tauri 2 handles fallback automatically).

title: 2026-05-02 — Initial layout templates generated by `/andromeda-design` Phase 8
body:
## 2026-05-02 — Initial layout templates generated by `/andromeda-design` Phase 8
**Section:** whole document (foundational). Surfaces covered: desktop-webview (compact widget + full dashboard) and desktop-native (tray icon + menu).
**Change:** one-shot generation establishing the body's per-surface layout truth:
- Compact widget — fixed quarter-screen glance surface: frameless titlebar, snap-to-edge, always-on-top, Halo canvas hero, read-only footer; Esc → tray; settings toggle expands to the full dashboard; no CSS media-query breakpoints (min-readable on a 13-inch laptop).
- Full dashboard — resizable, custom titlebar, nav "either tabs OR sidebar" (neither prescribed) over Traces / Metrics / Logs / Snapshots / Settings, per-service Halo on the constellation map hero; no hard breakpoints, nav may collapse tabs → hamburger at narrow widths.
- Tray — monochrome SVG glyph + unified Halo layer (WebGPU canvas or SVG-filter fallback) + flat right-click action menu, OS-native per platform conventions.
- Cross-surface IA — glance / exploration / ambient status; consistent Halo shader logic; shared Tauri 2 broadcast data feeds; same frameless titlebar on both webview surfaces.
- Signature — unified Halo on the compact-widget aggregated service-count badge (bottom-right of the canvas); per-service Halo dots on the constellation map; unified Halo around the tray glyph; data-driven (throughput → pulse frequency, error rate → LCH hue), not decorative.
- Motion — Investigation Capture Collapse on "Investigate"; continuous Halo "breathing" on all three surfaces (exempt from the chrome budget, separate WebGPU canvas layer); Settings-modal open/close over `duration-standard` within the `0.35` webview budget; instant OS-native tray-menu emergence per the `0.2` desktop-native expression level.
- Scope — desktop only (Windows / macOS / Linux); no mobile or touch surface.
- Deferred — snapshot-markdown viewer layout (modal vs. full-page) to the implementation route (snapshots via TauRPC `snapshot.generate`); deep-link / URL-hash structure, while committing to routable views (`/traces`, `/metrics`, `/logs`, `/snapshots`, `/settings`) + keyboard shortcuts.
**Why:** initial generation by `/andromeda-design` Phase 8. Build-ownership boundaries it set: custom titlebar drag region + window-control buttons → route specialist (design gives layout + token references; implementation owns the Tauri 2 IPC minimize / maximize / close); Halo State Pulse WebGPU canvas + WGSL shader → route + obs specialist (canvas init, shaders, data-feed subscription, reduced-motion degradation); TauRPC commands (`snapshot.generate`, `health` polling for the tray summary line, Settings submits, Investigate) → wired by the route specialist, logic in `ui-bridge`; DuckDB → TauRPC → React for constellation positions, `traces.query`, `metrics.query`, `logs.query` → `viz` owns the query schema, route specialist owns component integration.
**Ref:** NOT DERIVED

title: 2026-05-02 — Initial layout templates generated by `/andromeda-design` Phase 8
body:
## 2026-05-02 — Initial layout templates generated by `/andromeda-design` Phase 8

- **Section:** whole document (foundational). Surfaces covered: desktop-webview
  (compact widget + full dashboard) and desktop-native (tray icon + menu).
- **Change:** one-shot Phase 8 generation (no iteration loop) that established
  the per-surface layout truth now in the body:
  - **Key layout choices** — compact widget as a fixed quarter-screen glance
    surface (frameless titlebar, snap-to-edge, always-on-top, Halo canvas hero,
    read-only footer; Esc → tray; settings toggle expands to the full
    dashboard); full dashboard as a resizable window (custom titlebar for
    continuity, tabs-or-sidebar nav over Traces / Metrics / Logs / Snapshots /
    Settings, per-service Halo on the constellation map hero); tray icon as a
    monochrome SVG glyph with a unified Halo layer (WebGPU canvas or SVG-filter
    fallback) plus a flat right-click action menu.
  - **Cross-surface IA** — three-surface coherence (glance / exploration /
    ambient status) with consistent Halo shader logic and shared Tauri 2
    broadcast data feeds; the same frameless titlebar across both webview
    surfaces; an OS-native tray + menu respecting platform conventions.
  - **Signature placement** — unified Halo on the compact-widget aggregated
    service-count badge (bottom-right of the canvas); per-service Halo dots on
    the full-dashboard constellation map; unified Halo composited around the
    tray glyph; all data-driven (throughput → pulse frequency, error rate →
    LCH hue), not decorative.
  - **Motion triggers** — Investigation Capture Collapse on the full-dashboard
    "Investigate" action; continuous data-driven Halo "breathing" on all three
    surfaces (exempt from the chrome budget, separate WebGPU canvas layer);
    Settings-modal panel transitions over `duration-standard`; OS-native
    (instant) tray-menu emergence per the `0.2` desktop-native expression level.
- **Why:** initial generation by `/andromeda-design` Phase 8.
- **Body now:** these decisions ARE the current body — the desktop-webview and
  desktop-native surface sections (Primary screens, Wireframes, Components, IA
  notes). Four current-truth items that lived ONLY in the Decisions Log were
  folded into the body during v3 normalization:
  - **Responsive posture (webview)** → desktop-webview IA notes "Responsive
    behavior" — compact widget fixed quarter-screen with no CSS media-query
    breakpoints (min-readable on a 13-inch laptop); full dashboard resizable
    with no hard breakpoints, nav may collapse tabs → hamburger at narrow
    widths, both models valid.
  - **Snapshot detail-viewer deferral** → desktop-webview Primary screens
    (Snapshots view) — the snapshot-markdown viewer layout (modal vs.
    full-page) is deferred to the implementation route; snapshots are generated
    via the TauRPC `snapshot.generate` command.
  - **Desktop-only scope** → top-of-file scope note — Windows / macOS / Linux
    only; no mobile or touch surface; the tray follows platform conventions
    (no mobile gestures).
  - **Settings-modal panel-transition motion** → desktop-webview Settings modal
    component "Motion" — open / close eases over `duration-standard`, within the
    `0.35` webview budget.
- **Deferrals recorded (already body current-truth, no fold needed):** full
  dashboard navigation model committed to "either tabs OR sidebar" without
  prescribing which (body: Primary navigation component); deep-link / URL-hash
  route structure deferred downstream while committing to routable views
  (`/traces`, `/metrics`, `/logs`, `/snapshots`, `/settings`) + keyboard
  shortcuts (body: IA notes Deep-link convention + Keyboard shortcuts).
- **Handoff / ownership notes (recorded; build-ownership boundaries, not
  body-layout truth):**
  - **Custom titlebar** — drag region + window-control buttons owned by the
    route specialist (React + Tailwind in the webview); design provides layout
    structure + token references, implementation owns the exact Tauri 2 IPC
    calls (minimize / maximize / close).
  - **Halo State Pulse** — WebGPU canvas + WGSL shader for all three surfaces,
    SVG-filter fallback for the tray-icon halo when WebGPU is unavailable; the
    route + obs implementation specialist owns canvas init, shader authoring,
    data-feed subscription, and reduced-motion degradation.
  - **TauRPC command surface (IPC bridge)** — Settings-modal submits, Investigate
    clicks, and snapshot generation all trigger TauRPC commands (e.g.
    `snapshot.generate`, `health` polling for the tray summary line); the route
    specialist wires them and the `ui-bridge` crate (Tauri side) implements the
    logic.
  - **DuckDB query layer** — constellation positions (service topology),
    `traces.query`, `metrics.query`, and `logs.query` flow DuckDB → TauRPC →
    webview React components; the viz crate owns the query schema, the route
    specialist owns component integration.
  (Layout/token substance for each lives in the body; these record the original
  log's build-ownership boundaries.)
- **Marker:** none (initial generation). By: `/andromeda-design` Phase 8.

_Generated by `/andromeda-tests`. This file is the single source of truth
for all test strategy + harness contracts + quality gates. Read by
downstream skills (obs / a11y / route / setup-project per D26 cross-
cutting), tests-pass per-phase, combine + `/implement` (via phase loop)._

_Do not edit during phase loop runs (tests-pass / combine / `/implement`).
Manual edits between runs are fine._

_**Agent-driven invariant:** every test layer described in this plan must
be runnable end-to-end by an agent reading exit codes and structured
output. No human-in-the-loop checkpoints, no manual verification, no
visual regression with human review. If a surface cannot be agent-driven,
it is flagged "untestable" in test-scope.md Section 1 and handled via

title: 1. Test Scope Summary

body: **Test tier:** Standard (1)

**Justification:** Andromeda Pulse is a cross-platform desktop application (Windows/macOS/Linux via Tauri 2) with two primary surfaces (desktop-webview: React + WebGPU dashboard; desktop-native: tray icon + menu) and persistent in-memory data (DuckDB ring buffer holding 5–10 min of OTLP telemetry). The coverage scope spans 19 entities (8 library crates + ingest/buffer/viz layers + OTLP anti-pattern enforcement + Tauri capability gating + plugin sandbox + MCP sidecar), with 7 critical user-facing flows (ingest + visualize, generate curated snapshots, query via MCP, plugin lifecycle, widget ↔ dashboard toggle, real-time push, workspace detection). Security tier is Minimal (loopback-only binding, no persistent user accounts, no encrypted data at rest), but the architecture explicitly rejects 28+ attack vectors and enforces high-quality rejection logic (path canonicalization, SQL parameter binding, post-protobuf invariant checks, capability-scoped WASM sandbox, Minisign signature verification). Creator's risk tolerance signals "portfolio-worthy GPU-accelerated visualization" and "approach Jaeger UI quality", implying above-MVP quality bar. The agent-driven development style requires every test layer to be machine-parseable and runnable end-to-end with no human in the loop.
**Coverage scope (testable entities):**
| Entity | Source | Testability | Reason if Not Fully Testable |

| **P5: Widget compact mode ↔ dashboard expansion ↔ tray icon visibility toggle** | desktop-webview (React widget + dashboard layouts) + desktop-native (tray icon + menu) + Tauri window management + TauRPC state sync | Agent: runs the 17-stage `cargo xtask webview-drive` leg (six window-mechanics stages — `traces-scroll` · `connection-status` · `findings-window` · `report-window` · `dashboard-toggle` · `dashboard-close` — added at `2026-08-23-headful-leg-extension`) and asserts each stage as two independent halves (obs record / DOM) — `viz.query.traces` `row_count > 0` · `interpretation.incident.created` `created = true` · `investigate.run_action.request` `status = "success"` after a real press of `button[aria-label="Investigate"]` · the shared `EmptyState` hint on `/metrics` + `/logs` · and the terminal widget-close obs half — the `ui.layout.transition {layout_mode_from: compact-widget, layout_mode_to: hidden}` record AND the `tray.signpost.shown` record with `window_label == "compact-widget"`, both required — after a real press of `button[aria-label="Close to tray"]` (live on the Windows dev host since 2026-08-23; a code-driven RED arm, `--no-inject --expect-absent <STAGE>`, confirms the telemetry-dependent stages redden while `investigate` stays green) → invokes TauRPC `health` to confirm window state in metadata (optional, may not be present) → window resize, tray-icon repaint and notification delivery remain IPC-surrogate only, deferred to the headful suite. | Creator Brief: "Quarter-screen widget mode — default surface; Click to expand — opens full dashboard window; widget remains mounted (returns to compact mode on close); Tray icon (secondary) — traffic-light status; click cycles widget visibility" |

| **P6: Real-time push of spans/metrics/logs via Tauri IPC Channel** | buffer (DuckDB) + TauRPC IPC Channels (`pulse://stream/spans`, `pulse://stream/metrics`, `pulse://stream/logs`) + desktop-webview (listener) + Real-time push contract (Arrow IPC payloads) | Agent: subscribes to channel `pulse://stream/spans` via Tauri test client → sends gRPC trace to `:4317` → awaits Channel event (timeout 5s) → receives binary Arrow IPC payload → decodes schema (column names: trace_id, span_name, duration_ms, etc.) → asserts row count > 0 and schema matches contract. | Architecture Standard Contracts: "Real-time push contract (Tauri IPC channels) — live span/metric/log streams using Tauri 2 IPC `Channel` API with binary Arrow IPC payloads; event names are `pulse://stream/spans`, `pulse://stream/metrics`, `pulse://stream/logs`" |

| **P7: Workspace detection (host project context correlation)** | workspace-detector module + TauRPC `workspace.detect` / `workspace.list` | Agent: (test harness runs inside repo with `.andromeda/` marker or typical project structure) → invokes TauRPC `workspace.detect` → asserts response.workspace contains detected project name / root path / VCS info (git, cargo.toml, etc.) → (out-of-repo test scenarios untestable in standard agent-driven harness; assume repo structure is present). | Creator Brief: "Snapshot path detection — if cwd has `.andromeda/` → `.andromeda/pulse/{timestamp}.md`; else → `~/.cache/andromeda-pulse/snapshots/{timestamp}.md`"; Architecture Workspace: "workspace-detector — detection of host project context for telemetry correlation" |
**Coverage triggers:**
| Trigger Type | Source | Required Test Type |

| **security-vector-coverage: OTLP loopback-only binding** | Security Plan Vector 1: "OTLP receivers bound to 127.0.0.1 only" | Negative test: Attempt env var override `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_GRPC_BIND=0.0.0.0:4317` → assert canonicalization + confinement rejects; assert live receiver only accepts loopback source (connect from non-loopback IP must fail at TCP level or IPC auth). |

| **security-vector-coverage: DuckDB SQL injection prevention** | Security Plan Vector 2, Anti-Pattern: "NEVER format user input directly into SQL … ALWAYS use `Connection::prepare` with `?` placeholders and parameter binding" | Negative test: `snapshot.generate` with service_filter containing SQL injection payload (e.g., `"my-service'; DROP TABLE spans; --"`) → assert query executes safely (payload treated as literal string, no table dropped); assert output schema unchanged. |

| **security-vector-coverage: OTLP post-prost invariant checks** | Security Plan Anti-Pattern: "NEVER skip post-`prost`-decode invariant checks on OTLP payloads … `span_id` (8 bytes), `trace_id` (16 bytes), attribute key sizes, etc. must be checked" | Negative test: Send gRPC span with malformed span_id (< 8 bytes) or trace_id (> 16 bytes) → assert ingest rejects and logs error (rows not inserted); assert no panic in buffer layer. |

| **security-vector-coverage: Tauri IPC capability gating** | Security Plan Vector 2: "Tauri 2 capability gating `pulse:default`"; Anti-Pattern: "NEVER add TauRPC procedure without matching capability entry" | Negative test: Attempt to invoke undeclared procedure (not in `pulse:default` capability list) → assert TauRPC rejects with AppError; positive test: call declared procedure (`app_info`, `health`, `traces.query`, etc.) → assert success. Xtask drift check enforces crate/capability sync. |

| **security-vector-coverage: Path canonicalization + confinement** | Security Plan Vector 5: "Canonicalize and confine the **product-binary** `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*_PATH` / `*_DIR` env vars"; Anti-Pattern: "NEVER read a product-binary path env var without `Path::canonicalize()` + confinement assertion" — harness/xtask-only tool-locator vars (`ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MSEDGEDRIVER_PATH`) are carved out and guarded by trim + `is_file()` + clean skip instead | Negative test: Set `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_PLUGIN_DIR=~/.andromeda-pulse/plugins/../../../` (escape attempt) → assert canonicalization resolves and confinement blocks traversal; assert only loads plugins from resolved safe dir. Negative test: symlink chain in plugin dir → assert resolved canonically; TOCTOU race attempt → assert atomic. **L4 arm (chunk `2026-08-26-l4-runtime-security-residuals`):** the plugin-dir recipe above is unchanged, but for `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MODEL_PATH` / `_LLAMA_CUDA_BIN_PATH` / `_LLAMA_CPU_BIN_PATH` the confinement assertion requires `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_ALLOW_ROOT` to be SET (unset ⇒ structural-hardening arm only; set-but-unresolvable ⇒ every candidate rejected, fail-closed). Landed coverage: `pulse-app/tests/unit_llamacli_inference.rs` (9 path-guard + 6 prompt-bound + 4 allow-root-resolution branches, mutation-checked). |

| **security-vector-coverage: DefaultBodyLimit on OTLP HTTP** | Security Plan Anti-Pattern: "NEVER trust `Content-Length` or trailers as substitute for `DefaultBodyLimit` on OTLP HTTP `:4318`" | Negative test: POST oversized payload (> 8 MB, size limit not specified in arch, assume 8 MB default) to `:4318 /v1/traces` → assert HTTP 413 Payload Too Large or axum rejection; assert no panic or unbounded memory allocation. |

| **security-vector-coverage: Cranelift-only WASM** | Security Plan Anti-Pattern: "NEVER use non-Cranelift `wasmtime` feature flag on x86_64" | Build-time test: Assert `wasmtime` Cargo.lock resolved with Cranelift feature enabled (or only available backend); negative test: Attempt build with alternate backend → build fails or CI reject (enforced by the ci.yml supply-chain `run:` step per §9, landed chunk `2026-08-29-advisory-backlog`; no xtask covers this assertion). |

| **security-vector-coverage: MCP feature + runtime gating** | Security Plan Vector 4: "gated by compile-time `--features mcp-server` AND runtime `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED=true`" | Negative test: (1) attempt to spawn MCP sidecar without feature flag compile → build fails; (2) runtime env var unset, attempt to spawn → assert sidecar not spawned (cannot find binary or refused at startup). Positive test: both gates enabled → sidecar spawns and accepts JSON-RPC 2.0. Both gates are the stdio sidecar's: since chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process the same nine tools also answer through the console engine's door under neither gate, admitted by the door's owner check (the peer's kernel-read account equal to the engine's own; any other account, root included, closed with no byte) with the one write behind `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DOOR_RESOLVE`; that path's negative tests are the door's — another account refused at three layers and, since chunk 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door, another account receiving no byte through the stdio relay `andromeda-pulse-engine door` (exit 1 with the fixed line; both on the runner only), the write refused with `-32001` when the switch is `off` or rejected, also through the relay — per Surfaces under test, the door row. |

| **security-vector-coverage: Minisign updater signature verification** | Security Plan Vector 6: "Minisign Ed25519 signature verification is mandatory and cannot be disabled" | Positive test: Mock latest.json with valid Minisign signature → updater accepts. Negative test: Invalid signature (flipped bit in sig) → updater rejects update (no update downloaded). Negative test: Attempt to bypass verification via config → assert Tauri enforces (cannot override). |

| **security-vector-coverage: No self-OTLP dialing** (by-construction-satisfied) | Creator Brief Anti-Pattern: "Any future `ANDROMEDA_OBSERVER_URL`-shaped variable must explicitly distinguish 'outbound observer' (we *are* the observer — do not dial) from 'inbound receivers'" | No test generated: the config surface does not exist (no OTel SDK in self-runtime → no exporter → no `ANDROMEDA_OBSERVER_URL`-shaped variable), so self-dialing is impossible by construction (per obs-plan Phase 3.5 pivot). Deprecation history in test-plan-amendments.md. |

| **compliance-test: OTLP protocol compliance (gRPC)** | Architecture Stack: "tonic 0.14.x … gRPC server for OTLP/gRPC receiver on `:4317` with protobuf codegen"; "per opentelemetry-proto" | Contract test: Valid OTLP gRPC TraceService.Export RPC (per OpenTelemetry spec v1.x) → server responds with status OK and exports span to buffer. Valid MetricsService.Export and LogsService.Export RPCs similarly. Malformed requests (missing required fields) → server responds with gRPC error code (INVALID_ARGUMENT or UNIMPLEMENTED). |

| **compliance-test: OTLP protocol compliance (HTTP)** | Architecture Stack: "axum 0.8.x … HTTP server for OTLP/HTTP receiver on `:4318` supporting protobuf (JSON optional, not implemented)"; "per OpenTelemetry spec" | Contract test: Valid OTLP HTTP POST `/v1/traces` with protobuf body → 200 OK, export to buffer. Valid JSON body similarly. Unsupported media type (Content-Type: text/plain) → 415 Unsupported Media Type or server attempts to parse (spec permissive). Invalid protobuf wire format → server responds with error (no panic). |

| **performance-budget: WebGPU canvas throughput** | Creator Brief Risk Tolerance: "Hand-built Canvas falls over at 10k+ spans/sec. Pulse v2 uses WebGPU … Smooth animation; no jank at high cardinality"; "handles 10k+ spans/sec" (target throughput baseline) | Performance test (agent-driven): Inject 10,000 spans/sec to `:4317` gRPC for 10 seconds (100k total) → assert buffer ingests all without dropping; assert buffer memory usage stays within 5–10 min ring buffer window (no unbounded growth). Frame-budget validation, agent-driven: `cargo xtask perf:frame-sample` (chunk 2026-09-30-perf-budget-gate-reads-real-samples) grades `metric.webgpu.frame_duration_ms` p99 ≤ 33 ms on a Windows GPU dev host with the frame arm required (exit 0 PASS · 1 FAIL — 0 samples once healthy, or p99 > 33 ms · 2 INCONCLUSIVE; measured p99 2.6 ms, n = 7971). Not CI-wired: the hosted Windows runner exposed no WebGPU adapter (`ci#36723465727`), so on CI the unrequired frame arm prints `frame: cannot-evaluate: 0 samples, {cause}` with the cause derived from the log's `ui.webgpu.adapter` records — never PASS. Since chunk 2026-10-10-no-gate-stands-while-reading-nothing that line is the `lint-test` job's `perf:budget` step's alone (as measured on `ci#38042949735`: `… no adapter record in this log` beside `perf-budget: PASS`, the frame arm not required there): `cargo xtask ci-gates` grades no perf arm, so the boot job prints no perf-budget `frame:` line on any run, whether or not its smoke and `Boot series (equal source)` steps pass; since chunk 2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine its `Console engine cycle` step grades the memory arm as required through `check:engine-log` and prints one line `engine-log: budget frame and snapshot not graded (a console engine has no producer for either)`. Dated readings of the line that job printed before that chunk: `no WebGPU adapter (no_navigator_gpu)` on a run whose smoke read the app past its adapter request (as measured on one run, `ci#37979648967`: 2 adapter records, both `no_navigator_gpu`), and `no adapter record in this log` on a run whose smoke stopped the app before that request (`ci#36765040464`; obs-plan §10 frame row). The boot log still holds its `ui.webgpu.adapter` records on a run that reaches the settle verdict (not re-read on `ci#38042949735`). |

| **performance-budget: Snapshot token budget enforcement** | Creator Brief: "Token budget (10k / 25k / 50k preset)"; must-work scenario: "generates curated snapshot" with token limits | Performance test: Generate snapshot from 5000+ spans with token_budget=25000 → assert response.token_count <= 25000 (strict); assert snapshot quality (anomaly markers present, critical path extracted, not raw OTLP dump). Stress test: token_budget=10000 with 10k span backlog → assert snapshot still fits (aggressive culling expected). |

| **chaos-test: Buffer overflow / retention window enforcement** | Architecture: "DuckDB 1.5.x … in-memory ring buffer (5–10 min)" | Chaos test: Inject spans continuously at 10k/sec for 15 min (exceeds 10 min window) → assert oldest spans are evicted; assert buffer memory stays bounded within ring buffer max; assert no crash or corruption. Chaos test: Kill ingest channel mid-stream (close broadcast channel) → assert buffer gracefully pauses; assert next ingest reconnects and resumes. |

| **cross-surface-coordination: TauRPC ↔ IPC Channels consistency** | Architecture Standard Contracts: IPC procedures (`traces.query`) return paginated results; Channels (`pulse://stream/spans`) emit realtime Arrow batches | Coordination test: Subscribe to `pulse://stream/spans` channel → send gRPC trace → receive channel event → call `traces.query` TauRPC → assert returned row set includes span from channel event (no desync). |

| **cross-surface-coordination: Snapshot generation + Notification emit** | Creator Brief: "Notification — `Snapshot ready ({N} tokens). Paste in {AI tool} to investigate.`" | Coordination test: Invoke `snapshot.generate` TauRPC → await `pulse://stream/snapshot-progress` channel events (progress updates) → final event is completion → assert notification is emitted (captured via platform notification spy or IPC channel `pulse://stream/events`); assert notification text includes token count. |

| **multi-platform-compat: Windows WebView2 vs macOS WKWebView vs Linux GTK WebKit** | Architecture Stack: "WebView2 (Windows) and WKWebView (macOS/Linux)"; Design System Surfaces: "desktop-webview (React 19 + Tailwind CSS v4 webview) — Windows/macOS/Linux WebView2/WKWebView" | Platform compat test (matrix over Windows/macOS/Linux CI runners — no such matrix exists: since chunk 2026-10-09-ci-on-linux-alone the `ci` workflow runs on `ubuntu-22.04` alone, so the Windows and macOS arms of this trigger have no CI witness; they leave with the route entry `Other operating systems retired from the code`, P-113): Verify `tauri-driver` harness can boot app on each platform; verify IPC works consistently; verify WebGPU canvas is available (supported on Windows 11+, macOS 13+, Linux with GPU driver); verify tray icon renders (platform-specific implementation); verify notifications dispatch via native Notification Center / Action Center / freedesktop. Negative test: Older Windows 10 or unsupported Linux (no GPU) → graceful degradation or clear error message. |

| **load-test: OTLP receiver saturation (HTTP vs gRPC trade-off)** | Architecture: Two separate receiver ports (`:4317` gRPC, `:4318` HTTP) for protocol choice | Load test: Drive both receivers simultaneously; gRPC path with 100 concurrent clients each sending 1 span/sec (100 span/sec aggregate); HTTP path with 50 clients (50 span/sec); assert no cross-protocol interference; assert buffer ingests all (150 total/sec). Measure latency p50/p99 for span export RPC (must stay < 100ms for interactive UI). |

| **contract-test-against-OTLP-sandbox: OpenTelemetry protobuf evolution** | Standard Contracts: "TraceService, MetricsService, LogsService on `:4317` per opentelemetry-proto"; "POST /v1/traces, /v1/metrics, /v1/logs on `:4318` per OpenTelemetry spec" | Contract test: Use OpenTelemetry reference SDK (e.g., `opentelemetry-rust` crate) to generate valid spans/metrics/logs and send to app receivers; assert app accepts and buffers all (roundtrip test: generate → send → query back → assert match). Test with multiple protobuf versions (v1.0, v1.1, v1.2 if applicable) to ensure forward/backward compat. |

| **agent-driven-discipline: No manual verification checkpoints** | Development Style: "agent-driven. … deterministic harness invocations, machine-parseable outputs, schema-stable contracts" | Discipline trigger: Every test must exit with deterministic signal (exit code 0/non-zero, structured stdout/JSON, log line match) readable by CI agent without human review. No "visual inspection of canvas", no "did you see the blue glow?", no "try it manually first". WebGPU canvas rendering is out of E2E agent scope (pixel inspection not required); assert IPC contract and WebGPU compile success. Snapshot generation verified via token count and marker presence, not manual reading. Widget visibility toggle verified via IPC state, not screenshot comparison. |

| **agent-driven-discipline: Self-bootstrapping test data (no pre-baked DB)** | Test Harness Specification: "Test data strategy: self-bootstrapping fixture mechanism — seed via migrations + factories / fixture files / property-based generators; no developer-seeded DB allowed" | Discipline trigger: Every integration/E2E test must generate fixture data at runtime via OTLP ingest or Rust builders; no `.sql` scripts or pre-baked SQLite snapshots. Rationale: ensures repeatability, test isolation, and verifies ingest path actually works. Fixture data lifecycle is part of test harness, not manual pre-staging. |

title: Pending coverage triggers (documented gaps — not yet implemented; awaiting `/andromeda-tests` re-run)

data.head: ### Pending coverage triggers (documented gaps — not yet implemented; awaiting `/andromeda-tests` re-run)

body: These triggers are decided-and-recommended; most are not yet wired into the suite above (rows explicitly marked **LANDED** have since shipped and are retained for audit trail). Recorded here so the coverage gap is not silently lost; full decision context in test-plan-amendments.md.
| Trigger | Spec |

| `security-vector-coverage: AppError sanitization` | IPC error response must not contain stack traces, file paths, Rust struct names, or library versions; assert via grep on `agent-latest.jsonl`. (security-plan §Logging vector 2) |
| `security-vector-coverage: Plugin path basename only` | Load plugin with symlink chain → assert resolved path NOT in logs, only basename. (vector 3) |

| `security-vector-coverage: MCP response body redaction` | Call `query_traces` via MCP → assert `result_content` NOT in `agent-latest.jsonl`, only `result_type` + `result_count` metadata. This is the indirect-prompt-injection surface for MCP tool responses. (vector 4) |
| `security-vector-coverage: Path env var canonicalization log redaction` | Set `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_PLUGIN_DIR=../../etc/passwd` → assert canonicalization rejects + logs only basename. (vector 6) |

| `security-vector-coverage: Capability widening static analysis` — **LANDED, no longer pending** | Shipped as `cargo xtask capability-widening-check` (chunk #77; wired as a per-PR CI step at chunk #99) and now part of the §3 standard gate set — it parses each `pulse-app/capabilities/*.json` and asserts (a) `pulse:notification` holds only outbound emit permissions (no input handlers); (b) `pulse:tray` only outbound menu/icon (no incoming-event handlers); (c) `pulse:plugin-fs` limited to read of resolved plugin dir, no write/delete/execute, never exposed to webview JS. Fails with named permission + capability on widening detection. Row retained for audit trail; only the per-capability assertion detail remains to be re-confirmed against the xtask. |

| `living-artifact-tooling-rerun-coverage` | **RETIRED 2026-08-26 — its subject no longer exists.** The trigger required wrap-session Phase 5 to execute the Tooling command from each `.andromeda/context/{artifact}.md` METADATA at every wrap (skip-on-webview-only forbidden; the documented root cause of api-surface.md staleness). Both living-doc artifacts — `.andromeda/context/api-surface.md` and `dependency-tree.md` — were DELETED at commit `5a83771` (2026-06-28, "retire context/ markdown living-docs (superseded by code-graph tree.db)"), and no `context/` directory exists at any path today. The code-graph (`.andromeda/cache/{plane}/tree.db`, rebuilt on demand by /andromeda-phase + /andromeda-wrap-session) replaced them, and it is derived + gitignored, so it has no LIVING block to reconcile and cannot go stale in the way this trigger guarded. Retained as a row rather than deleted so the retirement is auditable; the staleness LESSON it encodes — a reconcile step that may be skipped will be, and divergence is observable only by running the tooling — survives in the code-graph refresh being unconditional at wrap Setup. |

| `harness-encoding-relay-coverage` | `scripts/agent-run.sh` / `.ps1` export `PYTHONUTF8=1` + `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` (PowerShell additionally sets `[Console]::OutputEncoding`/`InputEncoding`), but no harness leg asserts a child process actually receives UTF-8 — the relay ships verified only by parse-check + presence-of-export. Behavioural assertion pending. |

| `workspace-key-cross-process-coverage` | The app→sidecar key handoff is proven in-process (byte-equality of published vs read key, plus the absent-file fallback) and by `cargo build -p mcp-server --features mcp-server`, but no test spawns the sidecar as a subprocess against a data dir holding a published key and asserts the key-scoped query returns the app's rows. The blocker is CLEARED as of chunk 2026-08-15-corpus-key-persistence (cross-process encrypted-payload reads now succeed — a second process decrypted its predecessor's rows with 0 `decryption_failed`), so the leg is UNBLOCKED but still unimplemented. Qualifier: it presumes a host with a credential store OR a configured `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_CORPUS_PASSPHRASE` — the fallback is opt-in, not automatic. **MEASURED ONCE at smoke level** (chunk 2026-08-17-conductor-e2e-verification-closure): a real `andromeda-pulse-mcp` subprocess read the live AES-256-GCM corpus under the published `run/workspace-key` and returned the key-scoped row's `fingerprint_refs`, with the 2 persisted rows' `workspace` matching the published key byte-for-byte, 0 `corpus.read.undecryptable` and no keychain fallback — so the leg is now known-good in practice while STILL having no committed test. Chunks 2026-08-14-workspace-key-alignment (opened) + 2026-08-15-corpus-key-persistence (unblocked) + 2026-08-17-conductor-e2e-verification-closure (measured, uncommitted). |

| `mcp-incident-read-back-cross-process-coverage` | The deterministic incident read-back — MCP `retrieve_telemetry_slice.fingerprint_refs` and the Diagnostic Report's Evidence section, both non-vacuous since chunk 2026-08-17-conductor-e2e-verification-closure — is guarded ONLY by in-process `dispatch_tool` assertions in `pulse-app/tests/e2e_p3_mcp_incident_tools.rs` (whose `e2e_p3_` name is misleading: its own docstring points cross-process framing at `crates/mcp-server/tests/sidecar_subprocess.rs`). **Verified by search, not inferred:** the committed subprocess tests `tools/call` only the 4 telemetry tools (`query_traces` / `query_metrics` / `query_logs` / `generate_snapshot`); the 4 incident tools appear cross-process ONLY as `tools/list` NAME assertions (`sidecar_subprocess.rs:`), never with a content assertion. The real subprocess chain WAS proven live at that chunk's P3 smoke, but smoke evidence is not a regression guard — a future chunk needs a new test file spawning the sidecar and asserting incident-tool response CONTENT. Chunk 2026-08-17-conductor-e2e-verification-closure. **The owed content WIDENED at chunk 2026-08-27-incident-persist-vs-resolve-write-race:** `mark_incident_resolved` no longer returns `{"resolved": true}` unconditionally — a write the corpus monotonic guard DECLINES now returns an honest not-applied result — and that new response shape was covered ONLY by the in-process signature/compile path, so a revert to the always-true form would have passed every committed cross-process assertion. **NARROWED at chunk 2026-08-29-app-registry-reconciliation — the widened half is DISCHARGED, and the "ONLY as `tools/list` NAME assertions" claim above no longer holds for all four tools.** `pulse-app/tests/e2e_p3_mcp_resolve_content.rs` spawns a real `andromeda-pulse-mcp` subprocess against a shared on-disk encrypted corpus and asserts `mark_incident_resolved`'s response CONTENT in BOTH arms — the applied shape (`resolved: true` + the id it resolved) and the guard-declined shape (no success result; the error message reports the resolution was not applied, driven by seeding a row whose `updated_unix_nano` is newer than the sidecar's `now`). 2/2, and neither SKIPPED: both open the corpus with `OsKeychainBackend::new("com.andromeda.pulse")`, the same backend + service id the sidecar uses, with a clean skip only where no credential store exists. **It is FEATURE-GATED** (`cargo test --test e2e_p3_mcp_resolve_content -p pulse-app --features mcp-server`) and therefore sits OUTSIDE the default `--workspace` gate, like the other `--features mcp-server` pulse-app tests. **NARROWED again at chunk 2026-10-02-incident-events-readable-through-mcp — the ninth tool shipped WITH its cross-process content guard.** `retrieve_incident_events` (a fifth incident tool) has two committed legs: `crates/mcp-server/tests/incident_events_subprocess.rs` spawns the real sidecar against seeded rows and asserts the response CONTENT plus stderr and file-sink canary absence; `pulse-app/tests/e2e_p3_mcp_incident_events_content.rs` (`--features mcp-server`) drives the REAL producer `create_incident_from_l4_output` into the real sidecar and asserts the four-kind vocabulary with `created` first. Both clean-skip without an OS credential store (every CI runner) and both ran on the Linux dev host (`lacks [skip]` held, 16/16). **Still owed, so the row stays OPEN:** cross-process CONTENT for `retrieve_telemetry_slice.fingerprint_refs`, `retrieve_report`'s Evidence section, and `query_incident_list`. |

| `buffer-redaction-counter-unit-coverage` | The P-047 redaction counter shipped at chunk 2026-08-22-pii-scrubber-recall added three public `buffer` items — `BufferState::record_redactions(&self, n: u64)`, `BufferStateSnapshot.redactions_applied`, `BufferHeartbeat.redactions_applied` — with **no test inside the `buffer` crate**.
