| `render-posture-main-placement-coverage` | **NEW 2026-10-04-linux-launch-stays-up-on-nvidia-wayland.** `pulse_app::render_posture` is pinned at the lib level — `decide` per arm and the real `set_var` path through re-exec children in `pulse-app/tests/unit_render_posture.rs` (absent ⇒ `applied` + `1`; preset `0` ⇒ `preset_honoured`, not overwritten), the `app.boot.render.posture {posture, lever}` leaf and its emit-site capture in `pulse-app/tests/unit_observability_allowlist_render_posture.rs` — but its PRODUCTION placement in `pulse-app/src/main.rs` is not: `apply_linux_default()` must be the FIRST statement of `main()`, ahead of the tokio multi-thread runtime build (its `unsafe set_var` SAFETY rests on a single thread), and `emit_posture` must follow `observability::init` (it sits directly after `window::emit_boot_spans()`). Both were proven only by the chunk's gate-time placement probe (an `awk` over `main()` in its plan's Test Commands, re-run by that chunk's light gate alone) and its two dev-host operator legs on a real NVIDIA + Wayland display; CI's xvfb boot smoke neither reaches NVIDIA's EGL nor asserts the posture record. The same one-time-proof-for-a-gate class as `discovery-observer-wiring-coverage` / `exit-hook-main-composition-coverage`. Owed: a committed assertion over `main()`'s order (a seam or a source-order pin) that the apply call precedes every runtime / thread creation and the emit follows `observability::init` exactly once. **Narrowed 2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-closed:** a committed source-order pin over `main()` now exists — `main_calls_it_second_after_the_render_posture_step_and_before_the_runtime` in `pulse-app/tests/unit_xlib_threads.rs` reads `pulse-app/src/main.rs` and requires the first statement of `main()` to be the render-posture apply call, the second `xlib_threads::init();`, and the tokio runtime build after both (mutation-checked: the call moved below the runtime build, and moved above the render-posture step, each read red). So the apply-is-first and apply-precedes-the-runtime halves are pinned. Still owed: that `emit_posture` follows `observability::init` exactly once. **Anchor moved 2026-10-10-console-engine-entry-point:** `main()` no longer initialises the log sink itself — after its two first statements and its runtime build it calls `engine_boot::init_process` (the sink, its guard, the exit hook, the signal listener, the pid file), then `window::emit_boot_spans()` and `render_posture::emit_posture(..)` — so the still-owed pin reads: `emit_posture` follows the `engine_boot::init_process` call exactly once. The posture record stays the window's alone: `pulse-app/tests/integration_console_engine.rs` asserts the spawned console program writes no `app.boot.render.posture` record. |

| `quarantine-tracking-ps1-mirror-coverage` | **NEW 2026-10-10-no-gate-stands-while-reading-nothing.** `xtask/ci/quarantine-tracking-check.ps1` gained the absent-input arms of its `.sh` twin (a missing search dir → exit 1; a scan of zero `.rs` files → exit 1; the PASS lines counting the files scanned) with NO committed test: it was parsed by `pwsh` 7.6.6 on the dev host (0 parse errors) and never run, and no pin reads it. The `.sh` is pinned by tests that run it with `bash` over scratch roots (`empty_input_tests`, `xtask/src/main.rs`): five at that chunk, six since chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed. **Widened 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed:** the mirror gained the fifth search dir, `xtask/tests`, as the `.sh` did, again with NO committed test — parsed by `pwsh` (0 parse errors; its version not re-read) and never run; on the `.sh` side the new entry is pinned (`quarantine_check_reads_the_xtask_integration_tests`), and a missing `xtask/tests` fails the check. Owed: a pin that runs the mirror per arm, or the mirror leaves with the PowerShell scripts (the route entry `Other operating systems retired from the code`, where the gap is carried). |

| `verify-capability-matrix-verb-glue-coverage` | **NEW 2026-10-10-capability-record-re-based.** The capability record's verdict is pinned in-crate: 36 co-located pins in `xtask/src/capability_record.rs` (`mod tests`), one per arm over constructed records under `tempfile::TempDir`, plus one that reads the committed record over the committed route and asserts the clean line. The verb function `verify_capability_matrix` in `xtask/src/main.rs` has no pin: the JSON event line (target `xtask.verify_capability_matrix`), the report twin `target/capability-matrix/report.json` (`state` · `capability_count` · `claimed_count` · `retired_count` · `violation_count` · `reason` · `violations` · `generated_at`) and the process exit taken from `Verdict::exit_code`. The verb ran on one arm only, clean and exit 0 (on the dev host and in the `lint / test` job log of `ci#38049792921`); its exit 1 and exit 2 never ran through the verb, which takes no path. Owed: a pin over the twin's member set and the verb's exit per state. |

| `engine-boot-rejected-port-and-socket-census-coverage` | **NEW 2026-10-10-console-engine-entry-point.** `engine_boot::start` runs under four in-process arms (`pulse-app/tests/integration_engine_boot.rs`) and the console program under a spawned run (`pulse-app/tests/integration_console_engine.rs`), and three readings of the new boot are not committed. (1) The rejected-port arm: `EngineConfig` holds an optional port per receiver, and a `None` port records the bind as failed with `reason = "invalid_port"` and starts no receiver; the resolvers that return the rejection are pinned (`pulse-app/tests/unit_engine_boot_env.rs`), but no test drives `start` or the console program with a rejected port, so nothing committed fails if that arm binds anyway. (2) That no third socket listens is by construction (the shared boot binds two) and was not measured from the process's socket list. (3) The corpus-key lock file's placement outside the data dir is not asserted by the spawned run. Owed: an in-process or spawned arm with a rejected port variable reading the failed-bind record and a refusing port; a socket census on the spawned run; an assertion on the lock file's directory. **LANDED 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed:** all three readings are committed as spawned arms of `pulse-app/tests/integration_console_engine.rs` (7 arms, was 4), each read red before green: (1) under a rejected gRPC port variable the bind record reads failed with `invalid_port`, a connection to that port is refused and the HTTP receiver alone stands in the census; (2) a socket census read from the process's own socket list under `/proc` finds exactly the two receivers on `127.0.0.1` and no socket beyond them; (3) the corpus-key lock file sits in the directory the environment gives, with and without a runtime dir handed, zero bytes, mode `0o600`, nothing under the data dir, its name and the lock directory's path 0 times in the log family. Read on the spawned console engine; `integration_engine_boot.rs` still drives no rejected port in process. **Re-read at chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process:** the census set is now the two receivers on `127.0.0.1` and one `unix` listener at the canonical `run/door/sock` (set equality, both census arms), and under a rejected gRPC port the HTTP receiver and the door stand; the two arms are renamed `the_engine_listens_on_its_two_loopback_receivers_and_its_door_and_on_nothing_else` and `a_rejected_grpc_port_leaves_that_receiver_unstarted_and_the_http_receiver_and_the_door_listening`. "The HTTP receiver alone stands" in (1) and "no socket beyond them" in (2) are the readings of the landing chunk. Nothing further is owed on this row. |

| `engine-log-arm-mutation-and-engine-cycle-glue-coverage` | **NEW 2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine.** The pure decisions of the three new verbs are unit-pinned (`engine_log` 45 tests, `engine_cycle` 21) and one whole cycle is read on the dev host and on a runner, and three readings are not committed. (1) The red reading of `check:engine-log`'s arms is against stubs that pass everything (55 of 66 failed, then 66 of 66 passed): it shows each failing-input pin red against a check that grades nothing, not against a check wrong in one arm — no mutation of the written code was run. (2) The orchestration `engine_cycle::drive` and the verb glue `engine_log::run_check` / `run_settled` have no unit pin and are read only by the whole cycle; of the seven refusal labels three are pinned through `refusal` (`not-linux`, `shared-port`, `data-dir-holds-a-log-family`) and four are returned by `drive` alone and named by no test (`home-unset`, `path-unset`, `data-dir-unusable`, `injector-build-failed`; as searched at that chunk's wrap). (3) A red cycle has not been seen on a runner: a cycle refused before its boot writes no log, and the upload then fails on no file — two red steps for one cause, the designed reading. Owed: one mutation per arm of `check:engine-log`; a pin per remaining refusal label; a runner reading of a red cycle when one occurs. **Narrowed 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed:** (1) closed — one mutation per arm, seven of seven, each one line: each reddened pins (6, 3, 7, 9, 7, 8, 8 of 45) and changed the arm's own line over the kept log of one real engine cycle, and the 45 pins and the nine original lines stood again after the reverts (that chunk's `evidence/mutations.md`). Limits: one mutation per arm, on its passing side, over one real log (n = 1), an input all seven arms can grade; six of the 45 pins also read the whole verdict, so any arm's FAIL reddens them; and one heartbeat pin, `a_gap_over_45_seconds_between_two_ticks_of_one_target_fails_with_no_error_record`, stayed green under the inverted gap comparison, because its log's two other targets carry ordinary gaps the inversion fails (nine other pins reddened). (2) Closed for the labels: the refusal labels are eight (`port-taken` added at that chunk) and each is named by a test — three through `refusal`, five by `xtask/tests/engine_cycle_refusals.rs` on the built verb (`home-unset`, `path-unset`, `data-dir-unusable`, `injector-build-failed`, `port-taken`) — and `engine_cycle::drive` runs under committed tests: those five refusals and one whole failing cycle on a real engine, which ends the engine it started. Still owed: (3) a runner reading of a red cycle when one occurs; and `engine_log::run_check` / `run_settled` have no pin of their own beyond the cycle. What is still owed, that heartbeat pin included, is owned by the route entry `Engine end-to-end gate reachable` (the operator's word at that chunk's route-resolve card, the pc overseer, 2026-10-10). |

| `pre-push-engine-cycle-stage-glue-coverage` | **NEW 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed.** `pre-push:linux`'s sixth stage runs a real console engine cycle (§3 → Per-chunk gate discipline), and it is pinned at its pure decision (`decide_ci_gates`, seven pins in `xtask/src/pre_push.rs`) and by one pin that runs the stage's own teardown against a real process (`end_cycle_ends_the_process_the_stage_data_dir_s_pid_file_names`). The glue `pre_push::read_engine_cycle` has no pin of its own: it is read only by the check itself — four green runs on the dev host, not a committed test and not a CI step. Not read live, and not pinned beyond the decision: a taken port on 24317 / 24318 (the `engine-port-taken` wiring of the stage's probe), and the stage's teardown after a cycle that left its engine running. Owed: a committed reading of the stage over a taken cycle port and over a cycle that leaves its engine running. Owner: the route entry `Engine end-to-end gate reachable` (the operator's word at that chunk's route-resolve card, the pc overseer, 2026-10-10). |

| `door-timeout-interrupt-real-query-coverage` | **NEW 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process.** A `tools/call` through the console engine's door that passes `CALL_TIMEOUT` (5 s) answers `-32002`, and the door then interrupts its own read connection through a DuckDB interrupt handle (`EngineTools::interrupt`, `pulse-app/src/door.rs`). The time bound, the answer and the next call being answered are pinned in process over a stand-in whose interrupt is only counted (`pulse-app/tests/unit_door.rs`, `a_call_over_its_time_bound_answers_timed_out_and_the_next_call_is_answered`); that the interrupt ends a REAL running query is shown at no tier — no query of that chunk runs long enough. Owed: an integration-tier arm over a real long-running query on the engine's own stores. Owner: the route entry `Door admission lifecycle and bounds`. |
(The `chunk-gate-baseline-coverage` and `boot-smoke-coverage` triggers are already active disciplines — see §3 "Per-chunk gate discipline".)

title: 2. Test Strategy

body: **Test pyramid (per Standard tier):**
| Level | Coverage focus | Standard tier depth |

| Unit | Pure functions, isolated module logic (per-crate tests: ingest, buffer, viz, ui-bridge, snapshot, workspace-detector, plugins, mcp-server, corpus, triage, security, interpretation, and the dev-only test-support) | Comprehensive — 75% line coverage minimum; all module boundaries tested with mocked dependencies |

| Integration | Cross-module + IPC + DB + external boundaries (OTLP receivers to buffer roundtrip; TauRPC IPC to buffer query; Channel subscription flow) | Required — all Standard Contracts tested; each surface driver tested with live receiver + buffer |
| E2E | All 7 critical paths via surfaces (P1–P7 from test-scope Section 4) | All critical paths — each via tauri-driver (desktop-webview) or direct IPC client (TauRPC/MCP/Channels) |

| Property-based | Invariant assertions over random inputs (post-prost OTLP invariant checks; DuckDB retention window edge cases; Arrow schema validation) | Selective per trigger — performance-budget and chaos triggers in test-scope Sec 5 require property tests (10k spans/sec stress) |

| Performance / Load | Budget assertions on perf-critical paths (10k spans/sec throughput; token budget enforcement) | Trigger-driven — performance-budget and load-test triggers in test-scope Sec 5 require these |

| Chaos / Fault | Failure injection (buffer retention window enforcement; broadcast channel disconnect; WASM sandbox escape attempts) | Trigger-driven — chaos-test and security-vector triggers require these |
**Agent-runnable invariants (apply across all levels):**
- Every test layer produces machine-parseable output (exit code + structured stdout / JSON / log line)

- No human-in-loop verification, no manual screenshot comparison. **Headful GUI automation is IN scope when it is agent-driven** (operator ruling 2026-08-22): `tauri-driver` + `WebdriverIO`, invoked by `cargo xtask webview-drive`, presses real production controls across a 17-stage path in the live Tauri window, and the verdict comes from an exit code plus BOTH the app's own obs-log records and the driver's DOM report artifact — never from a human looking at it. The driver reports; only the Rust caller asserts. What stays banned is the human-in-the-loop half: a person confirming the result, or a screenshot approved by eye. Playwright/CDP (`connectOverCDP`) attaches successfully but remains UNADOPTED (measured 2026-08-23-webview-self-verify)
- Deterministic — no flaky retries, no real `setTimeout`, no real network except localhost stub (tonic gRPC on `:4317`, axum HTTP on `:4318`)
- Self-bootstrapping fixtures — no developer-seeded data; all fixture data generated at test runtime via OTLP ingest or Rust builders
**Test directory + naming conventions:**

- **Directory pattern:** co-located with source under each crate's `src/` (no separate `tests/` directory per upstream-context arch Test-Relevant Conventions) — **EXCEPT the `pulse-app` binary crate**, whose `[lib] test = false` (the Windows WebView2 load workaround) makes co-located `mod tests` in LIB sources compile under clippy but never run — **`main.rs` is exempt**: it is a `[[bin]]` target — the `pulse-app` package has two since chunk 2026-10-10-console-engine-entry-point, `src/main.rs` and `src/bin/andromeda-pulse-engine.rs` (three lines, no test) — whose tests genuinely execute; since that chunk it holds one, `emit_taurpc_bindings`: the 14 resolver tests left its `mod tests` for `pulse-app/tests/unit_engine_boot_env.rs` under the same names when the resolvers moved to `pulse_app::engine_boot` as `pub` + `#[doc(hidden)]` items. pulse-app's unit-shaped probes therefore live as separate integration-target files under `pulse-app/tests/*.rs`, reaching module internals via `pub` + `#[doc(hidden)]` accessors. **A mechanical RATCHET enforces this since chunk 2026-08-30-diagnostics-un-muting-harness-truth-sweep** (`pulse_app_src_carries_no_new_dead_test_attributes` in `pulse-app/tests/unit_observability_allowlist_sweep.rs`) — and since chunk 2026-08-30-dead-lib-src-test-migration it is a FLAT ZERO for every pulse-app lib-src file: `LEGACY_DEAD_BASELINE` drained to EMPTY, so any `#[test]` / `#[tokio::test]` reappearing in `pulse-app/src/` reds the build; `main.rs` exempt. **A second separate `tests/` directory since chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed: `xtask/tests/`** — the `xtask` package's first integration tests, two test binaries (`agent_run_shell.rs`, `engine_cycle_refusals.rs`) over a shared module `xtask/tests/common/mod.rs` (`#![allow(dead_code)]`, since each binary uses a part of it). They sit outside `src/` because they drive the committed script, the built `harness:engine-cycle` verb and the built engine as processes, which a co-located `mod tests` cannot; xtask's unit pins stay co-located in `xtask/src`. The directory is read by `cargo xtask check:english-sources` (a sixth root) and `cargo xtask quarantine-tracking` (a fifth search dir), and its absence fails both. Framework and runner are unchanged (libtest under `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci`), and no dependency was added
- **File naming:** standard Rust test module naming (`#[cfg(test)] mod tests { … }`)

- **Test function naming:** `#[test]` functions and `#[tokio::test]` for async; per-module test submodules live in `src/` for the library crates and for xtask's unit pins, while pulse-app's are `#[test]` fns in `pulse-app/tests/*.rs` and xtask's process-level pins are `#[test]` fns in `xtask/tests/*.rs`

title: 4. Unit Test Strategy

body: **Framework (Rust crates):** `cargo test` (libtest bundled with the pinned rustc 1.95.0, `rust-toolchain.toml`; the workspace declares `rust-version = "1.95"` in `[workspace.package]`, inherited by all 17 members, equal to the pin and set by the resolved dependency graph — 28 packages declare 1.95.0 (wasmtime 48.0.5, cranelift 0.135.5, pulley 48.0.5) while the workspace's own code needs only ≥ 1.89 (`std::fs::File::lock`); clippy reads its MSRV from that value, and the xtask test `declared_floor_equals_the_pinned_channel` holds it equal to the pin at major.minor in every `cargo nextest run --workspace`) + `cargo-nextest` 0.9.x (per-process isolation). Three unit binaries shell out of Rust. Since chunk 2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-named-from-a-run the `xtask` unit binary shells out to the host C compiler: `harness_witness::tests::built_library` (Linux only) builds `scripts/exit-witness.c` with `cc` and runs seven controls on the built library — a missing `cc` FAILS them, never skips them. And `pulse-app/tests/unit_l4_grammar.rs` runs the vendored, test-only, stdlib Python 3 converter `pulse-app/vendor/llama-cpp/json_schema_to_grammar.py` (llama.cpp b9305, MIT) through the first of `python3` / `python` that prints `Python 3`, and asserts the committed `l4-output.gbnf` equals its output — a missing interpreter FAILS the test, never skips it (a skip reads as a pass in nextest's counts); since chunk 2026-10-05-l4-runs-the-founder-s-pick-with-its-authors-settings. And since chunk 2026-10-10-no-ci-step-reads-nothing `pulse-app/tests/a11y_perf_workflow.rs` runs `node` on `pulse-app/ui/tests-a11y/regression-detector.mjs` (`a11y_regression_detector_fails_when_its_baseline_is_absent`) and asserts a non-zero exit with `baseline not found` on stderr — a missing `node` FAILS the pin, never skips it. A fourth loads a host library without shelling out: since chunk 2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-closed `pulse-app/tests/unit_xlib_threads.rs` (its three arm pins, Linux only) loads the host's `libX11.so.6` through `pulse_app::xlib_threads::init_from` and, for the symbol-not-found arm, `libc.so.6` — a host without `libX11.so.6` FAILS the found-arm pin, never skips it

**Framework (webview unit tests, since chunk #11):** `vitest` 4.x (4.1.11 with `@vitest/mocker` 4.1.11 since chunk 2026-09-29-p-025-hue-shift-observable-made-gradable — the vitest 3 mocker is vulnerable, GHSA-82fw) with `jsdom` 26 environment + `@testing-library/react` 16 for DOM-shape assertions on React 19 components. Landed chunk #11 as Q1 resolution: minimal React + Vite + Vitest tooling at chunk #11 (the then-planned full stack — TanStack Router, shadcn/ui, react-aria-components, motion/react — deferred to chunks #13/#15/#25 per route §2; what SHIPPED is react-aria-components without shadcn/Radix, corrected as measured 2026-08-30). Emits JUnit XML to `target/junit-ui.xml` (matches `cargo-nextest --message-format junit` shape) for agent-driven discipline; `vitest.config.mjs` lives at `pulse-app/ui/vitest.config.mjs` with `setupFiles: ["./src/test-setup.ts"]` registering `@testing-library/react` `afterEach(cleanup)`.

**Coverage tool:** `cargo-llvm-cov` 0.8.5 (LLVM source-based coverage; in CI it runs in the `coverage` job on `ubuntu-22.04`, the `ci` workflow's one runner system since chunk 2026-10-09-ci-on-linux-alone)

**Coverage target:** ≥ 75% line coverage, ≥ 85% function coverage (Standard tier per Section 10). The ≥ 70% branch threshold is RETIRED as never measured — PROVISIONAL: retired on the operator's reading (the pc overseer, 2026-10-10; chunk 2026-10-10-no-gate-stands-while-reading-nothing), awaiting the founder's own word. The arm never read a number: it read `Branch: 0/0 = 100.0%` on every run read, because a branch count needs a compiler channel the project does not pin — branch instrumentation is a nightly-only compiler feature (`-Z coverage-options=branch`, `cargo llvm-cov --branch`), the project pins `1.95.0`, and `cargo xtask test:coverage` asks for no branch count (as measured on the `coverage-linux` artifact of `ci#38038281709`: 144 `BRF:0` and 144 `BRH:0` records, no `BRDA:` line). A real branch count would need branch instrumentation on the toolchain the project pins — the arm returns when that feature is stable on the pinned channel, or when the founder admits a second channel for the `coverage` job — with a measured first reading before any threshold is stated (the workspace's branch coverage was never measured). The two thresholds that stay are measured today with `xtask/` excluded — TEMPORARILY, per the founder's 2026-09-29 ruling, until the next epoch-boundary code audit revisits it (see §10). Webview presentational components (e.g., `pulse-app/ui/src/components/icons/`) explicitly EXCLUDED from this gate at Foundation pre-shell stage; integration coverage applies when `tauri-driver` E2E lands at chunk #25 (webview shell). Scope decision documented per chunk #11 plan acceptance criterion.
**Conventions:**

- **Test file location:**
  - **Rust:** co-located `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { … }` within each LIBRARY crate's source (ingest, buffer, viz, ui-bridge, snapshot, corpus, workspace-detector, plugins, mcp-server, triage, security, interpretation, and since chunk 2026-10-10-shared-telemetry-test-data the dev-only test-support, in `crates/test-support/src/otlp.rs` and `ports.rs`); `pulse-app` is the exception — `[lib] test = false` means its unit probes live in `pulse-app/tests/*.rs` (113 top-level `pulse-app/tests/*.rs` files as of chunk 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door — the one new `unit_door_bridge.rs` — 112 at its base; 112 as of chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process — the three new ones `unit_door.rs`, `unit_observability_allowlist_door.rs`, `integration_door.rs` — 109 at its base; 109 as of chunk 2026-10-10-console-engine-entry-point — the six new ones `unit_engine_boot_env.rs`, `unit_console_commands.rs`, `unit_observability_allowlist_boot_engine.rs`, `unit_engine_boot_seam.rs`, `integration_engine_boot.rs`, `integration_console_engine.rs` — 103 at its base; 102 as of chunk 2026-10-05-l4-runs-the-founder-s-pick-with-its-authors-settings — the new one `unit_l4_grammar.rs` — 101 at its base and at chunk 2026-10-04-linux-launch-stays-up-on-nvidia-wayland, 99 at that chunk's base; 92 at chunk 2026-08-30-dead-lib-src-test-migration, was 80) and assert against `pub` + `#[doc(hidden)]` surfaces. The convention holds with ZERO exceptions since that chunk: 0 `#[test]` / `#[tokio::test]` remain in any pulse-app lib source (`LEGACY_DEAD_BASELINE` EMPTY; `main.rs` a `[[bin]]` exemption holding one test, `emit_taurpc_bindings`, since chunk 2026-10-10-console-engine-entry-point — the package's second `[[bin]]`, `src/bin/andromeda-pulse-engine.rs`, carries none). `pulse-app/tests/*.rs` still counts 109 at chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed, which added no file there (three arms to `integration_console_engine.rs`, 7 in all); it counts 112 at chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process. The `xtask` package keeps its unit pins co-located in `xtask/src` and, since that chunk, holds its integration-tier pins of the script, of the cycle verb's refusals and of one failing cycle in `xtask/tests/` (§2 Directory pattern)
  - **Webview:** co-located `*.test.tsx` adjacent to source under `pulse-app/ui/src/`
- **Test function naming:** `#[test] fn test_<entity>_<scenario>()` (e.g., `#[test] fn test_trace_span_builder_with_12_byte_span_id_rejects()`)
- **Test grouping:** flat functions per module (no nested describe blocks; Rust convention is flat)

**Fixture pattern at unit level:** telemetry test data comes from one set of factories, `test_support::otlp` in the dev-only member `crates/test-support` (since chunk 2026-10-10-shared-telemetry-test-data; §3 Test data bootstrap): a test sets what it reasons about and every other value takes a fixed default — no clock is read and nothing is random. The member has no `rstest` dependency; `rstest` 0.26.1 `#[fixture]` stays the fixture form of the crates that already use it. There is no `MockTraceSpan` and no duration setter
**What unit tests cover:**
- **ingest crate:** `prost` message parsing; TraceService RPC handler; OTLP invariant checks (span_id/trace_id length validation); gRPC error responses; HTTP content-type validation

- **buffer crate:** DuckDB in-memory initialization; Arrow appender insert path; schema validation; retention window eviction logic (via `tokio::time::pause()`); and — since chunk 2026-08-22-log-records-identity — the `log_records` identity surface: `schema::tests::log_records_primary_key_includes_seq_ordinal` (the 4-column PK contract, asserted via `information_schema.key_column_usage`. **The stated rationale for that route — "a duplicate-INSERT probe is a documented hang on this build" — was DISPROVED 2026-08-28:** a plain prepared duplicate INSERT returns `Constraint Error: Duplicate key … violates primary key constraint` in 0.05 s at libduckdb-sys 1.10502. The hang was specific to the Arrow `Appender::flush()` path, not to PK enforcement, and is itself closed at 1.10505. The `information_schema` route may stay on other grounds — it asserts the CONTRACT rather than the behaviour — but not on that one; the source comment above `spans_primary_key_is_composite_trace_id_span_id` states the measured behaviour since chunk 2026-08-30-diagnostics-un-muting-harness-truth-sweep (`crates/buffer/src/schema.rs:`), while a sibling comment above the `metrics_points` key test still states the disproved cause (`crates/buffer/src/schema.rs:`, read 2026-10-09)) and `appender::tests::append_logs_batch_same_tick_same_severity_keeps_both_records` (the same-tick / same-severity behaviour, run on a worker thread under a 30s `recv_timeout` so a hang fails rather than wedges). Since chunk 2026-08-23-ingestion-scrub-coverage the crate also covers the **PII-redaction write boundary**: `appender::tests` pins, per column, that a credential-shaped canary is stored redacted and a legitimate value survives byte-identical across `spans.service_name` / `span_events.name` / `metrics_points.metric_name` / `log_records.severity_text`, plus `redaction_counter_folds_once_per_batch_across_all_four_builders` (all four builders reporting one tally each, and its separation from `record_feed_counts`) — which closed the `buffer-redaction-counter-unit-coverage` trigger. Since chunk 2026-08-23-metrics-points-identity the crate additionally covers the **`metrics_points` identity surface** — `schema::tests::metrics_points_primary_key_includes_seq_ordinal` (the 4-column PK, same `information_schema` route — but NOT the same hang rationale, which was disproved 2026-08-28; see the `log_records` clause above) and three `appender::tests` behavioural pins on a worker thread under an explicit timeout: the label-differing pair, the two distinct credential names that redact alike, and a non-colliding control proving the pre-fix loss was whole-batch — plus the **post-append fold** pair in `consumer::tests` (`dispatch_folds_redactions_after_a_successful_append` / `dispatch_folds_no_redactions_when_the_append_is_rejected`, which discriminate only as a pair) and DIRECT `state::tests` pins on both seq allocators, which closed `buffer-log-seq-allocator-unit-coverage`. Since chunk 2026-08-23-metrics-points-labels the redaction pin set is **FIVE persisted client-controlled cells**, adding `metrics_points.labels`: `credential_label_values_redact_in_both_classes_and_keys_survive` pins BOTH canary classes — the KEYED one (`{password: "hunter2"}`, reachable only because the scrub input is the joined `key=value` form) and the BARE one — and asserts the label KEY survives verbatim in both; `benign_and_high_entropy_label_values_survive_byte_identical` is the selectivity control (a benign pair plus a hex digest and a UUID from the scrubber's own false-positive corpus stay `Allowed`); `label_differing_points_read_back_distinguishable`, `label_encoding_is_attribute_order_independent` and `empty_attribute_set_stores_the_empty_string` cover the stored shape, with `viz`'s `query_metrics_returns_labels_distinguishing_otherwise_identical_points` covering the READ path. The tally pin keeps its name `redaction_counter_folds_once_per_batch_across_all_four_builders` — the BUILDER count is still four; only the scrub-site count moved to five. Since chunk `2026-08-28-duplicate-span-replay-fails-loudly` the crate additionally carries the **duplicate-identity replay pin** — `appender::tests::append_after_a_constraint_violating_flush_returns_instead_of_hanging`, which seeds a batch, replays its exact identities, and asserts the FOLLOWING batch still lands, on a worker thread under an explicit `recv_timeout` per the hang-safe form. It is the measurement of record for that chunk: 30 s timeout at libduckdb-sys 1.10502, 0.06 s pass at 1.10505, same test and same production code. **No tracked in-crate `buffer` gap remains.**

- **security crate:** the P-047 scrubber pattern catalog — recall and false-positive `#[rstest]` corpora co-located in `crates/security/src/scrubber.rs`, spanning EIGHT category arms since chunk 2026-08-22-pii-scrubber-recall added `provider_key` (anchored-prefix + length floor over published issuer prefixes, ordered after the keyed `api_key` / `secret_kv` arms so those keep their categories, and before `credit_card` so a digit-heavy key is not mis-labelled). The false-positive half is a first-class guard, not an afterthought: ordinary high-entropy identifiers (hex digests, UUIDs, base64-ish blobs, hyphenated job names, dotted handler paths) must keep returning `ScrubbedValue::Allowed(_)`. `scrub_attribute` and the `ScrubbedValue` contract are asserted unchanged. Since chunk 2026-09-29-scrubber-path-false-positive the `credit_card` arm (Luhn over whole-group windows) carries two more corpora: `scrubber_redacts_luhn_valid_card_forms` (8 cases — contiguous, spaced, hyphenated, Amex 4-6-5, behind `key=`, beside an unrelated digit group) and `scrubber_allows_non_card_digit_runs` (7 cases, byte-identical `Allowed` — date-time stamps in path / `workspace=` key / `PROJECT:` forms, a 19-digit nanosecond timestamp, and the Luhn-invalid `4532-1234-5678-9010`), mutation-checked so each rejection branch discriminates (crate suite 54, as measured by `cargo nextest run -p security` at that chunk; 39 → 54). Since chunk 2026-09-30-span-level-redaction the crate also covers the span-masking primitive `mask_secret_spans` / `MaskedValue` with 31 co-located `span_mask` pins: one embedded mid-text canary per category (8 exact masked strings), verdict equality with `scrub_attribute` over both corpora plus two proptests, the class-aware extent (keyed to end of line · bare whole token · `credit_card` digit-group run), catalog-order merges, single-token parity with whole-value replacement, byte-identical allowed values, and idempotence (corpus + proptests, the bounded fixpoint) — mutation-checked so the keyed extent, the merge, the span masking itself and the fixpoint each redden their pins; `proptest-regressions/scrubber.txt` replays the two discriminating seeds. Crate suite 85 (`cargo nextest list -p security --profile ci`; 54 → 85)

- **viz crate:** Aggregation queries (traces.query / metrics.query / logs.query); pagination logic; time-bucket grouping; the read-connection isolation pin landed 2026-08-26 (`query::tests::read_connection_returns_a_distinct_usable_connection` — asserts the clone is a DISTINCT `Arc` and still sees the same in-memory database, since a fallback returning the SAME `Arc` would satisfy every query assertion while restoring the obs-plan §10 contention it exists to remove). **Its scope stops at the helper** — the three `pulse-app` router call sites that must USE it are unpinned; see the §1 `viz-read-connection-router-wiring-coverage` trigger
- **ui-bridge crate:** TauRPC procedure routing; error serialization to AppError enum (NEVER expose stack traces)
- **snapshot crate:** Token-counting logic; dedup accumulator; anomaly marker detection; p50/p95/p99 computation

- **workspace-detector crate:** `.andromeda/` marker detection; VCS metadata parsing; path canonicalization; the workspace-key surface — `workspace_key` derivation (detected root vs `data_dir` fallback, verbatim `\\?\` preservation), the `publish_workspace_key` / `read_published_workspace_key` / `workspace_key_path` round-trip, bounded-read validation (≤ `MAX_WORKSPACE_KEY_BYTES` = 4096, UTF-8, trailing-newline trim, empty + control-char rejection), and the canonicalize-and-confine write guard (chunk 2026-08-14-workspace-key-alignment; crate suite 18 → 26)

- **corpus crate:** keychain key resolution across both P-049 branches — OS-store-primary wins when it serves, passphrase fallback engages + warns when it does not, and the store's error surfaces when no passphrase is configured (the fallback is opt-in); `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_CORPUS_PASSPHRASE` bounded parse (non-empty, ≤ 1024 bytes, unset ⇒ not-configured); BLAKE3 derivation determinism + distinctness by passphrase and by service id; the `disposition` module (orphan scan across the 4 payload-bearing tables — 5 → 4 at chunk 2026-08-30-diagnostics-un-muting-harness-truth-sweep, `baseline_state` dropped at corpus SCHEMA_VERSION 2 — `service_registry` spared, inventory-before-purge, rows preserved on a failed inventory write, idempotence); the v1→v2 LADDER migration pins (a v1 database converges to v2 with `baseline_state` dropped and `user_version` stamped 2; a fresh database creates v2 directly; a NEWER version still errors as mismatch); the incident lifecycle-event pins on `update_incident_status` (one `incident_events` row per status VALUE-change inside the guarded transaction; a same-status refresh records nothing; a `DeclinedStale` write records nothing); read-path skip-and-count (mixed corpus returns readable rows, by-id resolves to not-found). **Cross-process key persistence is proven by a test that re-executes its own test binary** — an in-process two-instance check would have passed while the defect was live, because keyring's non-persisting store was process-GLOBAL; it skips cleanly where no credential store exists, and any real entry it mints uses a test-scoped service name with cleanup so the operator's store is never polluted (chunk 2026-08-15-corpus-key-persistence; crate suite → 70). **The store-less skip arm leaves no lock file** (chunk 2026-10-04-declared-rust-floor-matches-the-code; crate suite 87 → 88): that test's skip arm takes the lock before the store call fails, so it removes its own test-scoped lock file before returning; `corpus_key_skip_arm_leaves_no_lock_file` (`cfg(target_os = "linux")`) re-executes the test binary `--exact keychain::tests::corpus_key_survives_a_real_process_boundary --nocapture` with `env_clear()` and `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` set to a fresh TempDir, and asserts the pair (the child printed the `[skip] no OS credential store …` line, the count of `andromeda-pulse-corpus-key-*.lock` in that TempDir) == (true, 0) — the `[skip]` half keeps it from passing vacuously; RED at base `(true, 1)` and under the cleanup deleted; the only new `remove_file` is in `mod tests`, so the product's never-delete lock-file contract is unchanged. **Concurrent first-run creation is witnessed the same way** (chunk 2026-10-04-corpus-key-creation-is-race-free; crate suite 82 → 87, every fn named `race_free`): `corpus_key_race_free_across_concurrent_first_run_processes` spawns 8 re-exec children of the test binary against one EMPTY test-scoped entry, releases them together through a stdin barrier (no `sleep`), and asserts every child exited 0 and wrote its sink, exactly 1 distinct key, that key equal to the one the store holds, and the lock file present with length 0 — the entry and lock file are removed BEFORE asserting, keys compared in-process and never printed; RED on the prior unlocked code (8 distinct, 7 returned a key the store no longer held) and mutation-checked (the unlocked body restored → RED again). Pins beside it: the entry-keyed lock-file name (`andromeda-pulse-corpus-key-{h16}.lock`, ASCII, distinct per service and per account); the Linux lock-dir rule (`cfg(target_os = "linux")`: `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` unset or blank → the temp dir; set to a directory → it, canonicalized; set to a file, a missing path or a relative path → `Err(Unavailable)`); fail-closed fetch with the lock dir unusable (`Err`, the entry still absent afterwards). These legs clean-skip with one `[skip] no OS credential store …` line where no credential store answers — including any run whose environment carries neither `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` nor `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` (measured under `env -i` at that chunk's stage 5 of the pre-push stages, then run by hand; since chunk 2026-10-09-pre-push-check-native-on-linux that stage is `cargo xtask pre-push:linux`'s own `test` stage, whose constructed environment holds neither variable, pinned by set equality — there the clean-skip is stated, not measured, the stage's log holding no output of a passing test); the skip line reaches a gate log only with `--success-output immediate`, so a gate asserting the leg RAN reads `lacks [skip]` on that form, never nextest's skip count

- **triage crate:** the cold-start-window resolver — `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_BASELINE_BOOTSTRAP_SECONDS` bounded parse (rejects zero / empty / unparseable / at-or-above `WINDOW_DURATION_SECONDS`, trims surrounding whitespace, unset is byte-identical to the 3600s default, and every rejection falls back rather than panicking) and `Thresholds::from_env` carrying the resolved bound without disturbing any other threshold; the `BaselineState` bootstrap-window surface (a boot-resolved short window reaches the gate where the same instant under the default is still `Learning`; the resume-from-corpus path applies the bound, not just the fresh path; a deserialized state defaults to the non-zero window, since a zero would mark every service `Ready` at once); `ActivityFloor::bootstrap_state` boundary behaviour at and either side of a non-default window. **The clock is injected as an explicit `now_nanos` parameter, not via `tokio::time::pause()`** — these functions take the instant as an argument, so there is no ambient clock to control and parameter injection is the stronger form (chunk 2026-08-16-baseline-family-reachability; crate suite +12). The digest render's `OVERALL:` state word (chunk 2026-10-01-real-model-incident-surfacing): `degraded` when the active-incident bypass holds, else `anomalous` when the digest carries ≥ 1 cue, else `nominal`, with the parenthetical `({n} active incident(s); {m} cue(s))` — pinned by 3 in-crate `overall_line_*` tests over `triage::contract::{render_payload, cue_summary}` (`#[doc(hidden)] pub`), mutation-checked (restoring Tier1-reads-nominal reds the cue-bearing pin), plus the pulse-app pin `pii_scrub_fixture_overall_line_matches_the_render` tying the scrub fixture to the real renderer. The digest's framing lines (chunk 2026-10-04-l4-interpretation-names-its-triggering-cue): exactly one `TRIGGER: {cue_cause_label}` line keyed on the FIRST cue, directly after `OVERALL:`, and none without a cue; and a static corpus framing note directly under the unchanged `CORPUS MATCHES:` header when matches exist, absent otherwise — pinned by 5 in-crate tests (`render_payload_names_the_trigger_from_the_first_cue` · `render_payload_omits_the_trigger_line_without_a_cue` · `render_payload_frames_corpus_matches_as_other_incidents` · `render_payload_omits_the_corpus_framing_note_without_matches` · `render_payload_framing_lines_are_ascii`, every `CueKind`), mutation-checked (keying the line on the LAST cue reds the first-cue pin; dropping the note reds its pin and the probe's S4 pin). The two "omits" pins hold on a tree that never emits either line, so they guard only as the negative half of their pair. The corpus selection under a triggering scope (chunk 2026-10-07-l4-probe-reproduces-the-canary-history-miss): `select_corpus_matches` takes `triggering_scope: Option<&str>`, and with `Some(scope)` its scope arm keeps a candidate only when the candidate's `scope_id` equals that scope and is an active scope — the fingerprint arm unchanged, the narrowing before the cap and only ever removing, `None` selecting as before; `assemble`, the one production caller, passes the triggering cue's `scope_id` — pinned by 5 in-crate tests (`select_corpus_matches_drops_other_scopes_matches_under_a_triggering_scope` · `select_corpus_matches_keeps_every_active_scope_without_a_triggering_scope` · `select_corpus_matches_narrows_before_the_cap_and_only_removes` · `assemble_drops_other_scopes_corpus_lines_under_a_cue_scope` · `assemble_keeps_every_scopes_corpus_lines_without_a_cue_scope`), mutation-checked (checks 65–69; reverting the product change alone reds them); crate suite 497 passed

- **interpretation crate:** the citable-evidence prompt surface (chunk 2026-08-26-interpretation-brief-completeness; 5 in-crate `prompt.rs` pins) — the `CITABLE_OPEN_MARKER`/`CITABLE_CLOSE_MARKER` delimited section renders supplied ids verbatim between markers in all three tier builders; the section orders after Current Digest and before Corpus Retrieval / Output Instructions; an EMPTY citable list renders the explicit none-instruction ("emit an empty evidence_refs array") rather than omitting the section; `CITING_INSTRUCTION` (copy-verbatim / never-invent) lands in every tier's Output Instructions; supplied-order preservation (dedup is the pulse-app caller's job). Versioning metadata pins ride the `PROMPT_VERSION_*` consts, so the v2.6 / v1.5-fallback / v1.5-reflection lineage (bumped together at chunk 2026-10-06-l4-first-hypothesis-names-the-triggering-service; v2.5 / v1.4-* at 2026-10-04-l4-rank-1-hypothesis-names-the-retry-on-every-storm-shape; v2.4 / v1.3-* at 2026-10-04-l4-interpretation-names-its-triggering-cue; v2.3 / v1.2-* at 2026-10-01-real-model-incident-surfacing) is asserted without literal duplication; the shared ASCII `TRIGGER_FRAMING_INSTRUCTION` (the digest's TRIGGER line names the signal the title, symptom and first hypothesis describe; the first hypothesis statement names that signal in the TRIGGER line's own words; another abnormal metric on the same service is its cause or effect, never a separate first hypothesis; CORPUS MATCHES lines are other incidents; and, since chunk 2026-10-06-l4-first-hypothesis-names-the-triggering-service, when the cue line under ATTENTION CUES carries a scope_id the first hypothesis statement names that value exactly as written and attributes the signal to nothing else, a service whose name merely contains it included) sits exactly once in every tier's Output Instructions, after `CITING_INSTRUCTION` — pinned by `framing_instruction_present_in_every_tier_output_instructions` (mutation-checked: removing it from the fallback builder alone reds it), its first-hypothesis obligation clause pinned exactly once in every tier's composed prompt by `every_tier_obliges_the_first_hypothesis_to_name_the_trigger_signal` (mutation-checked: reverting the product text alone reads `left: 0, right: 1`), its scope obligation clause pinned exactly once in every tier's composed prompt by `every_tier_obliges_the_first_hypothesis_to_name_the_cue_scope` (chunk 2026-10-06-l4-first-hypothesis-names-the-triggering-service; red before green on the untouched instruction, `left: 0, right: 1`; mutation-checked: cutting the sentence from the const reds it; `-p interpretation` 130 pins at that chunk, 129 at its base), its ASCII cleanliness covered by `composed_prompt_templates_are_ascii_clean_for_argv_transport`; and the embedded L4 output schema's property ORDER — `decision` / `severity` after `hypotheses`, before `investigation_steps`, content unchanged — is pinned by `primary_prompt_schema_lists_decision_and_severity_after_the_analysis`, because constrained generation emits keys in schema order and the earlier order had the model commit to a decision before writing any analysis (measured: `decision` was the 3rd generated key in 30/30 runs; chunk 2026-10-01-real-model-incident-surfacing evidence `arm-matrix.md`). **The Linux CUDA presence probe's candidate set** (chunk 2026-10-04-l4-hardware-probe-finds-cuda-on-arch-layout-hosts; 6 co-located `cuda_probe_` pins in `hardware.rs`, 13 run cases) over the private root-taking seam `cuda_driver_present_under(root)` that the Linux arm of `detect_gpu_present` calls with `/`: an 8-case `#[rstest]` over `CUDA_PROBE_DIRS` × `CUDA_PROBE_NAMES` (`usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu` · `usr/local/cuda/lib64` · `usr/lib` · `usr/lib64` × `libcuda.so` · `libcuda.so.1`), each alone reading present; an empty root and the unprobed `usr/lib/libcudart.so` · `usr/lib/libcuda.so.2` · `opt/cuda/libcuda.so` reading absent (exact match, never prefix or search); the Arch symlink chain `libcuda.so → libcuda.so.1 → libcuda.so.610.57.04` reading present and a dangling link absent (`cfg(unix)`); and an exact-set pin on the two production constants. Fixtures are real files and symlinks under `tempfile::TempDir` (§8 Filesystem) — no pin reads the host's `/usr/lib*` or calls `detect_gpu_present` / `HardwareProfileDetector::new()`, so none is host-dependent. RED 8/13 against the pre-chunk set; mutation-checked: dropping `usr/lib` reddens 4, dropping `libcuda.so.1` reddens 5, and reverting the Linux arm to an inline array reddens `cargo clippy` with dead-code errors (the `cfg_attr(not(target_os = "linux"), allow(dead_code))` leaves the Linux build no allowance, so clippy is the arm-wiring guard)
- **plugins crate:** WASM Component Model component loading; WIT contract binding validation; capability check (negative test: attempt disallowed import)
- **mcp-server crate:** JSON-RPC 2.0 frame parsing; tool call routing; schema validation; feature-gate build verification

- **test-support crate (dev-only, chunk 2026-10-10-shared-telemetry-test-data):** the `otlp` factories (10 tests) — two builds from the same calls are equal; an unset event time is the one fixed instant and an unset service the one fixed name; ids have their wire lengths and unset span ids differ by position; what a test sets on a span and its event, a metric point and a log record is read back. The `ports` claim (4 tests) — a claimed number lies in 20000–31999 and is no harness port; two live claims differ; the lock file of a live claim cannot be locked again; a claimed port binds on loopback. Its edges are pinned from `xtask` (`test_support_edges`, 5 tests: no member names it outside `[dev-dependencies]`, it depends on `ingest` alone, it is a member some member uses), and the reading of its defaults at the write boundary is `buffer`'s `consumer::tests::a_default_built_batch_of_every_kind_lands_whole_with_no_redaction` (`rows_ingested` equal to the rows sent, `redactions_applied` 0, `append_rejections` 0)

- **webview React components (pulse-app/ui/src/components/):** DOM-shape contracts (`svg` `viewBox` / `aria-*` attrs / `focusable` / `className` passthrough); decorative-vs-meaningful ARIA flip pattern (icon defaults to `aria-hidden="true"`; `aria-label` override flips to `role="img"`); `currentColor` propagation (no hardcoded hex); size prop pass-through (16/20/24 grid); dispatcher-vs-named-component output equivalence (`<Icon glyph="aperture" />` matches `<Aperture />`); banned-element grep (no inline SVG `<animate>` / `<animateTransform>` / `<animateMotion>` / `<set>` / gradient / filter)
**What unit tests do NOT cover** (handled at integration/E2E):
- Full OTLP ingest → buffer → query roundtrip (integration)
- Tauri window visibility + tray icon rendering (E2E via tauri-driver)
- External HTTP services (mocked at unit level)

title: 5. Integration Test Strategy

body: **Driver(s):**
- **Module ↔ module:** direct Rust function calls with shared `rstest` fixtures (in-process)

- **Module ↔ DuckDB:** `duckdb-rs` in-memory connection, seeded by OTLP ingest through the live receiver, by direct in-memory inserts, or — in the crates that take `test-support` (`buffer`, `pulse-app`, `xtask`) — by resource-level batches from the `test_support::otlp` factories (`resource_spans()` / `resource_metrics()` / `resource_logs()`). No Arrow-batch factory exists: the `MockArrowBatch` builder this row once named was dropped from §3 item 6 at chunk 2026-10-10-shared-telemetry-test-data
- **Module ↔ OTLP receiver:** `tonic` native gRPC client (0.14.5) sending to loopback `:4317`; `axum-test` 18.7.0 for HTTP `:4318` unit tests; `reqwest` 0.12.x for live receiver E2E
- **Module ↔ TauRPC IPC:** `tauri::test::mock_builder()` + `get_ipc_response()` for in-process IPC testing; live Tauri app via E2E layer
- **Module ↔ MCP sidecar:** `tokio::process::Command` spawning subprocess + JSON-RPC 2.0 client (`serde_json`)
**Boundary types covered:**
| Boundary | Test approach | Tools |
| ingest → buffer (gRPC TraceService.Export → DuckDB rows) | Send valid gRPC message via `tonic` client; query DuckDB via `Connection::query_map` | `tonic` 0.14.5, `duckdb-rs` 1.5.x |

| buffer → viz (DuckDB query → Arrow batch aggregation) | Seed the in-memory DuckDB directly (or via OTLP ingest); invoke `viz::aggregator::query(…)`; assert Arrow schema. No Arrow-batch factory exists (the `MockArrowBatch` of §3 item 6 was dropped at chunk 2026-10-10-shared-telemetry-test-data), and `viz` does not take `test-support` (a dev-dependency of `buffer`, `pulse-app` and `xtask` only) | `duckdb-rs`, `arrow-rs` 55.x |
| viz → ui-bridge (aggregation result → TauRPC response) | Invoke `traces.query` via `tauri::test::mock_builder()`; assert JSON response shape | `tauri::test` module |
| snapshot → buffer (token counting against DuckDB rows) | Stage 500 spans in DuckDB; invoke `snapshot::generate(…)`; assert `response.token_count <= budget` | `duckdb-rs` |

| plugins → runtime (WASM load / invoke with capability gate) | Load fixture WASM from `tests/fixtures/plugins/`; invoke via `wasmtime::component`; negative test: attempt unauthorized import | `wasmtime` 48.x (lockfile-resolved 48.0.5 as of 2026-10-04; arch family floor 25+), `bindgen!` macro |

| workspace-detector → filesystem (path canonicalization) | Create temp dir with `.andromeda/` marker; set `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR=$TMPDIR`; invoke `workspace::detect()`; assert canonical path | `assert_fs` 1.x, `assert_cmd` 2.x |

| pulse-app boot → `<data_dir>/run/workspace-key` → mcp-server `init_incident_context` (cross-process key handoff) | Publish the app's resolved key (atomic `.tmp`+rename), read it back through the sidecar's read path; assert byte-equality with the app's filter key, and that an absent/invalid file falls back to `data_dir` on both ends | `tempfile` 3.x; `tokio::process::Command` for the sidecar-subprocess leg per Module ↔ MCP sidecar |
**Setup / teardown lifecycle:**

- **Per-test fresh:** `tokio::test` with `#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]` for concurrent OTLP ingest tests; `tempfile::TempDir` for filesystem tests; ephemeral `DuckDB::open_in_memory()` for buffer tests
- **Shared session:** None (all tests isolated per Standard tier discipline)
**Cross-module patterns covered:**
- **app_info contract:** Invoke IPC, assert response includes `name`, `version`, `rust_version`, `tauri_version`, `features` string
- **health contract:** Invoke IPC, assert `status` enum, subsystems object with required fields, `pid` integer
- **ready contract:** Invoke IPC, assert `ready` boolean, checks object with duckdb_connection / ingest_mpsc_capacity_pct fields
- **traces.query contract:** Invoke IPC with time_range + filters, assert response is paginated result set with trace_id / span_name / duration_ms / error_count fields
- **OTLP gRPC TraceService contract:** Send valid OTLP TraceService.Export RPC, assert gRPC Code::OK response + row inserted in buffer

- **OTLP HTTP contract:** POST `/v1/traces` with a protobuf body, assert 200 OK + row inserted **(MEASURED 2026-08-22: this build is protobuf-only — `application/json` returns 415 Unsupported Media Type; `crates/ingest/src/http.rs:` accepts `application/x-protobuf` alone. Arch §Conventions already hedges HTTP/JSON as optional, so the receiver is spec-conformant; these recipes must send protobuf.)**
- **Real-time Channel contract:** Subscribe to `pulse://stream/spans`, trigger gRPC ingest, assert Arrow IPC payload received with schema-valid RecordBatch
- **MCP tools contract:** Send JSON-RPC 2.0 `tools/call` with `query_traces` method, assert response is array of trace objects with required fields

title: 6. E2E Test Strategy

body: **Drivers per surface:**
| Surface | Driver | Mode | Notes |

| **desktop-webview (React + Tauri)** | `@crabnebula/tauri-driver` 2.x + `webdriverio` 9.x, invoked by `cargo xtask webview-drive [--expect-absent <STAGE>] [--no-inject]` (an unknown stage id is a hard error listing the valid ids) — **no `mocha` and no `@wdio/*` test-runner is installed** (measured 2026-08-23) | native (Windows, live); headless xvfb-run (Linux) not yet exercised | Drives a **17-stage live path** — launch → boot-geometry → traces-empty → traces-populate → traces-scroll → native-menu-suppressed → connection-status → storm-incident → findings-window → report-window → report-copy → investigate → empty-states → dashboard-toggle → dashboard-close → widget-close → signpost-repeat (six window-mechanics stages added at `2026-08-23-headful-leg-extension`; two more at `2026-08-24-headful-mechanics-probe-race-disposition`, where `widget-close` STOPPED being terminal — `signpost-repeat` follows it deliberately, programmatically restoring the widget so a SECOND real close press proves the P-063 signpost fires on every close, not merely the first; `boot-geometry` at `2026-08-30-diagnostics-un-muting-harness-truth-sweep` — a DOM-only observer stage right after launch whose driver record carries the compact widget's `outer_position`/`outer_size` + current-monitor rect + `monitor_scale`, and whose Rust verdict RE-DERIVES the app's own snap formula (`wx == mx + mw − round(480.0 × scale) − 24 && wy == my + 24`, `WIDGET_DEFAULT_WIDTH` × scale + `WIDGET_EDGE_MARGIN`, TopRight default) rather than comparing against a recorded constant — obs half None by design, three committed pins prove the verdict discriminates (accepts the measured 2056/24 fixture, rejects the wrong-inset 2040, rejects missing fields), the geometry-READ half the declined-on-measurement `setWindowRect` probe left open; every new id is `--expect-absent`-eligible with no CLI change). **Two window-mechanic stages were DECLINED on measurement at that chunk, not deferred:** a mechanics probe drove W3C pointer Actions and `setWindowRect` against the live WRY window and both executed WITHOUT THROWING while producing zero delta (`drag_delta {dx:0,dy:0}`, `resize_delta {dw:0,dh:0}`, no error field) — the silent no-op this harness exists to catch — so a drag stage and a resize stage (and with the latter, P-082's multi-window-size half) cannot be written non-vacuously through this transport. `geometry_readable` was `true` in the same probe, so window geometry can still be READ; only synthesized input is unavailable. `native-menu-suppressed` is the sanctioned fallback for the third: a native WebView2 menu is unobservable to WebDriver, so the stage asserts the SUPPRESSION side (a real `contextmenu` dispatched in the shipped production bundle is `defaultPrevented`, plus the canvas `dragstart` half) — evidence vitest cannot give, since it exercises the hook in jsdom under a stubbed PROD flag. **A read-only observer stage must not perturb what follows it:** that stage's first draft sat late in the leg and navigated back to `/traces` to make a canvas present, which left downstream window state unlike the pristine flow and killed the RED arm's WebDriver session at `dashboard-close` (measured: pristine 13-stage RED arm 184s PASS, the same arm with the route change no completion at 1200s across three ceilings); re-homing it to where the leg is already on `/traces` restored the arm to 183s PASS — with telemetry entering only over real OTLP via `crates/ingest/examples/inject_demo.rs` (built outside the timed section, invoked by path) and the deterministic-L4 gate `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC` set into the driver's spawn env (the app under test is a grandchild process, so it cannot inherit the caller's shell). `pulse-app/ui/tests-e2e/webview-drive.mjs` drives and REPORTS only — it asserts nothing, emitting DOM observations to a per-run TempDir `webview-drive-stages.json` (`{stages:[{stage,observed,…}]}`); the assertions and the verdict live in Rust (`xtask/src/webview_drive.rs`), which reads BOTH the app's own obs log and that artifact and reports each stage as two independent halves (`StageHalves{obs,dom}`, `None` = inapplicable) — a combined boolean cannot say whether telemetry failed to land or merely failed to reach the screen. Every stage predicate matches an effect FIELD, never the target alone. The win32 driver ships via the napi optional dep `@crabnebula/tauri-driver-win32-x64-msvc`; `msedgedriver` is located by `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MSEDGEDRIVER_PATH` and must match the installed WebView2 Runtime — unset ⇒ clean SKIP (exit 0), which is why a green exit code alone is not evidence the leg ran. Canvas pixel inspection remains out of scope. **A SECOND driver serves this surface** (recorded 2026-08-23-a11y-verification): the browser-driven a11y chain — Playwright + axe/pa11y/Lighthouse under `cargo xtask test:a11y`, real Chromium against the built `ui/dist` — which is where real-keypress DOM behaviour is pinned (the TraceTable roving-tabindex traversal), and which the §6 P5 residual already leans on. The two are complementary: tauri-driver exercises the LIVE window and the app's own obs log; the a11y chain exercises the built frontend with IPC mocked at the webview boundary. **LAUNCH RACE ROOT-CAUSED + DRIVER-REMEDIATED (`2026-08-23-headful-leg-extension`; supersedes the 2026-08-23-a11y-verification MEASURED-FLAKY note):** each boot under the automation environment loses the initial navigation of ~ONE of the four webviews (victim ~random — measured across 7 boots: findings ×2, report ×2, main ×2, none ×1), and nothing re-navigates a victim: `show()` ≠ navigate, which is why the earlier toggle-press recovery measured 0/10 and why a longer wait could never fix it. The prior 1-in-4/1-in-5 `launch` failures were this race striking `main`; the Tauri window label is init-script-injected into `about:blank` documents too, so label-readability is NOT a navigation signal — only `getUrl()` leaving `about:blank` is. Remediation (no wait, no retry): the driver re-navigates `about:blank` victims at launch, before any stage asserts, and RECORDS it (`recovered_from_blank` in the stage record; 6/6 recoveries succeeded; both pristine GREEN runs drove all 13 stages). **Boundary — MEASURED 2026-08-25 (`2026-08-24-headful-mechanics-probe-race-disposition`), superseding the 2026-08-24 "production exposure UNMEASURED; no confining mechanism identified" wording.** The open half was closed by shipping the measurement instrument the boundary said did not exist: `pulse_app::window::spawn_navigation_check` reads each declared window's navigation state once per boot, post-settle, and emits `app.boot.window.navigation` (`window_label` · `navigated` · `reason`; INFO on navigated, WARN on `about:blank`) — so a healthy boot is now POSITIVE evidence per window rather than the absence of a complaint. **Result: 0 blank windows across 36 windows / 9 plain boots** (direct-binary, no driver attached, fresh data dir per boot). Under the automation environment the same race struck 6 of 7 boots, so the two rates are not close. The detector was itself validated rather than trusted: collapsing `NAVIGATION_SETTLE` to 0 made the WARN branch fire (`blank=1`, victim `report`), proving the branch executes and both fields reach the log unredacted — a detector that has never fired proves plumbing, not behaviour. **NO product-side guard shipped, by measurement and by construction:** the race does not reproduce on plain boots, and the CARRY-dictated site could not host a guard anyway — Tauri 2's `WindowEvent` has no Shown/Visible variant (source-verified: Resized · Moved · CloseRequested · Destroyed · Focused · ScaleFactorChanged · DragDrop · ThemeChanged · Suspended · Resumed), and `findings`/`report`/`main` are shown from the FRONTEND. **Residual, stated honestly:** n=9 excludes a race at automation frequency, not a rare one; the shipped detector is what makes any future occurrence visible instead of silent. Still not CI-wired, so the leg gates nothing today |
| **TauRPC IPC procedures** | `tauri::test::mock_builder()` in Rust harness | in-process | Fast unit-level IPC contract tests; no webview overhead |
| **MCP stdio sidecar** | `tokio::process::Command` + JSON-RPC 2.0 client | direct subprocess | Spawn with feature flag + env var; write frames to stdin, parse stdout |
| **OTLP/gRPC receiver** | `tonic` native client | direct loopback `:4317` | Send synthetic spans; query buffer via TauRPC to assert ingestion |
| **OTLP/HTTP receiver** | `reqwest` 0.12.x async HTTP client | direct loopback `:4318` | Send protobuf payloads; assert 200 OK + buffer rows |
| **Real-time Channels** | Tauri IPC Channel subscription in Rust harness | in-process async | Subscribe to `pulse://stream/spans`, trigger ingest, decode Arrow IPC payload |

**Selector strategy:** **measured per surface** (operator ruling 2026-08-23). The TauRPC IPC surface is still procedure-based, but the headful `webview-drive` leg IS DOM-driven, so a strategy applies: bind to the **accessible name** wherever one ships (`button[aria-label="Investigate"]`, `button[aria-label="Close to tray"]`, `role="img"` on `ConnectionDot`) — a name regression then fails the stage — and to `data-testid` where no accessible name exists (`EmptyState`, the dashboard footer). Never xpath, never a hashed/utility class. **The Traces surface ships its own anchors and the leg now binds to them** (anchors: 2026-08-23-a11y-verification; migration DISCHARGED at `2026-08-23-headful-leg-extension`): `region[aria-label="Telemetry traces chart"]` on the constellation wrapper, the native `table` element, and `.trace-row` rows — with `data-testid="trace-table-empty"` deliberately RETAINED, because the empty state is a plain `<td>` message cell shipping no accessible anchor, exactly the case the data-testid tier exists for. Measure the selector at HEAD before pinning it, and measure a claimed ABSENCE the same way, against the component that actually owns the surface: the `Minimize to tray` precedent was a phantom name, while the Traces `region`/`table` "absence" was itself phantom — the `table` role was always present and the region lives on a sibling component (see §1 Pending coverage triggers).
**Critical path scenarios** (translated from test-scope Section 4):

title: Scenario: P1 — Receive OTLP telemetry (gRPC), visualize in WebGPU dashboard

data.head: #### Scenario: P1 — Receive OTLP telemetry (gRPC), visualize in WebGPU dashboard

body: - **Surfaces involved:** OTLP/gRPC receiver (`:4317`), ingest module, buffer (DuckDB), viz aggregation, TauRPC `traces.query`, desktop-webview (WebGPU canvas)

- **Steps:**
  1. Boot `pulse-app` via `boot` command; confirm `health` returns `status: "ok"` and ports ready
  2. Generate 100 synthetic spans — the builder form is the `test_support::otlp` factories and their `trace_request()` (§3 Test data bootstrap; no `MockTraceSpan` exists) → serialize to OTLP gRPC protobuf
  3. Send batch to `:4317` via `tonic` client; assert gRPC Code::OK response
  4. Poll `health` command every 500ms; assert `subsystems.buffer.rows_ingested >= 100` within 5s
  5. Invoke TauRPC `traces.query({service: "test-app", time_range: [now-60s, now]})` via test client
  6. Assert response.rows.length > 0; verify trace_id and span_name fields match sent data
  7. (WebGPU canvas rendering unverified; assertion on IPC contract only per agent-driven discipline)

- **Verification signal:**
  - Step 3: gRPC response code == OK
  - Step 4: `status.subsystems.buffer.rows_ingested` increments from 0 to >= 100 within 5s
  - Step 6: response.rows contains entry with matching service_name, trace_id from step 2
- **Cleanup:** `cleanup` command; verify ports `:4317` / `:4318` no longer accept connections

title: Scenario: P2 — Generate token-efficient curated snapshot (not raw dump)

data.head: #### Scenario: P2 — Generate token-efficient curated snapshot (not raw dump)

body: - **Surfaces involved:** buffer (DuckDB), snapshot module, TauRPC `snapshot.generate`, desktop-webview (UI trigger), tauri-plugin-notification, Tauri IPC Channels (`pulse://stream/snapshot-progress`)

- **Steps:**
  1. Boot app; confirm health OK
  2. Populate buffer with 500 synthetic spans (varying service_name, latency_ms, error flags) via OTLP gRPC ingest loop
  3. Subscribe to channel `pulse://stream/snapshot-progress` via Tauri test client's IPC Channel handler (async)
  4. Invoke TauRPC `snapshot.generate({time_range: [now-600s, now], token_budget: 25000})` via test client
  5. Assert response.markdown contains anomaly markers (regex: `⚠|🔴|critical.*path`)
  6. Assert response.token_count <= 25000 (strict)
  7. Assert response.dedup_count > 0 (non-raw OTLP dump evidenced by dedup)
  8. Assert response.markdown contains p50/p95/p99 latency aggregates (evidence of curated analysis)
  9. Await `pulse://stream/snapshot-progress` channel events (timeout 10s); assert final event signals completion
  10. Assert notification is emitted via IPC channel `pulse://stream/events` subscription (async); assert event payload includes token_count field (platform notification delivery to Notification Center / Action Center / freedesktop verified separately via tauri-driver headful E2E suite)

- **Verification signal:**
  - Step 5: regex match on markdown for anomaly markers
  - Step 6: response.token_count <= 25000
  - Step 7: response.dedup_count > 0
  - Step 9: channel completion event received within timeout
  - Step 10: notification event emitted with token_count field present
- **Cleanup:** unsubscribe from channels; as above

title: Scenario: P3 — MCP server query (agent-accessible telemetry)

data.head: #### Scenario: P3 — MCP server query (agent-accessible telemetry)

body: - **Surfaces involved:** MCP stdio sidecar (feature-gated), buffer access, JSON-RPC 2.0 contract

- **Steps:**
  1. Boot app with `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED=true --features mcp-server` via cargo build
  2. Spawn `./target/debug/andromeda-pulse --features mcp-server` via `tokio::process::Command` with stdin/stdout piped
  3. Populate buffer with 100 synthetic spans via OTLP ingest
  4. Write JSON-RPC 2.0 frame to sidecar stdin: `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"query_traces","arguments":{"time_range":["2026-05-02T16:10:00Z","2026-05-02T16:20:00Z"],"service_filter":"test-app","limit":100}}}`
  5. Parse stdout line-delimited JSON; extract `result.traces` array
  6. Assert `result.traces.length > 0`; verify each row has trace_id / span_name / duration_ms fields

- **Verification signal:**
  - Step 5: JSON-RPC response has `result` key (not `error`)
  - Step 6: `result.traces` is array with correct schema
- **Cleanup:** send SIGTERM to sidecar PID; verify exit code 0; verify no zombie process

- **Current residual (chunk 2026-08-17-conductor-e2e-verification-closure):** the subprocess steps above are committed ONLY for the 4 telemetry tools. The **incident**-tool read-back leg (`retrieve_telemetry_slice` / `retrieve_report` / `query_incident_list` / `mark_incident_resolved`) is committed only as **in-process `dispatch_tool`** assertions in `pulse-app/tests/e2e_p3_mcp_incident_tools.rs` — despite that file's `e2e_p3_` name, its own docstring points cross-process framing at `crates/mcp-server/tests/sidecar_subprocess.rs`, where the incident tools appear only as `tools/list` NAME assertions. The JSON-RPC subprocess form for the deterministic evidence read-back has been proven live as smoke evidence, not as a committed step. **Widened at chunk 2026-08-27-incident-persist-vs-resolve-write-race:** `mark_incident_resolved` gained an honest not-applied result for a write the corpus monotonic guard declines. **That half is DISCHARGED at chunk 2026-08-29-app-registry-reconciliation** — `pulse-app/tests/e2e_p3_mcp_resolve_content.rs` spawns the real sidecar subprocess and asserts `mark_incident_resolved`'s response CONTENT in both the applied and the guard-declined arms (feature-gated behind `--features mcp-server`, so outside the default workspace gate). The residual is therefore **re-scoped to the remaining three incident tools** — `retrieve_telemetry_slice` / `retrieve_report` / `query_incident_list` — which are still committed only as in-process `dispatch_tool` assertions. **The ninth tool, `retrieve_incident_events` (chunk 2026-10-02-incident-events-readable-through-mcp), shipped with the subprocess form COMMITTED** — `crates/mcp-server/tests/incident_events_subprocess.rs` and the real-producer → real-sidecar leg `pulse-app/tests/e2e_p3_mcp_incident_events_content.rs` (`--features mcp-server`) — so the residual stays exactly those three read-back tools. Tracked as `mcp-incident-read-back-cross-process-coverage` in §1.

title: Scenario: P4 — Plugin lifecycle (load, reload, invoke with capability scoping)

data.head: #### Scenario: P4 — Plugin lifecycle (load, reload, invoke with capability scoping)

body: - **Surfaces involved:** plugins module (WASM Component Model), TauRPC `plugins.list` / `plugins.reload` / `plugins.invoke`, `~/.andromeda-pulse/plugins/` filesystem

- **Steps:**
  1. Boot app; confirm health OK
  2. Stage fixture WASM module at `~/.andromeda-pulse/plugins/test-plugin.wasm` (pre-compiled minimal Component Model binary)
  3. Invoke TauRPC `plugins.reload()` via test client
  4. Invoke TauRPC `plugins.list()` via test client; assert response.plugins contains entry with name "test-plugin"
  5. Invoke TauRPC `plugins.invoke({plugin: "test-plugin", capability: "transform_spans", input: […100 synthetic spans…]})` via test client
  6. Assert response.transformed_spans.length > 0; verify output schema matches input
  7. Negative test: attempt `plugins.invoke({…, capability: "disallowed_capability"})` → assert rejection due to capability gating (not in plugin's WIT contract)

- **Verification signal:**
  - Step 4: response.plugins array contains name "test-plugin"
  - Step 6: response.transformed_spans schema valid
  - Step 7: gRPC Code::FAILED_PRECONDITION or AppError variant indicating capability denied
- **Cleanup:** remove `~/.andromeda-pulse/plugins/test-plugin.wasm`; invoke `plugins.reload()` to confirm removal

title: Scenario: P5 — Widget compact mode ↔ dashboard expansion ↔ tray icon visibility toggle

data.head: #### Scenario: P5 — Widget compact mode ↔ dashboard expansion ↔ tray icon visibility toggle

body: - **Surfaces involved:** desktop-webview (React layouts), desktop-native (tray icon), Tauri window management, TauRPC state sync

- **Status:** PARTIALLY DISCHARGED 2026-08-23, widened the same day. `cargo xtask webview-drive` drives **seventeen** stages in the live Tauri window on the Windows dev host — launch → boot-geometry → traces-empty → traces-populate → traces-scroll → native-menu-suppressed → connection-status → storm-incident → findings-window → report-window → report-copy → investigate → empty-states → dashboard-toggle → dashboard-close → **widget-close** → signpost-repeat — asserting each against the app's own obs log and/or the driver's DOM report. `widget-close` sends the app to the tray but is NO LONGER terminal — `signpost-repeat` follows it deliberately since `2026-08-24-headful-mechanics-probe-race-disposition`, restoring the widget to prove the close signpost fires on EVERY close; its obs half is STRENGTHENED since `2026-08-23-headful-leg-extension` — it requires the `ui.layout.transition {layout_mode_from: compact-widget, layout_mode_to: hidden}` record AND the `tray.signpost.shown` record carrying `window_label == "compact-widget"` (bare record presence no longer satisfies) after pressing the production `button[aria-label="Close to tray"]` — and it is no longer the only guard on `core:window:allow-close`: the `allow-show`+`allow-close` revoke mutation reddens FIVE stages (widget-close, findings-window, report-window, dashboard-toggle, dashboard-close) with every control still found and pressed. Two RED arms exist and are NOT equivalent: the telemetry-suppression arm is **code** (`--no-inject --expect-absent <STAGE>`, run every time it is invoked), while the capability-revoke arm remains **by hand** (see §1 `webview-drive-mutation-arm-not-gated`). The residual narrows to **window resize, tray-icon repaint and OS-notification delivery**, which stay deferred to a headful suite; those remain IPC-surrogate only
- **Agent-driven surrogate:** Verify IPC contract consistency via TauRPC `health` command; assert response shape validity

- **Steps (IPC contract surrogate only):**
  1. Boot app; confirm health OK
  2. Invoke TauRPC `health` command; inspect for optional window_state metadata (may not be present in current arch)
  3. Verify IPC response is valid JSON with required subsystem fields

- **Verification signal (contract level only):**
  - Step 3: IPC response shape is valid JSON; no window pixel validation

- **Full P5 coverage (headful tauri-driver):** Actual window resize, tray icon visibility toggle, and notification emission require `tauri-driver` headful mode with platform-specific GUI automation; documented separately in the tauri-driver E2E suite (see Section 9 CI Integration, E2E tests stage). **Corrected 2026-08-23:** headful tauri-driver is NO LONGER "not agent-driven" — `cargo xtask webview-drive` drives it agent-side end to end (operator ruling 2026-08-22), and since `2026-08-30-diagnostics-un-muting-harness-truth-sweep` it drives a 17-stage assembled path (16 at `2026-08-27-report-window-copy-affordance`; 15 at `2026-08-24-headful-mechanics-probe-race-disposition`; 13 at `2026-08-23-headful-leg-extension`; 7 at `2026-08-23-integration-ux-e2e-test`), not a single press. **Resize is no longer "deferred" — it is DECLINED on measurement:** `setWindowRect` reaches the WRY window and returns cleanly with `resize_delta {dw:0,dh:0}`, so no driver-side resize stage can exist on this host, and the same probe declined a drag stage for the same reason. What still defers is the tray-repaint / notification surface, not the headful mode itself — and the leg is still dev-host-only, not CI-wired (§9)

- **Current residual (per chunk #99 tag gate):** the P5 tray/window matrix is covered by the IPC surrogate above PLUS the browser-driven a11y chain (real Chromium against the built webview); the `tauri-driver` headful suite stays deferred (chunk #51 Path A' precedent). This is a documented residual, not a silent coverage claim.
- **Cleanup:** as above
- **Trade-off:** P5 is partially covered at agent-driven level (IPC contract) and fully covered at headful level (GUI automation); no gap in total coverage, only scoping boundary

title: Scenario: P6 — Real-time push of spans/metrics/logs via Tauri IPC Channel

data.head: #### Scenario: P6 — Real-time push of spans/metrics/logs via Tauri IPC Channel

body: - **Surfaces involved:** buffer (DuckDB), TauRPC IPC Channels (`pulse://stream/spans`, `pulse://stream/metrics`, `pulse://stream/logs`), desktop-webview (listener), Arrow IPC payloads

- **Steps:**
  1. Boot app; confirm health OK
  2. Subscribe to channel `pulse://stream/spans` via Tauri test client's IPC Channel handler (async)
  3. Send 50 synthetic gRPC trace spans to `:4317` via `tonic` client
  4. Await Channel event (timeout 5s); receive binary Arrow IPC payload
  5. Decode payload via `arrow_ipc::StreamReader::try_new(bytes, None)`; extract RecordBatch
  6. Assert schema column names == [trace_id, span_name, duration_ms, …]; assert RecordBatch.num_rows() > 0

- **Verification signal:**
  - Step 5: `StreamReader::try_new` succeeds (valid Arrow IPC format)
  - Step 6: schema and row count assertions pass
- **Cleanup:** unsubscribe from channel; as above

title: Scenario: P7 — Workspace detection (host project context correlation)

data.head: #### Scenario: P7 — Workspace detection (host project context correlation)

body: - **Surfaces involved:** workspace-detector module, TauRPC `workspace.detect` / `workspace.list`

- **Steps:**
  1. Boot app with CWD set to repository root (has `.andromeda/` marker by design)
  2. Invoke TauRPC `workspace.detect()` via test client
  3. Assert response.workspace object contains: project_name (string), root_path (canonical absolute path), vcs_type ("git"), vcs_root (path to `.git/`)
  4. Invoke TauRPC `workspace.list()` via test client; assert response is array of detected workspace metadata

- **Verification signal:**
  - Step 3: response.workspace has required keys
  - Step 4: response is array with at least 1 entry
- **Notes:** Out-of-repo test scenarios untestable in standard agent-driven harness (assumes CWD is repository)
- **Cleanup:** as above

title: 7. Test Data & Fixtures

body: **Fixture library:** `rstest` 0.26.1 (Rust parameterized / fixture decorator pattern)
**Seed strategies:**
| Data type | Strategy | Lifecycle |

| **Persistent data — DuckDB rows** | OTLP ingest via `tonic` gRPC client + the `test_support::otlp` factories (or their resource-level batches handed to the buffer) | per-test fresh via ephemeral in-memory DuckDB + `tempfile::TempDir` |
