| **WASM fixtures** | Pre-compiled minimal Component Model `.wasm` binaries in `tests/fixtures/plugins/` (committed to repo) | per-suite (shared read-only) |
| **Config overrides** | Environment variables (`ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR=$TMPDIR`, `RUST_LOG=debug`) | per-test |
| **Randomized data** | `proptest` 1.10.0 arbitrary generators (OTLP invariant tests, stress tests) | seeded deterministically per test (regression files in `proptest-regressions/`) |
| **Time-sensitive data** | `tokio::time::pause()` + `tokio::time::advance(Duration)` for retention window tests | injected per test |
**Self-bootstrapping requirement:**
- Tests MUST seed their own OTLP data — no pre-populated DuckDB snapshots

- Builder factories: one set, `test_support::otlp` in the dev-only member `crates/test-support` (`span_event()`, `span()`, `metric_point()`, `gauge()`, `log_record()`, `resource()`), built at chunk 2026-10-10-shared-telemetry-test-data. Event time, service and string attributes are settable; every default is fixed and crosses the write boundary unmasked (a default batch of every kind reads `rows_ingested` 7, `redactions_applied` 0, `append_rejections` 0). The per-crate `MockTraceSpan` / `MockArrowBatch` / `MockMetricPoint` trio this bullet once named was never built and is dropped; no Arrow-batch factory exists (§3 item 6 / §1 `test-data-bootstrap-factories-unimplemented`). Tests the factories do not yet serve keep self-bootstrapping via OTLP ingest through the live receiver, per-test in-memory DuckDB seeding, and `rstest` fixtures
- `boot` command runs migrations (if any) and fixtures automatically (N/A for in-memory DuckDB)
**Test data lifecycle:**
- **Per-test:** isolated via `tempfile::TempDir` + in-memory DuckDB
- **Per-session:** `cleanup` command removes test data directory; Rust `drop(temp_dir)` on test exit
- **CI:** ephemeral test environment per pipeline run (GitHub Actions runner is stateless)

title: 8. Mocking & Stubbing Discipline

body: **What to mock:**
- **External HTTP APIs:** Mock `tauri-plugin-updater`'s GitHub Releases fetch via `httpmock` 0.7.x or fallback `mockito` 1.6.x; mock latest.json with Minisign signature (valid and invalid variants)
- **External services not under test:** None in current arch (loopback-only OTLP)
- **Time:** `tokio::time::pause()` + `advance()` built into tokio (no third-party) for retention window tests
- **Filesystem:** `tempfile::TempDir` + `assert_fs` symlink helpers for path canonicalization negative tests (real temp dir, not mocked)
- **Random sources:** `proptest` 1.10.0 with seed control via `proptest-regressions/` regression files
**What NOT to mock:**
- Pure functions in modules under test (test directly)
- DuckDB at integration level (use in-memory instance per test)
- OTLP receivers in E2E tests (drive via live `tonic` client + `reqwest`)
- Code paths the agent must verify end-to-end (those go in E2E scenarios)
**Mocking libraries (specific from research):**
| Concern | Library | Pattern |
| HTTP mocking (updater latest.json) | `httpmock` 0.7.x (MSRV check needed; fallback `mockito` 1.6.x if MSRV friction) | `MockServer::start()` + `mock.assert()` for signature verification tests |
| Time mocking (retention window) | `tokio::time::pause()` (built-in, no dependency) | `#[tokio::test(start_paused = true)]` + `tokio::time::advance(Duration::from_secs(700))` |
| Process mocking (MCP sidecar) | `tokio::process::Command` (built-in) | spawn, pipe stdin/stdout, send JSON-RPC 2.0 frames |
| OTLP client stub | `tonic` 0.14.5 (same library as receiver) | `TraceServiceClient::connect("http://127.0.0.1:4317")` for live receiver tests |
| HTTP client stub | `reqwest` 0.12.x + `axum-test` 18.7.0 | `axum-test::TestServer` for unit tests; `reqwest::Client` for E2E receiver tests |
| Trait stub (Buffer/Viz boundaries) | `mockall` 0.13.x with `#[automock]` macro | generate `MockBufferClient` etc. for IPC procedure tests without full pipeline |
**Anti-monkey-patching:** All traits used for testing have constructor-injected `Arc<dyn Trait>` dependencies (not runtime patching)

title: 9. CI Integration

body: **Platform:** GitHub Actions (per upstream-context arch CI/CD Platform)
**Pipeline structure:**
| Stage | Runs | Parallel | Cache |

| **Lint + tests (`lint-test` job)** | one job on `ubuntu-22.04`, check name `lint / test (ubuntu-22.04)` (no matrix since chunk 2026-10-09-ci-on-linux-alone; pinned by `ci_workflow_runs_on_linux_only`): `cargo fmt --check` + the "No Cyrillic in sources" step, `cargo xtask check:english-sources` (since chunk 2026-10-01-real-model-incident-surfacing, replacing an inline `shell: python` scan that crashed with `UnicodeEncodeError` on the Windows runner; ASCII-only `::error` annotations + a `{verdict, hits, files_scanned}` verdict, exit 0 clean · 1 findings · 2 cannot-evaluate; measured `clean` on windows-latest, `ci#36893004900`) + `cargo clippy --workspace` → the xtask gates → `cargo xtask test` (the step's name since chunk 2026-10-10-no-gate-stands-while-reading-nothing); directly after it, since chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process, the step `Door refuses another account` — a plain `run` step with no `if:`, no `continue-on-error` and no upload, which runs `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci --no-tests=fail --success-output immediate -E 'binary(integration_door) & (test(=another_account_is_refused_at_each_of_three_layers) | test(=another_account_through_the_bridge_receives_nothing))'` (two arms since chunk 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door; the first alone until it), keeps the output in `$RUNNER_TEMP/door-other-account.txt`, and exits non-zero unless nextest exited 0, the file is not empty, it holds `door other-account arm: directory refused, socket mode refused, account check refused` and it holds `door bridge other-account arm: no byte reached another account through the bridge, the account check refused` (else `::error::the bridge other-account arm did not read the account check refusing`) — so either arm that skipped, or the three-layer arm reading a layer open, fails the step although it passes in the workspace run; it needs `python3` and a second account on the runner reachable by `sudo -n` (root, and `-u nobody`), and the step's own text holds no `sudo`; pinned by pins and `bash -e` witnesses in `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs` (42 tests since chunk 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door, among them `door_other_account_step_fails_a_bridge_arm_that_skipped`; 41 at the previous chunk, 35 before it), `cargo` standing as a shell function that prints a captured file; green on `ci#38097928056`, where `nobody` was refused by the kernel at the 0700 directory and at the 0600 socket (errno 13) and root passed both and was closed by the door's account check at all three layers; the workspace run counted 3174 tests on the dev host at that chunk (3132 at the previous one); green again on `ci#38227488889` (the pushed tip `2595b5cc`, chunk 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door), where the relay's four other-account readings (`nobody` and root, at the modes as made and with the outer layers opened) each exited 1 with 0 bytes on standard output and the three-layer readings repeated; the workspace run counted 3186 tests at that chunk. **The door is PROVISIONAL — a boundary widening, one item:** the endpoint, the owner check, the reach of the nine tools and of the one write, the write-switch variable and this workflow step, which runs a client as a second account, are the operator's answers (the pc overseer: at that chunk's P4 dialog, 2026-10-10, and the operator's reading of 2026-10-11 at its wrap); the founder's own word is owed on the surface itself, nothing of it is ratified, and every other statement of the door in this plan rests on this one. Then, as unconditional steps, `cargo xtask perf:slo-load`, which selects its one test with `--workspace -E 'binary(perf_slo_10k_spans)'` so it reuses the test build (chunk 2026-09-29-ci-wall-time-and-round-trips), then `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile perf-samples --no-tests=fail` — every nextest invocation of the job fails on a selection that matches no test since chunk 2026-10-10-no-gate-stands-while-reading-nothing: this line spells `--no-tests=fail`, and `cargo xtask test` and `cargo xtask perf:slo-load` pass nextest the same flag from argument lists a pin reads (`empty_input_tests::every_nextest_argument_list_fails_on_an_empty_selection`, with `test:coverage` and `perf:load-profiles`; nextest's own exit is 4, and the verb maps a failed status to exit 1); the three steps ran 2908, 1 and 1 tests on `ci#38042949735` — (the `pulse-app/tests/perf_budget_samples.rs` producer: real obs sink into `target/tmp/perf-budget-samples/`, 30 000 spans over 30 s, 3 buffer ticks, 50 snapshots), `cargo xtask perf:budget --data-dir target/tmp/perf-budget-samples --require memory,snapshot`, and an `if: always()` upload `logs-perf-samples-${{ runner.os }}` (chunk 2026-09-30-perf-budget-gate-reads-real-samples). The workspace tests need a C compiler (`cc`) on the runner since chunk 2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-named-from-a-run: the xtask `harness_witness` controls build `scripts/exit-witness.c` with the runner's own `cc` — no setup step; a missing `cc` fails them, never skips them — green in the `lint / test` job of `ci#38019133294`, the compiler's version not read from that run. They also need the host's Xlib, `libX11.so.6`, since chunk 2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-closed: `unit_xlib_threads`'s found-arm pin loads it through `pulse_app::xlib_threads::init_from` — no setup step; a runner without the library fails that pin, never skips it — green in the `lint / test` job of `ci#38026637514` (attempt 1). The workspace tests also need a Python 3 interpreter on the runner since chunk 2026-10-05-l4-runs-the-founder-s-pick-with-its-authors-settings: `unit_l4_grammar` runs the vendored stdlib-only `pulse-app/vendor/llama-cpp/json_schema_to_grammar.py` (llama.cpp b9305, MIT) through the runner's own `python3` / `python` — no setup step; a missing interpreter fails the test, never skips it — green on ubuntu-22.04 / macos-latest / windows-latest, `ci#37327846820`. And they need `node` on PATH since chunk 2026-10-10-no-ci-step-reads-nothing: `a11y_regression_detector_fails_when_its_baseline_is_absent` (`pulse-app/tests/a11y_perf_workflow.rs`) runs the a11y regression detector with the runner's `node`, which the job's `Setup Node` step provides — a missing `node` fails the pin, never skips it — green in the `lint / test` job of `ci#38035474359`, the Node version not read from that run. And they need `bash` and `awk` on PATH since chunk 2026-10-10-no-gate-stands-while-reading-nothing: four witness tests in `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs` cut the `Enforce coverage thresholds` step's script out of `ci.yml` by the step's name and run it with `bash -e` over constructed `lcov.info` files, and five xtask pins (`empty_input_tests`; six since chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed) run `xtask/ci/quarantine-tracking-check.sh` with `bash` over scratch roots — no setup step; a missing `bash` or `awk` fails the witness and a missing `bash` fails the quarantine pins, never skips them — green in the `lint / test` job of `ci#38042949735`, neither tool's version read from that run. And since chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed the workspace run needs `bash`, a Linux `/proc`, an advisory file lock under `target/` (`target/test-ports/`) and the engine built in the test profile (a `--workspace` run builds it): the two `xtask/tests` binaries (25 tests) run the committed `scripts/agent-run.sh` and the built `harness:engine-cycle` verb on real console engines, and three new spawned arms of `integration_console_engine.rs` read `/proc` — no setup step, and the workflow is not edited; the same tests run in the `mcp-test` and `coverage` jobs; green on `ci#38079305603`, where the workspace run counted 3112 tests (3064 on the previous chunk's verdict run) and the failing-cycle pin passed in `lint / test`, a job that builds only the test profile, by running the committed script from a scratch root that links the built engine | one job, parallel with every other job | deps + rustup (`shared-key: lint-test-${{ runner.os }}`, which resolves to `lint-test-Linux` alone; `cache-on-failure: true`; the key the `mcp-test` and `a11y` jobs restore read-only) |

| **Release build** | no `release` job since chunk 2026-10-09-ci-on-linux-alone (it built macOS and Windows only, and no CI job compiles or tests on those systems now). The release-profile builds the workflow runs are the `supply-chain` job's `cargo auditable build --workspace --release` and the `boot` job's `cargo build --workspace --release --features mcp-server`, both pinned by `ci_workflow_keeps_the_linux_release_build_witnesses` (`pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs`); no frame boot step (the CI Windows `perf:frame-sample` leg shipped in `d708ad7` was removed in `c6eb395`) | inside those two jobs | none of its own: no job writes `release-${{ runner.os }}` any more (the cache readings are in architecture §Infrastructure Patterns → CI/CD approach) |

| **MCP-feature tests (`mcp-test` job)** | Linux: `cargo nextest run --workspace --features mcp-server --profile ci --no-tests=fail` — a selection that matches no test fails the job (since chunk 2026-10-10-no-gate-stands-while-reading-nothing; pinned by `ci_workflow_nextest_runs_fail_on_an_empty_selection`; the runner's cargo-nextest 0.9.133 took the flag and ran 2946 tests, as measured on `ci#38042949735`) | own job | restore-only `lint-test-Linux` |

| **A11y suite** | `cargo xtask test:a11y` — **runs in CI today**, measured green on run `ci#36574279289` (6/6 checks, `464f2a3`; chunk 2026-09-29-p-025-hue-shift-observable-made-gradable, the first real CI run after the workflow-parse fix), with the Playwright chromium browser installed before it; since chunk 2026-09-29-ci-wall-time-and-round-trips in its own `a11y` job, on `ubuntu-22.04` alone since chunk 2026-10-09-ci-on-linux-alone (check name `a11y (ubuntu-22.04)`) — `npm run build --prefix pulse-app/ui` → Playwright chromium → `cargo xtask test:a11y`, uploads `a11y-violations-*` / `playwright-a11y-report-*` `if: always()` (each failing its step when it finds no file, since chunk 2026-10-10-no-ci-step-reads-nothing), rust cache restored read-only from `lint-test-${{ runner.os }}` (`xtask/src/main.rs:` delegates to `npm run test:a11y --prefix pulse-app/ui`): `verify:contrast` → Playwright/axe → Lighthouse → pa11y → aggregator → regression-detector, which reads the baseline committed in the tree (`pulse-app/ui/tests-a11y/baselines/a11y-violations-summary.json`) and, since chunk 2026-10-10-no-ci-step-reads-nothing, exits 1 with `regression-detector: baseline not found at {path}` when that file is absent (pinned by `a11y_regression_baseline_is_committed_in_the_tree` and `a11y_regression_detector_fails_when_its_baseline_is_absent`, `pulse-app/tests/a11y_perf_workflow.rs`; the absent arm is held by the pin on the dev host and was not read on a runner). The job downloads nothing: its PR-only `a11y-violations-base` download had no producer in any workflow (`Artifact not found` on `ci#38031822696`) and left at that chunk | n/a (single Chromium worker) | node + `npm ci` + `npm run build` (the harness serves `ui/dist`); the zero-new-tuple diff reads the tree baseline, nothing is downloaded | **MEASURED 2026-08-23-a11y-verification:** this table previously listed no a11y stage, which read as "the a11y suite is not CI-wired" — false since chunk #99. Gate conditions are unchanged (axe critical/serious = 0, Lighthouse ≥ 90, pa11y 0 errors, zero new baseline tuples). |

| **Supply chain** | ci.yml `supply-chain` job: SHA-pinned setup-node → the Cranelift-only WASM assertion → `cargo xtask check:npm-supply-chain` as a plain `run:` step (exit 0 green · 1 findings/policy red · 2 cannot-evaluate) — the npm advisory/license/ban gate over `pulse-app/ui`, policy at `pulse-app/ui/npm-policy.json`; the gate step itself needs NO `npm ci` (the license walk and `npm audit` are lockfile-only) and runs BEFORE the job's own `npm ci` + `npm run build` steps, so a red gate skips the install, the UI build and the auditable build (as measured at chunk `2026-10-06-npm-supply-chain-gate-is-green-again`: those steps read `skipped` on the red commits and `success` on `fc4ebdf`) ; the job's `cargo auditable build --workspace --release` is the Linux workspace release build (the duplicate plain release build was removed, chunk 2026-09-29-ci-wall-time-and-round-trips); the job also runs `cargo audit` as the plain step `run: cargo audit` (step `cargo audit (RustSec advisory DB)`, since chunk 2026-10-09-supply-chain-job-same-on-push-and-pull-request): no action, no token, no soft-fail, the runner image's own `cargo-audit`; exit 0 clean (informational advisories allowed) · 1 a vulnerability · 2 could not evaluate, red on 1 and on 2; the same on a `pull_request` run and on a `push` run (green on the push run `ci#37964887106` on `main`); pinned by `ci_workflow_audit_step_is_a_plain_run_step` and by the `cargo audit` entry of `ci_workflow_test_gates_no_continue_on_error`; its red-on-a-finding arm is measured on the dev host only (a control lockfile: exit 1, `RUSTSEC-2020-0071`), not on a runner | n/a | cargo, restore-only `boot-Linux` — landed chunk `2026-08-30-npm-advisory-coverage` |

| **Staged artifacts** | ci.yml: `cargo xtask check:staged-artifacts` as a plain named `run:` step directly after the capability-drift step (exit 0 staged-clean · 1 staged-drift · 2 cannot-evaluate) — asserts the git-index copies of `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` + all `pulse-app/capabilities/*.json` against `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` / `staged_gate::EXPECTED_GRANTS`; NO third-party action added, workflow `permissions:` untouched | n/a | deps + rustup — landed chunk `2026-08-30-staged-bindings-assertion` |

| **Boot smoke (harness)** | ci.yml's Linux `boot` job (chunk 2026-09-29-ci-wall-time-and-round-trips): `cargo build --workspace --release --features mcp-server` → `Build the exit witness` → the "Boot pulse-app smoke" step → `Boot series (equal source)` → `cargo xtask ci-gates` over the log the smoke wrote (skipped when the smoke or the series fails; since chunk 2026-10-10-no-gate-stands-while-reading-nothing the verb reads two arms over the `agent-latest.jsonl*` family under the resolved log dir — zero-spans, the family holds at least one record, and zero-panic, no `app.panic.fatal` record at level ERROR — exit 0 PASS with exactly `ci-gates: zero-spans PASS ({n} log records across {k} file(s))` and `ci-gates: zero-panic PASS` · 1 FAIL on members holding zero records or on a panic record, named by its member's file name and line alone · 2 cannot-evaluate when the log dir is absent or holds no family member, `::error::ci-gates: cannot-evaluate (no agent-latest.jsonl* file in the log dir)`; it prints no heartbeat line and no perf-budget or frame line, and makes no heartbeat gap check — since chunk 2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine the gap check over the console engine's log is the cycle step's, next, and none is made over the window's log; as measured on `ci#38042949735`: 110 log records across 1 file, both PASS lines) → `Console engine cycle` (since that chunk: `if: always()`, a plain `run: cargo xtask harness:engine-cycle --data-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/andromeda-pulse-engine-data"`, no soft-fail key; it names no `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` and runs on a data dir other than the job's own; its `check:engine-log` grades the engine's log on seven arms, the `heartbeat-gap` arm — a gap over 45 000 ms between consecutive `ingest.tick` / `buffer.tick` / `connection.tick` records — among them: §3 → Per-chunk gate discipline, Engine cycle gate form) → upload `logs-boot-${{ runner.os }}` `if: always()` → upload `logs-engine-${{ runner.os }}` (since that chunk: `if: always()`, path `${{ runner.temp }}/andromeda-pulse-engine-data/logs/` — the engine's log family plus the boot verb's `boot.log` and `build.log` — `if-no-files-found: error`, `retention-days: 14`) (`ci-gates` runs in this job only; no job of the workflow runs on macOS or Windows). The two steps around the smoke, since chunk 2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-named-from-a-run: `Build the exit witness` (`cc -shared -fPIC -O2` builds `scripts/exit-witness.c` into `$RUNNER_TEMP` and names it through `$GITHUB_ENV` as `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_EXIT_WITNESS_LIB`; no `LD_PRELOAD` in the step — the boot verb sets it on the window app's spawn line alone, and `boot engine` sets none) and `Boot series (equal source)` (`if: always()`, a plain `run: cargo xtask harness:boot-series --count 7`, no soft-fail key). `cargo xtask harness:boot-series --count N` (1 to 16) boots the release app N more times, ordinals 2 to N+1 (the smoke is ordinal 1), each one cycle (`boot`, `harness:settled`, `status`, `cleanup`; after a failed `boot` the two middle verbs are skipped, `cleanup` always runs) under its own `xvfb-run` on its own data dir `series/boot-{ordinal}/`, a cycle bounded at 1200 s; it prints one pretty-JSON verdict `{verdict, boots, settled, ended, other, per_boot}`, also written to `logs/boot-series.json`: `all-settled` exit 0 · `self-ended` 1 · `not-all-settled` 1 · `cannot-evaluate` 2. So one run of the job reads eight boots, and a boot that ended by itself fails the job (`self-ended`), in either of two ways: its settle verdict reads `ended`, or — since chunk 2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-closed — it ended before the boot verb read ready. Such a boot takes no settle verdict (its `verdict`, `app_exit_record` and `windows_settled` stay null); the series reads its exit record and witness label from the boot's own data dir into `ended` and `exit_witness` and counts it `ended`, unless the record is the boot verb's own `signal 15 (TERM)` or `signal 9 (KILL)` or there is none (those stay `other`). Ordinal 1 is listed from the smoke's own exit record and witness label when the top data dir holds no `logs/harness-settled.json` and that record is an own end, and stays out of the counts. The member sets, the `cycle` labels, the verdict set, the exit codes and the kept files are unchanged. That read never ran on a runner (below); it is read on a real process by a local leg and pinned per arm. As measured on `ci#38019133294`, before that change: red, seven of eight boots ended by themselves, the series step 4 min 27 s. As measured on `ci#38026637514` (attempts 1 to 3, one merge commit): each attempt 8 of 8 boots settled, `boot-series.json` `all-settled` with `"settled": 7`; 24 boots, 0 self-ended, all of which reached ready. The smoke step (since chunk 2026-10-09-boot-smoke-s-early-exit-found-and-closed), after the Linux system libraries (Tauri/WebKitGTK/dbus/xvfb) install: it creates the data dir's `logs/`, then inside ONE `xvfb-run -e "$ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR/logs/xvfb.log"` runs, in order, `bash scripts/agent-run.sh boot || exit 1` → `cargo xtask harness:settled; a=$?` → `status; b=$?` → `cleanup; c=$?` → `test "$a$b$c" = 000` — no `set -e` in the inner script, so `cleanup` runs whatever the two before it returned. `cargo xtask harness:settled [--timeout-seconds N]` (default 30, refused below 8) reads `settled` (exit 0: an `app.boot.window.navigation` record for each of `compact-widget`, `main`, `findings`, `report`, and a live pid) · `ended` (exit 1: the pid is dead) · `not-settled` (exit 1: the timeout passed) · `cannot-evaluate` (exit 2), prints `{verdict, pid, ended, app_exit_record, windows_settled, display, session_bus, exit_witness}` — eight members since chunk 2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-named-from-a-run, `exit_witness` one closed label (`unset` (no witness file) · `unreadable` · `loaded` · `exit-call` · `runtime-exit` · `no-record`), the verdict set, the exit codes and the other seven unchanged — and writes the same object to `logs/harness-settled.json`; the uploaded `logs-boot-Linux` still holds the smoke's five files (`agent-latest.jsonl.{date}`, `boot.log`, `build.log`, `harness-settled.json`, `xvfb.log`) and, since the same chunk, `exit-witness.jsonl`, `boot-series.json` and `series/boot-{2..8}/` with five files each (four where a boot took no settle verdict) — all harness-written, none read by the product; the series' own data dirs (`series/boot-{ordinal}/`, not under `logs/`) are not uploaded. Pinned by four workflow tests in `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs` (the order inside one `xvfb-run`; cleanup running regardless; the error file under `logs/` and that dir uploaded; no soft-fail key on the step) and, for the two added steps, three more in the same file (the library built before the smoke and named through `$GITHUB_ENV`; the series after the smoke and before `ci-gates` under `if: always()`; no `continue-on-error`, `retry` or `|| true` on the series step) and, for the cycle step and its upload, four more (the cycle after `ci-gates` under `if: always()` with its exact `run` line; a data dir of its own; no `continue-on-error`, `retry` or `|| true`; the one upload named `logs-engine-…`, after the cycle, with its four lines). As measured on `ci#38065768197`: the cycle step `success`, `logs-engine-Linux` 5482 B. The four invocations share `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR`, which every job exports to `$GITHUB_ENV` from a step right after harden-runner — `runner.*` is unavailable in workflow- and job-level `env:`, pinned by the `workflow_env_references_no_step_only_context` and `data_dir_export_precedes_every_consumer` self-lint guards (chunk 2026-09-29-p-025-hue-shift-observable-made-gradable) — **GATING since chunk 2026-08-30-agent-harness-teardown-truth** (`continue-on-error: true` dropped, operator-approved: a truthful exit code CI ignores stays ignored) | n/a | deps + rustup (`shared-key: boot-Linux`, `cache-on-failure: true`; the boot verb's own pre-build rides it) |
| **Unit tests** | `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci --filter-expr 'not (integration or e2e)'` | yes | deps + rustup |

| **Integration tests** | `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci --filter-expr 'integration'` | partial — per-process isolation separates processes, not port numbers: a port bound to 0, read and released can be handed to another test that starts at the same instant. As measured at chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed, one of seven hand runs of the three port-using binaries failed one arm on a picked port another process held, and after the change 14 of 14 hand runs were green (a count, not an exclusion). The binaries `agent_run_shell`, `engine_cycle_refusals` and `integration_console_engine` therefore claim each port under an advisory file lock in `target/test-ports/`. Since chunk 2026-10-10-shared-telemetry-test-data the claim is ONE definition, `test_support::ports::claim_port` (dev-only member `crates/test-support`), and a fourth binary takes it: `pulse-app/tests/integration_engine_boot.rs` hands the engine two claimed ports in each of its four in-process arms and no longer picks by bind-and-release — the carry the route entry `Shared telemetry test data` owned is closed, and no test in that file, `xtask/src/harness_ready.rs` or `xtask/src/engine_cycle.rs` binds port 0 and releases it. Two `xtask` unit tests and the member's own four tests claim too. As measured at that chunk, seven of seven hand runs of the four binaries were green (a count, not an exclusion). Since chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process a fifth binary takes the claim, `pulse-app/tests/integration_door.rs` (its spawned engines' two ports), and `integration_engine_boot.rs` holds 11 tests (6 before; five door arms added) — "four in-process arms" above is the reading of chunk 2026-10-10-shared-telemetry-test-data. At the door chunk seven of seven repeated runs of the five binaries were green, 48 tests each (a count, not an exclusion) | deps + rustup |

| **E2E tests** | `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci --filter-expr 'e2e'` + `cargo xtask webview-drive [--expect-absent <STAGE>] [--no-inject]` (NOT `wdio` — no wdio runner is installed) | n/a — no job carries a matrix, and this leg is wired into no workflow | deps + rustup + webdriver. **MEASURED 2026-08-23: the webview-drive leg is NOT wired into any workflow yet** — it runs on the dev host only, and that is still true after it grew to a 17-stage path (`2026-08-30-diagnostics-un-muting-harness-truth-sweep`; 16 at `2026-08-27-report-window-copy-affordance`; 15 at `2026-08-24-headful-mechanics-probe-race-disposition`; 13 at `2026-08-23-headful-leg-extension`; 7 at `2026-08-23-integration-ux-e2e-test`). Wiring it requires an `msedgedriver` on the runner matched to that runner's WebView2/Edge build, exposed via `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MSEDGEDRIVER_PATH`; absent that, the leg skips clean rather than failing — so a CI wiring must assert the leg RAN (its per-stage report), never just its exit code. A CI run would also need `node` on the runner and the injector prebuilt, since the leg spawns `crates/ingest/examples/inject_demo` by path |

| **Coverage report** | `cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --lcov --output-path lcov.info --summary-only`, with `xtask/` excluded from the measure TEMPORARILY via `COVERAGE_IGNORE_FILENAME_REGEX` (see §10) | own `coverage` job | registry only (`shared-key: coverage`, `cache-targets: false`, `cache-on-failure: true` — an instrumented target cache would not fit the 10 GB repository cap, so the instrumented build runs uncached every round) |

| **Quality gates** | Parse lcov.info; assert coverage >= 75% line / 85% function (no branch threshold: retired, PROVISIONAL — §4 Coverage target); a report tracking 0 lines or 0 functions fails the step (`::error::lcov.info tracks {n} lines and {m} functions — coverage gate cannot pass a report that tracks nothing`, exit 1), and an absent `lcov.info` fails it (since chunk 2026-10-10-no-gate-stands-while-reading-nothing; the step's own script is run by four witness tests in `pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs`); assert zero flaky tests | n/a | n/a |

**Matrix builds:** none. Each of the six jobs of `ci.yml` declares `runs-on: ubuntu-22.04`, with no `strategy` block and no `needs:` edge, and the workflow names no other system, matrix value or `runner.os ==` condition — pinned by `ci_workflow_runs_on_linux_only` (`pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs`; chunk 2026-10-09-ci-on-linux-alone). The other-system arms of the code and the `.ps1` harness halves have no CI witness; they leave with the later P-113 route entries.

**Test report format:** the Rust suite writes no JUnit XML and no reporter action reads one: `cargo xtask test` asks nextest for `libtest-json`, `.config/nextest.toml` holds no `junit` key, and no workflow uses `dorny/test-reporter` (as measured at chunk 2026-10-10-no-ci-step-reads-nothing, where the `Upload nextest junit artifact` step left `ci.yml` — it had found no file on `ci#38031822696`). A run is read by its exit code and the nextest output in the job log; no inline PR annotation is produced. The webview suite's own `target/junit-ui.xml` (vitest; §1 and §4) is written and stands
**Build failure conditions:**
- Any unit / integration / E2E test fails (exit code != 0)

- The Linux boot-smoke harness cycle fails — `boot` non-zero (build failure, or no `ready` verdict inside the readiness window; the step ends there), `cargo xtask harness:settled` non-zero (`ended` or `not-settled` exit 1, `cannot-evaluate` exit 2), `status` not `running-healthy`, or `cleanup` emitting any non-`clean` verdict token (exit 1); `cleanup` runs whatever `harness:settled` and `status` returned, and the step passes only when all three exit 0. Since chunk 2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-named-from-a-run the `boot` job also fails when its `Build the exit witness` step fails, or when `cargo xtask harness:boot-series --count 7` is non-zero — `self-ended` (a boot ended by itself: its settle verdict read `ended`, or, since chunk 2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-closed, it took no settle verdict and its exit record is an end the app made itself, any record but `signal 15 (TERM)` / `signal 9 (KILL)`) or `not-all-settled` exit 1, `cannot-evaluate` exit 2; the series runs `if: always()` after the smoke, with no soft-fail key, and `ci-gates` is skipped when the smoke or the series fails; where it runs, the job also fails when `cargo xtask ci-gates` is non-zero — exit 1 when the log family holds zero records or an `app.panic.fatal` record at ERROR, exit 2 when the log dir holds no `agent-latest.jsonl*` member (since chunk 2026-10-10-no-gate-stands-while-reading-nothing an absent log no longer reads exit 0); since chunk 2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine the job also fails when `cargo xtask harness:engine-cycle` is non-zero — `fail` exit 1 (any verb exit other than 0 or 2, an ERROR record in the engine's log family, or a witness file) or `cannot-evaluate` exit 2 (a refusal, a verb exit of 2, a verb that did not run) — the step running `if: always()` whatever the smoke, the series and `ci-gates` returned, with no soft-fail key
- Line coverage < 75% OR function < 85%, OR an `lcov.info` that is absent or tracks 0 lines or 0 functions (no branch condition: retired, PROVISIONAL — §4 Coverage target)

- The `lint-test` step `Door refuses another account` fails (since chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process): its one nextest selection (two arms since chunk 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door) exits non-zero or matches no test, its captured output is empty, or the output lacks either arm's sentence — the three-layer sentence or the bridge sentence — the case when either arm skipped for want of a second account, the three-layer arm read the socket's mode as not refusing, or the relay arm did not read the account check refusing; no soft-fail key, pinned by `ci_workflow_runs_the_door_other_account_arm_after_the_test_step_with_no_soft_fail`, the step witnesses and `door_other_account_step_fails_a_bridge_arm_that_skipped`
- Flaky test detected (any test flake is quarantine + manual fix required; no auto-retry)
- Clippy warnings (deny) OR fmt check fails OR deny bans violations (`cargo deny check`)

- An upload step of `ci.yml` finds no file: each of the seven uploads (the seventh, `logs-engine-${{ runner.os }}`, since chunk 2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine) carries `if-no-files-found: error`, the first six since chunk 2026-10-10-no-ci-step-reads-nothing (pinned by `ci_workflow_uploads_fail_when_they_find_no_file`; read on a runner only where the producer did not run, `ci#38034700885`, never where one ran and wrote nothing; the a11y upload has three path members and fails only when none matches)
- The a11y regression baseline is absent from the tree, or the run holds a violation tuple it lacks (the A11y suite row above)

No step of `ci.yml` carries `continue-on-error` and none downloads an artifact, so no condition above is softened: `ci_workflow_test_gates_no_continue_on_error` reads every step block (its listed-gate arm keeps 14 commands, `cargo audit` among them) and `ci_workflow_makes_no_download_without_a_producer` holds any later download to an artifact some workflow uploads (`pulse-app/tests/quality_gate_workflow.rs`; since chunk 2026-10-10-no-ci-step-reads-nothing).
**Cargo deny enforcement:**

```toml
[bans]
multiple-versions = "deny"
# Enforces: tonic 0.14.x pinned (no 0.13.x duplicate via opentelemetry-otlp transitive)
```
**Cranelift-only WASM enforcement:**

```bash
# CI step: verify wasmtime Cargo.lock has Cranelift enabled
cargo tree -p wasmtime | grep -q "cranelift" || { echo "FAILED: non-Cranelift wasmtime"; exit 1; }
```

SHIPPED at chunk `2026-08-29-advisory-backlog` as the named `run:` step "Cranelift-only WASM backend assertion (test-plan §9)" in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s `supply-chain` job (a plain `run:` step — no new action, so no SHA-pin obligation). The snippet had been aspirational until then — measured MISSING from ci.yml at that chunk's research.
**Capability verification matrix (CI step, runs after capability-drift):**

`cargo xtask verify:capability-matrix` reads two fixed in-repo files, with no path argument and no environment variable: `docs/capability-record.json`, the one current record of all 82 capability ids P-001–P-082, each `claimed` or `retired` (36 claimed and 46 retired, as measured at chunk 2026-10-10-capability-record-re-based), and `andromeda-pulse-0.4.0/working-route.md`. Exit 0 clean · 1 findings · 2 cannot-evaluate (the record absent, unreadable, not JSON or without a `capabilities` array; the route absent or unreadable). It holds all 82 ids to the form — the id set exactly P-001…P-082 once each, one of the two dispositions, the `legend` equal to the module's three closed sets — and validates the proofs of claimed ids only. A claimed entry names its carrying 0.4.0 requirement ids in `carried_by` (P-083…P-129; empty only with a `note` saying why none carries it), has at least one scenario that is not `source-evidence`, a known scenario kind (`nextest-file` · `ui-test` · `a11y-spec` · `ci-script` · `source-evidence`, each a file ref that must exist, its `contains` anchor found; `by-construction` · `external` · `manual`, each needing the entry's `note`) and one of nine verification modes (automated-nextest, automated-a11y, automated-e2e, xtask-gate, env-gated-runtime, manual-sr-supplemental, by-construction, dynamic-external, manual). A retired entry carries no scenario, mode or `carried_by`; it names its `surfaces` (closed words `window` · `model` · `desktop` · `workspace` · `training-export` · `corpus-encryption`), the working-route entry titles that remove it in `removed_by` (each a title the route carries) and its `guard` (`runs` · `part` · `none`, with what a CI job runs in `by` and what no gate runs in `unrun`). The gate checks no proof file of a retired entry: the entries that remove a surface delete those files. The id set is closed in `xtask/src/capability_record.rs` — a missing, duplicated or out-of-range id is a finding — so a change of the set lands in the module and the record in the same chunk. The gate reads the working route, so a route-resolve that renames, retires or splits an entry the record names reddens the verb and the pin `the_committed_record_reads_clean_over_the_committed_route` (in every workspace test run) until the record is corrected in that wrap's chunk. `docs/v0_2_0/capability-verification-matrix.json` (P-001–P-060) and `andromeda-pulse-0.3.0/verification-matrix.json` (P-061–P-082) are superseded by the record and read by no gate.

title: 10. Quality Gates & Coverage Targets

body: **Coverage thresholds (Standard tier per test-scope Section 6):**
| Tier | Line coverage | Branch coverage | Function coverage |
| Standard | ≥ 75% | not enforced — the ≥ 70% threshold is retired as never measured, PROVISIONAL (§4 Coverage target) | ≥ 85% |
**Cumulative across workspace:**
- Exclude generated code (`prost` protobuf stubs, `taurpc` IPC bindings), test fixtures, and mock implementations from coverage
- `cargo llvm-cov` default includes all src/ and tests/; use `--exclude-files` for generated code if needed

- **`xtask/` is excluded from the measure — TEMPORARILY** (founder ruling, 2026-09-29; `COVERAGE_IGNORE_FILENAME_REGEX` in `cargo xtask test:coverage`, chunk 2026-09-29-p-025-hue-shift-observable-made-gradable). Measured on the CI lcov: line 84.3 % / function 83.95 % with xtask, 88.6 % / 87.80 % without — the function gate failed with it. The exclusion is not a settled scope: the next epoch-boundary code audit revisits coverage quality, thresholds above 85 %, and xtask's re-inclusion.

- **`crates/test-support` is INSIDE the measure — against the first bullet, until the route entry `Scenario legs driven against the console engine` takes it out** (chunk 2026-10-10-shared-telemetry-test-data; the operator's word, the pc overseer, 2026-10-11: the rule says fixtures are outside the measure, so the measure is what moves). The crate is test fixtures — the telemetry test factories and the test port claim — and `COVERAGE_IGNORE_FILENAME_REGEX` names `xtask/` alone. As measured on the `coverage` job of `ci#38088083705`: line 35070/38688 = 90.6 % and function 3695/4129 = 89.5 % with the crate inside; the previous chunk's run, before the crate existed, read 34620/38214 = 90.6 % and 3623/4056 = 89.3 %, above both thresholds too.
**Performance budgets** (Standard tier, trigger-driven per test-scope Sec 5):
| Path / operation | p50 | p95 | p99 |
| **OTLP gRPC TraceService.Export RPC** | 10ms | 50ms | 100ms |
| **OTLP HTTP POST /v1/traces** | 15ms | 60ms | 120ms |
| **TauRPC `traces.query` roundtrip** | 20ms | 80ms | 150ms |
| **Snapshot generation (500 spans, 25k token budget)** | 100ms | 300ms | 500ms |
| **DuckDB buffer insert (Arrow appender)** | 5ms | 20ms | 50ms |
| **WebGPU 10k spans/sec sustained throughput** | frame rate >= 30 fps | frame rate >= 25 fps | frame rate >= 20 fps |

> **Frame-budget assertion (authority: obs-plan §10).** The WebGPU fps figures above are descriptive intent only. The ASSERTED budget binds to obs-plan §10's ms-form metric `metric.webgpu.frame_duration_ms` p99 ≤ 33 ms; the `perf_budget` grader's frame arm asserts the ms-form, with a PASS only from the dev-host `perf:frame-sample` (on CI the frame arm reads 0 samples and prints the named cannot-evaluate line, never PASS), and no test asserts an fps number. obs-plan §10 ms-values govern over the fps row (stricter + jq-aggregatable per the `metric.*` convention).

title: Load profiles (release / tag gate)

body: Four-profile load suite in `pulse-app/tests/perf_load_profiles.rs`, orchestrated by `cargo xtask perf:load-profiles` (which then applies the in-process `xtask::perf_budget` grader with no arm required and prints `perf:load-profiles: perf-budget {verdict}`; the check scripts it once called were deleted at chunk 2026-09-30-perf-budget-gate-reads-real-samples). Runs behind nextest `[profile.load-profiles]` (`default-filter = "binary(perf_load_profiles)"`, `test-threads = 1`). A second opt-in profile, `[profile.perf-samples]` (`default-filter = "binary(perf_budget_samples)"`, `test-threads = 1`, `retries = 0`, `slow-timeout = { period = "60s", terminate-after = 5 }`), selects the CI perf-sample producer — a sample source for the CI perf gate, not a load profile, CI-wired on lint-test Linux; the default profile excludes both binaries (`not binary(perf_load_profiles) and not binary(perf_budget_samples)`). Profiles (dist-arch v3):
| Profile | Load | Assertion |
| baseline | 1k spans/s × 60s | zero drops |
| high | 10k spans/s × 5 min | L1a Q1–Q7 p99 < 500 ms at production 20s cadence |
| burst | 50k spans/s × 30s | ≤ 60s recovery |
| sustained-extreme | 50k spans/s × 5 min | degraded-but-functional; zero L0 loss inside retention |

The chunk #54 `perf_slo_10k_spans.rs` single-profile test remains the fast per-PR gate; the four-profile suite is the release/tag gate. Future load-shaped tests join the `load-profiles` nextest profile rather than `#[ignore]` (`#[ignore]` stays reserved for flake quarantine).
**Zero-flakiness budget:** Flaky tests are NOT tolerated. If a test flakes once:
1. Quarantine immediately (skip in CI via `#[ignore]` or GitHub Actions conditional)
2. Root-cause investigation required (not retry-once budget)
3. Fix or delete test before unquarantining
4. Rationale: agent-driven dev cannot distinguish flake from real bug; retry policies mask actual failures
**Build failure conditions:**
- Any test failure (unit / integration / E2E)
- Coverage below threshold for Standard tier (75% line, 85% function), or a coverage report that tracks nothing
- Performance budget regression (p99 latency > specified threshold)
- Flaky test observed (immediate fail; no auto-retry)
- Lint / typecheck failure

title: Compliance Test Coverage

body: _Skipped for Standard tier + Minimal security tier (no compliance triggers in test-scope Section 5 require formal compliance controls)_

title: 11. Test Anti-Patterns (NEVER do these)
Test Strategy

body: - NEVER violate test pyramid — avoid heavy E2E with sparse unit tests (slow + brittle feedback loop); Standard tier requires 75% line coverage at unit level
- NEVER over-mock at integration level (mocking OTLP gRPC receiver in `traces.query` test defeats the point) — use live loopback `:4317` / `:4318` + in-memory DuckDB
- NEVER run tests sequentially when parallelizable — `cargo nextest` enables parallel per-process by default (respects test isolation)
- NEVER skip `cargo deny check bans` (tonic 0.14 vs opentelemetry-otlp duplicate would cause linker conflicts)

title: Unit

body: - NEVER test implementation details (private crate-internal functions) — test public module boundaries
- NEVER write assertions against builder fixture-internal IDs (e.g., assert `mock_span.internal_id == 42`) — assert on contract (span_id is 8 bytes, trace_id is 16 bytes)
- NEVER use `unwrap()` in tests without clear panic message — use `expect("reason why this must succeed")` or assert with context

title: Integration

body: - NEVER mock DuckDB at integration level — always use ephemeral in-memory instance (`duckdb::open_in_memory()`)
- NEVER skip cleanup between integration tests (e.g., shared DuckDB connection across tests) — creates order-dependent failures
- NEVER assert on raw OTLP protobuf bytes (e.g., `assert_eq!(response.encode(), expected_bytes)`) — assert on decoded fields (service_name, latency_ms, etc.)

title: E2E

body: - NEVER use xpath selectors — tauri-driver uses W3C WebDriver, prefer accessible-name / role-based selectors, or `data-testid` where no accessible name ships (**operative since 2026-08-23-integration-ux-e2e-test**: the webview-drive leg is DOM-driven, so this ban binds — it was moot only while the sole surface was procedure-based TauRPC)
- NEVER use `sleep(N)` for synchronization — wait for explicit signal via `health` status polling or Channel event subscription

- NEVER use brittle CSS selectors with hashed class names — accessible name first, `data-testid` as the fallback, never a hashed/utility class (**operative since 2026-08-23-integration-ux-e2e-test**, same reason as the xpath ban above)
- NEVER include visual regression checks requiring human approval (Percy / Chromatic) — pixel inspection is agent-untestable; assert IPC contract instead

title: Test Data

body: - NEVER use production telemetry dumps in tests — generate synthetic telemetry via the `test_support::otlp` factories (or OTLP ingest where a crate cannot take them)
- NEVER share mutable state across parallel tests — each test gets `tempfile::TempDir` + in-memory DuckDB
- NEVER use non-deterministic generators without seed control — `proptest` regression files in `proptest-regressions/` ensure replay
- NEVER pre-populate test DB via `.sql` scripts or SQLite snapshots — all fixture data generated at runtime

title: Mocking

body: - NEVER mock the OTLP receiver you're testing — use live `tonic` gRPC client against loopback `:4317`
- NEVER use `mockall` for external libraries (e.g., tokio, tonic) — use real implementations; mock only traits you own
- NEVER monkey-patch production code at runtime (e.g., `std::env::set_var` mid-test without cleanup) — use constructor injection (`#[fixture] fn config() -> Config { … }`)
- NEVER serialize mocks into log files — mocks are test infrastructure only; assert on real behavior

title: CI

body: - NEVER reference third-party GitHub Actions by floating tag (e.g., `tauri-action@v0`) — pin by 40-char commit SHA
- NEVER run tests sequentially in CI (set `--test-threads=1` only for debugging; remove before commit)
- NEVER ignore flaky tests — quarantine and fix immediately; flake = real bug
- NEVER lower coverage threshold to pass build — raise code quality instead

title: Quality

body: - NEVER add retry-once policies for flaky tests (masks real failures)
- NEVER commit `#[ignore]` tests without open GitHub issue (tracking reason for skip)
- NEVER ship release with known test failures — all gates must be green

title: Universal (agent-driven specific)

body: - NEVER use Percy / Chromatic / Applitools (visual regression with human review) — agent cannot approve screenshots
- NEVER include manual smoke step ("developer verifies build before deploy") — all verification automated
- NEVER use Selenium IDE / Playwright codegen-recorder as test author — use as headless runner only
- NEVER include "human reviews canvas" in test steps — canvas compilation success is sufficient (pixel inspection out of scope)
- NEVER use real network calls without mocks (e.g., calling external GitHub API in tests) — use loopback stubs
- NEVER use real time (`std::time::Instant::now()`, `chrono::Utc::now()`) without injection — use `tokio::time::pause()` for determinism
- NEVER expose secrets in test output (log PII, raw OTLP payloads with credentials) — use data sanitizers or explicit filtering

title: Project-specific (andromeda-pulse)

body: - OTLP self-dialing (receiver instrumented with exporter pointing back to own `:4317`/`:4318`) is prevented **by construction** — no OTel SDK is linked into the self-observation runtime, so no exporter exists to misconfigure and no `ANDROMEDA_OBSERVER_URL`-shaped config surface exists (per obs-plan Phase 3.5 pivot). No negative test required. (Previously a "NEVER self-dial / negative test must assert" rule; deprecation history in test-plan-amendments.md.)
- NEVER dump raw OTLP JSON as snapshot (defeats token-efficiency design goal) — snapshot tests must assert dedup, anomaly markers, aggregates
- NEVER skip post-`prost` OTLP invariant checks (span_id != 8 bytes, trace_id != 16 bytes must be rejected) — negative tests validate
- NEVER bind OTLP receivers to `0.0.0.0` (breaks loopback-only security model) — tests must assert rejection of non-loopback binds

title: 5-command implementation

body: **`boot`** — start the product for testing:

- **Command body:** PRE-BUILD under the verb's own exported env (`cargo build --bin pulse-app --release`, then `cargo build -p xtask` — the readiness poll shells `cargo xtask`, so a stale xtask would otherwise rebuild inside the timed window), then spawn `target/release/pulse-app[.exe]` BY PATH in background — the `cargo run` wrapper is GONE, and the app's own `write_pid_file` writes the canonical pid (chunk 2026-08-30-agent-harness-teardown-truth; sh live-proven, ps1 mirrored — its boot/`ended` leg driven live once by hand at chunk 2026-09-30-perf-budget-gate-reads-real-samples, a committed leg still owed via the §1 `harness-cleanup-verdict-and-boot-spawn-shell-coverage` trigger). Since chunk 2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine the sh `boot` takes one optional word — none is the window app, as above; `engine` is the console engine; any other word is usage, exit 2, before a directory is made: `boot engine` pre-builds `cargo build --bin andromeda-pulse-engine --release` and xtask, spawns `target/release/andromeda-pulse-engine run` BY PATH under the same waiting wrapper (spawn record and exit record as for the window app) and polls `cargo xtask harness:ready --program console`. The word is sh only (`agent-run.ps1` is unchanged, so the two scripts no longer take the same words). Since chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed it is pinned at shell level by `xtask/tests/agent_run_shell.rs` — `boot engine` reading ready and `cleanup` then ending the engine clean, bare `boot` resolving the window program, `status engine` and bare `status` on a running engine, any other word after `boot` or `status` usage, exit 2 and no data dir — as are the `boot` failure arms (the engine build failing, the xtask build failing, the built binary absent, no spawn record, never ready, killed during the poll); the exit-witness arm and the ps1 leg stay without a committed test (the same §1 trigger's open clauses). The word is still read end to end by `cargo xtask harness:engine-cycle` (§3 → Per-chunk gate discipline, Engine cycle gate form). The sh verb runs the app under a waiting subshell — the subshell's own stdin, stdout and stderr are `/dev/null`; the app's stdout and stderr go to `logs/boot.log` under the data dir — that writes the app pid to `run/andromeda-pulse.spawn` and, on reaping the app, its end to `run/andromeda-pulse.exit` (`exit N` or `signal N (NAME)`) — once `boot` returns, the app is otherwise an orphan whose end status nothing can read; `boot` takes the app pid from the spawn record, and none within 5 s is `boot: the app did not start (no spawn record)`, exit 1 (chunk 2026-09-29-ci-wall-time-and-round-trips). `agent-run.ps1 boot` mirrors the recorder since chunk 2026-09-30-perf-budget-gate-reads-real-samples: a hidden `powershell -EncodedCommand` wrapper launches the app, writes `run/andromeda-pulse.spawn` (the app pid) and on the app's exit `run/andromeda-pulse.exit` (`exit N`, ASCII, no BOM); `boot` polls the spawn record ≤ 5 s (50 × 100 ms), else prints `boot: the app did not start (no spawn record)` and exits 1, and on a failed readiness poll prints `app ended: {record}` or `app still running (pid N) but never reported healthy` before cleanup. Since chunk 2026-10-09-boot-smoke-s-early-exit-found-and-closed its readiness poll goes through `Invoke-Ready` (`cargo xtask harness:ready`) and its still-running arm carries the sh verb's conditional `the receivers never both accepted: …` line (Exit code, below); that edit was parsed by `pwsh` with 0 parse errors and has never run — no CI job and no dev host runs the script. The exit-witness arm, sh only and the window program's alone (since chunk 2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-named-from-a-run; `scripts/agent-run.ps1` unchanged; `boot engine` never reads the variable, sets no preload, and neither removes nor creates the witness file): bare `boot` reads the harness-only `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_EXIT_WITNESS_LIB`, trimmed — unset or blank, the app is spawned as before; a regular file, the window app's spawn command runs with `LD_PRELOAD` set to it and `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_EXIT_WITNESS_FILE` set to `{data dir}/logs/exit-witness.jsonl`, neither exported, so the pre-build and every other verb run without them; a stale `logs/exit-witness.jsonl` of the same data dir is removed before the spawn; set and not a regular file is refused before the pre-build (Exit code, below). The library is `scripts/exit-witness.c` (built by `cc -shared -fPIC -O2`; it interposes `exit`, `_exit`, `_Exit`, `quick_exit`, `abort`, removes `LD_PRELOAD` and its file variable from the process environment at load, and is inert when the file variable is unset). Neither variable is read by `pulse-app`'s own code. The arm has no committed shell-level test (the §1 `harness-cleanup-verdict-and-boot-spawn-shell-coverage` trigger). The 5-command set is unchanged: no sixth verb. Env vars unchanged: `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR=$TMPDIR/andromeda-test-$$` (per-test isolation), `RUST_LOG=debug`, optional `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_GRPC_PORT=0 ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_HTTP_PORT=0` (ephemeral ports)

- **Readiness signal:** Poll `cargo xtask harness:ready` (`xtask/src/harness_ready.rs`, since chunk `2026-10-09-boot-smoke-s-early-exit-found-and-closed`; the scripts thread `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_{DATA_DIR,PIDFILE,LOGFILE}` into the xtask child as they did for the status poll; since chunk 2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine the sh script asks `--program window` under bare `boot` and `--program console` under `boot engine`) until its verdict is `ready`: the `cargo xtask harness:status` verdict the `status` verb uses reads `running-healthy` AND both receivers read `accepting`. Since chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed a receiver reads `accepting` when a TCP connection is accepted on `127.0.0.1` at the port resolved from `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_GRPC_PORT` / `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_HTTP_PORT` (defaults 4317 / 4318), each attempt bounded at one second, AND the log family holds, after its last `app.boot.engine` record, an INFO record of that receiver's bind target (`app.boot.otlp.grpc.bind` / `app.boot.otlp.http.bind`) whose `bind_address` is `127.0.0.1:` and that port; `foreign` when the connection is accepted and no such record stands (a failed-bind ERROR record, a record for another port or of the other receiver, a record before the last boot record, a log with no boot record at all); `refusing` when no connection is accepted. An accepted loopback connection alone does not say whose listener accepted it: as measured at that chunk, with a test's own listener on the gRPC port `boot engine` printed `boot: ready` at the earlier decision. The decision holds for both programs; the verdict words, the exits and the six members are unchanged. One pretty-JSON object on stdout — `{verdict: ready | not-ready | wrong-program | ended | cannot-evaluate, pid, ended, program, otlp_grpc, otlp_http}`, six members since chunk 2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine (pinned by set equality), each receiver label `accepting` | `foreign` | `refusing` (`null` on `cannot-evaluate`; three labels since chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed, two before), `ended` the exit record when the verdict is `ended`, `program` the status verdict's own member — exit 0 `ready` · 1 `not-ready`, `wrong-program` or `ended` · 2 `cannot-evaluate` (paths unresolvable, or a port variable that is not 1 to 65535). `wrong-program` is the status verdict for the program asked (the log family's last `app.boot.engine` record names the other program, or none) and holds whatever the receivers answer; a dead pid is `ended` whatever was asked; with no flag, as the ps1 verb calls it, the verdict reads as before plus the member. The pure `decide_ready` (two `Receiver` values since chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed) is pinned per arm, the `wrong-program` arm included, with eight pins added at that chunk for the bound-record reading, and the probe against a real loopback listener and a closed port; the `foreign` reading is read live on a console engine by one committed boot arm (`xtask/tests/agent_run_shell.rs`) and, for the window program, pinned at the decision only. **The gap recorded at chunk `2026-10-09-supply-chain-job-same-on-push-and-pull-request` is CLOSED:** until this chunk the sh verb reported ready on the `running-healthy` verdict alone and confirmed no handshake (on `ci#37964887106` ready printed 12 ms after the app's first log record, before `app.boot.otlp.grpc.bind`); as measured at chunk `2026-10-09-boot-smoke-s-early-exit-found-and-closed`, ready follows both bind records — by 0.097 s on the dev host and by 0.453 s on `ci#37979648967`. The ps1 verb polls the same verdict through `Invoke-Ready`; that edit is parsed, never run. What stays open is not readiness. Who ends the app is named from one run: as measured on `ci#38019133294` (chunk 2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-named-from-a-run), seven of eight boots ended by themselves — three after `boot: ready`, four before the poll could read ready — and each of the seven kept witness lines reads `_exit(1)`, `errno` 11, on the main thread, called from a static function of `libgdk-3.so.0` entered from Xlib's `_XIOError` (under `_XReply`, `XGetWindowProperty`, `gdk_x11_screen_supports_net_wm_hint`), an end that cannot be logged, hence no `app.exit`. The `errno` 11 those lines record is a stale value, not a member of the ending call: no system call failed at the stop. The cause was measured and closed at chunk 2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-closed. No read failed: under a debugger, at the stop in `_XIOError`, the connection reported no error (`xcb_connection_has_error` read 0; one capture of one ending), and Xlib raised the I/O error because its own bookkeeping held no reply for the request while a second thread, `tao` 0.35.0's device-event thread, was inside Xlib — the runner's Xlib 1.7.5 does not initialise its thread support when it loads, the dev host's 1.8.13 does. The runner's builds are read from Ubuntu's own packages: the three Xlib frames are exact return addresses in `libx11-6 1.7.5-1ubuntu0.3`, and the GDK function is `gdk_x_io_error` in `libgtk-3-0 3.24.33-1ubuntu2.2`. The variation is what shows the cause: under the runner's Xlib on the dev host 26 of 32 boots self-ended without the initialisation and 0 of 8 with it. `pulse-app` now calls `xlib_threads::init()` as the second statement of `main()`, before any thread is built (architecture §Stack and Technologies), and, as measured on `ci#38026637514` (attempts 1 to 3, one merge commit), 24 boots read 0 self-ended, against 12 of 16 on the two runs before. P-129's ref is written on those three attempts. Not traced: the step inside Xlib by which the reply is lost. Not measured: whether the witness library or the series contributed to the earlier rate on the runner (on the dev host the arm with nothing preloaded ended 8 of 8 and the arm with the witness 6 of 8)

- **Exit code:** 0 on `ready`; non-zero when no `ready` verdict arrives inside the window, and — in the sh verb, since chunk 2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-named-from-a-run — exit 1 with `boot: exit witness library not found` on stderr, before the pre-build, when `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_EXIT_WITNESS_LIB` is set and names no regular file (driven once by hand, no committed test — the §1 `harness-cleanup-verdict-and-boot-spawn-shell-coverage` trigger). On the readiness failure path the sh verb names how the app ended — `app ended: {record}` from the exit record, or `app still running (pid N) but never reported healthy`, followed, when the last readiness verdict held a `refusing` label, by `the receivers never both accepted: OTLP gRPC 127.0.0.1:{port}, OTLP HTTP 127.0.0.1:{port}` (chunk 2026-10-09-boot-smoke-s-early-exit-found-and-closed), and, when it held a `foreign` label, by `a receiver port accepts but this run's log holds no bound record for it: OTLP gRPC 127.0.0.1:{port}, OTLP HTTP 127.0.0.1:{port}` (chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed; both lines can print) — and runs `bash "$0" cleanup`. Since that 2026-10-10 chunk three committed pins in `xtask/tests/agent_run_shell.rs` read the receivers line, neither line and the `foreign` line on a real console engine (the `foreign` arm ends `cleanup: ports-lingering`, the test's own listener still holding the port; the other never-ready arms read `clean`). `agent-run.ps1` is not edited: its readiness branch matches `refusing` alone and prints no `foreign` line. The self-invocation is of long standing (chunk 2026-09-29-p-025-hue-shift-observable-made-gradable — the script is git mode 100755 since then; at 100644 the self-invocation died with exit 126 on a checkout, so the branch never ran)

- **Timeout:** 10s default for process boot + readiness, and since chunk 2026-08-30-agent-harness-teardown-truth the default is HONEST: the release build AND the xtask build run BEFORE the timed window (the pre-build split), so neither a cold compile nor the env-triggered thin-LTO relink is inside it (measured boot-to-ready 1.953s on a warm target under the untouched 10s default, when ready was the status verdict alone; under `harness:ready`, as measured at chunk 2026-10-09-boot-smoke-s-early-exit-found-and-closed, `boot` returned 0.296 s after the app's first log record on the dev host, and on `ci#37979648967` ready printed 0.596 s after it — both inside the untouched default). `HARNESS_STATUS_TIMEOUT` remains the override. History: before the split, the exported `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*` set re-fingerprinted the release build INSIDE the window — a 180s override died at SIGTERM mid-rustc, 900s succeeded (measured 2026-08-30-acl-rejection-logging) — which is the relink the pre-build now absorbs
**`run`** — invoke test suites:

- **Command body:** `cargo nextest run --workspace --message-format libtest-json --profile ci 2>&1 | tee target/test-run.log` (via `cargo-nextest` 0.9.x per test-research; for per-unit invocation: `cargo test --lib ingest` or `cargo nextest run --filter-expr 'ingest'`)
- **Exit code semantics:** 0 on all-pass; non-zero = failure count (e.g., 5 failures → exit 5)

- **Output format:** nextest's `libtest-json` stream (the Command body's `--message-format libtest-json`, teed to `target/test-run.log`) + final-line regex `test result: ok. ([0-9]+) passed` for structured parsing; no JUnit XML is written (as measured at chunk 2026-10-10-no-ci-step-reads-nothing: `.config/nextest.toml` holds no `junit` key)
- **Test selection:** `cargo nextest run --filter-expr 'package(ingest) and test(::grpc::)' ` for fast iteration

- **Narrow a `pulse-app` run with `--filter-expr` / `-E` under `--workspace`, not with `-p`.** Measured 2026-08-15: `cargo nextest run -p pulse-app -E 'binary(…)'` failed to link the pulse-app test binaries with `crate X required to be available in rlib format` naming dependency crates (`muda`, `wasmtime_internal_cache`, `libduckdb_sys`, `arrow_cast`) **immediately after a green `cargo build --workspace --tests`** — `--workspace` unifies features across members while `-p` resolves a narrower subgraph, so the artifacts the build produced are not the ones the `-p` resolution wants. Re-running the same selection under `--workspace` compiled and passed clean. This does not make every `-p` form unusable (`cargo test --test <name> -p pulse-app` remains the documented single-binary path for the rlib family); it means a `-p` selection must not be assumed compatible with artifacts a `--workspace` build produced — match the scope of the run to the scope of the build.
**`status`** — query product state (REAL-PROCESS verdict since chunk `2026-08-30-diagnostics-un-muting-harness-truth-sweep`):

- **Command body:** `cargo xtask harness:status [--program window|console]` (`xtask/src/harness_status.rs`), invoked by both `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1}` `status` verbs, which thread `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_{DATA_DIR,PIDFILE,LOGFILE}` into the xtask child. Since chunk 2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine the sh `status` takes one optional word — none passes `--program window`, `engine` passes `--program console`, any other word is usage, exit 2 — while `agent-run.ps1 status` takes no word and passes no flag. The verdict derives OUT-of-process from the registered `run/andromeda-pulse.pid` file, a liveness probe of the pid it holds (`ps -o stat=` on Unix, where a zombie `Z` counts as dead; `tasklist` on Windows), and the log family's newest-member mtime — a dead pid is `not-running` whatever the log's freshness says (chunk 2026-09-29-p-025-hue-shift-observable-made-gradable; before it, a crashed app read `running-healthy` for up to 60 s, measured on a CI boot smoke whose app panicked in 12 ms). The pure `classify(pid, alive, newest_log)` is pinned per arm, dead-pid and exited-child included, with its probe parsers pinned too. It is NOT a TauRPC `health` envelope and NOT computed in-script. It REPLACES the prior in-xtask-process `current_health()` call, which exited 0 unconditionally and could never say "not running" (the wrong-reason-pass this section previously recorded).
- **Verdict JSON (stdout):**

```json
  {
    "verdict": "running-healthy" | "stale" | "wrong-program" | "not-running" | "cannot-evaluate",
    "pid": 12345,
    "ended": null | "exit 0" | "signal 11 (SEGV)",
    "program": "window" | "console" | "unknown",
    "log_file_basename": "agent-latest.jsonl.2026-08-30",
    "last_write_age_seconds": 4,
    "stale_after_seconds": 60
  }
  ```

- **Exit code semantics:** 0 `running-healthy` (live pid + log written within `STALE_AFTER_SECONDS` 60) · 1 `stale` (live pid, log silent past the threshold) · 1 `wrong-program` (since chunk 2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine: with `--program`, a `running-healthy` or `stale` run whose log family records another program, or none) · 1 `not-running` (no live pid — a dead or zombie pid is `not-running` whatever the log says) · 2 `cannot-evaluate` (paths unresolvable). `not-running` and `cannot-evaluate` stand whatever program was asked, and with no flag the verdict is as before plus the `program` member: the label of the LAST `app.boot.engine` record of the log family, `unknown` when the family holds no such record or a label that is neither `window` nor `console`. The object has seven members since that chunk, pinned by set equality. `classify(pid, alive, newest_log)` is a pure fn unit-pinned per arm, the dead-pid and exited-child cases included; its signature is unchanged, and the program read beside it (`program_of`, `graded_arm`, `for_program`) is pinned per arm too. `ended` (chunk 2026-09-29-ci-wall-time-and-round-trips) is the `run/andromeda-pulse.exit` record beside the pidfile, bounded to one line of ≤ 48 printable ASCII chars (anything else reads as no record, unit-pinned), reported only when the verdict is not `running-healthy`; real under both scripts since chunk 2026-09-30-perf-budget-gate-reads-real-samples, when the ps1 wrapper began writing the record (measured `"ended": "exit -1"`, `not-running`, exit 1, after `Stop-Process -Force`, whose `TerminateProcess(-1)` code the grammar accepts). The `ended` member changed no arm and no exit code.
**`cleanup`** — tear down:

- **Command body:** Read the pid from `$PID_FILE` (the app's own `write_pid_file` value is canonical; the boot-time spawn pid covers only the crashed-before-write window); probe liveness across both pid spaces (msys `kill -0` first, then a genuinely-probing PowerShell `Get-Process` fallback — never `taskkill`/`tasklist /X` forms, never a `||` branch that manufactures the answer); TERM, bounded liveness-poll wait, KILL escalation
- **Idempotency:** safe to call twice — an absent pidfile with both ports refusing is `clean`

- **Verification:** the verdict derives ONLY from independent probes — pid liveness + TCP handshake on the RESOLVED `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_{GRPC,HTTP}_PORT` at `127.0.0.1` — never from the terminate call's own status. **The 2026-08-30-acl-rejection-logging wrong-reason-pass is CLOSED** (chunk 2026-08-30-agent-harness-teardown-truth, measured RED→GREEN on the sh script: RED at HEAD reproduced cleanup-exit-0 with the app alive and both ports accepting; GREEN shows non-zero on every survival shape and zero on verified teardown; ps1 mirrored in lockstep, its live leg owed via the §1 `harness-cleanup-verdict-and-boot-spawn-shell-coverage` trigger).

- **Exit code:** ONE bounded stdout token — `cleanup: clean | app-survived | ports-lingering | no-pid-ports-accepting` — exit 0 ONLY on `clean` (pid gone or never present, both ports refusing); exit 1 otherwise. The exit code is again evidence of teardown
**`logs`** — fetch product logs:

- **Command body:** resolve the ROTATED log FAMILY `agent-latest.jsonl*` across three precedence-ordered bases — the env override (`ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LOGFILE`, else `$ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR/logs/agent-latest.jsonl`), then `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/agent-latest.jsonl`, then the data-dir `logs/` — taking the NEWEST match within the first base that resolves (the glob expands in lexical order and the date suffix sorts ascending), and `tail -F` it; exit 1 with a diagnostic when no base resolves. **The `*` is load-bearing, not cosmetic:** the sink is `tracing_appender::rolling::daily(log_dir, "agent-latest.jsonl")`, which DATE-SUFFIXES every file (`agent-latest.jsonl.YYYY-MM-DD`), so a bare-name reader — or the `*.log` glob this line carried until 2026-08-26 — silently finds nothing and the caller then false-reports an empty log on a perfectly healthy boot. Matches obs-plan §3 Log file location (daily rotation; previous day's file read when the current one does not yet exist) and the shipped `scripts/agent-run.sh`.
- **Format:** JSON lines from `tracing-subscriber` with `{"timestamp":"2026-05-02T16:18:34.567Z","level":"INFO","target":"ingest::grpc","message":"…","fields":{…}}`
- **Retention window:** all on-disk logs for test session (not auto-purged within test harness; agent may tail last 1000 lines)
- **Agent parsing:** `jq 'select(.level == "ERROR") | .message' logs.jsonl | head -20` for errors; `grep -o "rows_ingested: [0-9]*" logs.jsonl | tail -1` for last ingest count

title: Status endpoint shape

body: _This is the TauRPC `health` IPC payload (arch §Standard Contracts), unchanged — it is NOT the `status` verb's output: since chunk `2026-08-30-diagnostics-un-muting-harness-truth-sweep` the harness `status` verb emits the `harness:status` verdict JSON above, and this envelope is reached only through IPC (`health`)._
**Agent reads:**
- `status == "ok"` for healthy; `"degraded"` acceptable if non-blocking subsystem failure
- `subsystems.*.status` all == `"initialized" | "ready"` (no `"error"`)
- `subsystems.buffer.rows_ingested` increment confirms OTLP ingest occurred
- `subsystems.ingest_channel.broadcast_subscribers >= 1` if real-time streams active
- `pid` matched against spawned process PID for identity verification

title: Log format
Log format

body: **Stream:** `RUST_LOG=debug cargo nextest run --workspace 2>&1 | tee test.log`
**Format:** Rust `tracing` crate JSON output via `tracing-subscriber::fmt().json().init()`
**Example:**
**Agent-parseable signals:**
- Error detection: `jq 'select(.level == "ERROR") | .message' test.log | head -20`
- Ingest confirmation: `grep 'TraceService.Export received' test.log | tail -1`
- Subsystem startup: `grep 'listening on 127.0.0.1:4317' test.log` (confirm gRPC bind)
- Data leakage check: `! grep 'query parameters:' test.log` (assert no SQL params logged; validates anti-pattern)

title: PID file
PID file

body: - **Location:** `<data_dir>/run/andromeda-pulse.pid` on every platform — `<data_dir>` is `resolve_data_dir()` (overridable via `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR`), and the harness-only `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_PIDFILE` overrides the whole path. The single form the scripts, the shared boot's `write_pid_file` (`pulse_app::engine_boot`, called through `engine_boot::init_process`), and arch §Occupied Resources all use (the former per-OS `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`/`$TMPDIR`/`%LOCALAPPDATA%` set was stale v1 text, measured false at chunk 2026-08-30-agent-harness-teardown-truth)

- **Lifecycle:** 
  - `boot` writes a provisional pid — since chunk 2026-09-29-ci-wall-time-and-round-trips the one the waiting wrapper records in `run/andromeda-pulse.spawn` — and the app's own `write_pid_file` overwrites the default pidfile with its canonical pid at boot (measured live earlier: file held app pid 59828, not the script's `$!` 128125 — msys pid space ≠ Windows pid space). Beside the pidfile the harness (never the product binary) also writes `run/andromeda-pulse.spawn` and `run/andromeda-pulse.exit`; the latter is the `ended` that `harness:status`, `harness:ready` and `harness:settled` report, and since chunk 2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine what `cargo xtask check:engine-log` reads, through `read_ended`, for its `process-end` arm
  - `status` reads the pidfile, probes that pid's liveness (a dead or zombie pid is `not-running`), and reads the log-family mtime via `cargo xtask harness:status`
  - `cleanup` terminates the pid the FILE holds (canonical), probing/killing across both pid spaces (msys `kill` first, PowerShell `Get-Process`/`Stop-Process` fallback — never `taskkill`/`tasklist` forms); the wrapper-pid defect is CLOSED (chunk 2026-08-30-agent-harness-teardown-truth)
  - since chunk 2026-10-10-console-engine-entry-point BOTH product programs call `write_pid_file` — the window app `pulse-app` and the console program `andromeda-pulse-engine run` — at the same path, so the file holds the pid of whichever program started last on that data dir. Since chunk 2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine the sh verbs are aimed at either program: bare `boot` builds and spawns `pulse-app`, `boot engine` builds and spawns `andromeda-pulse-engine run`; `status` and `boot`'s readiness poll ask for a program and read `wrong-program` when the log family's last `app.boot.engine` record names the other one, or none; `cleanup` still terminates whatever pid the file holds, so what keeps it on the right program is the data dir, one per run
- **Format:** single decimal PID on one line, no newline-stripping needed (portable)
