title: Test data bootstrap

body: - **Strategy:** Self-bootstrapping via OTLP ingest (tests send synthetic spans to live receiver)

- **Mechanism:** Rust builder factories — one set, `test_support::otlp` in the dev-only member `crates/test-support` (chunk 2026-10-10-shared-telemetry-test-data): a test sets what it reasons about and the rest takes a default
  - `resource().service("test-app").span(span().trace_id([0u8; 16]).span_id([0u8; 8])).trace_request()` → the export request a test sends via a `tonic` client to the engine's gRPC port (`logs_request()` for log records; no metrics export request is built)
  - `resource_spans()` / `resource_metrics()` / `resource_logs()` on the same builder → the resource-level batches a test hands the buffer
  - Defaults are fixed constants (an unset event time, an unset service); an unset span id is the span's position under its resource plus one; a span ends `SPAN_DURATION_NANOS` after its start (no duration setter); no clock is read and nothing is random. `rstest` composition stays in a consuming crate that already carries `rstest`; the member has no `rstest` dependency

- **Per-test isolation:** `tempfile::TempDir` + `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR=$TMPDIR/test-$$` ensures fresh DuckDB `:memory:` per test; `tokio::time::pause()` for deterministic clock in retention tests; retention window override via config env `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_BUFFER_RETENTION_SEC=300` (verify old rows discarded after TTL expiry)
- **Cleanup:** `cleanup` command removes test data directory; explicit `drop(temp_dir)` in Rust tests

title: Bootstrap phases
Bootstrap phases

body: 1. **test-runner-install:** `cargo-nextest` 0.9.x (per Phase 2 research; provides per-process isolation for port-binding tests — isolation of processes only: it does not keep two tests from being handed one port number, so the port-using suites — the spawned ones and, since chunk 2026-10-10-shared-telemetry-test-data, the in-process arms of `integration_engine_boot.rs` — claim their ports through `test_support::ports::claim_port`, §9 Integration tests row)
2. **5-command-discipline-wire:** Materialize `scripts/agent-run.sh` with 5-command bodies (boot / run / status / cleanup / logs) per Section 3 above
3. **status-endpoint-implement:** Wire TauRPC `health` command to return required fields (status / subsystems / pid / uptime_ms)
4. **log-format-bind-with-obs:** Configure `tracing-subscriber::fmt().json()` to emit JSON per-line format (binds with obs-plan §3 JSON schema)
5. **pid-file-commitment-wire:** Write `<data_dir>/run/andromeda-pulse.pid` at boot (data-dir-relative, per §3 PID file → Location); read + verify at cleanup

6. **test-data-bootstrap-wire:** ONE set of telemetry test factories, built at chunk `2026-10-10-shared-telemetry-test-data`: `test_support::otlp` in the dev-only workspace member `crates/test-support` — spans with their events, metric points (integer points of a gauge) and log records, assembled under one resource into the export requests a test sends and the resource-level batches a test hands the buffer; event time, service and string attributes settable, every default fixed, no clock and nothing random. The member is taken as a dev-dependency by `buffer`, `pulse-app` and `xtask` and depends on `ingest` alone. Dropped from this item (the operator's word, the pc overseer, 2026-10-11: a mandated factory nothing calls is retired from the item, not kept as owed; an entry that needs one builds it with its consumer): the names `MockTraceSpan` / `MockArrowBatch` / `MockMetricPoint`, the one-factory-per-crate placement (`ingest` / `buffer` / `viz`), and the Arrow-batch factory, which was never built. Also not built, for lack of a caller: a metrics export request, a span-duration setter, a no-resource form; the version setter waits for the stored column that reads it (route entry `Span keeps its identity`). The `rstest` fixture half landed earlier and is in use in the crates that carry it; the member itself has no `rstest` dependency. Tests the set does not yet serve self-bootstrap (§7) by OTLP ingest through the live receiver plus per-test in-memory DuckDB seeding; the hand-built residue is counted in §1 `test-data-bootstrap-factories-unimplemented`
7. **coverage-tooling-install:** `cargo-llvm-cov` 0.8.5 for LCOV/Cobertura output

8. **quality-gate-config-emit:** GitHub Actions workflow enforces: line coverage ≥ 75%, function coverage ≥ 85% (the branch ≥ 70% arm is retired as never measured, PROVISIONAL — test-plan §4 Coverage target), zero-flakiness (no retries), perf-budget < 100ms p99 for RPC latency

title: Per-chunk gate discipline

body: Every `/andromeda-phase`-authored chunk plan's `## Test Commands` section MUST include the **standard gate set** (unconditional, regardless of webview-only / Rust-only / mixed scope):

```
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo xtask capability-widening-check
cargo xtask check:ingest-progress
cargo xtask check:staged-artifacts        # staged bindings + capability grants vs pins (exit 0/1/2; also runs inside capability-drift)
cargo xtask capability-drift              # BEFORE the workspace nextest — see the ordering note below
cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci
```

**The merge-base probe (operator leg, directly before the push).** Every plan that lists a build-branch push lists this entry directly before it, keyed `leg = 'operator'`, `env = []`, `expect = ['exit 0']`:

```
m="$(git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main | cut -f1)" && test -n "$m" && git merge-base --is-ancestor "$m" HEAD
```

It reads the remote's `main` as it stands at that moment and is red when the build branch does not contain it: exit 1 when `main`'s head is not an ancestor of HEAD, exit 128 when that commit is not in the local repository (`main` moved and was not brought in), non-zero when the remote read returns nothing. A red is brought to the operator before any push; the pass never clears it by a fetch, a merge or a rebase of its own. Why it exists: the pull-request run builds the tip merged with `main`, while `cargo xtask pre-push:linux` builds the tip alone, and the two are equal only while `main` is an ancestor of the build branch. As measured at chunk 2026-10-10-no-ci-step-reads-nothing: the tip `3049966f` read green locally and its merge with `main` did not compile (`ci#38034700885`), because the branch carried by hand a change `main` also held and git kept both copies of one test once the chunk edited beside them; `main` was then recorded as merged with the tree unchanged, and the run of `2ec4d439` read green (`ci#38035474359`). The probe read exit 0 on that chunk's final tree. Added on the operator's word at that chunk's wrap (the pc overseer, 2026-10-10): a check that runs, not a sentence that is remembered.

Each leg gets its OWN fresh data dir so neither reads the other's residue, and the RED leg records its expected ERROR (target + `reject_reason`) as evidence rather than as a gate failure. (Codified 2026-08-23 at chunk `2026-08-23-metrics-points-identity`, whose RED leg recorded one `duckdb.append` ERROR with `reject_reason: "append_failed"` by design.) `bash scripts/agent-run.sh status` still runs as the listed harness gate — and since chunk `2026-08-30-diagnostics-un-muting-harness-truth-sweep` it is TRUTHFUL about liveness: the verb delegates to `cargo xtask harness:status`, so a no-app run exits non-zero with `verdict: "not-running"` (live-proven 2026-08-30 — the 2026-08-23 "exits 0 and emits a full payload even when nothing is running" measurement described the retired in-process form); the direct-binary artifacts remain the evidence of record for run-specific claims. Measured 2026-08-15 (chunk 2026-08-15-tier-1-incident-path-investigation): two full boots on separate fresh data dirs verified a boot-time allowlist change that no in-process form could observe, since the fields under test are only produced by a live storm. The in-process 5-command harness does not catch trait-level binding-emission panics that fire at boot in a non-Tokio context (e.g. the `crates/ui-bridge/src/health.rs` "there is no reactor running" panic). On smoke failure the chunk surfaces "green per scope; runtime blocked" rather than blocking commit. Tracked as coverage trigger `boot-smoke-coverage`.

**Process-end witness form (integration tier).** A claim that a record SURVIVES THE PROCESS ENDING is cross-process, so it is witnessed by re-exec children, never in-process (chunk `2026-10-01-conductor-return`, `pulse-app/tests/integration_exit_cause_record.rs`): the parent re-runs the test binary with `--exact <fn>` and an arm name in the environment; each child calls `observability::init` on its OWN TempDir data dir, ends its process through ONE class, and the parent reads the child's `agent-latest.jsonl*` family only after the child has ended — exactly one `app.exit` per loggable class, its fields rendered, 0 full paths, 0 planted canary. Child-ran proof is IN-ARM: each arm requires the child's `app.boot.tracing.init` record, because child stdout is discarded (`Stdio::null()`) and a `--no-capture` read shows nothing from children. A once-flag whose sink's only drain is a guard drop is pinned by the emitter's RETURN value reported through the child's exit code, never by a file read — the first flush closes the sink, so a second record can never reach the file and a file read passes with the flag removed (measured: the whole once-guard neutralized left every file-reading arm green). Arms that only Unix can run (`std::process::exit` reaching `atexit`; SIGTERM ending the child BY signal 15) are `cfg(unix)` — run natively by `cargo nextest run --workspace` on the Linux dev host (Omarchy, since the 2026-10-03 host move; measured 2575 = 2573 + these two arms at chunk `2026-10-02-incident-events-readable-through-mcp`) and by CI `lint-test` on `ubuntu-22.04` (the `cfg(unix)` arms have no macOS CI witness since chunk 2026-10-09-ci-on-linux-alone); on a Windows host they are unrunnable. The form cannot reach the ends unloggable by construction (SIGKILL, `_exit`, Windows `TerminateProcess`, a Rust `std::process::exit` on Windows, pre-sink failures); RED at base is the block-shaped absence of the record (§3 Direct-binary smoke variant's shape rule). Since chunk 2026-10-10-console-engine-entry-point the form also has two arms over the production process start: the children of `pulse-app/tests/integration_engine_boot.rs` call `engine_boot::init_process` (the sink, the hooks and the pid file together), not `observability::init` alone, and each proves it ran by its `app.boot.tracing.init` and `app.boot.pid` records and a pid file holding its own pid.

**Spawned-program witness form (integration tier).** A claim about a product program's whole process — it boots with no display, both receivers accept, telemetry lands, its log is whole JSON, it ends by a signal leaving one `app.exit` — is witnessed by a `pulse-app/tests/integration_*.rs` test that spawns the BUILT product binary (first use: `andromeda-pulse-engine run`, `pulse-app/tests/integration_console_engine.rs`, chunk 2026-10-10-console-engine-entry-point): a cleared environment with no display variable and no session bus; its own TempDir data dir, also its working directory, and two claimed loopback ports passed through the two registered port variables — since chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed a number from 20000 to 31999 (24317 and 24318 left out), held for the test by an advisory lock (`File::try_lock`) on a file under the git-ignored `target/test-ports/` (never unlinked) and shown bindable when claimed, never bound to port 0, read and released: on the tree that picked that way one of seven hand runs of the three port-using binaries failed one arm on a port another process held, and 14 of 14 were green after (a count, not an exclusion); since chunk 2026-10-10-shared-telemetry-test-data the claim is one definition, `test_support::ports::claim_port` / `PortClaim` in the dev-only member `crates/test-support`, on the same terms (the two twins in `integration_console_engine.rs` and `xtask/tests/common/mod.rs` are removed; the lock directory is found from the crate's compile-time manifest directory, nothing read from the environment at run time; a panic when no port can be claimed), taken at that chunk by four port-using binaries, five since chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process (`integration_engine_boot`'s four in-process arms joined, two claimed ports each) and by two `xtask` unit tests, seven of seven hand runs of the four binaries green at that chunk (a count); what the engine is handed is unchanged in kind; the pid from `Child::id()`, never a shell's background pid, and a still-running child killed on drop; readiness read from both ports accepting, and records awaited by target under a bound, never a sleep for a count; the end by SIGTERM or SIGINT with the signal read from the exit status; the log family read after the end — every line a whole record, exactly one `app.exit` and it is last, both ports refusing, no log record on stdout or stderr, the data dir's top-level entries within `corpus`, `logs`, `run`. Three readings joined the form at chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed, each a spawned arm read red first (the file holds 7 arms, was 4): a rejected port variable (the failed-bind record `invalid_port`, a refused connection on that port, the other receiver alone listening — the other receiver and the door since chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process); a socket census of the process read from `/proc` (exactly the two loopback receivers, and no socket beyond them — since that chunk exactly those two and one `unix` listener at the canonical `run/door/sock`, by set equality); and the corpus-key lock file's directory, size and mode in both environments, a runtime dir handed and not handed, its name and the lock directory's path 0 times in the log family. 4317 and 4318 are bound by no test. The same chunk gave the `xtask` package a sibling of the form in `xtask/tests/` (`agent_run_shell.rs`, `engine_cycle_refusals.rs`): the committed `scripts/agent-run.sh` and the built `harness:engine-cycle` verb run by the real `bash` on a real console engine, under a cleared environment and claimed ports, the script's output printed on a failed assertion with the scratch path and the passphrase replaced. It runs inside `cargo nextest run --workspace` (`cargo xtask test` in `lint / test`, and the pre-push `test` stage), so the console program is run on every push inside the test suite; since chunk 2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine it also has a harness word (`boot engine` / `status engine`, sh only) and a workflow step (`Console engine cycle` in the `boot` job; the Engine cycle gate form, below). A chunk touching `pulse-app/src/console.rs` or `pulse-app/src/bin/andromeda-pulse-engine.rs` takes this test as its runtime gate; the window smoke boots `pulse-app` alone. Since chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process the form has a second spawned binary, `pulse-app/tests/integration_door.rs` (5 arms on `andromeda-pulse-engine run`: the owner answered from the engine's stores with a call record holding none of it; a request outside the tool set refused beside an answered call; an answer over the size bound refused beside the same query at a small limit; the write switch read from the environment; another account refused at three layers), which joins the port-using binaries taking `test_support::ports` — five, was four. Its other-account arm runs one client (`python3 -c`) under `sudo -n -u nobody` and under `sudo -n`, records each of its six readings as measured, and prints the sentence `door other-account arm: directory refused, socket mode refused, account check refused` only when `nobody` was refused at the socket's mode too; where `sudo -n true` fails it prints its skip sentence and passes, so the reading is taken on the runner by the `lint-test` step `Door refuses another account` (test-plan §9, which holds the door's PROVISIONAL sentence), never from nextest's pass count. Since chunk 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door `integration_door.rs` holds 7 arms (was 5): the five, plus a stdio agent reaching the door through the spawned `andromeda-pulse-engine door` word beside the spawned engine (one `door.call` per answered request, the data dir's file set unchanged, the pid file still the engine's) and another account through that word receiving nothing. The relay arm copies the built engine into its own temp dir at 0755 and runs it under `sudo -n -u nobody` and `sudo -n` (sudo's env_reset drops `LLVM_PROFILE_FILE`) — the second thing in the suite run as another account; where `sudo -n true` fails it prints `door bridge other-account arm: skipped, no second account` and passes, so its reading too is taken by that step. A chunk touching the `door` word is gated by this file and by `pulse-app/tests/unit_door_bridge.rs`, which also spawns the built word (PROVISIONAL with the door's item).

**Engine cycle gate form (runtime, console engine).** One whole run of the console engine under the harness is read by `cargo xtask harness:engine-cycle [--data-dir DIR] [--grpc-port N] [--http-port N]` (`xtask/src/engine_cycle.rs`; first use: chunk 2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine, in its gate block on the dev host and as the `boot` job's `Console engine cycle` step). Defaults: a fresh `target/engine-cycle/{UTC second}` and ports 24317 / 24318. It is refused before anything starts, `cannot-evaluate`, exit 2, on `not-linux` · `shared-port` (4317 or 4318 in either flag) · `data-dir-holds-a-log-family` · `port-taken` (either cycle port already accepting a connection; since chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed — read after the three before it and before the `HOME` read, so 4317 and 4318 are refused before any port is probed; stderr `harness:engine-cycle: cannot-evaluate (port-taken)`, the verdict object with nulls, nothing built or started, no data dir made), and on `home-unset` · `path-unset` · `data-dir-unusable` · `injector-build-failed` — eight labels, each named by a test since that chunk: three through `refusal`, five by `xtask/tests/engine_cycle_refusals.rs` on the built verb, beside one whole failing cycle on a real engine that ends the engine it started. Since that chunk the form is also run by `pre-push:linux`'s sixth stage (above; PROVISIONAL). It runs, in order: the injector build; `bash scripts/agent-run.sh boot engine`; `inject_demo --sustained --error-pct=0` by path; `cargo xtask harness:engine-settled`; the injector's end; `agent-run.sh status engine`; `agent-run.sh cleanup`; `cargo xtask check:engine-log` — after a failed boot the settle and status verbs are skipped, and cleanup and the check always run — every child under a cleared environment with the verb's pinned set and no session bus, runtime dir or display variable. One JSON object on stdout, eight members (`verdict`: `pass` 0 · `fail` 1 · `cannot-evaluate` 2; `boot`, `settled`, `status`, `cleanup`, `check`; `error_records`; `witness_file`); the children's output is on the verb's stderr. The gate reading: exit 0 with `"verdict": "pass"`, `"error_records": 0`, `"witness_file": "absent"`, `engine-log: PASS` and `cleanup: clean` in the merged output. Its two parts are verbs of their own: `cargo xtask harness:engine-settled [--timeout-seconds N]` (default 60, below 20 `cannot-evaluate`; it holds the run until the log holds what the check reads — two records of each of `ingest.tick`, `buffer.tick`, `connection.tick` and one non-zero `metric.buffer.memory_bytes` sample — since a boot of a few seconds holds one tick per target and could never fail a gap check; `settled` 0 · `ended` 1 · `wrong-program` 1 · `not-settled` 1 · `cannot-evaluate` 2) and `cargo xtask check:engine-log` (seven arms, `family` · `program` · `panic` · `heartbeat-gap` · `progress` · `process-end` · `budget`; exit 0 · 1 · 2, a FAIL on any arm outranking a cannot-evaluate; no arm reads PASS over an input it cannot grade). The full contracts are architecture §Occupied Resources → xtask CLI surfaces. The form is not a member of the standard gate set, and `cargo xtask check:ingest-progress` and `cargo xtask ci-gates` are unchanged by it, the former's NEUTRAL arm included. As measured at that chunk: the cycle took 19 to 41 s on the dev host and the step 100 s on `ci#38065768197`, one reading, where under the cycle's cleared child environment `boot engine` compiled `pulse-app` again in the release profile and the injector build compiled again in the dev profile, although the job's release build had already built the engine binary. Since chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process the cycle's engine also opens its door under the cycle's data dir and its log holds exactly one `app.boot.door` record, over which `cargo xtask check:engine-log` reads `PASS`; the verb, the script and the verdict shape are unchanged. The canonical socket path must be shorter than 108 bytes (107 binds): the default cycle data dir measured 99 bytes on the dev host at that chunk, and a deeper `--data-dir` boots with no door (`state` `path_too_long`, the record at WARN), the engine going on without one — a cycle that must read the door asserts `"state":"listening"` itself.

## 2026-06-10 — Chunk #99 tag gate: capability verification matrix + four-profile load suite; frame budget reconciled to obs §10
**Section:** §9 CI Integration, §10 Quality Gates (Load profiles + frame budget), §6 P5.
**Change:** 4 mechanisms adopted; no wire-contract or quality-gate threshold changed.
1. §9 "Capability verification matrix" — `docs/v0_2_0/capability-verification-matrix.json` enumerates all 60 P-001–P-060 capabilities with per-entry scenarios (56 automated-nextest, 2 automated-a11y, 1 by-construction [P-040 default-off], 1 env-gated-runtime [real llama-cli]); `cargo xtask verify:capability-matrix` validates ids/file-refs/grep-anchors, CI step after `capability-drift`.
2. §10 "Load profiles (release / tag gate)" — `pulse-app/tests/perf_load_profiles.rs`: baseline 1k spans/s × 60s zero-drops; high 10k × 5min with L1a Q1–Q7 p99 < 500ms at production 20s cadence; burst 50k × 30s with ≤ 60s recovery; sustained-extreme 50k × 5min degraded-but-functional, zero L0 loss inside retention. Runs under nextest `[profile.load-profiles]` (`default-filter = "binary(perf_load_profiles)"`, `test-threads = 1`; default profile excludes it) via `cargo xtask perf:load-profiles`. `perf_slo_10k_spans.rs` stays the fast per-PR gate.
3. §10 frame budget — the "WebGPU 10k spans/sec sustained ≥ 30 fps" row is RETAINED as descriptive intent; the ASSERTED budget is obs-plan §10's `metric.webgpu.frame_duration_ms` p99 ≤ 33ms. No test asserts an fps number.
4. §6 P5 "Current residual" — the tray/window matrix is covered by the IPC surrogate + the browser-driven a11y chain (real Chromium against the built webview); the tauri-driver headful suite stays deferred (documented residual, not a coverage claim).
The load suite found and fixed in-chunk 3 pipeline defects: retention-sweep connection monopolization, a Q7 timeout abandoning a mutex-holding task, L1a reads queuing behind append-path maintenance.
**Why:** obs-plan §10 ms-values govern over the test-plan §10 fps row (stricter + jq-aggregatable per the `metric.*` convention), resolving the fps-vs-ms drift. Standing rules: future load-shaped tests join the `load-profiles` nextest profile, never `#[ignore]` (reserved for flake quarantine); future capabilities (P-061+) extend the matrix JSON in the chunk that lands them (`verify:capability-matrix` fails CI on dangling ids/paths/anchors).

## 2026-10-10-no-ci-step-reads-nothing — the merge-base probe on the operator leg, directly before the push
**Section:** §3 → Per-chunk gate discipline (key file: one new paragraph, "The merge-base probe")
**Change:** Every plan that lists a build-branch push lists, as the entry directly before it, `m="$(git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main | cut -f1)" && test -n "$m" && git merge-base --is-ancestor "$m" HEAD`, keyed `leg = 'operator'`, `env = []`, `expect = ['exit 0']`. A red is brought to the operator before any push; the pass never clears it by a fetch, a merge or a rebase of its own. Was: no such entry; the standard gate set held nothing that read `main`.
**Why:** The pull-request run builds the tip merged with `main` and the local pre-push check builds the tip alone; at this chunk a tip that was green locally met a merge that did not compile. The operator ruled a check that runs over a sentence that is remembered, placed where the push entry sits (the operator, the pc overseer, at this wrap's route-resolve card, 2026-10-10).
**Kept:** No Tier-1 line was written for it: phase builds each plan's Test Commands from this section, so the probe reaches plans from here, and the two leaves that restate the gate set carry it. ## 2026-06-10 — Chunk #99 tag gate: capability verification matrix + four-profile load suite; frame budget reconciled to obs §10

- **Section:** §9 CI Integration, §10 Quality Gates (Load profiles + frame budget), §6 P5.
- **Trigger:** chunk #99 phase #96 (the v0.2.0 tag gate) via `cargo xtask verify:capability-matrix` + `cargo xtask perf:load-profiles`, applied at implement time per spec-drift-protocol Path A.
- **Change (4 adopted mechanisms; no wire-contract or quality-gate threshold changed):**
  1. **Capability verification matrix** — `docs/v0_2_0/capability-verification-matrix.json` enumerates all 60 P-001–P-060 capabilities with per-entry verification scenarios (modes: 56 automated-nextest, 2 automated-a11y, 1 by-construction [P-040 default-off — no auto-spawn path exists], 1 env-gated-runtime [real llama-cli integration per `.claude/rules/testing.md` 2026-05-25]). `cargo xtask verify:capability-matrix` validates ids/file-refs/grep-anchors and runs as a CI step after `capability-drift`.
  2. **Four-profile load suite** — `pulse-app/tests/perf_load_profiles.rs` implements dist-arch v3 profiles {baseline 1k spans/s × 60s zero-drops; high 10k × 5min with L1a Q1–Q7 p99 < 500ms at production 20s cadence; burst 50k × 30s with ≤ 60s recovery; sustained-extreme 50k × 5min degraded-but-functional with zero L0 loss inside retention}. Runs behind nextest `[profile.load-profiles]` (`default-filter = "binary(perf_load_profiles)"`, `test-threads = 1`; default profile excludes it), orchestrated by `cargo xtask perf:load-profiles` (then applies NEUTRAL-tolerant obs check scripts). Chunk #54 `perf_slo_10k_spans.rs` stays the fast per-PR gate; four-profile suite is the release/tag gate.
  3. **Frame-budget reconciliation (resolves the fps-vs-ms drift)** — §10's "WebGPU 10k spans/sec sustained ≥ 30 fps" row is RETAINED as descriptive intent, but the ASSERTED budget is obs-plan §10's ms-form `metric.webgpu.frame_duration_ms` p99 ≤ 33ms. All CI assertions bind to the ms-values; no test asserts an fps number.
  4. **tauri-driver headful residual recorded** — the P5 tray/window matrix is covered by the IPC surrogate + the repaired browser-driven a11y chain (real Chromium against the built webview); the tauri-driver headful suite stays deferred per the chunk #51 Path A' precedent (documented residual, not a silent coverage claim).
- **Defects surfaced (no threshold/wire change):** the load suite found + fixed in-chunk 3 real pipeline defects — retention-sweep connection monopolization, a Q7 timeout abandoning a mutex-holding task, and L1a reads queuing behind append-path maintenance (recorded in the obs-plan §12 sibling entry, same amendment record).
- **Usage scope:** future load-shaped tests join the `load-profiles` nextest profile rather than `#[ignore]` (`#[ignore]` stays reserved for flake quarantine); future capability additions (P-061+) extend the matrix JSON in the same chunk that lands the capability (`verify:capability-matrix` fails CI on dangling ids/paths/anchors).
- **Why / authority:** obs-plan §10 ms-values govern over the test-plan §10 fps row (stricter + jq-aggregatable per the `metric.*` convention).
- **Body now:** (1) → §9 "Capability verification matrix"; (2) → §10 "Load profiles (release / tag gate)"; (3) → §10 frame-budget note under the perf-budget table; (4) → §6 P5 "Current residual".
- **Cross-references:** obs-plan §12 "2026-06-10 — Chunk #99 tag gate" (same amendment record); dist-arch v3 `docs/v0_2_0/pulse-distillation-architecture.md` (profile definitions); `docs/v0_2_0/pulse-v0_2_0-route.md` §97 Phase 13 (chunk source); combined.md phase-96 cross-domain rot warning 5 (fps-vs-ms mismatch, resolved here).

title: 5-command implementation
body:
### 5-command implementation

**`boot`** — start the product for testing:
- **Command body:** PRE-BUILD under the verb's own exported env (`cargo build --bin pulse-app --release`, then `cargo build -p xtask` — the readiness poll shells `cargo xtask`, so a stale xtask would otherwise rebuild inside the timed window), then spawn `target/release/pulse-app[.exe]` BY PATH in background — the `cargo run` wrapper is GONE, and the app's own `write_pid_file` writes the canonical pid (chunk 2026-08-30-agent-harness-teardown-truth; sh live-proven, ps1 mirrored — its boot/`ended` leg driven live once by hand at chunk 2026-09-30-perf-budget-gate-reads-real-samples, a committed leg still owed via the §1 `harness-cleanup-verdict-and-boot-spawn-shell-coverage` trigger). The sh verb runs the app under a waiting subshell (stdin/stdout/stderr `/dev/null`) that writes the app pid to `run/andromeda-pulse.spawn` and, on reaping the app, its end to `run/andromeda-pulse.exit` (`exit N` or `signal N (NAME)`) — once `boot` returns, the app is otherwise an orphan whose end status nothing can read; `boot` takes the app pid from the spawn record, and none within 5 s is `boot: the app did not start (no spawn record)`, exit 1 (chunk 2026-09-29-ci-wall-time-and-round-trips). `agent-run.ps1 boot` mirrors the recorder since chunk 2026-09-30-perf-budget-gate-reads-real-samples: a hidden `powershell -EncodedCommand` wrapper launches the app, writes `run/andromeda-pulse.spawn` (the app pid) and on the app's exit `run/andromeda-pulse.exit` (`exit N`, ASCII, no BOM); `boot` polls the spawn record ≤ 5 s (50 × 100 ms), else prints `boot: the app did not start (no spawn record)` and exits 1, and on a failed readiness poll prints `app ended: {record}` or `app still running (pid N) but never reported healthy` before cleanup. Env vars unchanged: `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR=$TMPDIR/andromeda-test-$$` (per-test isolation), `RUST_LOG=debug`, optional `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_GRPC_PORT=0 ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_HTTP_PORT=0` (ephemeral ports)
- **Readiness signal:** Poll the same `cargo xtask harness:status` verdict the `status` verb uses (since chunk `2026-08-30-diagnostics-un-muting-harness-truth-sweep` — the scripts thread `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_{DATA_DIR,PIDFILE,LOGFILE}` into the xtask child) until it reports `running-healthy`; confirm TCP handshake succeeds on bound ports (log parse)
- **Exit code:** 0 on ready; non-zero on timeout or a non-`running-healthy` verdict. On that failure path the sh verb names how the app ended — `app ended: {record}` from the exit record, or still running — and runs `bash "$0" cleanup` (chunk 2026-09-29-p-025-hue-shift-observable-made-gradable — the script is git mode 100755 since then; at 100644 the self-invocation died with exit 126 on a checkout, so the branch never ran)
- **Timeout:** 10s default for process boot + readiness, and since chunk 2026-08-30-agent-harness-teardown-truth the default is HONEST: the release build AND the xtask build run BEFORE the timed window (the pre-build split), so neither a cold compile nor the env-triggered thin-LTO relink is inside it (measured boot-to-ready 1.953s on a warm target under the untouched 10s default). `HARNESS_STATUS_TIMEOUT` remains the override. History: before the split, the exported `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*` set re-fingerprinted the release build INSIDE the window — a 180s override died at SIGTERM mid-rustc, 900s succeeded (measured 2026-08-30-acl-rejection-logging) — which is the relink the pre-build now absorbs

**`run`** — invoke test suites:
- **Command body:** `cargo nextest run --workspace --message-format libtest-json --profile ci 2>&1 | tee target/test-run.log` (via `cargo-nextest` 0.9.x per test-research; for per-unit invocation: `cargo test --lib ingest` or `cargo nextest run --filter-expr 'ingest'`)
- **Exit code semantics:** 0 on all-pass; non-zero = failure count (e.g., 5 failures → exit 5)
- **Output format:** JUnit XML (nextest `--message-format junit --output-file target/nextest/junit.xml`) + final-line regex `test result: ok. ([0-9]+) passed` for structured parsing
- **Test selection:** `cargo nextest run --filter-expr 'package(ingest) and test(::grpc::)' ` for fast iteration
- **Narrow a `pulse-app` run with `--filter-expr` / `-E` under `--workspace`, not with `-p`.** Measured 2026-08-15: `cargo nextest run -p pulse-app -E 'binary(…)'` failed to link the pulse-app test binaries with `crate X required to be available in rlib format` naming dependency crates (`muda`, `wasmtime_internal_cache`, `libduckdb_sys`, `arrow_cast`) **immediately after a green `cargo build --workspace --tests`** — `--workspace` unifies features across members while `-p` resolves a narrower subgraph, so the artifacts the build produced are not the ones the `-p` resolution wants. Re-running the same selection under `--workspace` compiled and passed clean. This does not make every `-p` form unusable (`cargo test --test <name> -p pulse-app` remains the documented single-binary path for the rlib family); it means a `-p` selection must not be assumed compatible with artifacts a `--workspace` build produced — match the scope of the run to the scope of the build.

**`status`** — query product state (REAL-PROCESS verdict since chunk `2026-08-30-diagnostics-un-muting-harness-truth-sweep`):
- **Command body:** `cargo xtask harness:status` (`xtask/src/harness_status.rs`), invoked by both `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1}` `status` verbs, which thread `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_{DATA_DIR,PIDFILE,LOGFILE}` into the xtask child. The verdict derives OUT-of-process from the registered `run/andromeda-pulse.pid` file, a liveness probe of the pid it holds (`ps -o stat=` on Unix, where a zombie `Z` counts as dead; `tasklist` on Windows), and the log family's newest-member mtime — a dead pid is `not-running` whatever the log's freshness says (chunk 2026-09-29-p-025-hue-shift-observable-made-gradable; before it, a crashed app read `running-healthy` for up to 60 s, measured on a CI boot smoke whose app panicked in 12 ms). The pure `classify(pid, alive, newest_log)` is pinned per arm, dead-pid and exited-child included, with its probe parsers pinned too. It is NOT a TauRPC `health` envelope and NOT computed in-script. It REPLACES the prior in-xtask-process `current_health()` call, which exited 0 unconditionally and could never say "not running" (the wrong-reason-pass this section previously recorded).
- **Verdict JSON (stdout):**
  ```json
  {
    "verdict": "running-healthy" | "stale" | "not-running" | "cannot-evaluate",
    "pid": 12345,
    "ended": null | "exit 0" | "signal 11 (SEGV)",
    "log_file_basename": "agent-latest.jsonl.2026-08-30",
    "last_write_age_seconds": 4,
    "stale_after_seconds": 60
  }
  ```
- **Exit code semantics:** 0 `running-healthy` (live pid + log written within `STALE_AFTER_SECONDS` 60) · 1 `stale` (live pid, log silent past the threshold) · 1 `not-running` (no live pid — a dead or zombie pid is `not-running` whatever the log says) · 2 `cannot-evaluate` (paths unresolvable). `classify(pid, alive, newest_log)` is a pure fn unit-pinned per arm, the dead-pid and exited-child cases included. `ended` (chunk 2026-09-29-ci-wall-time-and-round-trips) is the `run/andromeda-pulse.exit` record beside the pidfile, bounded to one line of ≤ 48 printable ASCII chars (anything else reads as no record, unit-pinned), reported only when the verdict is not `running-healthy`; real under both scripts since chunk 2026-09-30-perf-budget-gate-reads-real-samples, when the ps1 wrapper began writing the record (measured `"ended": "exit -1"`, `not-running`, exit 1, after `Stop-Process -Force`, whose `TerminateProcess(-1)` code the grammar accepts). The arms and exit codes are unchanged.

**`cleanup`** — tear down:
- **Command body:** Read the pid from `$PID_FILE` (the app's own `write_pid_file` value is canonical; the boot-time spawn pid covers only the crashed-before-write window); probe liveness across both pid spaces (msys `kill -0` first, then a genuinely-probing PowerShell `Get-Process` fallback — never `taskkill`/`tasklist /X` forms, never a `||` branch that manufactures the answer); TERM, bounded liveness-poll wait, KILL escalation
- **Idempotency:** safe to call twice — an absent pidfile with both ports refusing is `clean`
- **Verification:** the verdict derives ONLY from independent probes — pid liveness + TCP handshake on the RESOLVED `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_{GRPC,HTTP}_PORT` at `127.0.0.1` — never from the terminate call's own status. **The 2026-08-30-acl-rejection-logging wrong-reason-pass is CLOSED** (chunk 2026-08-30-agent-harness-teardown-truth, measured RED→GREEN on the sh script: RED at HEAD reproduced cleanup-exit-0 with the app alive and both ports accepting; GREEN shows non-zero on every survival shape and zero on verified teardown; ps1 mirrored in lockstep, its live leg owed via the §1 `harness-cleanup-verdict-and-boot-spawn-shell-coverage` trigger).
- **Exit code:** ONE bounded stdout token — `cleanup: clean | app-survived | ports-lingering | no-pid-ports-accepting` — exit 0 ONLY on `clean` (pid gone or never present, both ports refusing); exit 1 otherwise. The exit code is again evidence of teardown

**`logs`** — fetch product logs:
- **Command body:** resolve the ROTATED log FAMILY `agent-latest.jsonl*` across three precedence-ordered bases — the env override (`ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LOGFILE`, else `$ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR/logs/agent-latest.jsonl`), then `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/agent-latest.jsonl`, then the data-dir `logs/` — taking the NEWEST match within the first base that resolves (the glob expands in lexical order and the date suffix sorts ascending), and `tail -F` it; exit 1 with a diagnostic when no base resolves. **The `*` is load-bearing, not cosmetic:** the sink is `tracing_appender::rolling::daily(log_dir, "agent-latest.jsonl")`, which DATE-SUFFIXES every file (`agent-latest.jsonl.YYYY-MM-DD`), so a bare-name reader — or the `*.log` glob this line carried until 2026-08-26 — silently finds nothing and the caller then false-reports an empty log on a perfectly healthy boot. Matches obs-plan §3 Log file location (daily rotation; previous day's file read when the current one does not yet exist) and the shipped `scripts/agent-run.sh`.
- **Format:** JSON lines from `tracing-subscriber` with `{"timestamp":"2026-05-02T16:18:34.567Z","level":"INFO","target":"ingest::grpc","message":"…","fields":{…}}`
- **Retention window:** all on-disk logs for test session (not auto-purged within test harness; agent may tail last 1000 lines)
- **Agent parsing:** `jq 'select(.level == "ERROR") | .message' logs.jsonl | head -20` for errors; `grep -o "rows_ingested: [0-9]*" logs.jsonl | tail -1` for last ingest count

title: Status endpoint shape
body:
### Status endpoint shape

_This is the TauRPC `health` IPC payload (arch §Standard Contracts), unchanged — it is NOT the `status` verb's output: since chunk `2026-08-30-diagnostics-un-muting-harness-truth-sweep` the harness `status` verb emits the `harness:status` verdict JSON above, and this envelope is reached only through IPC (`health`)._

```json
{
  "status": "ok" | "degraded" | "unhealthy",
  "subsystems": {
    "otlp_grpc_receiver": { "status": "initialized" | "error", "error_msg": null | "string" },
    "otlp_http_receiver": { "status": "initialized" | "error", "error_msg": null | "string" },
    "buffer": { "status": "ready" | "error", "rows_ingested": 1250, "retention_seconds": 600 },
    "ingest_channel": { "status": "ready" | "error", "broadcast_subscribers": 3 }
  },
  "uptime_ms": 5432,
  "pid": 12345
}
```

**Agent reads:**
- `status == "ok"` for healthy; `"degraded"` acceptable if non-blocking subsystem failure
- `subsystems.*.status` all == `"initialized" | "ready"` (no `"error"`)
- `subsystems.buffer.rows_ingested` increment confirms OTLP ingest occurred
- `subsystems.ingest_channel.broadcast_subscribers >= 1` if real-time streams active
- `pid` matched against spawned process PID for identity verification

title: Log format
body:
### Log format

**Stream:** `RUST_LOG=debug cargo nextest run --workspace 2>&1 | tee test.log`

**Format:** Rust `tracing` crate JSON output via `tracing-subscriber::fmt().json().init()`

**Example:**
```json
{"timestamp":"2026-05-02T16:18:34.567Z","level":"INFO","target":"ingest::grpc","message":"TraceService.Export received 10 spans","fields":{"span_count":10,"service":"my-app"}}
{"timestamp":"2026-05-02T16:18:35.123Z","level":"ERROR","target":"buffer","message":"Row insertion failed","fields":{"error_code":"INVARIANT_VIOLATION","reason":"span_id length != 8"}}
```

**Agent-parseable signals:**
- Error detection: `jq 'select(.level == "ERROR") | .message' test.log | head -20`
- Ingest confirmation: `grep 'TraceService.Export received' test.log | tail -1`
- Subsystem startup: `grep 'listening on 127.0.0.1:4317' test.log` (confirm gRPC bind)
- Data leakage check: `! grep 'query parameters:' test.log` (assert no SQL params logged; validates anti-pattern)

title: PID file
body:
### PID file

- **Location:** `<data_dir>/run/andromeda-pulse.pid` on every platform — `<data_dir>` is `resolve_data_dir()` (overridable via `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR`), and the harness-only `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_PIDFILE` overrides the whole path. The single form the scripts, the app's `write_pid_file`, and arch §Occupied Resources all use (the former per-OS `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`/`$TMPDIR`/`%LOCALAPPDATA%` set was stale v1 text, measured false at chunk 2026-08-30-agent-harness-teardown-truth)
- **Lifecycle:** 
  - `boot` writes a provisional pid — since chunk 2026-09-29-ci-wall-time-and-round-trips the one the waiting wrapper records in `run/andromeda-pulse.spawn` — and the app's own `write_pid_file` overwrites the default pidfile with its canonical pid at boot (measured live earlier: file held app pid 59828, not the script's `$!` 128125 — msys pid space ≠ Windows pid space). Beside the pidfile the harness (never the product binary) also writes `run/andromeda-pulse.spawn` and `run/andromeda-pulse.exit`; the latter is `harness:status`'s `ended`
  - `status` reads the pidfile, probes that pid's liveness (a dead or zombie pid is `not-running`), and reads the log-family mtime via `cargo xtask harness:status`
  - `cleanup` terminates the pid the FILE holds (canonical), probing/killing across both pid spaces (msys `kill` first, PowerShell `Get-Process`/`Stop-Process` fallback — never `taskkill`/`tasklist` forms); the wrapper-pid defect is CLOSED (chunk 2026-08-30-agent-harness-teardown-truth)
- **Format:** single decimal PID on one line, no newline-stripping needed (portable)

title: Test data bootstrap
body:
### Test data bootstrap

- **Strategy:** Self-bootstrapping via OTLP ingest (tests send synthetic spans to live receiver)
- **Mechanism:** Rust builder factories + `rstest` fixtures
  - `MockTraceSpan::builder().service("test-app").trace_id([0u8; 16]).span_id([0u8; 8]).duration_ms(50).build()` → serializes to OTLP protobuf, sent via `tonic` client to `:4317`
  - `#[fixture] fn test_spans() -> Vec<TraceSpan> { vec![MockTraceSpan::builder()...] }` → composed with other fixtures per `rstest` composition
- **Per-test isolation:** `tempfile::TempDir` + `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR=$TMPDIR/test-$$` ensures fresh DuckDB `:memory:` per test; `tokio::time::pause()` for deterministic clock in retention tests; retention window override via config env `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_BUFFER_RETENTION_SEC=300` (verify old rows discarded after TTL expiry)
- **Cleanup:** `cleanup` command removes test data directory; explicit `drop(temp_dir)` in Rust tests

title: Bootstrap phases
body:
### Bootstrap phases

1. **test-runner-install:** `cargo-nextest` 0.9.x (per Phase 2 research; provides per-process isolation for port-binding tests)
2. **5-command-discipline-wire:** Materialize `scripts/agent-run.sh` with 5-command bodies (boot / run / status / cleanup / logs) per Section 3 above
3. **status-endpoint-implement:** Wire TauRPC `health` command to return required fields (status / subsystems / pid / uptime_ms)
4. **log-format-bind-with-obs:** Configure `tracing-subscriber::fmt().json()` to emit JSON per-line format (binds with obs-plan §3 JSON schema)
5. **pid-file-commitment-wire:** Write `<data_dir>/run/andromeda-pulse.pid` at boot (data-dir-relative, per §3 PID file → Location); read + verify at cleanup
6. **test-data-bootstrap-wire:** Implement `MockTraceSpan` builder factories in `ingest` crate; `MockArrowBatch` in `buffer` crate; `MockMetricPoint` in `viz` crate; implement `rstest` fixtures for composition. **UNIMPLEMENTED — measured 2026-08-23 (chunk `2026-08-23-metrics-points-identity`): all THREE factories return 0 workspace hits**, so this item is an owed mandate, not shipped bootstrap. The `rstest` fixture half DID land and is in use. Self-bootstrapping (§7) is satisfied in practice by OTLP ingest through the live receiver plus per-test in-memory DuckDB seeding; tracked as §1 `test-data-bootstrap-factories-unimplemented`
7. **coverage-tooling-install:** `cargo-llvm-cov` 0.8.5 for LCOV/Cobertura output
8. **quality-gate-config-emit:** GitHub Actions workflow enforces: line coverage ≥ 75%, branch ≥ 70%, zero-flakiness (no retries), perf-budget < 100ms p99 for RPC latency

title: Per-chunk gate discipline
body:
### Per-chunk gate discipline

Every `/andromeda-phase`-authored chunk plan's `## Test Commands` section MUST include the **standard gate set** (unconditional, regardless of webview-only / Rust-only / mixed scope):

```
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo xtask capability-widening-check
cargo xtask check:ingest-progress
cargo xtask check:staged-artifacts        # staged bindings + capability grants vs pins (exit 0/1/2; also runs inside capability-drift)
cargo xtask capability-drift              # BEFORE the workspace nextest — see the ordering note below
cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci
cargo nextest run -p pulse-app --features mcp-server --bin pulse-app -E 'test(emit_taurpc_bindings)'   # bindings regen: the last cargo-adjacent step
git diff --quiet <chunk-base> -- pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts   # the close, for a chunk adding no procedure
npm run lint --prefix pulse-app/ui        # webview gates: only when pulse-app/ui/** touched
npm run typecheck --prefix pulse-app/ui
npm run test --prefix pulse-app/ui
```

`cargo xtask check:ingest-progress` (added 2026-08-26) fails a run whose buffer consumer stopped draining. It keys on PROGRESS, not liveness — the stall definition at obs-plan §3/§10 is tick ABSENCE >45s, which the measured 2026-08-26 wedge satisfied throughout while persisting nothing. Four arms: a `buffer.consumer.stalled` record whose `reason` is not `recovered` ⇒ exit 1 · a recovery record ⇒ green · advancing ticks ⇒ PASS · no `buffer.tick` at all ⇒ NEUTRAL. The NEUTRAL arm is what makes it safe unconditionally — a chunk that booted nothing has no stream to judge, exactly like the in-process `perf_budget` grader, whose all-empty verdict with no arm required is NEUTRAL, never PASS.

`cargo xtask smoke:gap-resume` (added 2026-08-28) is a **SCENARIO leg, deliberately NOT a member of the standard gate set above.** It drives the ingest wedge's real shape — seed → GAP long enough that every service crosses its bootstrap window and the silence family escalates to tier1 → resume — under the direct-binary smoke form below (fresh `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` + `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_BASELINE_BOOTSTRAP_SECONDS` + `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC` set into the spawned app), and takes its verdict from the shipped `ingest_progress::evaluate` rather than a second detector. ~13 min, dev-host only, not CI-wired. **THREE arms, and they are different tests** (a third was added 2026-08-28 by chunk `2026-08-28-ingest-consumer-block-under-gap-resume`): `--sustained` (arm B — continuous feed, no gap, so no storm can form) is gate-grade; **arm A became gate-grade on 2026-08-28** (chunk `2026-08-28-duplicate-span-replay-fails-loudly`) when the consumer-wedge defect it reproduced was closed by the `duckdb`/`libduckdb-sys` 1.10502 → 1.10505 bump — it now exits 0 under a **TWO-HALF precondition**: the silence storm must have formed AND at least one append must have been REJECTED on replayed identities (`StormEvidence.append_rejections`, fed by `duckdb.append` records carrying `reject_reason`). Both halves are required because arm A drives the injector with `--replay`: without the rejection half a clean drain would prove the collision was ABSENT rather than survived, which is a pass for the wrong reason. Measured at promotion: 120 of 2270 appends rejected, consumer draining across 54 buffer ticks. `--reconnect-only` (`conflicts_with = "sustained"`) seeds, then reconnects IMMEDIATELY with no idle gap, which is what established that the idle window is NOT the operative variable. **A red on arm A is now a REAL REGRESSION, not a designed state** — and the standing instruction survives the promotion: arm A must **never** be weakened, removed, or `--expect-absent`'d to obtain a green wrap. It is the only on-demand reproduction of this defect class, so the guard is what keeps a future red diagnosed rather than hidden. (The repair-route ownership pointer is discharged.) **Each arm carries its OWN precondition, and no arm may borrow another's:** a gap-arm pass with no silence storm in the log reports INCONCLUSIVE, not PASS; a storm in the control arm is likewise INCONCLUSIVE; and the reconnect arm — which has no storm by construction — instead requires FEED evidence (at least one `duckdb.append`, via `StormEvidence::fed()`), so a run where the producer never delivered cannot report a vacuous pass. **Known gap — CLOSED 2026-08-28** (chunk `2026-08-28-duplicate-span-replay-fails-loudly`): the leg now guards `observe_minutes` against the stall threshold its verdict reads, via `observe_window_supports_verdict()` and `const STALL_ANNOUNCEMENT_SECONDS: u64 = 450` in `xtask/src/gap_resume.rs` — a window below the threshold is refused as INCONCLUSIVE before the run starts, rather than producing a structurally-impossible PASS. Unit-pinned at the boundary (7 m refused / 8 m accepted / the 9 m default accepted). The original measurement stands as the reason the guard exists: `--observe-minutes=3` reported PASS over a consumer that had in fact stopped, because 180 s cannot reach the 450 s announcement (chunks `2026-08-28-ingest-consumer-initiating-freeze`, `2026-08-28-ingest-consumer-block-under-gap-resume`).

`cargo xtask smoke:external-resolve` (added 2026-08-29, chunk `2026-08-29-app-registry-reconciliation`) is the **second SCENARIO leg** in that family — likewise **NOT a member of the standard gate set**, dev-host only, not CI-wired, `xtask/src/external_resolve.rs` with `--bootstrap-seconds` / `--observe-seconds`. It runs the direct-binary smoke form (fresh `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` + `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_BASELINE_BOOTSTRAP_SECONDS` + `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC` set into the spawned app) and drives the app-registry-vs-durable-store divergence end to end: boot → finite storm over real OTLP → resolve an incident through a REAL `andromeda-pulse-mcp` subprocess → observe two 60 s persist cycles. **The verdict keys on `reconciled_count` (≥ 1) and `declined_count` (0) — explicitly NOT on `item_count`, which is printed as context only.** That exclusion is measured, not stylistic: under a mutation removing reconciliation, `item_count` still went 2 → 0 in BOTH arms, because the finite storm's auto-resolve fires 120 s after the last re-emission and the observation window covers it — a verdict keyed on the drop would have passed in both worlds. GREEN measured `reconciled 1 / declined 0`; the mutation arm measured `reconciled 0 / declined 2`, the pre-fix signature. **Two shaping constraints, both measured:** `--sustained` CANNOT drive this leg (it holds a constant error rate, so the cue evaluator's short/long EWMA ratio converges and never trips the gate — 0 incidents in 240 s), and the finite injector must be BACKGROUNDED rather than awaited, or the 120 s auto-resolve window closes before the external write lands and the sidecar has nothing active to resolve. Like its sibling it **proves its own preconditions** — no incident visible to the sidecar, or a resolve the guard did not apply, reports INCONCLUSIVE rather than PASS — and it refuses an `--observe-seconds` below two persist cycles up front (`observe_window_supports_verdict`), the same structurally-impossible-verdict guard `smoke:gap-resume` carries.

`cargo xtask smoke:hue-shift` (added 2026-09-29, chunk `2026-09-29-p-025-hue-shift-observable-made-gradable`) is the **third SCENARIO leg** — likewise **NOT a member of the standard gate set**, dev-host only, not CI-wired, `xtask/src/hue_shift.rs` (reusing `external_resolve`'s direct-binary helpers). It drives a finite storm against the release binary under the direct-binary smoke form and grades the P-025 observable `metric.constellation.hue_update_ms`: the rise sample against `interpretation.incident.created`, the fall sample against the first `triage.incident.auto_resolve.tick` with `resolved_count ≥ 1`, **each on anchor error ≤ 1000 ms** — the ≤ 2000 ms P-025 budget is context only, since Conductor's live leg grades P-025 itself. The storm is stopped once the rise paints, and both samples are graded even when the rise fails. Exit contract: 0 PASS · 1 FAIL · 2 INCONCLUSIVE — a precondition unmet (no incident formed) reports INCONCLUSIVE, never PASS; artifact under `target/hue-shift/`. Measured at that chunk: RED at the pre-fix HEAD, GREEN after (readings in its `evidence/`).

`cargo xtask smoke:discovery` (added 2026-09-30, chunk `2026-09-30-p-027-discovery-bound`) is the **fourth SCENARIO leg** — likewise **NOT a member of the standard gate set**, dev-host only, not CI-wired, `xtask/src/discovery.rs` (reusing `external_resolve`'s direct-binary helpers). It boots the release binary on a fresh data dir, waits (≤ 60 s) for a `services.list_with_states.request` record — the webview polling — then starts `inject_demo --sustained --error-pct=0` and grades the P-027 observable `metric.constellation.discovery_ms`: the first discovery record at or after the first `duckdb.append {table_name: spans}` (the first sighting — every injector batch carries all five demo services) within a 30 s observe window. PASS iff the first-sighting→dot interval ≤ 5000 ms AND the sample's own anchor (`timestamp − duration_ms`) lies ≤ 1000 ms from that append AND the log holds 0 `app.panic.fatal` and 0 ERROR; no sample in the window is FAIL, worded as an observation. It proves its own preconditions — no spans append, the webview not polling before it, or a data dir already holding a log family (pid reuse in the shared tempdir helper) reports INCONCLUSIVE, never PASS — and refuses a window below 21 s (`observe_window_supports_verdict`: a 15 s tick + a 1 s poll + margin, so the RED reading stays reachable). Exit contract: 0 PASS · 1 FAIL · 2 INCONCLUSIVE; artifact under `target/discovery/`. Measured at that chunk: RED at the base (interval 15 219 ms, anchor error 14 784 ms), GREEN after (177 ms, 6 ms) — readings in its `evidence/`.

`cargo xtask perf:frame-sample` (added 2026-09-30, chunk `2026-09-30-perf-budget-gate-reads-real-samples`, `xtask/src/perf_frame.rs`) is the **dev-host frame-budget gate** — NOT a member of the standard gate set and NOT CI-wired (the hosted Windows runner exposed no WebGPU adapter, `ci#36723465727`). Windows only; it needs the release `pulse-app.exe` and `examples/inject_demo.exe` and free :4317/:4318, boots the app on a fresh TempDir with `WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS` (the SwiftShader WebGPU flag set) on the app child only, polls ≤ 60 s for a first frame, feeds `inject_demo --sustained` for 30 s, tears down by pid with a port check, and grades the frame arm as required. Exit contract: 0 PASS · 1 FAIL (0 samples once healthy, or p99 > 33 ms) · 2 INCONCLUSIVE (not Windows, a binary missing, a port in use, the app never healthy); artifact under `target/perf-frame/<UTC stamp>/`; 2 unit pins (`platform_guard`, `child_env`). Measured at that chunk: p99 2.6 ms, n = 7971. Its CI sibling is `cargo xtask perf:budget --data-dir <DIR> --require <arm,arm>` — exit 0 PASS · 1 FAIL · 2 cannot-evaluate (an unknown arm, no log family under `<DIR>/logs`, or every arm empty with none required).

`cargo xtask pre-push:linux` (added 2026-09-29, chunk `2026-09-29-ci-wall-time-and-round-trips`, `xtask/src/pre_push.rs`) is the **local Linux pre-push check** — an xtask verb because the 5-command `agent-run` discipline admits no sixth verb; NOT a CI step; it requires a Windows host with the WSL `Ubuntu` distro (`wsl.exe`), so since the dev host moved to Omarchy Linux (2026-10-03) it cannot run on the dev host — at chunk `2026-10-02-incident-events-readable-through-mcp` its six stages ran natively and env-isolated in its place under a founder ruling (2026-10-03; green re-run, 2575/2575), and porting the verb to native Linux is its own route entry ("pre-push:linux runs natively on Linux", placed after "Retry-storm interpretation names its cause"). It syncs a distro clone to HEAD plus the working tree (one binary patch through a temporary index, verified by tree-id equality) and runs the Linux-reachable gates in order, stopping at the first failure — six stages since chunk `2026-10-01-real-model-incident-surfacing`: `script-modes` (`scripts/agent-run.sh` git mode 100755) · `source-lint` (`cargo xtask check:english-sources` in the clone — the same English-only source gate ci.yml's `lint-test` runs, so a Cyrillic literal reds locally before a push) · `npm` (`npm ci` + `npm run build`) · `clippy` (`--workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`) · `test` (`cargo xtask test`) · `ci-gates` over a fresh data dir seeded with non-metric records. Exit 0 green · 1 red · 2 cannot-evaluate; one pretty-JSON verdict `{verdict, reason, head, tree, stages[{name, ok, ms}], missing[], remediation, cache{bytes, cap, cleaned}}` plus `target/pre-push/report.json`. A pinned tool or package missing (the toolchain channel, ci.yml's Node major and apt list, `jq` / `git` / `xvfb-run` / `cc`) reads `cannot-evaluate` with the one apt remediation line, never green; it binds no port and starts no `pulse-app`. Measured green 2026-09-29 (5/5 stages, 2408 → 2411 Linux tests; ~12 min cold, warm test stage 24.9 s); measured green 2026-10-01 with the sixth stage (6/6 stages ×2, `source-lint` 7.4 s; chunk `2026-10-01-real-model-incident-surfacing` evidence `operator-pass.md`). Fragility: its Node 24 is the Viola repo's `~/.local/viola-node/bin` install in the distro — the distro's apt ships Node 22 / npm 9 — so losing that install turns the verb `cannot-evaluate`.

`cargo xtask capability-drift` runs BEFORE the default-features `cargo nextest run --workspace` (the overseer's founder-delegated directive of 2026-09-30, first run at chunk 2026-09-30-dual-license). That workspace run rewrites `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` to the no-mcp shape (`taurpc`'s `export_types()` on every `Router::into_handler()`), so a drift read placed after it read a clobbered worktree; before it, the worktree bindings are still the committed mcp shape. The `--features mcp-server` `emit_taurpc_bindings` regen then follows the workspace run as the LAST cargo-adjacent step, repairing what that run rewrote, and a probe named against the chunk base closes the sequence: `git diff --quiet <chunk-base> -- pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts`, exit 0 meaning the bindings end byte-identical to the base. That close is what was measured, for a chunk that adds no TauRPC procedure. A chunk that CHANGES the procedure set closes instead with (first run at chunk 2026-09-30-perf-instruments-measure-their-budgets, approved by the operator at its wrap): the `--features mcp-server` regen after the workspace run → two content probes on the worktree bindings (the new procedure's name; `grep -c '"mcp":'` ≥ 1) → `git add` of the regenerated bindings WITH the `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` pin (index only, no commit) → `check:staged-artifacts`, then `capability-drift` LAST — both read the staged copy, and before the regen the committed bindings lack the pinned procedure, so drift cannot run earlier. The regen must also PRECEDE the `ui/dist` build and every release build a live leg drives: the taurpc proxy resolves methods against the `ARGS_MAP` bundled into `ui/dist`, so a dist built before the regen ships without the new method and a fire-and-forget caller no-ops silently (measured at that chunk: 1 bundle occurrence — the caller's own property access — vs 2 once rebuilt after the regen). `cargo xtask check:staged-artifacts` (added 2026-08-30-staged-bindings-assertion, `xtask/src/staged_gate.rs`) makes the staged assertion CODE inside the gate itself: it reads the git-INDEX copies of `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` + all `pulse-app/capabilities/*.json` (via a `git ls-files --stage` health probe then `git show :<path>` per subject) against `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` + `staged_gate::EXPECTED_GRANTS`, with one pretty-JSON verdict on stdout (`{gate:"staged-artifacts", arm, verdict, bindings{…}, grants{…}}`), arms `staged-clean`/`staged-drift`/`cannot-evaluate` at exit 0/1/2, report twin `target/staged-artifacts/report.json`, and a staged DELETION of a subject or an UNPINNED `pulse-app/capabilities/*.json` file findings-RED (no neutral arm) — and `capability_drift()` RUNS that same staged assertion after its unchanged worktree diff, folding ANY non-clean staged outcome into its existing 0/1 failure exit. The worktree can be correct while the index carries a clobbered version — exactly what the staged read catches (playbook.md 2026-08-22's ORDERING rule stands; its interim manual `git show | grep` assertion is superseded by the shipped gate).

The webview gates (`npm run lint` / `typecheck` / `test`) are excluded only when the chunk's Files-to-modify / New-files lists touch zero `pulse-app/ui/**` paths. Tracked as coverage trigger `chunk-gate-baseline-coverage`. Rationale: without an unconditional baseline at every chunk, gate-coverage drift accumulates and surfaces only when a downstream chunk's broader gate list catches a pre-existing failure.

**Boot-smoke gate (conditional).** Chunks whose plan touches a boot/setup path — `pulse-app/src/main.rs`, `crates/ui-bridge/src/`, `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` (boot-time subscriber/allowlist init, before the OTLP bind), `pulse-app/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`, or `pulse-app/capabilities/*.json` — MUST additionally include a runtime smoke gate: `cd pulse-app && npx @tauri-apps/cli dev` with a 60-second timeout, watching stdout for boot-completion signals (`Local:` / `ready in` / `Compiled successfully`) before SIGTERM.

**Direct-binary smoke variant (accepted alternative form).** When the verification needs runtime state neither `npx @tauri-apps/cli dev` nor the harness `run` verb can express — a fresh `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR`, an env-gated mode such as `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC=true`, or a sustained OTLP load from `inject_demo` — launch the product binary directly under those env vars in EITHER profile (`target/debug/pulse-app.exe` or `target/release/pulse-app.exe`; the harness `boot` verb itself IS the direct-binary form since chunk 2026-08-30-agent-harness-teardown-truth — it pre-builds then launches `target/release/pulse-app[.exe]` by path, no `cargo run` wrapper), seed over the real receiver, then assert from the run's own artifacts: 0 `app.panic.fatal` / 0 `ERROR` in `<data_dir>/logs/agent-latest.jsonl*`, and clean shutdown by SPECIFIC pid (`powershell -NoProfile -Command "Stop-Process -Id <pid> -Force"`) with `:4317`/`:4318` confirmed released. **The clean-log assertion binds the GREEN leg only.** A MEASURE-FIRST chunk runs the same form twice — once at HEAD to witness the defect, once after the fix — and the RED leg is by construction an unhealthy run. **What the RED leg PRODUCES depends on the defect's shape, and only one of the two shapes emits an ERROR.** A REJECT-shaped defect (a write refused, a batch failed) emits the ERROR it is measuring, so asserting 0 ERROR over it would contradict the measurement. A **BLOCK-shaped** defect emits nothing at all — nothing returns, so nothing reports — and a RED leg over it carries **0 `ERROR` and 0 `app.panic.fatal`**, which makes the clean-log assertion pass **VACUOUSLY** (the same wrong-reason-pass hazard this section already records for the `status` verb). For that shape the evidence of record is **absence of progress**: a frozen `rows_ingested`, consecutive zero-delta `buffer.tick`s, `buffer.consumer.stalled`, `ingest.channel.full`. Measured 2026-08-28 (chunk `2026-08-28-ingest-consumer-initiating-freeze`): a RED leg reproduced a 450 s consumer stall with 0 ERROR and 0 panics throughout. Decide which shape the leg is measuring BEFORE choosing its evidence. Each leg gets its OWN fresh data dir so neither reads the other's residue, and the RED leg records its expected ERROR (target + `reject_reason`) as evidence rather than as a gate failure. (Codified 2026-08-23 at chunk `2026-08-23-metrics-points-identity`, whose RED leg recorded one `duckdb.append` ERROR with `reject_reason: "append_failed"` by design.) `bash scripts/agent-run.sh status` still runs as the listed harness gate — and since chunk `2026-08-30-diagnostics-un-muting-harness-truth-sweep` it is TRUTHFUL about liveness: the verb delegates to `cargo xtask harness:status`, so a no-app run exits non-zero with `verdict: "not-running"` (live-proven 2026-08-30 — the 2026-08-23 "exits 0 and emits a full payload even when nothing is running" measurement described the retired in-process form); the direct-binary artifacts remain the evidence of record for run-specific claims. Measured 2026-08-15 (chunk 2026-08-15-tier-1-incident-path-investigation): two full boots on separate fresh data dirs verified a boot-time allowlist change that no in-process form could observe, since the fields under test are only produced by a live storm. The in-process 5-command harness does not catch trait-level binding-emission panics that fire at boot in a non-Tokio context (e.g. the `crates/ui-bridge/src/health.rs` "there is no reactor running" panic). On smoke failure the chunk surfaces "green per scope; runtime blocked" rather than blocking commit. Tracked as coverage trigger `boot-smoke-coverage`.

**Process-end witness form (integration tier).** A claim that a record SURVIVES THE PROCESS ENDING is cross-process, so it is witnessed by re-exec children, never in-process (chunk `2026-10-01-conductor-return`, `pulse-app/tests/integration_exit_cause_record.rs`): the parent re-runs the test binary with `--exact <fn>` and an arm name in the environment; each child calls `observability::init` on its OWN TempDir data dir, ends its process through ONE class, and the parent reads the child's `agent-latest.jsonl*` family only after the child has ended — exactly one `app.exit` per loggable class, its fields rendered, 0 full paths, 0 planted canary. Child-ran proof is IN-ARM: each arm requires the child's `app.boot.tracing.init` record, because child stdout is discarded (`Stdio::null()`) and a `--no-capture` read shows nothing from children. A once-flag whose sink's only drain is a guard drop is pinned by the emitter's RETURN value reported through the child's exit code, never by a file read — the first flush closes the sink, so a second record can never reach the file and a file read passes with the flag removed (measured: the whole once-guard neutralized left every file-reading arm green). Arms that only Unix can run (`std::process::exit` reaching `atexit`; SIGTERM ending the child BY signal 15) are `cfg(unix)` — run natively by `cargo nextest run --workspace` on the Linux dev host (Omarchy, since the 2026-10-03 host move; measured 2575 = 2573 + these two arms at chunk `2026-10-02-incident-events-readable-through-mcp`) and by CI lint-test Linux/macOS; on a Windows host they are unrunnable. The form cannot reach the ends unloggable by construction (SIGKILL, `_exit`, Windows `TerminateProcess`, a Rust `std::process::exit` on Windows, pre-sink failures); RED at base is the block-shaped absence of the record (§3 Direct-binary smoke variant's shape rule).
