body:
_Generated by `/andromeda-obs`. This file is the single source of truth
for all observability strategy + harness contracts + SLO invariants.
Read by downstream skills (a11y / route / setup-project per D26
cross-cutting), obs-pass per-phase, combine + `/implement` (via phase
loop)._

_Do not edit during phase loop runs (obs-pass / combine / `/implement`).
Manual edits between runs are fine._

_**Agent-driven invariant:** every telemetry signal described in this
plan must be readable by an agent from a snapshot or pasted log
excerpt. No human-only dashboards, no proprietary APM lock-in, no
human-review-gated log analysis. If a surface cannot be agent-readable,
it is flagged "not-instrumentable" in obs-scope.md Section 1 and
handled via boundary instrumentation only._

title: 1. Obs Scope Summary

body: **Obs tier:** Standard (1)
**Justification:**

- **Cross-platform desktop scope:** Tauri 2 desktop app (Windows/macOS/Linux) with 8 instrumentable modules (ingest, buffer, viz, ui-bridge, snapshot, workspace-detector, plugins, mcp-server), 9 major surfaces (desktop-webview, desktop-native, IPC-internal, API service gRPC, API service HTTP, CLI, library-only plugin host, MCP stdio and, since chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process, the console engine's door — JSON-RPC 2.0 over a Unix-domain socket, console program only; 8 before it), and 7 critical user-facing must-trace paths (P1–P7: receive-and-visualize OTLP, curated snapshots, MCP tool queries, plugin lifecycle, UI layout transitions, real-time Arrow IPC push, workspace detection).

- **Standard-tier drivers:** security_tier=Minimal (loopback-only binding, no user accounts, in-memory data, no compliance); tests_tier=Standard (span coverage across 19 testable entities, 7 critical paths, 28+ rejected attack vectors, agent-driven deterministic signals). Obs matches tests at Standard — the multi-surface complexity, perf-budget enforcement, and PII-scrubbing rigor warrant rich structured `tracing` instrumentation.

- **Multi-surface trace propagation:** cross-surface W3C `traceparent` correlation — span fields at receiver entry, IPC envelope `traceparent` carried into TauRPC handler spans, Arrow metadata `_trace_context` field on push streams.

- **Creator perf-budget SLOs:** token-efficient curated-snapshot guarantees plus frontend telemetry (WebGPU frame timing + skeleton-pulse durations over the hand-rolled TauRPC `telemetry.frontend.*` bridge — `web-vitals` RETIRED 2026-08-30, see §3 Frontend bridge) flow into the same `tracing` JSON log via the TauRPC bridge as `metric.*` events; the security plan's 6 logging-sensitive vectors drive `#[tracing::instrument(skip(...))]` field exclusion + custom subscriber Layer redaction.

- **Architectural choice (self-observation runtime):** uses ONLY the `tracing` ecosystem (`tracing` 0.1 + `tracing-subscriber` 0.3 JSON formatter + `tracing-appender` daily file sink + `tracing-error` SpanTrace) — NO OTel SDK is linked into the product binary for self-observation. External OTLP receiving (`tonic`/`axum`/`prost`/`opentelemetry-proto`) is unaffected (wire-format parsing only, no OTel SDK runtime required). By construction there is no exporter to misconfigure and no recursion concern — the JSON file at `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/agent-latest.jsonl` IS the agent-readable surface.
**Instrumentation scope (entities needing instrumentation):**
| Entity | Source | Instrumentability | Reason if not fully instrumentable |

| **ingest (OTLP receivers)** | Arch: Stack + Workspace | instrumentable | gRPC (`tonic` 0.14.x) and HTTP (`axum` 0.8.x) receivers require span/trace context propagation via W3C traceparent and gRPC metadata; ingest span boundary (arch excerpt Section 1) |

| **buffer (DuckDB ring + Arrow)** | Arch: Stack + Workspace | instrumentable | DuckDB 1.5.x query instrumentation for appender latency; Arrow zero-copy IPC instrumentation for append operations; storage and query boundary (arch excerpt Section 1) |

| **viz (query layer)** | Arch: Workspace | instrumentable | TauRPC query surface feeding WebGPU canvas; visualization query boundary; span instrumentation on `traces.query`, `metrics.query`, `logs.query` (arch excerpt Section 1) |

| **ui-bridge (TauRPC)** | Arch: Stack + Workspace | instrumentable | TauRPC routers for all command surfaces with trace context propagation in IPC envelope; IPC boundary (arch excerpt Section 1, Section 3 Standard Contracts) |

| **snapshot (markdown generator)** | Arch: Workspace + Creator Brief | instrumentable | Token budget enforcement and curation pipeline telemetry (dedup count, anomaly detection markers); curation boundary (arch excerpt Section 1, creator brief Section 6: "token-efficient curated snapshot", "token_count ≤ 25000") |

| **workspace-detector** | Arch: Workspace | instrumentable | Project discovery boundary; `.andromeda/` marker detection; structured logs on workspace detection success/failure (arch excerpt Section 1) |

| **plugins (Wasmtime)** | Arch: Stack + Workspace | instrumentable | Loaded plugin count and per-plugin invocation latency; capability-scoped sandboxing requires spans per capability grant; plugin invocation boundary (arch excerpt Section 1, tests excerpt P4) |

| **mcp-server (hand-rolled JSON-RPC stdio)** | Arch: Stack + Workspace | boundary-only | MCP stdio surface feature-gated (`--features mcp-server`); instrumentation at boundary (stdin JSON-RPC 2.0 request/response); tool response bodies must NOT be logged (security plan vector 4); MCP protocol boundary (arch excerpt Section 1, Section 2 Vector 4) |

| **Tauri app bundle** | Arch: Stack + Obs-Relevant Conventions | instrumentable | Service identity per arch bundle identifier `com.andromeda.pulse` and binary name `andromeda-pulse`; app lifecycle spans (boot, shutdown); built-in Tauri command interception for IPC tracing (arch excerpt Section 1) |

| **WebView2 / WKWebView (frontend)** | Arch: Stack + Design System | instrumentable | WebGPU canvas performance instrumentation via DOM `performance.now()` + `device.queue.onSubmittedWorkDone()`; bridged to backend via TauRPC `telemetry.frontend.record_*` commands → `tracing::info!(target: "metric.{name}", ...)` events (`web-vitals` RETIRED 2026-08-30 — measured never installed; page-load-shaped metrics do not fit a persistent fixed-layout desktop webview; the hand-rolled bridge is the DECIDED mechanism). NO browser OTel SDK linked into the webview — recursion-free by construction (see Section 3 Snapshot/paste-to-AI integration). (design system excerpt Section 3: "skeleton pulse", "LCP proxy") |

| **OS notifications (native)** | Arch: Stack | boundary-only | `tauri-plugin-notification` 2.x emits native OS notifications; instrument boundary (notification dismiss/interaction events); no telemetry from OS internals (arch excerpt Section 1) |

| **tauri-plugin-updater** | Arch: Stack | boundary-only | Minisign Ed25519 verification boundary; instrument update check/download/install transitions; no telemetry from GitHub Releases API itself (arch excerpt Section 1) |

| **tokio runtime** | Arch: Stack | instrumentable | Async runtime spans for spawn, task scheduling, channel operations; `tokio::sync::mpsc` + `tokio::sync::broadcast` channel capacity metrics and subscriber counts (arch excerpt Section 1: "emit metrics on channel capacity and subscriber counts") |

| **DuckDB in-memory ring buffer** | Arch: Stack | instrumentable | Ring buffer retention window enforcement (5–10 min configurable); overflow/eviction telemetry required for chaos tests (tests excerpt: "assert oldest spans evicted; buffer memory stays bounded") |

| **Apache Arrow IPC** | Arch: Stack | instrumentable | Zero-copy serialization latency; size-capped untrusted plugin-returned Arrow IPC (security plan anti-pattern: "Untrusted plugin-returned Arrow IPC without size cap"); schema validation on deserialize (arch excerpt Section 1) |

| **error handling (thiserror + anyhow)** | Arch: Stack | instrumentable | Module-internal error enums via `thiserror` 2.x; boundary catch-all via `anyhow` 1.x; structured error tags for categorization (arch excerpt Section 1); `AppError` enum conversion at IPC bridge (security plan Section 2, vector 2) |

| **config management** | Arch: Stack | instrumentable | Layered config (env vars > user file > defaults) with structured logs on config load success/failure; path canonicalization validation per security plan CWE-22 anti-pattern (arch excerpt Section 1, security plan Section 2 anti-patterns) |

| **plugin file path resolution** | Arch: Stack + Security Plan | instrumentable | Symlink canonicalization per security plan CWE-22; basename-only logging (no full paths) per security plan vector 3 (security plan Section 2, vector 3) |

| **OTLP HTTP body size limit** | Arch: Stack | instrumentable | `axum` DefaultBodyLimit on `:4318 /v1/traces` POST; instrument boundary rejection (413 / parse error); chaos test coverage (tests excerpt: "POST oversized payload > 8 MB → assert HTTP 413") |

| **Cranelift-only WASM backend** | Arch: Stack | not-instrumentable | Build-time feature (wasmtime Cranelift feature flag); not runtime telemetry; compile-time gate only (tests excerpt: "Build-time test: assert wasmtime resolved with Cranelift feature") |

| **GitHub Actions CI/CD** | Arch: CI/CD Platform | boundary-only | External CI/CD system; instrument GitHub Releases webhook boundary only; no GitHub Actions API telemetry in app (arch excerpt Section 1) |
| **Configuration schema** | Arch: Stack | not-instrumentable | Static configuration parsing (env vars, TOML file); no runtime telemetry generation (configuration is input, not runtime entity) |
**Telemetry surfaces:**
| Surface | Backend instrumentation hooks | Frontend instrumentation hooks | Sink | Service identity | Notes |

| **desktop-webview (Windows WebView2 + macOS WKWebView + Linux GTK WebKit, React 19 + Tailwind v4)** | `tracing` 0.1 + `tracing-subscriber` JSON formatter; `#[tracing::instrument]` attribute on TauRPC router methods (Rust); trace context propagation via IPC envelope `traceparent` field treated as plain `tracing` span field; `tokio` runtime async span propagation via `tracing::Span::current().in_current_span()` | WebGPU frame timing via DOM `performance.now()` + `device.queue.onSubmittedWorkDone()` → TauRPC `telemetry.frontend.record_frame_ms(duration_ms, wgpu_backend)` → backend `tracing::info!(target: "metric.webgpu.frame_duration_ms", ...)`; skeleton pulse duration / empty-state counter via same TauRPC bridge (the DECIDED frontend mechanism — `web-vitals` 5.x and its `record_web_vital` → `metric.web_vital.{name}` chain RETIRED 2026-08-30: measured never installed, no producer and no consumer existed, page-load metrics do not fit a persistent desktop webview) | structured JSON via `tracing-subscriber` JSON formatter to `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/agent-latest.jsonl` (daily rotation via `tracing-appender`) — single agent-readable surface | `service.name`: `com.andromeda.pulse` (Tauri bundle identifier, arch excerpt Section 1); `service.version`: from `Cargo.toml` `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")` or runtime read from `tauri.conf.json`; `deployment.environment`: `production` (hardcoded for desktop app) — embedded as `fields.service_name` / `fields.service_version` on every log line via subscriber-level default fields | Frontend has NO browser OTel SDK and NO direct file access — all frontend telemetry goes through TauRPC → backend tracing. Single JSON log file is the unified self-observation surface for both backend and frontend. Eliminates the "browser exporter targeting own `:4318`" recursion concern by construction. |

| **desktop-native (tray icon via NotifyIcon/NSStatusItem/AppIndicator; Windows/macOS/Linux)** | Tauri lifecycle hooks emit `tracing::info!(target: "tray.{event}", ...)` events on tray visibility / menu interaction / notification dismiss / notification action; `tracing` events ride the same JSON file sink as the rest of the app | None (native tray is UI only; no browser runtime) | structured JSON via shared `tracing-subscriber` sink (single file) | `service.name`: `com.andromeda.pulse`; `service.version`: from `Cargo.toml` / `tauri.conf.json`; `deployment.environment`: `production` | Tray events are emitted at the boundary (dismiss / action click); OS notification center internals are out of scope. Self-observation surface is unified with backend + webview-bridged events in one JSON file. |

| **IPC-internal (Tauri TauRPC + tokio channels)** | `#[tracing::instrument(skip_all, fields(traceparent = %tp))]` on each TauRPC router method; `tracing` spans wrap entire command execution; tokio channel utilization emitted as `tracing::info!(target: "metric.channel.{name}", capacity_pct = X, subscribers = Y, ...)` events per heartbeat tick | N/A | structured JSON via shared `tracing-subscriber` sink | `service.name`: `com.andromeda.pulse` (unified app); trace context propagated via IPC envelope `traceparent` field, attached to span as a regular `tracing` field | IPC envelope (TauRPC command struct) carries optional `traceparent` field per W3C convention; receiver attaches it to the local span. tokio channel pressure emitted as `tracing` events every 10-30s tick. |

| **API service (OTLP/gRPC `:4317` + OTLP/HTTP `:4318`)** | `#[tracing::instrument(skip(req), fields(rpc.system = "grpc", rpc.service, rpc.method, span_count))]` on each tonic gRPC service method handler; manual `tower::Layer` (or `tower-http::TraceLayer`) on the axum router emits HTTP request/response spans; W3C `traceparent` extracted from gRPC metadata (`grpc-trace-bin`) or HTTP header at request entry, attached to the local `tracing` span as a `traceparent` field; OTLP payload parse latency wrapped by inner `parse.protobuf` span | N/A (external clients control their own SDKs) | structured JSON via shared `tracing-subscriber` sink (NOT the OTLP receivers themselves — those are the product's external surface, not its self-observation channel) | `service.name`: `com.andromeda.pulse`; `service.version`: from Cargo metadata; `deployment.environment`: `production` | Loopback-only binding (security plan Section 2): `127.0.0.1:4317` (gRPC) and `127.0.0.1:4318` (HTTP); negative test rejection of `0.0.0.0` override. Ingest boundary `tracing` events use `skip(...)` to keep raw OTLP attributes out of self-observation logs (security plan vector 1). |

| **CLI (command-line entrypoint via `andromeda-pulse` binary)** | `tracing` 0.1 + `tracing-subscriber` JSON formatter at boot; structured `tracing::error!` on startup failure / config validation failure; **Observability harness specification:**

- **Tracing init:** `tracing` 0.1 + `tracing-subscriber` 0.3 with JSON formatter as the SOLE self-observation runtime — NO OTel SDK linked into the product binary for self-observation (the product's CORE function of receiving external OTLP via `tonic`/`axum`/`prost`/`opentelemetry-proto` is unaffected; those crates handle wire format only and don't require an OTel SDK). Initialization order: (1) Load config + validate log level (`ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LOG_LEVEL` env var with fallback `RUST_LOG`), (2) build `tracing-subscriber::registry()` composing `EnvFilter::from_env(...)` + ONE `fmt::layer().json().with_writer(non_blocking_file_appender)` + `ErrorLayer` (no stderr layer — as measured at chunk `2026-10-02-incident-events-readable-through-mcp`), (3) install panic hook calling `tracing::error!(target: "app.panic.fatal", ...)`, (4) `engine_boot::start` binds the OTLP receivers, then — window app only — the Tauri app. Boot-time before HTTP/gRPC bind. Since chunk 2026-10-10-console-engine-entry-point steps (1)–(3) and what follows them are the process start both programs call once, `engine_boot::init_process`: after init it parks the returned `WorkerGuard` in a process-wide slot (`hold_log_guard` — `init` keeps returning it), installs the at-exit hook (`install_exit_hook`) and, on Unix, the SIGTERM/SIGINT listener (`install_signal_listener`), then records the start instant and writes the pid file; the console program (`andromeda-pulse-engine run`) has no event loop and ends by SIGTERM or SIGINT through that listener with one `app.exit` of class `signal`; the window app's Tauri app runs through `run_return`, whose exit code goes to `exit_after_event_loop` (record `app.exit` → drop the guard → `std::process::exit` with the same code) — `WorkerGuard::drop` is the non-blocking file sink's only drain, and a plain `run` ends in tao's `process::exit` with the worker undrained (§6 `app.exit`). Why this approach: by not linking an OTel SDK into the self-runtime, the "OTel monitoring an OTel monitor" recursion concern disappears by construction — there is no exporter to point anywhere, and the file-sink JSON line IS the agent-readable surface.

- **Service identity:** `service.name` = `com.andromeda.pulse` (compile-time: Tauri bundle identifier, arch excerpt Section 1); `service.version` = `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")` at compile time (or runtime read from `tauri.conf.json` for the desktop bundle build); `deployment.environment` = `production` (hardcoded for desktop app; no staging/dev distinction at runtime). Embedded as default fields on every `tracing` event via `tracing_subscriber::fmt::Layer::with_default_fields([service_name, service_version, deployment_environment])` so every JSON log line carries identity without per-call boilerplate.

- **Logging stack:** `tracing` 0.1 + `tracing-subscriber` 0.3 JSON formatter + `tracing-appender` 0.2 daily-rolling file sink + `tracing-error` 0.2 SpanTrace for sanitized error chains. The app has a SINGLE sink: the file `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/agent-latest.jsonl`, always JSON-only — no stderr `tracing` layer, no TTY pretty-print (as measured at chunk `2026-10-02-incident-events-readable-through-mcp`: `observability::init` builds the file layer only). For the mcp-server sidecar (rmcp 3.x — resolved 3.1.4 — a declared-but-unused anchor dependency; the JSON-RPC 2.0 layer is hand-rolled serde at `crates/mcp-server/src/jsonrpc.rs`), stderr is forced JSON (TTY check disabled) — stdout is reserved for JSON-RPC 2.0 framing and ANY accidental stdout write would corrupt the protocol. The console program's `door` word (the stdio relay, since chunk 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door) writes no `tracing` output at all; its stdout is reserved for the door's answer lines.
- **Log format JSON schema:** Verbatim from tests excerpt Section 5 Test Plan Excerpt → Test Harness Contract Summary (binding contract — obs aligns to tests, not vice versa):

Optional fields supported per `fields` map: `trace_id` / `span_id` (W3C traceparent treated as plain string fields when extracted from external client headers), `duration_ms`, `span_count`, plus per-trigger context fields (e.g., `plugin_path_basename`, `query_id`, `param_count`, `token_count_actual`, `token_budget_limit`, `body_size_bytes`, `webview_backend`, `tray_api`, `wgpu_backend`). Log entry structure matches JSON-per-line convention for agent paste-to-AI workflows.

- **Log file location:** `<data_dir>/logs/agent-latest.jsonl`, where `<data_dir>` is `resolve_data_dir()` — `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` when set, else per-platform `%APPDATA%\andromeda-pulse\` (Windows), `~/Library/Application Support/com.andromeda.pulse/` (macOS), `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/andromeda-pulse/` else `~/.andromeda-pulse/` (Linux) — aligned with arch §Filesystem locations (the former `%APPDATA%\Andromeda Pulse\logs\` / `~/.local/share/com.andromeda.pulse/logs/` forms were measured false against `resolve_data_dir()` at chunk 2026-08-30-agent-harness-teardown-truth); agent paste-to-AI workflow reads this file for debugging. Daily rotation via `tracing-appender::rolling::daily(...)`.

- **Snapshot / paste-to-AI integration:** Two cleanly separated surfaces.
  - **External-OTLP snapshot** (the product's CORE feature): `snapshot.generate` TauRPC command produces curated markdown from EXTERNAL clients' OTLP data stored in DuckDB ring buffer, saved to `~/.andromeda-pulse/snapshots/{timestamp}.md` per creator brief Section 6 pipeline (time window → filter → curate (dedup, anomaly markers, critical-path extraction, p50/p95/p99 aggregation) → format → token budget enforced ≤ 10k/25k/50k). Four of the sidecar's nine MCP tools (`query_traces`, `query_metrics`, `query_logs`, `generate_snapshot`) over the hand-rolled JSON-RPC stdio layer expose the same pipeline to AI clients; the other five (`query_incident_list`, `retrieve_report`, `retrieve_telemetry_slice`, `mark_incident_resolved`, `retrieve_incident_events`) read the incident corpus. Tool response bodies — all nine — NEVER logged in self-observation file (security plan vector 4); only `result_type` + `result_count` metadata captured.
  - **Self-observation paste-to-AI** (the product's debug surface): the agent reads `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/agent-latest.jsonl` directly (JSON-per-line; greppable / jq-able / paste-to-LLM-able). No separate snapshot needed — the JSON log file IS the snapshot. The two surfaces NEVER intersect: external OTLP data lives in DuckDB; self-observation lives in the JSON file.

- **Trace context propagation:** W3C `traceparent` header (HTTP) and gRPC metadata (`grpc-trace-bin`) extracted at receiver entry per arch Standard Contracts. The extracted traceparent is attached to the local `tracing` span as a regular field (`%traceparent`); downstream `#[tracing::instrument]` calls inherit via `tracing::Span::current()` so a single trace_id ties together the gRPC ingest span → DuckDB append span → TauRPC `traces.query` span → frontend channel emit. IPC envelope (TauRPC command struct) carries optional `traceparent` field; receiver handlers extract and attach to span fields. Real-time push streams (`pulse://stream/spans`, etc.) carry trace context in Arrow metadata column (`_trace_context` schema field) for end-to-end correlation. NOTE: this propagation is for correlation across the product's internal pipeline — the `traceparent` value is treated as an opaque string in `tracing` events, not bound to any OTel SDK trace context.

- **Heartbeat ticks:** Long-running subsystems emit `tracing::info!(target: "{module}.tick", ...)` events every 10–30 seconds via `tokio::time::interval`: `ingest.tick` (`span_count`, `buffer_capacity_pct`, `broadcast_subscribers`), `buffer.tick` (`rows_ingested`, `retention_window_active`, `eviction_count`, `span_events_seen`, `fingerprints_computed`, `observer_invocations`, `redactions_applied`, `rows_ingested_delta`, `last_append_age_seconds`, `append_rejections`), `viz.tick` (`query_latency_ms`, `subscribers_active`), `plugins.tick` (`loaded_count`, `active_invocations`). `ingest.tick` and `buffer.tick` (with `connection.tick`) come from the shared engine boot and are in both programs' logs; `viz.tick` and `plugins.tick` are the window app's alone — the console program `andromeda-pulse-engine` never emits them (chunk 2026-10-10-console-engine-entry-point), and a missing tick is read against the ticks the program emits. **Stall detection has TWO signals, and tick presence is only the first.** (a) LIVENESS — missing tick for >45s = stall signal (agent reads recent ticks via tail of JSON file). (b) PROGRESS — a consumer can keep ticking while it drains nothing: measured 2026-08-26, `rows_ingested` froze while `{ingest,buffer}.tick` emitted normally for 16 minutes and every liveness check read healthy. `rows_ingested_delta` staying 0 while the ingest channel still holds queued work is that condition, surfaced as `buffer.consumer.stalled`; `last_append_age_seconds` dates the most recent append. `health` IPC command exposes the same fields synchronously for active liveness probing per arch Standard Contracts — and, being tick-derived, it reports liveness rather than progress for the same reason.

| **cross-surface-trace-propagation** | Tests excerpt: "Snapshot generation + Notification emit — Invoke `snapshot.generate` TauRPC → await `pulse://stream/snapshot-progress` events → assert notification emitted with token count" | Implement trace_id inheritance: `snapshot.generate` TauRPC command extracts traceparent from IPC envelope; all child spans (`snapshot.render.markdown`, `snapshot.token.count.validate`) inherit same trace_id; notify desktop-native surface via `pulse://stream/snapshot-progress` channel event with trace_id in metadata; native notification includes snapshot completion log line with trace_id. |

| **multi-platform-exporter-compat** | Tests excerpt: "Windows WebView2 vs macOS WKWebView vs Linux GTK WebKit — verify tauri-driver harness boots app; IPC works consistently; WebGPU canvas available; tray icon renders; notifications dispatch via native API" | Emit platform-specific startup spans: `app.boot.webview.init` with tag `webview_backend: "WebView2" | "WKWebView" | "GTKWebKit"`; `app.boot.gpu.check` with tag `wgpu_backend: "vulkan" | "metal" | "dx12"` — the compile-target default backend (`detect_wgpu_backend()`, a `cfg!(target_os)` switch), not an adapter probe (its former `gpu_available` field was a hardcoded `false` and was removed at chunk 2026-09-30-perf-budget-gate-reads-real-samples); the truthful adapter-state record is `ui.webgpu.adapter` {`outcome`, `window_label`} — one per canvas-mount adapter request, reported by the webview through `telemetry.frontend.record_webgpu_adapter`, INFO on `obtained` and WARN otherwise (§6 warn row) — witnessed live on the dev-host `perf:frame-sample` leg (the only recorded `obtained` records) and in the CI boot job's log as `outcome: no_navigator_gpu` at WARN on every run that reaches the settle verdict — the smoke runs `cargo xtask harness:settled` before `status` and `cleanup`, so it reads the app past the adapter request (as measured on one run, `ci#37979648967`: 2 records; under the former step order four of seven boot-job logs of 2026-10-09 held it; §10 frame row); `app.boot.tray.init` with tag `tray_api: "NotifyIcon" | "NSStatusItem" | "AppIndicator"`. Assert all platform-specific spans present in expected platform's logs — the window app's log: `main` emits these three through its own `window::emit_boot_spans()`, not the shared boot, and the console program `andromeda-pulse-engine` emits none of them (its files name no window start, pinned by source text). |

| **error-budget-SLO** | Tests tier = Standard (cross-input from tests excerpt Section 5); obs typically matches tests tier → Standard obs | Implement zero-unlogged-panics invariant: set `std::panic::set_hook()` in app boot to emit structured error log on panic + emit span `app.panic.fatal` with `panic_message: string`, `backtrace: array of strings` (or stack address list if backtrace disabled); log file + CLI output both capture panic. Test: trigger panic in non-critical task → verify panic span + panic log line present in `agent-latest.jsonl`. SLO: error budget = 0 panics/month. |

| **creator-explicit-telemetry** | Creator brief Section 6: "Real-time push: Service health constellation... Throughput counter (events/sec with smooth animation)" | Emit `tracing::trace!(target: "metric.ingest.throughput_events_per_sec", value = N.NN, ...)` on every 100ms tick. The realtime number flows to the frontend constellation widget via the `pulse://stream/metrics` Arrow IPC channel (the product's external streaming pipeline) — animation source data is identical to what the agent reads from the JSON log file, so the same number appears in both surfaces. |

| **creator-explicit-telemetry** | Creator brief Section 6: "Live trace view — span tree with timing, per-service filter... Latency heatmap strip; Error rate sparkline + count" | Aggregation runs INSIDE DuckDB queries on the EXTERNAL OTLP data path (the product's core pipeline) — `viz.query.traces` span body emits `tracing::info!(target: "metric.trace.latency_percentiles", service_name = ..., p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, max_ms, error_count, error_rate_percent, time_window_seconds, ...)` once per query. WebGPU compute shader reads aggregated histogram buckets from the same DuckDB result set sent over `pulse://stream/metrics` Arrow IPC. Self-observation log captures the aggregation event for agent traceability; the frontend reads the actual buckets from the channel payload (faster path, no JSON parse). |

title: 2. Telemetry Strategy

body: **Telemetry signal pyramid (per tier):**
| Signal | Coverage focus | Tier-specific depth |

| Spans / Traces | Critical paths (P1-P7) + module boundaries (ingest, buffer, viz, plugins, snapshot) | Standard: all 7 must-trace paths covered via `#[tracing::instrument]` attribute on each handler; trace context inherited via `tracing::Span::current()`; spans serialize to the JSON log file as enter/exit events with span IDs |

| Structured Logs | Boundary calls + state transitions + errors | Standard: JSON-per-line via `tracing-subscriber` JSON formatter; logging-sensitive vectors (Sec 5) apply `#[instrument(skip(...))]` field exclusion + custom subscriber Layer redaction; heartbeat ticks emit `info`-level events |

| Errors | Captured panics + module-boundary errors | Standard: `std::panic::set_hook` → `tracing::error!`; `tracing-error` 0.2 SpanTrace for sanitized error chains (user-defined spans only, no Rust struct names per Vector 2); optional `sentry-rust` 0.46 / `sentry-tauri` 0.5 (opt-in via `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_SENTRY_DSN`, default off; uses Sentry's own SDK, no OTel bridge) |

| Metrics | Counters / histograms / gauges per critical path | Standard: emitted as `tracing::info!(target: "metric.{name}", value = N, ...)` events with `metric.*` target convention; agent computes percentiles from the event stream when reading the JSON log file; SLO-critical budgets are asserted by `cargo xtask perf:budget` over that stream (§10) — no bench suite exists (as measured at chunk 2026-10-10-no-ci-step-reads-nothing) |
| Audit Logs | Compliance trail for privileged ops | N/A — security_tier=Minimal, no compliance triggers |
**Agent-readable invariants (apply across all signals):**
- Every signal produces machine-parseable output: JSON-per-line via `tracing-subscriber` JSON formatter to a single file (`~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/agent-latest.jsonl`); the file IS the agent surface
- No human-only dashboards, no Grafana / Kibana / Datadog UI as sole consumption
- No proprietary APM SDKs as primary exporter (Sentry is opt-in, not default)
- No human-review-gated log analysis ("ops team reviews daily")
- Every panic captured with structured SpanTrace (via `tracing-error`, no full Rust struct names per Vector 2)

- Every cross-surface call attaches W3C traceparent as a plain `tracing` span field at the boundary (gRPC metadata extraction via manual middleware on tonic; HTTP header extraction via manual `tower::Layer` or `tower-http::TraceLayer` on axum; IPC envelope `traceparent` field on TauRPC commands; Arrow `_trace_context` metadata column on push streams) — propagation downstream via `tracing::Span::current()` so a single trace_id ties together the entire pipeline

- NO OTel SDK linked into the self-observation runtime — recursion-free by construction (the only tools that touch OTLP wire format are `tonic` + `axum` + `prost` + `opentelemetry-proto`, which decode incoming external client telemetry; none of those require an OTel SDK runtime)
**Naming conventions:**
- **Span naming:** `{module}.{operation}` pattern (e.g., `ingest.grpc.export.request`, `duckdb.append`, `plugin.invoke.request`, `snapshot.generate.request`); avoid high-cardinality names

- **Metric event naming:** `metric.{module}.{measure}` target prefix on `tracing` events (e.g., `metric.snapshot.token_count_ms`, `metric.buffer.ingest_throughput_spans_per_sec`, `metric.webgpu.frame_duration_ms`, `metric.trace.latency_percentiles`, and the three frontend-bridged delegated-timing observables `metric.constellation.hue_update_ms` / `metric.constellation.discovery_ms` / `metric.findings.counter_refresh_ms`)
- **Log fields:** structured JSON with required fields per Section 6 (timestamp, level, target, message, fields with trace_id/span_id when available)

- **Default subscriber fields:** every event carries `service.name` (`com.andromeda.pulse`), `service.version` (from `Cargo.toml`), `deployment.environment` (`production`) — set once at subscriber init via `Layer::with_default_fields(...)` so individual `tracing::info!` calls don't repeat the boilerplate

title: 3. Observability Harness Contract

body: Architecture committed to the harness pattern (verbatim from upstream-context Architecture Excerpt's Observability Hints): "`opentelemetry-stdout` (or file exporter targeting `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/`) is the only exporter the product itself uses for its own telemetry". This obs plan strengthens that commitment by going one step further: NO OTel SDK is linked into the self-observation runtime at all. The product's own debug telemetry uses ONLY the `tracing` ecosystem with a JSON file sink. The product's external surfaces (OTLP receivers ingesting third-party clients) continue to use `tonic` + `axum` + `prost` + `opentelemetry-proto` for wire format parsing — those crates parse OTLP without requiring an OTel SDK runtime, so the two pipelines remain cleanly separated.
Contracts: .andromeda/registries/obs-plan-contracts.toml — ask registry.py contracts; read one contracts/obs-plan/{key}.md; never whole.

title: 4. Span / Trace Coverage

body: **Span naming convention:** `{module}.{operation}` (e.g., `ingest.grpc.export.request`, `duckdb.append`, `snapshot.generate.request`, `plugin.invoke.request`). Avoid high-cardinality span names (no per-user-ID names, no per-trace-ID names).

**Span kind convention** (`tracing` 0.1 has no native `SpanKind` enum — encoded as a `span.kind` field on the `#[tracing::instrument]` attribute, e.g., `#[tracing::instrument(fields(span.kind = "server"))]`):
- `span.kind = "server"` — inbound handlers: `ingest.grpc.export.request` (gRPC), `ingest.http.export.request` (HTTP POST), TauRPC command handlers, MCP tool invocations
- `span.kind = "internal"` — internal operations: `duckdb.append`, `snapshot.generate.request`, `plugin.invoke.request`, `buffer.tick`, `workspace.detect`
- `span.kind = "client"` — not heavily used (app is receiver, not client); may appear for query/invoke spans if modeled as request-response
**Instrumentation per surface (manual `#[tracing::instrument]` throughout — NO OTel SDK auto-instrumentation crates linked):**
| Surface | Hook strategy | Manual instrumentation | Notes |

| API service gRPC `:4317` | Manual `#[tracing::instrument(skip(req), fields(rpc.system = "grpc", rpc.service, rpc.method, span_count, traceparent))]` on each tonic gRPC service method handler | `gRPC` interceptor extracts `grpc-trace-bin` metadata header at request entry, attaches as `traceparent` span field; OTLP payload `span_count` attribute populated post-protobuf parse | tonic 0.14.x compatibility via plain `tracing` integration; no OTel-flavored crate needed |

| API service HTTP `:4318` | Manual `tower::Layer` (or `tower-http::TraceLayer` for plain `tracing` spans) on the axum router; `#[tracing::instrument]` on each handler | HTTP request/response span wrapping; body-size validation spans (DefaultBodyLimit 8MB rejection); `traceparent` header extracted at request entry, attached to span fields | axum 0.8.x compatible; emits regular `tracing` spans (not OTel-flavored); 413 spans emit on DefaultBodyLimit rejection |

| IPC-internal (TauRPC) | Manual `#[tracing::instrument(skip_all, fields(traceparent = %tp))]` on each router method | Each TauRPC router method: extract envelope traceparent → attach to span fields; span wraps entire command execution | Child spans inherit context via `tracing::Span::current()` |

| Desktop-webview (React 19) | NO browser OTel SDK; frontend instruments via custom JS → the hand-rolled TauRPC `telemetry.frontend.record_*` bridge → backend tracing (`web-vitals` RETIRED 2026-08-30 — never installed; the `metric.web_vital.{name}` chain never had a producer) | Custom JS captures component lifecycle, skeleton pulse duration, empty/error state counters → TauRPC `telemetry.frontend.record_*` commands → backend tracing events | WebGPU canvas frame-time via DOM `performance.now()` + `device.queue.onSubmittedWorkDone()` → TauRPC `telemetry.frontend.record_frame_ms` → backend `tracing::info!(target: "metric.webgpu.frame_duration_ms")`; eliminates browser→backend OTLP recursion concern |

| Plugin host (wasmtime) | Manual `#[tracing::instrument(skip(input, output))]` on host-side plugin invocation wrappers | Host-side wrappers around `wasmtime::component::Instance::call(...)` + capability check + invocation; emit `plugin.load.request`, `plugin.invoke.request` spans | WASM sandbox is untrusted and capability-scoped — guests have no host-side observability access; host-only instrumentation per must-trace P4 |

| CLI / main binary | Manual `#[tracing::instrument]` on workspace-detect / config-load / startup functions | Root span `app.boot` wraps main(); child spans for workspace detection, config load, receiver startup | Startup-phase spans emit prior to spawning async runtime; logged to the JSON file sink (the app has no stderr layer). Two entries since chunk 2026-10-10-console-engine-entry-point — the window app's `main` and the console program's (`andromeda-pulse-engine`), both through `engine_boot::init_process` then `engine_boot::start`: a console `run` carries `app.boot.tracing.init`, `app.boot.pid`, the panic and process-end records, `app.boot.engine` and every record the shared engine wiring emits, and none of the window's boot records; since chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process a console `run` also writes `app.boot.door` once per boot (the engine-cycle kept log held exactly one, `"state":"listening"`) and, when a caller uses the door, `door.call` / `door.refused` and the called tools' own records (`viz.query.traces` / `.metrics` / `.logs`, the `viz.query` fallback warning, and for `generate_snapshot` `metric.snapshot.token_count_ms` + `snapshot.token.count.validate` — not enumerated from a log at that chunk); the window app writes no door record; `version` and a refused command line emit nothing, and so does `door` (the stdio relay, since chunk 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door), which opens no sink — each request it relays is recorded by the running console engine as `door.call` (one per answered request), and a refused account reaching the door as `door.refused` |

| Desktop-native (tray icon) | Tauri lifecycle hooks emit `tracing::info!(target: "tray.{event}", ...)` on tray visibility / menu interaction / notification dismiss / notification action | Hook into Tauri tray icon / menu event handlers + `tauri-plugin-notification` event listeners; emit `tray.visibility.toggle`, `tray.menu.interaction`, `tray.notification.dismiss`, `tray.notification.action` spans | Boundary events only (no native OS telemetry intrusion); `service.name` = `com.andromeda.pulse`; events ride same JSON file sink as backend |

| MCP stdio (hand-rolled JSON-RPC 2.0, rmcp 3.x declared-but-unused, feature-gated) | Compile-time gate: `--features mcp-server`; runtime gate: `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED=true`; `tracing-subscriber` writer forced to `std::io::stderr` (stdout reserved for JSON-RPC 2.0 framing); manual `#[tracing::instrument]` on each tool method handler | `mcp.tools.call.request` span wraps each tool invocation; `mcp.feature.gate.check` span on double-gate validation; `mcp.response.emit` span on result serialization (response bodies NOT logged per Vector 4 — only `result_type` + `result_count`) | Boundary is stdin/stdout JSON-RPC 2.0; ANY accidental stdout write corrupts protocol — all tracing forced stderr-JSON; double-gate enforced per security plan + must-trace P3 |

| The door (console engine; JSON-RPC 2.0 over the Unix-domain socket `{data dir}/run/door/sock`; Unix only — `#[cfg(unix)] mod socket`; chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process) | Three `tracing` log events and no span, on the engine's one file sink; no feature gate and no runtime gate — admission is the kernel-read peer account compared with the engine's own (`door::admits`), the one write behind `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DOOR_RESOLVE` | `app.boot.door` once per boot of a program that seats the door (`door::emit_boot`); `door.call` once per request that is answered (`door::emit_call`); `door.refused` per refused connection or line (`door::emit_refused`) — fields and levels in §6 and §8 | Seated in `engine_boot::start` for `Program::Console` only; the window program writes no door record. PROVISIONAL — §4 Scenario P3 |
**Must-trace path scenarios:**

title: Scenario: P1 — Receive OTLP telemetry (gRPC), visualize in WebGPU dashboard

data.head: #### Scenario: P1 — Receive OTLP telemetry (gRPC), visualize in WebGPU dashboard

body: - **Surfaces involved:** API service (gRPC `:4317`), buffer (DuckDB), viz (query layer), desktop-webview (WebGPU canvas), IPC-internal (TauRPC)

- **Must-trace spans:** `otlp.grpc.export.request` (gRPC handler entry) → `duckdb.append` (appender write latency) → `tauri.channel.emit` (emit to `pulse://stream/spans` Arrow IPC) → TauRPC `traces.query` (user invokes query) → `viz.query.traces` (query execution)

- **Metric event emitted (frontend-bridged):** `metric.webgpu.frame_duration_ms` — WebGPU canvas frame timing measured in the webview via DOM `performance.now()` + `device.queue.onSubmittedWorkDone()`, bridged through TauRPC `telemetry.frontend.record_frame_ms` command, emitted on the backend as a `tracing::info!(target: "metric.webgpu.frame_duration_ms", duration_ms, wgpu_backend, webview_backend, ...)` event

- **Required span attributes:** `otlp.grpc.export.request`: `span_count` (from gRPC RPC payload), `service` (from span attributes, scrubbed per vector 1), `trace_ids` (list of trace IDs in batch); `duckdb.append`: `duration_ms`, `rows_appended`; `viz.query.traces`: `query_id`, `param_count`, `time_window_seconds`
- **Required log fields:** `trace_id`, `span_id`, `span_count`, `service`, `buffer.rows_ingested`, `duration_ms` (per WebGPU frame metric event), `wgpu_backend`, `webview_backend`
- **Cleanup:** gRPC handler auto-ends span; append operation completes span; query spans end on result return; canvas frame span ends post-render

title: Scenario: P2 — Generate token-efficient curated snapshot

data.head: #### Scenario: P2 — Generate token-efficient curated snapshot

body: - **Surfaces involved:** Desktop-webview (TauRPC invocation), buffer (DuckDB queries), snapshot (markdown generator), IPC-internal

- **Must-trace spans:** TauRPC `snapshot.generate({time_range, token_budget})` (entry, parent `session.snapshot`) → `duckdb.query.aggregation` (aggregate metrics + dedup) → `snapshot.render.markdown` (markdown generation) → `snapshot.token.count.validate` (enforce budget limit)

- **Required span attributes:** `snapshot.generate.request`: `token_budget` (10k/25k/50k), `time_range_start`, `time_range_end`, `service_filter`; `duckdb.query.aggregation`: `query_id`, `dedup_count`, `output_row_count`; `snapshot.render.markdown`: `markdown_size_bytes`, `section_count`; `snapshot.token.count.validate`: `token_count_actual`, `token_budget_limit`, `budget_exceeded`
- **Required log fields:** `trace_id`, `token_budget`, `token_count_actual`, `dedup_count`, `anomaly_markers` (array), `time_range_start`, `time_range_end`, `service_filter`
- **Cleanup:** TauRPC command spans end post-response; async markdown generation task awaits completion before snapshot file write

title: Scenario: P3 — MCP server query (JSON-RPC 2.0 tool call)

data.head: #### Scenario: P3 — MCP server query (JSON-RPC 2.0 tool call)

body: - **Surfaces involved:** CLI (hand-rolled JSON-RPC stdio), IPC-internal, buffer (DuckDB); since chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process also the console engine's door (the second carrier, below), reached over its socket directly or, since chunk 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door, by a stdio agent through `andromeda-pulse-engine door`

- **Must-trace spans:** `mcp.tools.call.request` (JSON-RPC 2.0 stdin method parse) → `mcp.feature.gate.check` (compile-time + runtime gate validation) → the per-tool read — `duckdb.query.traces` / `.metrics` / `.logs` for the telemetry tools; a corpus read for the incident tools (`retrieve_incident_events`'s `CorpusWriter::load_incident_events` emits no span of its own, its error surfacing as JSON-RPC -32603) → `mcp.tools.call.response` (emit JSON result to stdout)

- **Required span attributes:** `mcp.tools.call.request`: `method` (one of the nine `ALL_TOOL_NAMES`: query_traces / query_metrics / query_logs / generate_snapshot / query_incident_list / retrieve_report / retrieve_telemetry_slice / mark_incident_resolved / retrieve_incident_events — bounded), `params_count`; `mcp.feature.gate.check`: `feature_flag_enabled`, `env_var_mcp_enabled`; `duckdb.query.*`: `query_id`, `param_count`, `time_range_start`, `time_range_end`, `service_filter`; `mcp.tools.call.response`: `result_type` (not `result_content`; `incident_events` for `retrieve_incident_events`), `result_count` (its `events` length)
- **Required log fields:** `trace_id`, `method`, `time_range_start`, `time_range_end`, `service_filter`, `result.count`, `feature_flag_enabled`, `env_var_mcp_enabled`
- **Cleanup:** the hand-rolled `jsonrpc.rs` stdio loop closes the JSON-RPC stream (measured chunk `2026-08-29-advisory-backlog` — nothing rmcp-provided runs); spans end after stdout result sent

- **Two carriers since chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process.** Everything above is the first, the stdio sidecar, unchanged: the `mcp.tools.call.request` → `mcp.feature.gate.check` → per-tool read → `mcp.tools.call.response` chain through `dispatch_tool`. The second is the door inside the console engine's process (`andromeda-pulse-engine run`; JSON-RPC 2.0, one request per line, over the Unix-domain socket `{data dir}/run/door/sock`; Unix only, the window program seats none): `tools/call` runs `mcp_server::tools::call_tool` over `door::EngineTools`, which writes no `mcp.*` record and passes no feature or runtime gate. That carrier's one record per call is the log event `door.call` {`method`, `tool`, `outcome`, `write`, `result_type`, `result_count`, `answer_bytes`, `duration_ms`} — once per request that is answered (a request with no `id` is not answered and leaves none), written before the answer line, INFO for `ok` and WARN otherwise, never ERROR; a refused connection or line leaves `door.refused` {`reason`, `peer`} at WARN. The tools' own callee records (`viz.query.traces` / `.metrics` / `.logs`, and for `generate_snapshot` `metric.snapshot.token_count_ms` + `snapshot.token.count.validate`) are written by the console engine on such a call; which of them a real call wrote was not enumerated from a log at that chunk. The door closes an idle connection at 30 s and answers a call over 5 s with `-32002`. Since chunk 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door the door carrier is reached two ways: a client of `{data dir}/run/door/sock` directly, or a stdio agent through `andromeda-pulse-engine door` (the relay: one connection per request line, the write side shut after it, the whole answer read and then written to standard output unchanged). Through the relay each answered request leaves one `door.call` in the engine's log, a notification none, and no `door.refused {reason: idle}`; another account's relay reading that reaches the door leaves one `door.refused {other_account, other}` and the relay exits 1 with its fixed standard-error line and 0 bytes on standard output; the relay writes no record itself. **The door is PROVISIONAL — a boundary widening, one item:** the endpoint, the owner check, the reach of the nine tools and of the one write, the write-switch variable and the workflow step that runs a client as a second account are the operator's answers (the pc overseer: at that chunk's P4 dialog, 2026-10-10, and the operator's reading of 2026-10-11 at its wrap); the founder's own word is owed on the surface itself, nothing of it is ratified, and every other statement of the door in this plan rests on this one.

title: Scenario: P4 — Plugin lifecycle (load, invoke, unload)

data.head: #### Scenario: P4 — Plugin lifecycle (load, invoke, unload)

body: - **Surfaces involved:** IPC-internal (TauRPC), library-only (plugin host, wasmtime)

- **Must-trace spans:** TauRPC `plugins.reload` (entry) → `plugin.load.request` (load WASM file) → `wasmtime.instantiate` (module instantiation) → TauRPC `plugins.invoke({plugin, capability, input})` (invocation command) → `plugin.capability.check` (capability gating) → `plugin.invoke.request` (execute capability, or `plugin.invoke.error` on rejection)

- **Required span attributes:** `plugin.load.request`: `plugin_path_basename` (not full path), `wasm_size_bytes`, `duration_ms`; `wasmtime.instantiate`: `module_name`, `export_count`; `plugin.capability.check`: `capability_name`, `capability_allowed`, `error_msg` (if rejected); `plugin.invoke.request`: `plugin_name`, `capability_name`, `input_schema` (Arrow column names), `output_schema`, `duration_ms`
- **Required log fields:** `trace_id`, `plugin_name`, `plugin_path_basename`, `capability_name`, `capability_allowed`, `error_msg`, `duration_ms`, `wasm_size_bytes`
- **Cleanup:** plugin.load span ends after instantiation; capability.check span ends on allow/deny decision; invoke spans end post-execution; errors logged at WARN/ERROR level

title: Scenario: P5 — Widget compact mode ↔ dashboard expansion ↔ tray icon visibility toggle

data.head: #### Scenario: P5 — Widget compact mode ↔ dashboard expansion ↔ tray icon visibility toggle

body: - **Surfaces involved:** Desktop-webview (TauRPC layout command), desktop-native (tray icon), IPC-internal

- **Must-trace spans:** TauRPC `layout.update({mode})` (layout change command) → `ui.layout.transition` (frontend state change) → `tray.visibility.toggle` (tray icon update) → `ipc.health.check` (consistency verification)

- **Required span attributes:** `ui.layout.transition`: `layout_mode_from`, `layout_mode_to`, `duration_ms`; `tray.visibility.toggle`: `tray_visible` (true/false); `ipc.health.check`: `health.status` (ok/degraded/unhealthy), `health.subsystems` (JSON)
- **Required log fields:** `trace_id`, `layout_mode_from`, `layout_mode_to`, `tray_visible`, `health.status`, `health.subsystems`, `ipc.contract.valid`
- **Cleanup:** Frontend state change spans end post-DOM update; health check span ends after response returned

title: Scenario: P6 — Real-time push via Tauri IPC Channel (binary Arrow IPC)

data.head: #### Scenario: P6 — Real-time push via Tauri IPC Channel (binary Arrow IPC)

body: - **Surfaces involved:** API service (gRPC ingest), IPC-internal (Tauri Channel), desktop-webview (channel subscriber)

- **Must-trace spans:** `otlp.grpc.export.request` (external client sends gRPC span) → `tauri.channel.emit` (app emits `pulse://stream/spans` Arrow IPC event) → frontend `tauri.channel.subscribe` (listen for events)

- **Required span attributes:** `otlp.grpc.export.request`: `span_count`; `tauri.channel.emit` wraps Arrow IPC serialization with `channel_name`, `arrow_schema` (column names), `row_count`, `payload_size_bytes`, `schema_match` (validation attestation performed during serialization, attribute on the same span — no separate decode span needed at this boundary)
- **Required log fields:** `trace_id`, `channel_name`, `arrow_schema`, `row_count`, `payload_size_bytes`, `schema_match`
- **Cleanup:** Channel emit span ends after event dispatch + schema validation attestation

title: Scenario: P7 — Workspace detection (.andromeda/ marker)

body: - **Surfaces involved:** Desktop-native (app startup), workspace-detector, IPC-internal

- **Must-trace spans:** `app.boot` (app entry, parent) → `app.boot.workspace.detect` (startup workspace detection) → `filesystem.scan.gitroot` (find .git/) → `workspace.marker.check` (.andromeda/ present) → `workspace.identity.resolve` (project name resolution) → `app.boot.workspace_key` (publish of the resolved key to `{data_dir}/run/workspace-key` for the MCP sidecar; INFO on success, WARN on failure — chunk 2026-08-14-workspace-key-alignment)

- **Required span attributes:** `app.boot.workspace.detect`: `workspace.root_path` (canonicalized), `workspace.project_name`, `detection_latency_ms`; `filesystem.scan.gitroot`: `vcs_type` (git), `vcs_root` (path to .git/)

- **Required log fields:** `trace_id`, `workspace.root_path`, `workspace.project_name`, `vcs_type`, `vcs_root`, `marker_present`, `detection_latency_ms`; on `app.boot.workspace_key` ONLY `workspace_root_basename` + `key_bytes` (INFO) or `error_category` + `error_detail` (WARN) — the full workspace path never appears on this event (§8)
- **Cleanup:** workspace.detect span ends after identity resolved; .andromeda/ marker check ends with boolean result; vcs_root discovery ends post-scan

title: 5. Metric Coverage

body: **Metric emission convention:** every metric is emitted as a `tracing::info!` (or `tracing::trace!` for high-frequency 100ms ticks) event with target prefix `metric.{module}.{measure}` and a numeric `value` field plus enumerated label fields. The agent computes percentiles / counters / gauges by reading the JSON log file with `jq` or by tailing it during a debug session. NO OTel SDK Histogram/Counter/Gauge instruments are used — the `tracing` event stream is the single observability primitive.
**Conceptual instrument types** (mapped onto `tracing` events for consumption convention):
| Conceptual type | Use case | Example tracing targets |
| Counter (monotonic) | Count of events accumulated over time | `metric.buffer.evicted_span_count` (per tick increment), `metric.ingest.span.count` (per heartbeat) |

| Counter (monotonic, tick-aggregated as FIELDS) | Fingerprint-feed throughput — `span_events_seen` / `fingerprints_computed` / `observer_invocations`, folded once per batch by `BufferState::record_feed_counts` and ridden out as fields on the existing 15s `buffer.tick` rather than as separate `metric.buffer.*` targets. Counts only, no labels. Equality of `observer_invocations` with `fingerprints_computed` is the signal that the storm detector's feed is actually being fed, rather than that being inferred from downstream silence. Per-span-event emission is barred by the §11 hot-path rule | fields on `buffer.tick` |

| Counter (monotonic, tick-aggregated as FIELDS) | PII-redaction throughput — `redactions_applied`, folded once per batch by `BufferState::record_redactions` and ridden out as a field on the same 15s `buffer.tick`. Deliberately a SEPARATE fold from `record_feed_counts`, because the redaction paths and the fingerprint-feed paths do not coincide (the log-record path applies redactions while producing no feed counts). Aggregate count only — never the matched value, its category, the attribute key, or a `service_name` label. **Scope is FIVE scrub sites across the four `buffer::appender` record-batch builders** (widened 2026-08-23 by chunk `2026-08-23-ingestion-scrub-coverage` from the `scrub_otlp_field` log/exception paths to the four column boundaries — `spans.service_name`, `span_events.name`, `metrics_points.metric_name`, `log_records.severity_text` — then to a fifth by chunk `2026-08-23-metrics-points-labels`: `metrics_points.labels`). The BUILDER count is still four; only the scrub-site count moved. **Unit: one increment per REDACTED LABEL PAIR, not per persisted cell** — a single data point can carry several redacted pairs inside one `labels` cell, and each counts. **At the four column sites the unit is one increment per redacted VALUE, however many spans it masked** — since chunk `2026-09-30-span-level-redaction` (founder ratification at P4 2026-10-01, «Ок давай по типу правила») `scrub_otlp_field` masks each secret in place (`mask_secret_spans`) and increments once when the value carried any (as measured at the chunk's e2e: 4 values carrying 10 masked spans → 4; live wire 0 → 4). **Counts redactions to PERSISTED cells ONLY — structurally, since chunk `2026-08-23-metrics-points-identity`:** each builder RETURNS its per-batch tally (`Result<Option<(RecordBatch, u64)>, Error>`) and `record_redactions` is folded at each table's OWN post-append site in `consumer::dispatch_batch`, so a batch the appender rejects at `flush()` contributes zero. Per-table granularity is load-bearing: in the spans arm a `span_events` failure must not discard the count for rows `spans` already stored. (`build_spans_record_batch` consequently takes no `&BufferState` at all.) Before that chunk the fold fired INSIDE the builders and the rule did not hold — measured live at `redactions_applied: 2` with `rows_ingested: 0` on a rejected batch. A scrub applied purely for identity consistency on a non-stored path is likewise UNCOUNTED — `extract_service_name` takes an `Option<&mut u64>` and its two non-storing callers (the storm `FingerprintObserver`, the baseline `SpanObserver` tap) pass `None`, which is why a canary in all five scrubbed cells reads 5 and not 6 (one redacted pair in the `labels` cell). The drain/template path (`snapshot_state` / `write_template_to_table`) masks through `mask_secret_spans` directly and carries its own tick fields. Makes P-047 scrubber recall gradeable from outside the process rather than only by reading stored rows back. Per-field emission is barred by the §11 hot-path rule | field on `buffer.tick` |

| Counter (monotonic, tick-aggregated as FIELDS) | Drain progress — `rows_ingested_delta` (rows landed since the previous tick) and `last_append_age_seconds` (whole seconds since the most recent append, derived from `BufferStateSnapshot.last_append_at_nanos`), both ridden out on the same 15s `buffer.tick`, whose field set stands at 15 since `append_rejections` joined it (chunk 2026-08-30-diagnostics-un-muting-harness-truth-sweep). These exist because `rows_ingested` ALONE cannot separate a stalled consumer from an idle producer — both leave it static, which is precisely why the 2026-08-26 wedge read as healthy for 16 minutes. The discriminator is the ingest channel's occupancy: an idle producer drains it to empty, a stalled consumer leaves work queued. `last_append_at_nanos` refreshes on EVERY append and is deliberately distinct from the latch-once `first_append_at_nanos` (a latching age would climb on a perfectly healthy buffer). One clock read per batch, never per row; per-batch emission is barred by the §11 hot-path rule | fields on `buffer.tick` |

| Counter (monotonic, tick-aggregated as FIELDS) | Append rejections — `append_rejections`, folded once per FAILED batch at `run_consumer`'s two error arms via `BufferState::record_append_rejection` and ridden out on the same 15s `buffer.tick` (chunk `2026-08-30-diagnostics-un-muting-harness-truth-sweep`). Aggregate count only — never batch, span, service or fingerprint identity; the per-failure `duckdb.append` ERROR record (target + `reject_reason`) is byte-unchanged and remains the diagnostic detail, this field is the trend. Exists because a rejection burst (e.g. the 2026-08-28 replayed-identity shape: 120 rejected batches) was previously countable only by grepping ERROR records — the tick now carries the rate. Per-batch emission of a counter event is barred by the §11 hot-path rule | field on `buffer.tick` |

| Counter (monotonic, tick-aggregated as FIELDS) | Cue-admission bound — `cues_latched` (cues the `CueLatch` refused this cycle because their condition was already signalled, had not escalated, and was inside the refractory window) and `latch_tracked` (live conditions the latch holds after the cycle's eviction pass), folded onto the existing `triage.cue.tick` heartbeat and bringing its field set to 9. Cue evaluators re-derive from current state, so a persistent condition yields an identical cue every tick, and BOTH cadence entry points are fed by emission — Suggested cues via `CadenceTriggerChannel`, Autonomous cues via the general cue broadcast — which is why the bound sits at emission and one mechanism covers both (chunk 2026-08-26-cadence-runaway-blocking-pool; measured wedge 4,590 cues → 2,671 immediate cycles → 26,821 L1a queries in 16 min, against 220 in a matched control). `latch_tracked` is the field that makes the residual visible: the bound limits repetition PER CONDITION, not the number of distinct conditions. Per-cue emission is barred by the §11 hot-path rule | fields on `triage.cue.tick` |

| Counter (monotonic, tick-aggregated as FIELDS) | Cadence cycle rate — `cycles_executed`, folded onto the existing 15s `cadence.tick` heartbeat and bringing its field set to 8. The value was already accumulated in `cumulative_cycles` and then DISCARDED via `let _ =`, so the rate could only be read by counting per-trigger `cadence.trigger` records out of the log family — the forensic read chunk 2026-08-26-cadence-runaway-blocking-pool exists to remove. Aggregate count only; per-trigger emission is barred by the §11 hot-path rule (and `cadence.trigger` itself, at one record per cycle, is why the wedge log reached 131 MB) | field on `cadence.tick` |

| Distribution / "histogram" | Per-event value samples; agent computes p50/p95/p99/max from event stream | `metric.snapshot.token_count_ms`, `metric.webgpu.frame_duration_ms`, `metric.buffer.memory_bytes`, `metric.trace.latency_percentiles` |
| Gauge | Current state value sampled per tick | `metric.ingest.channel.broadcast_subscribers`, `metric.buffer.rows_active`, `metric.plugins.loaded_count` |

**Naming conventions:** `metric.{module}.{measure}` target prefix (e.g., `metric.snapshot.token_count_ms`, `metric.buffer.memory_bytes`). Cardinality discipline applies: label fields bounded to enumerated values only (no per-trace-ID labels, no per-user-ID labels, no per-arbitrary-request-path labels).
**Per-surface / per-path metric events:**
| Operation | Target | Conceptual type | Unit | Labels (event fields) | Update frequency |

| Snapshot generation | `metric.snapshot.token_count_ms` | Distribution | ms | `token_budget: 10000 \| 25000 \| 50000`, `time_range_minutes: N`, `token_count_actual`, `dedup_count`, `budget_exceeded: bool` | Per snapshot generation (on-demand), emitted once by `GenerationTimer`: `duration_ms` / `value` are fractional ms spanning load + curate + format — excluding the resolver's file writes, clipboard and notification; no sample on `AnchorEncodingFailed` or a load / curate failure (§10 snapshot row) |

| WebGPU canvas render | `metric.webgpu.frame_duration_ms` | Distribution | ms | `wgpu_backend: vulkan \| metal \| dx12`, `webview_backend: WebView2 \| WKWebView \| GTKWebKit`, `timing_method: cpu \| gpu` | Per frame (~60 Hz) — bridged through TauRPC `telemetry.frontend.record_frame_ms` |
| Buffer memory | `metric.buffer.memory_bytes` | Gauge (per tick) | bytes | `retention_window_seconds: 300 \| 600`, `rows_active`, `eviction_count_since_last_tick` | Per heartbeat tick (15s) |
| Ingest throughput (animation) | `metric.ingest.throughput_events_per_sec` | Distribution | events/sec | `event_type: span \| metric \| log` | Every 100ms tick |

| Trace latency percentiles (per query) | `metric.trace.latency_percentiles` | Distribution | ms | `service_name` (unbounded: client-supplied via OTLP), `p50_ms`, `p95_ms`, `p99_ms`, `max_ms`, `time_window_seconds`, `error_count`, `error_rate_percent` | Per viz query (on-demand) — DuckDB computes the percentiles; `service_name` cardinality is unbounded by design (external clients control their service.name); query-time aggregation only, not time-series-stored |

| Error count per service | `metric.trace.error_count` | Counter | errors | `service_name` (unbounded: client-supplied via OTLP), `error_type: {enum}` (e.g., `exception`, `timeout`, `protocol_error`) | Per viz query aggregation; `service_name` unbounded as above; `error_type` bounded to known categories |
| Channel subscriber count | `metric.ingest.channel.broadcast_subscribers` | Gauge | count | `channel_name: pulse://stream/spans \| metrics \| logs` | Per heartbeat tick (15s) |
| Plugin loaded count | `metric.plugins.loaded_count` | Gauge | count | n/a | Per reload operation |
| Evicted span count | `metric.buffer.evicted_span_count` | Counter | spans | `retention_window_seconds: 600` | Per heartbeat tick, when eviction observed |

**Why `tracing` events instead of an OTel Meter:** the unified JSON file is sufficient for agent paste-to-AI workflows. Aggregation happens in two places: (1) the snapshot pipeline (which already curates external client OTLP data and can the same way curate self-observation events), (2) the test harness post-test analysis (`jq` over the log file for SLO assertions). SLO enforcement is `cargo xtask perf:budget` grading the same event stream against the §10 budgets — no OTel Meter dependency needed. No bench suite exists, so nothing asserts a regression against an earlier run (as measured at chunk 2026-10-10-no-ci-step-reads-nothing).

**Metric label cardinality discipline:** Labels bounded to enumerated values only for product-internal metrics (`wgpu_backend` to {vulkan, metal, dx12}; `webview_backend` to {WebView2, WKWebView, GTKWebKit}; `retention_window_seconds` to {300, 600}; `event_type` to {span, metric, log}; `error_type` to a known category list). **Exception** for query-time aggregation metrics (`metric.trace.latency_percentiles`, `metric.trace.error_count`): `service_name` is intentionally unbounded — external OTLP clients control their own `service.name` attribute, and the product cannot constrain it. These metrics are emitted ONLY at query time (per `viz.query.traces` invocation) and consumed immediately by the requesting view; they are NOT time-series-stored, so cardinality explosion is scoped to a single query's memory rather than long-term metric retention. No per-trace-ID, per-user-ID, or per-arbitrary-request-path labels in any metric.

title: 6. Log Coverage

body: **Log format JSON schema:** Verbatim from upstream-context Section 5 Test Plan Excerpt → Test Harness Contract Summary (binding contract):
**Required fields (every log line):**
- `timestamp` (ISO 8601 format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.fffZ`)
- `level` (debug / info / warn / error)
- `target` (module path, e.g., `ingest::grpc`, `buffer::appender`, `plugin::host`, or `metric.{module}.{measure}` for metric events)
- `message` (human-readable summary, <200 chars)

- `fields` (map of structured attributes — always present, may be empty `{}`)
  - `service.name` / `service.version` / `deployment.environment` — populated as default subscriber fields
  - `trace_id` (optional, W3C 32 hex chars; populated when traceparent extracted at receiver entry — treated as plain string field)
  - `span_id` (optional, W3C 16 hex chars; same as above)
  - Per-trigger fields per Section 5 (span_count, service, duration_ms, token_count_actual, value, etc.)
**Log levels mapping:**
| Level | Use case | Example |
| `error` | Module-boundary errors + captured panics + unrecoverable failures | `error!(target: "app.panic.fatal", "panic")`, `error!(target: "ingest.grpc.parse.error", ...)` on malformed OTLP |

| `warn` | Recoverable errors + degraded performance + retry-able | `warn!(target: "config.load.path_validation", "path canonicalization rejected")` on CWE-22 violation; `warn!(target: "mcp.gate.check", "MCP enabled but feature flag absent")`; `warn!(target: "app.boot.buffer.degraded", reason, consequence)` — fires ONCE per boot when the buffer connection is absent, because the fallback drains and discards ingest batches while ingest's own counters keep climbing, making a degraded boot otherwise indistinguishable from a healthy one; `warn!(target: "corpus.keychain.fallback", backend_kind, reason, consequence)` — ONCE per boot when the passphrase branch serves the corpus key instead of the OS credential store, for the same reason (a reduced-custody boot is otherwise indistinguishable from a keychain-primary one); `warn!(target: "corpus.orphan.disposition", disposition_outcome, rows_purged, tables_affected)` — once per boot pass, aggregate counts only; `warn!(target: "corpus.read.undecryptable", query_id, rows_skipped)` — ONE aggregate per QUERY, never per row (§11 hot-path spam ban), so a corpus holding undecryptable rows degrades visibly instead of going dark; `warn!(target: "triage.baseline.bootstrap_window.override", resolved_seconds, default_seconds, reason)` — ONCE per boot and only when the resolved cold-start window differs from the 3600s default, because an env-shortened (or env-rejected) bound silently changes when every service becomes eligible for silence detection, making such a boot otherwise indistinguishable from a default one; `warn!(target: "buffer.consumer.stalled", reason, consequence, stalled_seconds, buffer_capacity_pct)` — emitted by the drain-progress classifier ONCE per healthy→stalled transition and once again on recovery, never per batch, because a wedged consumer keeps emitting `buffer.tick` and is otherwise indistinguishable from a healthy one (measured 2026-08-26: `rows_ingested` frozen 16 minutes, 0 ERROR, all ticks normal); fires only after 30 consecutive non-draining ticks (450s), deliberately above §10's 420s sustained-drain cap so an in-spec drain cannot trip it (chunk 2026-08-26-ingest-consumer-stall-under-sustained-load); `warn!(target: "app.boot.window.navigation", window_label, navigated, reason)` — at most ONCE PER WINDOW PER BOOT (bounded by the 4-entry declared-window set), fired post-settle and off any hot path, INFO when the window navigated and WARN when it is still on `about:blank`, because a webview that loses its initial navigation is never re-navigated (`show()` is not navigation) and surfaces as a blank window on first open, which no other signal distinguishes from a healthy boot (chunk 2026-08-24-headful-mechanics-probe-race-disposition); `warn!(target: "app.exit", exit_class, exit_code, exit_code_known, signal)` — EXACTLY ONCE per process end (a process-wide once-flag, first emitter wins; the emitter then drops the only `WorkerGuard`, so no second record can reach the file), off any hot path per §11: WARN for `signal` (SIGTERM/SIGINT on Unix, recorded from a runtime task, then the same signal re-raised with the default disposition so the process still ends BY it), ERROR for a non-zero `event_loop` exit and every `outside_event_loop` end (the `atexit` hook, which hands off to a `pulse-exit-reporter` thread and waits ≤ 2 s — `exit_code` 0 with `exit_code_known: false`, because `libc` binds no `on_exit`), INFO for a zero-code `event_loop` exit (Tray Quit), because a process end otherwise leaves no record at all — the 69f0b93 Linux CI boot smoke ended `exit 1` with 0 `app.panic.fatal` and no cause; the loggable and unloggable ends are listed in §7 (chunk 2026-10-01-conductor-return); `warn!(target: "app.boot.render.posture", posture, lever)` — EXACTLY ONCE per window-app boot (the console program emits none, asserted on a spawned run), emitted by `main` after `engine_boot::init_process` has initialised the sink (the decision is taken at the head of `main()`, where no subscriber exists, and carried as a value), off any hot path per §11: WARN for `preset_honoured` (a launch-env value of `__NV_DISABLE_EXPLICIT_SYNC` was honoured — an overridden posture), INFO for `applied` (the Linux default `1` was set) and `not_applicable` (macOS / Windows), because a preset-honoured boot is otherwise indistinguishable from a default-applied one; `lever` carries the variable NAME only, never its value (chunk 2026-10-04-linux-launch-stays-up-on-nvidia-wayland); `warn!(target: "app.boot.engine", program, interpretation, reason)` — EXACTLY ONCE per `engine_boot::start`, so once per boot of either program, off any hot path per §11: WARN when `interpretation` is `none` (the console program with `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_DETERMINISTIC` unset seats no runner — cues and digests are produced and no incident forms), INFO for `model` and `deterministic`; the one record that names which program booted and what sits in the interpretation seat, all three fields closed labels (§8; chunk 2026-10-10-console-engine-entry-point); `warn!(target: "app.boot.door", state, resolve_write)` — once per boot of a program that seats the door (the console program on Unix; the window app writes none), off any hot path per §11: INFO when `state` is `listening` and the switch is not `rejected`, WARN otherwise (`path_too_long` | `in_use` | `occupied` | `bind_failed`, in each of which the engine goes on with no door; or `resolve_write` `rejected`); `warn!(target: "door.call", method, tool, outcome, write, result_type, result_count, answer_bytes, duration_ms)` — once per request that is answered, written before the answer line, INFO for `ok` and WARN for the other eight outcomes; `warn!(target: "door.refused", reason, peer)` — WARN, one per refused connection or line (`other_account` | `too_many_connections` | `request_too_large` | `idle`); none of the three is ever written at ERROR (§8; chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process; PROVISIONAL — §4 Scenario P3); `warn!(target: "interpretation.model.allow_root", confinement, root_basename)` — EXACTLY ONCE per window-app boot (the console program reads no `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_ALLOW_ROOT`, constructs no `LlamaCliInference` and writes no `interpretation.model.*` record), WARN when `confinement = "unconfined"` (no `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_L4_ALLOW_ROOT` set, so the L4 model/binary paths resolve unconfined) or `"unresolvable"` (set but not a directory ⇒ fail-closed, every candidate rejected), and INFO when `"enforced"` — because an unconfined L4 boot is otherwise indistinguishable from a confined one, which is precisely what made the prior posture a silent convention; `warn!(target: "interpretation.model.load.error", env_var, error_category, path_basename, recovery_action)` — per REJECTED candidate, bounded to the two path reads at `LlamaCliInference::new` and therefore off any hot path per §11, with `error_category` drawn from the bounded set `traversal_component` | `path_too_long` | `canonicalize_failed` | `not_regular_file` | `outside_allow_root` | `allow_root_unresolvable` (chunk 2026-08-26-l4-runtime-security-residuals); `warn!(target: "ui.ipc.rejection", error_category, window_label, payload_bytes)` — ONCE per capability-rejected webview IPC (never per invoke; off any hot path per §11), reported from the webview catch through `telemetry.frontend.record_ipc_rejection` with `error_category` bounded by a closed serde enum (`acl_rejected` | `other`, classified webview-side from the rejection value), because a capability-rejected IPC otherwise leaves no record at all and a revoked grant is indistinguishable from a working affordance (measured: granted world 0×, revoked world exactly one record while `copy_state: "error"` kept the UX byte-identical — chunk 2026-08-30-acl-rejection-logging); `warn!(target: "ui.webgpu.adapter", outcome, window_label)` — ONCE per canvas-mount WebGPU adapter request (once per `requestWebGPUAdapter()` return path, never per frame; off any hot path per §11), reported fire-and-forget from `canvas/adapter-state.ts::reportAdapterOutcome` through `telemetry.frontend.record_webgpu_adapter` (the 6th `telemetry.frontend.*` method — the founder's ratification at P4 2026-09-30: «Да, делай»), INFO on `obtained` and WARN on `no_navigator_gpu` | `adapter_null` | `adapter_request_rejected` | `device_request_failed` (a closed serde enum; an unknown value is rejected), so a 0-frame run can name its cause from its own log (§10 frame row; chunk 2026-09-30-perf-instruments-measure-their-budgets) |
| `info` | Boundary call summaries + state transitions + heartbeat ticks | `info!(target: "ingest.grpc", "export received N spans")`, `info!(target: "ingest.tick", "heartbeat")` |
| `debug` | Internal control flow detail (gated by `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LOG_LEVEL=debug` or `RUST_LOG=debug`) | `debug!(target: "buffer.append", "writing to ring buffer")` |

| `trace` | Span events + per-record processing detail (gated by `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LOG_LEVEL=trace` or `RUST_LOG=trace`) | `trace!(target: "arrow.ipc.decode", "column {:?} validated")` — log at entry only if unhidden by flag |
**Per-module log levels:**
| Module | Recommended level | Reason |
| `ingest` (gRPC + HTTP receivers) | `info` (boundary calls) / `debug` (parsing detail) | Baseline info on export RPC received; debug on protobuf field extraction |
| `buffer` (DuckDB + appender) | `info` (append operations) / `debug` (row-level ops) | Baseline info on append completion; debug per-row processing |
| `viz` (query layer) | `info` (query execution) / `debug` (aggregation detail) | Baseline info on query start/end; debug on metric bucket assembly |
| `snapshot` (markdown generator) | `info` (generation summary) / `debug` (curation pipeline) | Baseline info on snapshot completion + token count; debug on dedup/anomaly detection |
| `plugins` (host) | `info` (load/invoke summary) / `debug` (capability checks) | Baseline info on plugin load/invoke; debug on per-capability gate |
| `workspace-detector` | `info` (detection summary) / `debug` (scan detail) | Baseline info on workspace root + project name; debug on .git/ traversal |
| `ui-bridge` (TauRPC) | `info` (command invocations) / `debug` (IPC detail) | Baseline info on TauRPC method call; debug on envelope parse |
| `mcp-server` (stdio sidecar) | `info` (tool calls) / `debug` (JSON-RPC detail) | Baseline info on tool method invocation; debug on request parse |
**Sink configuration** (from Section 3):
- App (Tauri + receivers): file JSON-only (`~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/agent-latest.jsonl`); no stderr `tracing` sink
- MCP server (hand-rolled JSON-RPC stdio): stderr JSON-only (prevent stdout JSON-RPC corruption) — NO pretty-print (binary protocol overhead)
- File rotation: daily rotation via `tracing-appender::rolling::daily(...)`
**Boundary-call wrappers (must-log events):**
| Boundary | Must-log fields | Example span |
| gRPC RPC entry/exit | `method`, `status`, `span_count` (from request), `latency_ms` | `otlp.grpc.export.request` |
| HTTP POST entry/exit | `route`, `status_code`, `body_size_bytes`, `latency_ms` | `ingest.http.export.request` |
| DuckDB query | `query_id`, `param_count`, `row_count_returned`, `duration_ms` (NOT query text per vector 5) | `duckdb.query.aggregation` |
| TauRPC invocation | `method_name`, `argument_digest` (hash, not content), `result_type`, `latency_ms` | TauRPC router method span |
| Plugin invocation | `plugin_name`, `capability_name`, `duration_ms` | `plugin.invoke.request` |
| Snapshot generation | `token_budget`, `token_count_actual`, `dedup_count`, `time_range_minutes` | `snapshot.generate.request` |

title: 7. Error Capture & Reporting

body: **Default error path (mandatory, always-on, no external service):** `std::panic::set_hook` → `tracing::error!(target: "app.panic.fatal", ...)` with `tracing-error` SpanTrace for sanitized error context. No external SaaS required for Standard tier; the JSON log file at `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/agent-latest.jsonl` IS the error capture surface, agent-readable directly.

**Optional external platform (opt-in only, default OFF):** `sentry-rust` 0.46 + `sentry-tauri` 0.5; Sentry uses its OWN SDK directly (NO OTel→Sentry bridge), running independently of the always-on `tracing` path and honoring the same scrubbing rules. Enable via `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_SENTRY_DSN` env var or Settings UI toggle (empty/unset = no-op); default-off per creator brief ("every byte of telemetry stays on the developer's machine").
**`before_send` scrubbing pattern** (REQUIRED if Sentry enabled):
- Scrub OTLP request payloads (may contain user code fragments per Vector 1)
- Strip stack traces of file paths beyond project root (kernel/stdlib paths redacted)
- Sanitize `AppError` stack traces — remove Rust struct names, library versions; use `tracing-error` SpanTrace (user-defined spans only) per Vector 2
