Verified: the same unchanged in-crate pin timed out at 30 s on 1.10502 and passes in 0.06 s on 1.10505; `smoke:gap-resume` arm A then exited 0 with 120 of 2270 appends rejected on replayed identities across 54 buffer ticks, 249,514 log lines, 0 panics, and the ERROR set exactly those 120 `duckdb.append` / `append_failed` records. **Production reachability (unchanged as a fact about clients): a retrying OTLP exporter resending spans is normal client behaviour, and it now costs one rejected batch rather than the pipeline.** **Recorded, not explained:** at the SAME 1.10502, a `metrics_points` PK collision was measured to return a whole-batch ERROR (chunk `2026-08-23-metrics-points-identity`) while the `spans` path hung — the behaviour differed by table at one library version and the mechanism was never established; it is moot at 1.10505, where both return `Err`.
   **Three claims this entry previously made are FALSE and are retired here.** (a) *"`dispatch_batch` holds `conn.lock()` across every append, so BOTH shared-connection users die — the consumer and the retention sweep."* `run_retention` has held a dedicated `try_clone()`d connection since defect 1 above (`crates/buffer/src/retention.rs:`), touching the shared `conn` exactly once to make that clone — the shared appender connection has exactly ONE production user, so a held mutex cannot explain retention's stop. (b) *"the trigger has not been separated (an idle gap AND a new gRPC connection)."* The idle gap is **not** the operative variable: the `--reconnect-only` arm (seed → immediate reconnect, ~2 s, no gap) reproduces the wedge identically — same stall at 450 s, same `reason=rows_static_while_channel_queued`, same 3,240 rows. (c) *"WHY the first post-resume batch blocks is not yet established."* It is established, and it is not a connection-isolation fault at all: step probes recorded the baseline tap completing, `spawn_blocking` scheduling the task, `conn.appender()` opening and `append_record_batch` returning — only `flush()` never does. Blocking-pool starvation is separately excluded (771 `viz.query.traces` + 1,300 `metric.pipeline.l1a.*` completed after onset in the archived wedge).
   **Owner: the working-route entry "Duplicate-span replay fails loudly"**, whose modify-set is the appender (a post-failure flush must fail loudly, never hang) and the demo injector (whose per-process batch counter restarts at 0, so every restart re-emits identical `(trace_id, span_id)` pairs — the harness manufactures the collision that `smoke:gap-resume` arm A currently reproduces). **This defect is NOT evidence against the reference-connection mandate below** — that mandate is satisfied by the shipped code; the retired claim (a) is what wrongly implicated it.

**Reference connection pattern:** write (appender) / sweep (retention) / read (L1a + viz) isolation on the same `:memory:` database via `Connection::try_clone()` on each dedicated task. Any future DuckDB consumer with a multi-second statement MUST take a dedicated `try_clone()` connection, never the shared appender connection.

**A fourth consumer joined the isolated set 2026-08-26:** `viz`'s three production query fns (`query_traces` / `query_metrics` / `query_logs`) held the SHARED appender connection — `crates/viz` contained no `try_clone` at all — and since the Traces surface re-polls on a timer those reads recur for the window's whole lifetime. Fixed by `viz::query::read_connection`, taken once at `TracesApiImpl::new` / `MetricsApiImpl::new` / `LogsApiImpl::new`, with the same warn-on-fallback shape as `buffer::retention` and `TriageSqlState::new` (target `viz.query`, `fallback = "shared_connection"`). This was a violation of the mandate above rather than a new rule: the invariant was already correct and the code diverged from it. Verified live — a 10-minute sustained leg recorded 0 fallback WARNs with 405 `viz.query.traces` still served.

**Characterized-not-fixed:** the DuckDB append path performs multi-row-group maintenance that can block a single append inside `spawn_blocking` for >60s on a ~12.7M-row in-memory table. The mpsc channel (1024 batches) absorbs the pause; boundary rejections surface as LWW drops; every accepted span lands after recovery — "degraded-but-functional, zero L0 loss", in-spec.

**The drain-progress detector has been exercised against a live reproduction, not only against the archive.** `cargo xtask smoke:gap-resume` (test-plan §3) consumes `buffer.consumer.stalled` + `check:ingest-progress` as its verdict rather than adding a second detector, and on 2026-08-28 the detector fired correctly on a fresh wedge with its bounded tokens observed at the wire — `reason = rows_static_while_channel_queued`, `consequence = accepted_spans_not_persisted`, `stalled_seconds = 450`, `buffer_capacity_pct = 85.7` — announced ONCE per transition as specified. The 450s / 30-tick threshold and the exact-leaf field set are unchanged; this records that the mechanism is proven end-to-end on a defect it detected in the wild, which the 2026-08-26 archive measurement alone could not establish.

**Load-profile constraints:** sustained-profile drain is maintenance-tolerant (no eager no-progress panic; hard 420s drain cap); the load-profiles nextest terminate ceiling is 20min. Any future xtask check over `agent-latest.jsonl` must be NEUTRAL-tolerant for an UNREQUIRED arm (absent stream ≠ failure) so headless verification and full-app sessions share one grader — `perf:load-profiles` alone grades with no arm required since chunk 2026-10-10-no-gate-stands-while-reading-nothing (`ci-gates` left the grader: it runs no perf arm, both arms it keeps are reads it requires, and an absent log family is exit 2 `cannot-evaluate`, never NEUTRAL or PASS — the tolerance above is the perf grader's, for an arm no caller requires, and is not a licence for a gate to pass over an absent input); a caller that EXPECTS samples names the arm with `perf:budget --require`, and a required empty arm FAILs, which is what lets the CI perf gate fail. `cargo xtask check:engine-log` (chunk 2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine) is a third caller of the grader: it requires the memory arm in-process through `perf_budget::grade_arm`, has no NEUTRAL reading, states frame and snapshot as not graded on one line, and never passes over an input it cannot grade. As measured at chunk 2026-10-10-engine-harness-proofs-completed (its `evidence/mutations.md`): each of the check's seven arms, mutated by one line, reddened pins (6, 3, 7, 9, 7, 8, 8 of 45) and changed its own line over the kept log of one real console engine cycle, and the 45 pins and the nine original lines stood again after the reverts. The limit of that reading: one mutation per arm, on the arm's passing side, over one real log (n = 1) that all seven arms can grade — it shows each arm grades, and for an input an arm cannot grade the pins are still the only reading; one heartbeat pin stayed green under the inverted gap comparison (nine others reddened), its log's other two targets carrying ordinary gaps the inversion fails.

title: 11. Obs Anti-Patterns (NEVER do these)
Telemetry Strategy

body: - NEVER over-instrument hot paths (appender inner loop, per-row DuckDB operations) — span overhead matters; profile before adding spans to tight loops
- NEVER skip spans on critical user-facing paths (P1-P7) — agent loses debug ability
- NEVER let signal pyramid drift toward logs-only (spans give request-scoped context logs alone can't; metrics give distribution, trends)
- NEVER use vendor-lock OTLP schemas (Datadog APM SDK / NewRelic agent / AppDynamics); if you use error reporting platform (Sentry), ensure `before_send` scrubbing + local log export always works

title: Spans / Traces

body: - NEVER include raw OTLP attributes in span attributes (Vector 1 scrubbing) — include only `attributes_count` + `service_name_tag`
- NEVER use high-cardinality span names (per-user-ID names, per-trace-ID names, per-arbitrary-request-path) — kills distributed tracing storage
- NEVER skip trace context propagation across surface boundaries (IPC envelope, gRPC metadata, HTTP headers) — agent loses trace continuity for multi-surface debugging

- NEVER hold a `tracing::Span` guard across `.await` points without `.in_current_span()` — span context bleeds into unrelated tasks scheduled by tokio, breaking trace_id correlation and bloating memory until the holder drops
- NEVER serialize `anyhow::Error` directly across IPC boundary — convert to `AppError` enum + sanitize per Vector 2
- NEVER log full canonicalized plugin file paths (Vector 3) — basename only
- NEVER emit raw DuckDB query text in span attributes (Vector 5) — query_id + param_count only

title: Metrics

body: - NEVER use unbounded label cardinality in `tracing` event fields (service_name mapped to infinity, trace IDs, arbitrary request paths) — explodes per-line JSON size and `jq`-aggregation cost downstream; enumerate label values upfront (exception: query-time aggregation events emit unbounded `service_name` per Section 5 cardinality note — single-query scope only, not time-series-stored)

- NEVER format expensive `tracing` event payloads inside hot paths without level-gating — wrap heavy serialization in `if tracing::enabled!(Level::DEBUG) { ... }` for tight loops; field arg evaluation happens regardless of subscriber filter when the macro is reached

- NEVER skip p50/p95/p99 coverage on perf-budget metrics — emit raw per-event `value` field via `tracing::info!(target: "metric.*")`; agent computes percentiles by tailing the JSON file (no precomputed quantiles in the emission path — agent-side `jq` aggregation is the convention)
- NEVER use metrics as sole SLO signal without span tracing (need both for end-to-end visibility)

title: Logs

body: - NEVER use unstructured stderr text (agent can't parse fields) — always JSON-per-line to file sink
- NEVER skip `trace_id` / `span_id` fields in logs (when available) — agent loses correlation between logs and spans
- NEVER use multi-line stack traces without one-line serialization — breaks JSON-per-line parsing; use SpanTrace (tracing-error) instead of raw backtrace
- NEVER log in hot path at `info` level — spam costs throughput; use `trace` / `debug` gated by `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LOG_LEVEL` env var
- NEVER log raw OTLP attribute values (Vector 1), stack traces with struct names (Vector 2), full paths (Vector 3), MCP response content (Vector 4), or query parameters (Vector 5)

title: Error Reporting

body: - NEVER ship a real Sentry DSN in dev / committed to repo — security leak; use `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_SENTRY_DSN` env var only
- NEVER skip `before_send` scrubbing (if Sentry enabled) — PII leaks to external service
- NEVER enable error reporting by default — privacy violation; opt-in only (per creator brief: "every byte stays on developer's machine")
- NEVER use Sentry as the ONLY error sink — local panic hook + tracing::error log MUST always work even with Sentry disabled

title: PII Scrubbing

body: - NEVER include PII in logs / spans / metrics by default (default-deny posture) — scrub at source via `skip(...)` macro or redact at processor stage
- NEVER scrub only at sink stage (Sentry `before_send`) — scrub at processor stage so failures upstream don't leak; apply at multiple layers

- NEVER hardcode scrubbing rules in a single location — rules applied at multiple layers: `#[tracing::instrument(skip(...))]` at the source, custom `tracing-subscriber` Layer at the formatter stage, Sentry `before_send` at the network egress (if Sentry enabled)
- NEVER log plugin-returned Arrow IPC payloads (untrusted) — size-cap + schema validation only
- NEVER log snapshot file contents to stdout (security plan anti-pattern) — snapshot file write emits non-suppressible toast event

title: CI

body: - NEVER lose telemetry artifacts (log file + snapshot on failure) — uploaded as CI artifacts with retention
- NEVER use human-review-gated log analysis ("ops team reviews daily") without machine-parseable export — agent locked out
- NEVER skip snapshot generation on test failure — first-class debugging artifact
- NEVER rely on colored terminal output for CI parsing — CI artifacts MUST be structured (JSON) + machine-readable

title: SLO

body: - NEVER skip zero-unlogged-panics invariant — most basic obs guarantee; every panic logged with structured backtrace
- NEVER add retry-once policies for panic handling — masks real failures (parallel to tests' zero-flakiness invariant)

- NEVER define soft SLO budgets (no enforcement) — formal SLOs MUST trigger build / deploy failure when exhausted (e.g., memory max > 512 MB or snapshot p99 > 500 ms = `perf:budget` fails lint-test; the frame p99 > 33 ms gate runs on a GPU dev host via `perf:frame-sample`, since hosted runners expose no WebGPU adapter)
- NEVER defer error budget decisions to humans ("team will review monthly") — agent-driven SLO assertions in CI

title: Universal (agent-driven specific)

body: - NEVER use proprietary APM as ONLY exporter (Datadog APM SDK / NewRelic agent / AppDynamics as primary) — vendor schemas break paste-to-AI workflows; the JSON file at `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/agent-latest.jsonl` is the canonical agent surface

- NEVER use dashboards-only obs (Grafana / Kibana / Datadog UI as sole consumption surface) — every signal must have agent-readable consumption path (the JSON log file is the primary path; the curated markdown snapshot is the secondary path for external client OTLP data)
- NEVER use human-review-gated log analysis without machine-parseable export — blocks agent-driven debugging

- NEVER link an OTel SDK into the product's self-observation runtime — the `tracing` ecosystem alone produces JSON-per-line that the agent can read directly; adding an OTel SDK on top would only re-introduce the recursion concern this project already chose to avoid by construction
- NEVER hardcode service identity (`service.name = "myapp"`) — use compile-time `env!()` or runtime config per Section 3, with a single source of truth registered as a default subscriber field
- NEVER skip `before_send` scrubbing in error reporting (if Sentry enabled) — PII → external service = privacy violation

- NEVER write to stdout from any subsystem when running as the `andromeda-pulse-mcp` stdio sidecar — stdout is reserved for JSON-RPC 2.0 framing; ALL `tracing` output forced to stderr (JSON formatter); ANY accidental `println!` / `dbg!` / library stdout write corrupts the protocol and silently disconnects the MCP client. Since chunk 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door the ban reaches the console program's `door` word (the stdio relay): NEVER write to its stdout anything but the door's answer bytes, unchanged, or to its stderr anything but the one fixed line on exit 1; it installs no `tracing` subscriber and writes no record (PROVISIONAL with the door's item)

title: Project-specific (andromeda-pulse)

body: - NEVER feature-gate MCP server without runtime `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED=true` double-gate (security plan anti-pattern: "MCP double-gate omission") — compile-time flag (`--features mcp-server`) + runtime env var both required; the gate state is a `tracing` field on `mcp.feature.gate.check` span. The ban is the stdio sidecar's (`andromeda-pulse-mcp`) and stands unchanged for it. Since chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process the console engine's door serves the same nine tools behind neither gate (`pulse-app` links `mcp-server` in every build; `rmcp` still enters only under the feature), and since chunk 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door a stdio agent reaches them through `andromeda-pulse-engine door` behind neither gate; the door emits no gate-check span: its admission is the owner check on every accepted connection, and its state is read from `app.boot.door` (`state`, `resolve_write`) and `door.refused` (`reason`, `peer`) (PROVISIONAL — §4 Scenario P3)
- NEVER log MCP tool response bodies in the JSON log file (security plan vector 4 — indirect-prompt-injection surface for LLM clients) — only `result_type` + `result_count` metadata captured

- NEVER serialize plugin-returned Arrow IPC without size cap (untrusted) — bound to 8MB at the host boundary before re-emit on Tauri Channel; size violation emits `error`-level `tracing::error!` event

- NEVER conflate the product's external snapshot pipeline (curated markdown of EXTERNAL clients' OTLP data, the user-invoked feature) with the self-observation surface (the JSON log file at `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/`) — the two are independent; the agent reads the JSON file for the product's OWN debug trail and the snapshot file for the external clients' debug trail

title: Tracing init

body: - **Crate set:** `tracing` 0.1 (macro-driven instrumentation; `#[instrument]` attribute on router/handler methods) + `tracing-subscriber` 0.3 (JSON formatter + Layer composition + `EnvFilter`) + `tracing-appender` 0.2 (daily-rolling file sink, non-blocking writer) + `tracing-error` 0.2 (SpanTrace for sanitized error chains)

- **Init order:** Before Tauri app spawn; before HTTP/gRPC server bind. Sequence: (1) Load env vars + config → validate log level via `EnvFilter::from_env("ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LOG_LEVEL")` with fallback `RUST_LOG`, (2) Build the `tracing_subscriber::registry()` composing the non-blocking file appender layer (no stderr layer), (3) Install panic hook calling `tracing::error!(target: "app.panic.fatal", ...)` with `tracing-error` SpanTrace, (4) `engine_boot::start` spawns the engine tasks and binds the two OTLP receivers (tonic + axum) — in the window app before the Tauri builder (it was inside its setup closure), after `main`'s own window boot records and render posture; the window app alone then runs the Tauri app. Since chunk 2026-10-10-console-engine-entry-point steps (1)–(3) and the installs that follow them are ONE function, the process start both programs call once with the tokio runtime entered — `engine_boot::init_process(data_dir)`, called by the window app (`pulse-app`) and by the console program (`andromeda-pulse-engine run`). After (3) it hands the `WorkerGuard` `init` returns to a process-wide slot (`hold_log_guard`), installs the at-exit hook (`install_exit_hook`: a `pulse-exit-reporter` thread + `libc::atexit`) and, on Unix, the SIGTERM/SIGINT listener (`install_signal_listener`), then records the start instant and writes the pid file. The console program spawns no Tauri app and has no event loop: it ends by SIGTERM or SIGINT through the same listener (`app.exit` class `signal`, the signal re-raised), and it has the one file layer — no stderr or stdout log layer. The window app runs through `App::run_return`; its exit code goes to `exit_after_event_loop` (record `app.exit` → `flush_log_sink` drops the guard → `std::process::exit` with the SAME code). `WorkerGuard::drop` is the non-blocking file sink's only drain, so every exit path that can log drains it after its one record (§6 `app.exit`).
- **Init body sketch (≤ 5 lines):**

- **Why this approach:** by NOT linking an OTel SDK into the self-runtime, the "OTel monitoring an OTel monitor" recursion concern disappears by construction — there is no exporter to point anywhere, and the file-sink JSON line IS the agent-readable surface.

title: Logging stack
Logging stack

body: - **Library:** `tracing` 0.1 + `tracing-subscriber` 0.3 + `tracing-appender` 0.2 + `tracing-error` 0.2 (versions tracked in obs-research catalog; pinned at workspace level)
- **Format:** structured JSON-per-line matching binding contract (Section 6 log format JSON schema); agent-readable, machine-parseable; produced by `tracing_subscriber::fmt::Layer::json()`

- **Sink:** Single sink for app: the file `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/agent-latest.jsonl`, always JSON-only, via the non-blocking `tracing-appender` daily layer composed with `EnvFilter` + `ErrorLayer` — no stderr layer, no TTY pretty-print (as measured at chunk `2026-10-02-incident-events-readable-through-mcp`). For the mcp-server sidecar (rmcp 3.x resolved 3.1.4, declared-but-unused; hand-rolled JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio), stderr is forced JSON (no TTY check) — stdout is reserved for JSON-RPC 2.0 framing and ANY accidental stdout write would corrupt the protocol. The console program's `door` word (the stdio relay, chunk `2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door`; PROVISIONAL with the door's item) has no sink at all — no subscriber, no record — its stdout reserved for the door's JSON-RPC answer lines and its stderr for one fixed line on exit 1

- **Frontend bridge:** WebGPU frame timing + skeleton-pulse durations (and the three delegated timing observables) from the React webview flow through the hand-rolled TauRPC `telemetry.frontend.*` commands, which call `tracing::info!(target: "metric.{name}", ...)` on the backend — single JSON file is the unified self-observation surface. This is the DECIDED mechanism: `web-vitals` 5.x was RETIRED 2026-08-30 (operator ruling at the `2026-08-30-npm-advisory-coverage` wrap) — measured never installed (0 hits in package.json / package-lock.json / ui/src), its metrics (LCP/CLS/INP/FCP/TTFB) are page-load-shaped and do not fit a persistent fixed-layout desktop webview, and no producer or consumer of `metric.web_vital.*` ever existed

title: Snapshot / paste-to-AI integration

body: Two cleanly separated surfaces:
**External-OTLP snapshot** (the product's CORE feature — the thing users invoke):
- **Path:** `~/.andromeda-pulse/snapshots/{timestamp}.md` (curated markdown, not raw OTLP JSON); timestamp format `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`

- **Schema:** Curated markdown with header (`## Snapshot from {time_range_start} to {time_range_end}`), metadata (`token_count`, `dedup_count`, `service_filter`, `anomaly_markers` like "⚠ latency spike" / "🔴 error cluster"), aggregated metrics (p50/p95/p99/max per service), critical-path top-slow-spans, trace IDs for drill-down. Deduped (identical span trees counted once with emission count). NOT raw OTLP JSON dump (per tests excerpt P2 + creator brief Section 6)

- **Trigger:** TauRPC `snapshot.generate({time_range, token_budget: 10000 | 25000 | 50000})` from webview; span `session.snapshot` wraps the pipeline; child spans emit token-budget telemetry (Section 5 perf-budget-instruments)

- **MCP tools (hand-rolled JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio; rmcp 3.x declared-but-unused):** nine (`ALL_TOOL_NAMES`) — `query_traces`, `query_metrics`, `query_logs`, `generate_snapshot` are the JSON-RPC 2.0 interface to the same external-OTLP query pipeline; `query_incident_list`, `retrieve_report`, `retrieve_telemetry_slice`, `mark_incident_resolved` (chunk #94) and `retrieve_incident_events` (chunk `2026-10-02-incident-events-readable-through-mcp`) read the incident corpus. Through the stdio sidecar every tool emits `mcp.tools.call.request` (parent) → `mcp.tools.call.response` (result metadata only — `result_type` + `result_count`, NOT result_content per security plan vector 4) at `dispatch_tool`, which since chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process calls `mcp_server::tools::call_tool` (it returns `ToolAnswer { value, result_type, result_count }` and writes no record); `call_tool` has a second caller, `door::EngineTools` in the console engine, whose calls are recorded as `door.call` carrying `result_type` + `result_count` and never the answer, so vector 4 holds on both carriers. "Over stdio" in this label is the sidecar's transport and, since chunk `2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door`, also that of the `andromeda-pulse-engine door` relay, which carries each line to the door's Unix-domain socket; calls through the relay are recorded as `door.call` only (obs-plan §4 Scenario P3). The `duckdb.query.{traces|metrics|logs}` child belongs to the telemetry tools only
**Self-observation paste-to-AI** (the product's debug surface — the thing developers/agents read):
- **Path:** `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/agent-latest.jsonl` (the same JSON log file from Logging stack above)
- **Format:** JSON-per-line, immediately greppable / `jq`-able / paste-to-LLM-able
- **No separate snapshot needed** — the JSON log file IS the self-observation snapshot

The two surfaces NEVER intersect: external client OTLP data lives in DuckDB and is curated into the markdown snapshot; the product's own runtime telemetry lives in the JSON log file. By separating them, no recursion is possible.

title: Trace context propagation

body: - **HTTP boundaries (`:4318` OTLP/HTTP receiver on axum 0.8):** W3C `traceparent` header extracted at request entry via manual `tower::Layer` (or `tower-http::TraceLayer` for plain `tracing` spans, NOT OTel-flavored); attached as a regular field on the inner `#[tracing::instrument]` span (`fields(traceparent = %tp)`) — downstream calls inherit via `tracing::Span::current()`

- **gRPC boundaries (`:4317` OTLP/gRPC receiver on tonic 0.14):** gRPC metadata (`grpc-trace-bin` header) extracted at gRPC service method handler entry via manual interceptor; attached as a `traceparent` field on the local `#[tracing::instrument]` span; same propagation pattern as HTTP

- **IPC boundaries (TauRPC):** TauRPC router handlers manually extract optional `traceparent` field from IPC envelope; initialize the local span with `fields(traceparent = %tp)` so downstream `tracing::Span::current()` calls inherit
- **Internal async boundaries:** `tokio::spawn` calls use `.in_current_span()` extension trait (from `tracing` 0.1) to propagate span context into spawned tasks

- **Real-time push streams:** `pulse://stream/spans` etc. carry trace context in Arrow metadata column (`_trace_context` schema field) for end-to-end correlation. NOTE: `traceparent` value is treated as an opaque string in `tracing` events, not bound to any OTel SDK trace context

title: Heartbeat ticks

body: - **Tick interval:** 15s via `tokio::time::interval(Duration::from_secs(15))`, spawned in two groups since chunk 2026-10-10-console-engine-entry-point: the engine's three ticks (`ingest.tick`, `buffer.tick`, `connection.tick`) by `heartbeat::spawn_engine_ticks`, called once from `engine_boot::start` and so emitted by both programs; the window's two (`viz.tick`, `plugins.tick`) by `heartbeat::spawn_window_ticks`, called once from the window app's setup closure. The window app emits all five; the console program (`andromeda-pulse-engine run`) emits the three and never `viz.tick` or `plugins.tick`, so in a log whose `app.boot.engine` record reads `program: console` their absence is by design and not a stall; 100ms for the realtime throughput counter (separate high-frequency ticker for animation smoothness per creator brief)
- **Tick event format:** `tracing::info!(target: "{module}.tick", span_count=N, buffer_capacity_pct=M, broadcast_subscribers=X, "heartbeat")` — ride the same JSON file sink as the rest of the app

- **Stall detection (two signals — liveness AND progress):** (a) LIVENESS — agent reads recent ticks via tail of JSON file or CLI `logs` command; missing tick for >45s = stall signal; for a log whose `app.boot.engine` record reads `console` the gap is graded by the `heartbeat-gap` arm of `cargo xtask check:engine-log` (chunk 2026-10-10-agent-harness-drives-the-console-engine) over `ingest.tick`, `buffer.tick` and `connection.tick` only — fewer than two records of a target, or a record with no readable timestamp, is cannot-evaluate — and `viz.tick` / `plugins.tick` are never read; `health` IPC command exposes the same fields synchronously for active liveness probing per arch Standard Contracts. (b) PROGRESS — tick presence does not certify that work is moving: a wedged buffer consumer keeps ticking while `rows_ingested` stays frozen, which every liveness check reads as healthy (measured 2026-08-26). The companion signal is `rows_ingested_delta` remaining 0 across consecutive `buffer.tick`s while the ingest channel still holds queued work, announced once per transition on `buffer.consumer.stalled` and asserted by `cargo xtask check:ingest-progress`, which reads NEUTRAL, exit 0, over a family with no `buffer.tick`; the reading that cannot be neutral is the `progress` arm of `cargo xtask check:engine-log` over a console engine's log (same 2026-10-10 chunk)

**Complementarity with the `health` command:** Heartbeat ticks (asynchronous, 15s emission to the JSON log) and the TauRPC `health` command (synchronous status polling) serve different purposes and must not be conflated. Heartbeat ticks enable retroactive log analysis ("was the subsystem alive during this interval?"); the `health` command enables active liveness probing during boot (the test harness polls synchronously until status ok) and at runtime. Implementations emit tick events independent of `health` invocations, and return synchronous `health` status independent of tick history; both mechanisms remain and operate in parallel.

title: 2026-06-10 — Chunk #99 tag gate: frame-budget posture + L4 budgets + load-suite findings  →  folded to §10
body:
## 2026-06-10 — Chunk #99 tag gate: frame-budget posture + L4 budgets + load-suite findings  →  folded to §10
**Section:** 10.
**Change:** three operational findings folded into obs-plan §10 as current-truth; no §10 budget value changed.
- **Frame p99 ≤33ms two-state posture** — NEUTRAL when no webview (headless run): check scripts report NEUTRAL, not FAIL; ACTIVE when a booted app measures real frames; `write_run_window_log` scopes scripts to the run window. Both states verified at chunk #99 (ACTIVE: frame p99 = 27.3ms over 56,642 real frames, buffer max 152.4MB ≤ 512MB, zero panics/ERROR).
- **L4 per-hardware-profile latency budgets** in `xtask/ci/l4-latency-p99` confirmed canonical (no re-derivation).
- **DuckDB connection-isolation pattern + load constraints** — topology: write/sweep/read isolation on the same `:memory:` DB via `Connection::try_clone()`. 50k spans/s exposed 3 production defects, fixed in-chunk: (a) retention-sweep mutex starvation → dedicated sweep `try_clone()` connection + `MissedTickBehavior::Delay`; (b) timeout could not cancel a mutex-holding `spawn_blocking` query → dedicated read connection + `interrupt_handle().interrupt()`; (c) L1a read starvation behind row-group maintenance → dedicated read connection. Characterized-not-fixed: the append path can block >60s on a ~12.7M-row table (mpsc absorbs; zero L0 loss; in-spec). Load profile: sustained drain maintenance-tolerant (420s cap); nextest ceiling 20min; check scripts NEUTRAL-tolerant.
**Why:** chunk #99 tag-gate load-suite verification; sibling entry in test-plan §12.
**Ref:** NOT DERIVED

## 2026-08-14-fingerprint-feed-capture-repair — Fingerprint-feed counters + degraded-boot warn
**Section:** §1 Obs Scope Summary → Heartbeat ticks; §5 Metric Coverage → conceptual instrument types; §6 Log Coverage → log-level mapping (`warn` row); §8 PII Scrubbing → default-deny per-module allowlist
**Change:** `buffer.tick` fields gain `span_events_seen` / `fingerprints_computed` / `observer_invocations`, folded once per batch by `BufferState::record_feed_counts` and ridden out as tick FIELDS, not separate `metric.buffer.*` targets (per-span-event emission barred by the §11 hot-path rule); §5 gains the tick-aggregated counter row describing them; §6 records the new `app.boot.buffer.degraded` WARN target (`reason` + `consequence`, once per boot); §8's `buffer` allowlist gains the three counters (aggregate counts only, never identity) plus an explicit `app.boot.buffer.degraded` leaf.
**Why:** the instrumentation ships permanently (operator decision at /phase P4). Equality of `observer_invocations` with `fingerprints_computed` makes a live feed a POSITIVE reading; before, "nothing reached the storm detector" could only be inferred from downstream silence, which let a suspected dead feed go undiagnosed. The §8 leaf is load-bearing: `for_target`'s fallback would otherwise resolve the dotted boot target to an unrelated `app`-prefixed field set and redact both fields.

**Section:** §5 Metric Coverage → Conceptual instrument types, the `redactions_applied` Counter row
**Change:** the four `buffer::appender` record-batch builders now RETURN their per-batch tally (`Result<Option<(RecordBatch, u64)>, Error>`) and `BufferState::record_redactions` folds at each table's OWN post-append site in `consumer::dispatch_batch`, so a batch the appender rejects at `flush()` contributes zero. Per-table granularity is load-bearing (a `span_events` failure must not discard the count for rows `spans` already stored); `build_spans_record_batch` consequently takes no `&BufferState`. The "Counts redactions to PERSISTED cells ONLY" qualifier is now structural rather than aspirational, with the pre-chunk counter-example recorded (`redactions_applied: 2` with `rows_ingested: 0` on a rejected batch). **Why:** the rule this row states was measured FALSE at HEAD — the fold fired inside the builders before the append could fail; moving it made the stated rule true.
**Kept:** the other two `redactions_applied` mentions (the tick field list, the `buffer` allowlist) assert only tick membership and aggregate-only shape, both still true.

body:
## 2026-08-26-ingest-consumer-stall-under-sustained-load — drain progress: tick presence is liveness, not progress
**Section:** §1 Obs Scope Summary → Heartbeat ticks · §3 Observability Harness Contract → Stall detection · §5 Metric Coverage → tick-aggregated Counter rows · §6 Log Coverage → `warn` row · §8 PII Scrubbing → Default-deny posture (`buffer` whitelist + a new exact leaf) · §10 SLO Invariants → Standard+ invariants + DuckDB Connection Isolation
**Change:**
- (a) `buffer.tick` gains `rows_ingested_delta` + `last_append_age_seconds` (12 → 14 fields) at all THREE restating sites (§1 field list, §5 as its own tick-aggregated Counter row, §8 `buffer` whitelist).

## 2026-10-01-conductor-return — the process-end record `app.exit`
**Section:** §1 Obs Scope Summary → Tracing init · §3 Tracing init → Init order · §6 Log Coverage → `warn` row · §7 Error Capture & Reporting → Error classes captured · §8 PII Scrubbing → leaf list
**Change:**
- §1 / §3: the init order continues after the panic hook — `main` parks the `WorkerGuard` `init` returns (`hold_log_guard`; `init`'s signature unchanged), installs the at-exit hook (`install_exit_hook`: a `pulse-exit-reporter` thread + `libc::atexit`) and, on Unix, the SIGTERM/SIGINT listener; the app runs through `run_return`, its code to `exit_after_event_loop` (record → drop the guard → `std::process::exit` with the same code). `WorkerGuard::drop` is the file sink's only drain; a plain `run` ends in tao's `process::exit` with the worker undrained.
- §6: `app.exit {exit_class, exit_code, exit_code_known, signal}` — exactly once per process end (once-flag; the emitter drops the only guard), INFO zero-code event-loop exit, WARN SIGTERM/SIGINT (Unix, re-raised), ERROR non-zero event-loop exit and every `outside_event_loop` end (code unknown — `libc` binds no `on_exit`).
- §7: a new captured class, the process-end cause; unloggable by construction: SIGKILL, `_exit`, Windows `TerminateProcess`, a Rust `std::process::exit` on Windows (`ExitProcess` runs no `atexit`, as measured), pre-sink failures; a main-thread panic followed by one `outside_event_loop` record holds by construction only.
- §8: the `app.exit` EXACT leaf beside `app.panic.fatal` (all four fields; no bare `app` key; guard ×4 in `pulse-app/tests/`, mutation-checked).
**Why:** a process end left no record at all — the 69f0b93 Linux CI boot smoke ended `exit 1` with no cause; the record makes the next such end name its class. A once-flag whose only drain is a guard drop cannot be pinned by a file read (the first flush closes the sink) — pin it by return value.
**Kept:** §1 / §3 step (2) "stderr + file" sink clause left as written — a pre-existing drift (HEAD builds the file layer only), routed as a route CARRY, not this chunk's.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-10-02T12-54-57Z-wrap/

**Change:**
- Frame row: was "So the CI boot job witnesses the WARN arm on some runs and not on others" under a step that ran `boot` → `status` → `cleanup` back to back (the app alive 0.57 s to 1.40 s; four of seven logs with the record), per the entry "the boot job does not always stop the app before the webview's first call"; now the step runs `boot` → `cargo xtask harness:settled` → `status` → `cleanup` and reads the app once its four window records are in: as measured on `ci#37979648967`, the app lived 5.494 s, its log holds 2 `ui.webgpu.adapter` records, both `no_navigator_gpu`, and the `ci-gates` line read `frame: cannot-evaluate: 0 samples, no WebGPU adapter (no_navigator_gpu)` — one run measured, the expected line on every run that reaches the settle verdict. The seven-log readings stay as dated history of the former order.
- CI gates bullet: the boot-smoke frame line is no longer run-dependent; the lint-test `perf:budget` line was not re-read at this chunk.
- §1 row and §8 bullet: the CI witness of the WARN arm no longer depends on how long the app lives; the tally gains the ninth reading.

**Why:** the smoke's step order changed what every CI boot log holds. The two kept files are how a run in which the app ends by itself says what the job saw; they were classified routine harness evidence by the pc overseer (founder-delegated) at the plan review. title: 2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-closed — the CI boot job's self-end: cause measured, end closed
body:
## 2026-10-10-boot-smoke-s-self-end-closed — the CI boot job's self-end: cause measured, end closed
**Section:** §7 Error classes captured (Process-end cause) · §10 Performance budgets (the WebGPU canvas frame row) · §10 CI gates (the perf-budget bullet)
**Change:**
- Process-end cause: "Not measured: why the X connection's read failed, and the runner's own library build" retired. Now, as measured: no read failed (at the stop in `_XIOError` the connection reports no error; one capture of one ending); Xlib raised the I/O error because its own bookkeeping held no reply while a second thread, `tao` 0.35.0's device-event thread, was inside Xlib and the app had not initialised Xlib's thread support; Xlib 1.7.5 (the runner) does not do it at load, 1.8.13 (the dev host) does. The variation shows the cause: 26 of 32 boots self-ended without the initialisation, 0 of 8 with it, under the runner's Xlib on the dev host. The builds are read from Ubuntu's packages (`libx11-6 1.7.5-1ubuntu0.3`; `gdk_x_io_error` in `libgtk-3-0 3.24.33-1ubuntu2.2`). Not traced: the step inside Xlib by which the reply is lost.
- `errno` 11 on the `end` line is a stale value, not a member of the ending call. Was: "`_exit(1)` with `errno` 11".
- "The end is named, not closed; its owner is the route's closing entry" retired. Now: closed; `main` calls `pulse_app::xlib_threads::init()` second, before any thread, inert where the library or symbol is not found, no log record. `ci#38026637514`, attempts 1 to 3: 24 boots, 0 self-ended, against 12 of 16 before. No route entry owns it. The builds published before keep the defect on a host whose Xlib is older than 1.8; none was booted; what is done about them is the founder's.
- §10 frame row and CI gates: the smoke-and-series-both-pass case is measured (`ci#38026637514`, attempts 1 to 3, the frame line `… no WebGPU adapter (no_navigator_gpu)` in each boot job log); was expected from the step order. A series boot fails the job when it ended by itself: a settle verdict of `ended`, or no settle verdict and an own exit record (any but `signal 15 (TERM)` / `signal 9 (KILL)`).
**Why:** Phase research measured the mechanism the paragraph listed as unmeasured, and the chunk closed the end on the runner; the narrative still named it open with a route owner.
**Kept:** §9's log-file row stands: its `ci#38019133294` reading is dated and its description of `boot-series.json` still holds.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-10-10T06-10-23Z-wrap/

## 2026-10-10-no-ci-step-reads-nothing — which CI artifacts exist: two log uploads, no test-job log, no snapshot
**Section:** §9 Telemetry artifact handling (the Log file row, the Snapshot markdown row) · §9 Pipeline integration (the `xtask test`, `xtask test --release` and Integration tests rows) · §9 CI failure → artifact triage workflow
**Change:**
- Log file row: was the `lint-test` job (`logs-${{ runner.os }}`) and the `boot` job; now the `boot` job (`logs-boot-${{ runner.os }}`) and the lint-test perf-samples log (`logs-perf-samples-${{ runner.os }}`), two uploads. The `lint-test` job's `logs-${{ runner.os }}` upload found no file (no step of that job writes a log family under its data dir, `ci#38031822696`) and left. Each upload of `ci.yml` now carries `if-no-files-found: error`: an upload that finds no file fails its step, read on a runner only where the producer did not run (`ci#38034700885`), never where one ran and wrote nothing.
- Snapshot markdown row: was "uploaded as CI artifact" when an integration test fails; now "not produced in CI": no step of `ci.yml` writes or uploads a snapshot on a failed test.
- Pipeline integration: `xtask test` was "CI artifact `logs/agent-latest.jsonl`"; now the test run uploads nothing and the perf-samples producer after it writes the log `perf:budget` grades. The `xtask test --release` row is gone (no step runs it). Integration tests: was "logs artifact + snapshot markdown artifact"; now none uploaded.
- Triage workflow: was "Test failure → uploads `logs/agent-latest.jsonl`" and `gh run download <run_id> -n logs`; now a failed `boot` job uploads `logs-boot-Linux`, a failed test in `lint-test` uploads no app log, and the download names the artifact (`-n logs-boot-Linux`; no artifact of a run is named `logs`).
**Why:** Each sentence named an artifact no step produced. The chunk removed the uploads that found nothing and made the rest fail on nothing; the rows now say what a run keeps.
**Kept:** §11's two bans, "NEVER lose telemetry artifacts (log file + snapshot on failure)" and "NEVER skip snapshot generation on test failure", are not amended: they are requirements the workflow does not meet, and whether the version keeps them was put to the operator at this wrap's route-resolve card. body:
## 2026-10-10-no-gate-stands-while-reading-nothing — §10 CI gates: the zero-span, zero-panic and heartbeat bullets state what enforces them, and what nothing enforces
**Section:** §10 SLO Invariants & Telemetry Budgets → CI gates (the first three bullets)
**Change:**
- Zero-span bullet: was "Build fails if `xtask test` produces zero spans in log file … enforced by `xtask test` step exit code validation"; now the build fails when the boot job's log family holds no record, enforced by the `zero-spans` arm of `cargo xtask ci-gates` in the `boot` job, which counts log records of any target, not spans: zero records → exit 1, no family member → exit 2 `cannot-evaluate` (110 records on `ci#38042949735`). The reading the bullet used to state, a TEST RUN that produces zero spans failing the build, is stated as made by no CI step and unmet, carried on the working route. An empty test selection does fail: every nextest invocation spells `--no-tests=fail`.
- Zero-panic bullet: was enforced "by post-test `jq … | grep -q .` check"; now by the `zero-panic` arm of `ci-gates` in the `boot` job, read in-process: exit 1 with `::error::ci-gates: zero-panic FAIL: app.panic.fatal at {member file name}:{line}`, never the record's text or a path. No workflow step runs `jq`.
- Heartbeat bullet: was "Build fails if heartbeat tick stalls detected … enforced by post-test gap analysis"; now the > 45 s gap stays the stall signal and NO CI step makes the gap check; its CI enforcement is stated as unmet and carried on the working route. `xtask/ci/heartbeat-gap-check.{sh,ps1}` stays, called by `perf:load-profiles` alone, which no workflow runs.
**Why:** No `lint-test` step ever read a log for spans, and the gap check ran only inside `ci-gates` over a boot log holding one tick per target, where it could not fail; the chunk removed that arm. On the operator's direction the two promised readings are stated as unmet rather than reworded away, and their owner is a route annotation pinned at this wrap. The `jq` step never existed in the workflow; the arm read in-process before this chunk as after it.
**Kept:** §9 Pipeline integration's `xtask test` row already says that job writes no log family; unchanged.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-10-10T10-27-16Z-wrap/

## 2026-10-10-no-gate-stands-while-reading-nothing — ci-gates left the perf grader: the perf-budget bullet, the frame row, the load-profile paragraph and the log-file row
**Section:** §10 → CI gates (the perf-budget bullet) · §10 → Performance budgets (the WebGPU canvas frame row) · §10 → Load-profile constraints · §9 → Telemetry artifact handling (the Log file row)
**Change:**
- Perf-budget bullet: was "`ci-gates` grades the boot-smoke log with no arm required and prints `perf-budget NEUTRAL` over it"; now `cargo xtask ci-gates` grades no perf arm and prints no perf-budget or frame line (two arms, zero-spans and zero-panic; exits 0 · 1 · 2). The frame `cannot-evaluate` line on CI is the lint-test `perf:budget` step's alone, as read on `ci#38042949735` (`graded 120 record(s)`, memory PASS n=3, snapshot PASS n=50, `perf-budget: PASS`, and `frame: cannot-evaluate: 0 samples, no adapter record in this log`). The boot job's earlier lines stay as dated readings; "the lint-test `perf:budget` line was not re-read" is gone. The producer's command spells `--no-tests=fail`.
- Frame row: the boot job's `ci-gates` frame line was "the expected line on a run whose smoke step passes"; now that held until this chunk, and since it the boot job prints no frame line on any run. The boot log's `ui.webgpu.adapter` records were not re-read on `ci#38042949735`.
- Load-profile constraints: was "`ci-gates` and `perf:load-profiles` grade with no arm required"; now `perf:load-profiles` alone. The NEUTRAL tolerance is the perf grader's, for an arm no caller requires, and is not a licence for a gate to pass over an absent input: `ci-gates` exits 2 on an absent log family.
- Log file row: what `ci-gates` reads of the boot log is its record count and its panic read.
**Why:** The heartbeat and perf-budget arms of `ci-gates` could not fail on the boot job's log (one tick per target, one memory sample, no snapshot or frame record), so the chunk removed them; the enforced budget gate is the lint-test `perf:budget --require memory,snapshot` step, unchanged.
**Kept:** The frame arm stays ungraded on CI by the operator's 2026-09-30 decision; its `cannot-evaluate` line in the lint-test step is an unrequired arm's, beside a PASS decided by two required arms that each read samples.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-10-10T10-27-16Z-wrap/

title: 2026-10-10-console-engine-entry-point — the process start both programs call, per-program ticks, and the `app.boot.engine` leaf
body:
## 2026-10-10-console-engine-entry-point — the process start both programs call, per-program ticks, and the `app.boot.engine` leaf
**Section:** §1 (Telemetry surfaces: CLI row; Telemetry triggers: multi-platform row; harness specification: Tracing init, Heartbeat ticks) · §3 → Tracing init · §3 → Heartbeat ticks (Tick interval) · §4 (CLI / main binary row) · §6 (warn row: `app.boot.engine`, `app.boot.render.posture`, `interpretation.model.allow_root`) · §8 (`app.boot.engine`; `interpretation.model.allow_root`) · §9 (`xtask test` row; triage workflow) · §10 (Standard+ Heartbeat ticks; CI gates heartbeat bullet's target list)
**Change:**
- The process start is `engine_boot::init_process`, called once by each program with the runtime entered: the sink and its guard, the at-exit hook, the Unix signal listener, the start instant, the pid file. `engine_boot::start` then binds the receivers, in the window app before the Tauri builder. Was: `main` parks the guard and installs the hooks, then spawns Tauri and binds. The event-loop end (`run_return` → `exit_after_event_loop`) is the window app's alone; the console program has no event loop, ends by SIGTERM or SIGINT with one `app.exit` of class `signal`, and has no stderr or stdout log layer.
- Ticks are per program: `ingest.tick`, `buffer.tick`, `connection.tick` (`heartbeat::spawn_engine_ticks`, from `engine_boot::start`) in both; `viz.tick`, `plugins.tick` (`heartbeat::spawn_window_ticks`) in the window app alone. Their absence from a console log is by design. Was: one roster of four for the app.
- New exact leaf `app.boot.engine` {`program`, `interpretation`, `reason`}, three closed labels, registered in §6 (once per `engine_boot::start`; WARN when `interpretation` is `none`) and §8; no bare `app` key; guarded in `pulse-app/tests/unit_observability_allowlist_boot_engine.rs`.
- `app.boot.render.posture`, `interpretation.model.allow_root` and the three platform boot records are once per WINDOW-APP boot; the console program emits none.
- The CLI surface has a second entry point, `andromeda-pulse-engine`: `run` logs through the shared start; `version` and a refused command line write no record.
- §9: `lint-test` boots no window app; one test spawns the console program, whose log sits under the test's data dir and is uploaded by no step.
**Why:** The chunk moved the process start and the engine wiring into a boot two programs share, split the heartbeat spawn, and added one boot record; sentences true of the window app alone were stated for every boot.
**Kept:** §10's statement that NO CI step makes the heartbeat-gap check stands unnarrowed: one consecutive pair of ticks in a short test run is not that check, which is `Agent harness drives the console engine`'s (the pc overseer's wrap directive of 2026-10-10, relayed in a file). The stall label's `logs` command stays: it is the harness verb.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-10-10T14-17-29Z-wrap/

## 2026-08-26-ingest-consumer-stall-under-sustained-load — drain progress: tick presence is liveness, not progress
**Section:** §1 Obs Scope Summary → Heartbeat ticks · §3 Observability Harness Contract → Stall detection · §5 Metric Coverage → tick-aggregated Counter rows · §6 Log Coverage → `warn` row · §8 PII Scrubbing → Default-deny posture (`buffer` whitelist + a new exact leaf) · §10 SLO Invariants → Standard+ invariants + DuckDB Connection Isolation
**Change:** Six sections, three amendment groups. (a) `buffer.tick` gains `rows_ingested_delta` + `last_append_age_seconds` (12 → 14 fields), applied at all THREE restating sites (§1 field list, §5 as its own tick-aggregated Counter row, §8 `buffer` whitelist) per the triple-site rule. (b) The new transition target `buffer.consumer.stalled` registered at BOTH §6 (warn row: once per healthy→stalled transition and once on recovery, never per batch, firing only after 30 consecutive non-draining ticks = 450s) and §8 (EXACT leaf: `reason` · `consequence` · `stalled_seconds` · `buffer_capacity_pct`), per the dual-site rule. Its exactness is load-bearing in the OPPOSITE direction to the `app.`-prefixed leaves: a bare `buffer` key DOES exist, so the `for_target` fallback would resolve this target to the tick field set — which contains none of the four — and redact everything. (c) The stall DEFINITION qualified at all three sites that restate it (§1, §3, §10 Standard+): tick presence is LIVENESS, and drain progress is the companion PROGRESS signal. §10's DuckDB Connection Isolation additionally records viz's three production query fns joining the isolated set via `viz::query::read_connection`. §10's CI-gate bullet (heartbeat-gap-check) was checked and deliberately NOT amended — it describes what that script does, which remains true and asserts no exclusivity.
**Why:** The chunk measured a wedge in which `rows_ingested` froze for 16 minutes while all four ticks emitted normally with 0 ERROR and 0 panics — satisfying every liveness check while persisting nothing, so the doc's tick-absence definition could not express the condition the chunk's instrumentation exists to surface (report §Outcome + §Changes → Counts). The 450s threshold is sited deliberately above §10's own 420s sustained-drain cap so an in-spec drain cannot trip it. The viz isolation entry records a VIOLATION of the existing §10 mandate rather than a new rule — the invariant was already correct and the code had diverged; verified live at 0 fallback WARNs with 405 queries still served.

title: 2026-08-28-ingest-consumer-initiating-freeze — §10 isolation gains a FOURTH, OPEN defect + the drain detector proven on a live reproduction
body:
## 2026-08-28-ingest-consumer-initiating-freeze — §10 isolation gains a FOURTH, OPEN defect + the drain detector proven on a live reproduction
**Section:** §10 SLO Invariants → DuckDB Connection Isolation & Load-Profile Operational Constraints (three edits: the lead-in framing, a new defect 4, and a new detector-exercised paragraph)
**Change:** The subsection's lead-in now reads "three-fixed-plus-one-open, not a closed story", and a fourth entry records the **OPEN** consumer block under gap→resume: after the producer goes quiet long enough for the silence family to fire and then RESUMES, the consumer stops draining on the first post-resume batch and never appends again. `dispatch_batch` takes `conn.lock()` first and holds it across every append, so BOTH shared-connection users die (the consumer, and the retention sweep whose next 100s-cadence sweep never arrives) while `viz` survives on the cloned connection defect 3's sibling gave it. Measured `rows_ingested` frozen at 3,240 with the channel at 85.7 % and 24k+ accepted spans unpersisted for 9+ minutes, at **0 ERROR and 0 panics**. The entry states explicitly that this is NOT the characterized-not-fixed maintenance pause below (which needs a ~12.7M-row table and is bounded >60 s; this table held 3,240 rows), that WHY the batch blocks is not established, that the reproducing arm changes two variables at once (idle gap AND a new gRPC connection), and it names the repair route entry as owner — closing with the note that the reference-connection mandate is correct but NOT fully satisfied by shipped code. Separately, a new paragraph records that the drain-progress detector was exercised against a LIVE reproduction rather than only the archive: `cargo xtask smoke:gap-resume` consumes `buffer.consumer.stalled` + `check:ingest-progress` as its verdict instead of adding a second detector, and the tokens were observed at the wire (`reason = rows_static_while_channel_queued`, `consequence = accepted_spans_not_persisted`, `stalled_seconds = 450`, `buffer_capacity_pct = 85.7`), announced once per transition as specified. Threshold and field set unchanged.
**Why:** the detector-exercised half is the chunk plan's Expected-amendments floor. The defect-4 half went BEYOND the plan's "no semantic change" framing and beyond the operator's wrap directive, so it was ESCALATED and resolved WITH the operator, who chose to record the open defect: §10 previously enumerated three defects as identified-and-fixed plus a fourth consumer joining the isolated set, which reads as a solved problem — while a reproducible consumer death sits on exactly the connection the section's mandate governs. Recording it as open with a named owner strictly improves alignment and creates no spec-vs-impl mismatch, because "open and owned by entry X" is precisely true. No detector proposed either half (D-obs-instrumentation / -stack / -pii all returned clean, correctly — the chunk adds no obs target, no allowlist leaf, and no logging of user data); both were raised by the orchestrator under Validate check 5, the plan's Expected-amendments coverage floor.

**Change:** Defect 4 is retitled "Consumer block on a duplicate-key replay" and rewritten to the measured chain: a producer restart replays span identities already stored, the first replayed batch hits the `spans` composite PK and `Appender::flush()` returns `Err` (one `duckdb.append` ERROR, `reject_reason: "append_failed"`), and the NEXT batch's `flush()` hangs unbounded while holding the shared connection mutex — `rows_ingested` frozen at 3,240, channel 0 → 100 %, `ingest.channel.full`, `buffer.consumer.stalled` at 450 s, 24k+ spans unpersisted, 0 ERROR and 0 panics after the first. It carries verbatim: "a retrying OTLP exporter resending spans is normal client behaviour that reaches this hang." THREE prior claims are explicitly retired: (a) "BOTH shared-connection users die — the consumer and the retention sweep" (`run_retention` has held a dedicated `try_clone()`d connection since defect 1, `crates/buffer/src/retention.rs:72-86`; the shared connection has exactly ONE production user); (b) "the trigger has not been separated" (the `--reconnect-only` arm reproduces the wedge with no idle gap, so the idle window is not the operative variable); (c) "WHY the first post-resume batch blocks is not yet established" (step probes recorded the tap completing, `spawn_blocking` scheduling, `conn.appender()` opening and `append_record_batch` returning — only `flush()` never does; pool starvation separately excluded by 771 `viz.query.traces` + 1,300 `metric.pipeline.l1a.*` completing after onset). Owner moves to the working-route entry "Duplicate-span replay fails loudly" (modify-set: the appender + the demo injector). The lead-in gains a sentence stating the fourth defect is listed for investigative continuity, NOT as a connection-isolation violation, and that the reference-connection mandate IS satisfied by shipped code — replacing the retired "correct but NOT fully satisfied" claim.
**Why:** chunk `2026-08-28-ingest-consumer-block-under-gap-resume` measured all three claims false (report §Changes → "Spec claims disproved by measurement" #1 and #2, and §The attribution). Applied under the playbook's 2026-08-28 record-a-measured-OPEN-defect rule (routine-APPLY: the amendment records the defect as open and names its owner, never claiming the impl half is done) together with the 2026-08-15 APPLY-AS-MEASURED rule (an impl half exists but needs its own route entry). title: 3. Observability Harness Contract
body:
## 3. Observability Harness Contract

Architecture committed to the harness pattern (verbatim from upstream-context Architecture Excerpt's Observability Hints): "`opentelemetry-stdout` (or file exporter targeting `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/`) is the only exporter the product itself uses for its own telemetry". This obs plan strengthens that commitment by going one step further: NO OTel SDK is linked into the self-observation runtime at all. The product's own debug telemetry uses ONLY the `tracing` ecosystem with a JSON file sink. The product's external surfaces (OTLP receivers ingesting third-party clients) continue to use `tonic` + `axum` + `prost` + `opentelemetry-proto` for wire format parsing — those crates parse OTLP without requiring an OTel SDK runtime, so the two pipelines remain cleanly separated.

title: Tracing init
body:
### Tracing init

- **Crate set:** `tracing` 0.1 (macro-driven instrumentation; `#[instrument]` attribute on router/handler methods) + `tracing-subscriber` 0.3 (JSON formatter + Layer composition + `EnvFilter`) + `tracing-appender` 0.2 (daily-rolling file sink, non-blocking writer) + `tracing-error` 0.2 (SpanTrace for sanitized error chains)
- **Init order:** Before Tauri app spawn; before HTTP/gRPC server bind. Sequence: (1) Load env vars + config → validate log level via `EnvFilter::from_env("ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LOG_LEVEL")` with fallback `RUST_LOG`, (2) Build the `tracing_subscriber::registry()` composing the non-blocking file appender layer (no stderr layer), (3) Install panic hook calling `tracing::error!(target: "app.panic.fatal", ...)` with `tracing-error` SpanTrace, (4) Spawn Tauri app + bind OTLP receivers (tonic + axum). Between (3) and (4) `main` hands the `WorkerGuard` `init` returns to a process-wide slot (`hold_log_guard`), installs the at-exit hook (`install_exit_hook`: a `pulse-exit-reporter` thread + `libc::atexit`) and, on Unix, the SIGTERM/SIGINT listener (`install_signal_listener`). The app runs through `App::run_return`; its exit code goes to `exit_after_event_loop` (record `app.exit` → `flush_log_sink` drops the guard → `std::process::exit` with the SAME code). `WorkerGuard::drop` is the non-blocking file sink's only drain, so every exit path that can log drains it after its one record (§6 `app.exit`).
- **Init body sketch (≤ 5 lines):**
```rust
let (file_writer, _guard) = tracing_appender::non_blocking(rolling::daily(log_dir, "agent-latest.jsonl"));
tracing_subscriber::registry()
  .with(fmt::layer().json().with_writer(file_writer))
  .with(EnvFilter::from_env("ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LOG_LEVEL"))
  .with(ErrorLayer::default()).init();
std::panic::set_hook(Box::new(panic_to_tracing_error));
```
- **Why this approach:** by NOT linking an OTel SDK into the self-runtime, the "OTel monitoring an OTel monitor" recursion concern disappears by construction — there is no exporter to point anywhere, and the file-sink JSON line IS the agent-readable surface.

title: Service identity
body:
### Service identity

- **service.name:** compile-time constant `"com.andromeda.pulse"` (Tauri bundle identifier; fallback `env!("CARGO_PKG_NAME")` = "pulse-app"); for mcp-server sidecar: `"andromeda-pulse-mcp"` (distinct process identity per arch convention)
- **service.version:** compile-time `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")` (or runtime read from `tauri.conf.json` for the bundled desktop build)
- **deployment.environment:** hardcoded `"production"` (desktop app, no staging/dev distinction at runtime)
- **Default subscriber fields:** registered once at subscriber init via `tracing_subscriber::fmt::Layer::with_default_fields([service_name, service_version, deployment_environment])` — every emitted JSON line carries identity in the `fields` map without per-call boilerplate

title: Logging stack
body:
### Logging stack

- **Library:** `tracing` 0.1 + `tracing-subscriber` 0.3 + `tracing-appender` 0.2 + `tracing-error` 0.2 (versions tracked in obs-research catalog; pinned at workspace level)
- **Format:** structured JSON-per-line matching binding contract (Section 6 log format JSON schema); agent-readable, machine-parseable; produced by `tracing_subscriber::fmt::Layer::json()`
- **Sink:** Single sink for app: the file `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/agent-latest.jsonl`, always JSON-only, via the non-blocking `tracing-appender` daily layer composed with `EnvFilter` + `ErrorLayer` — no stderr layer, no TTY pretty-print (as measured at chunk `2026-10-02-incident-events-readable-through-mcp`). For the mcp-server sidecar (rmcp 3.x resolved 3.1.4, declared-but-unused; hand-rolled JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio), stderr is forced JSON (no TTY check) — stdout is reserved for JSON-RPC 2.0 framing and ANY accidental stdout write would corrupt the protocol
- **Frontend bridge:** WebGPU frame timing + skeleton-pulse durations (and the three delegated timing observables) from the React webview flow through the hand-rolled TauRPC `telemetry.frontend.*` commands, which call `tracing::info!(target: "metric.{name}", ...)` on the backend — single JSON file is the unified self-observation surface. This is the DECIDED mechanism: `web-vitals` 5.x was RETIRED 2026-08-30 (operator ruling at the `2026-08-30-npm-advisory-coverage` wrap) — measured never installed (0 hits in package.json / package-lock.json / ui/src), its metrics (LCP/CLS/INP/FCP/TTFB) are page-load-shaped and do not fit a persistent fixed-layout desktop webview, and no producer or consumer of `metric.web_vital.*` ever existed

title: Log format JSON schema
body:
### Log format JSON schema

Verbatim from upstream-context Section 5 Test Plan Excerpt → Test Harness Contract Summary (binding contract):
```json
{
  "timestamp": "2026-05-02T16:18:34.567Z",
  "level": "INFO",
  "target": "ingest::grpc",
  "message": "TraceService.Export received 10 spans",
  "fields": {
    "span_count": 10,
    "service": "my-app"
  }
}
```

Extensions (optional fields per Section 5 telemetry triggers):
- `trace_id` / `span_id` — W3C traceparent string fields, attached at receiver entry from external client headers; treated as opaque strings by `tracing` (no OTel SDK trace context binding)
- `duration_ms`, `span_count`, `service`
- Per-trigger fields: `plugin_path_basename`, `query_id`, `param_count`, `token_count_actual`, `token_budget_limit`, `body_size_bytes`, `webview_backend`, `tray_api`, `wgpu_backend`, `dedup_count`, `anomaly_markers`, `p50_ms`/`p95_ms`/`p99_ms`/`max_ms`, `error_rate_percent`, `value` (metric event payload)
- `service.name` / `service.version` / `deployment.environment` — populated as default subscriber fields per Service identity above

title: Log file location
body:
### Log file location

- **Path:** `<data_dir>/logs/agent-latest.jsonl` — `<data_dir>` from `resolve_data_dir()`: `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` when set, else `%APPDATA%\andromeda-pulse\` (Windows), `~/Library/Application Support/com.andromeda.pulse/` (macOS), `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/andromeda-pulse/` else `~/.andromeda-pulse/` (Linux) — per arch §Filesystem locations (Windows + Linux halves corrected to `resolve_data_dir()` at chunk 2026-08-30-agent-harness-teardown-truth; macOS unchanged)
- **Rotation:** Daily rotation via `tracing_appender::rolling::daily(log_dir, "agent-latest.jsonl")`; previous day's file read by agent if current not yet created

title: Snapshot / paste-to-AI integration
body:
### Snapshot / paste-to-AI integration

Two cleanly separated surfaces:

**External-OTLP snapshot** (the product's CORE feature — the thing users invoke):
- **Path:** `~/.andromeda-pulse/snapshots/{timestamp}.md` (curated markdown, not raw OTLP JSON); timestamp format `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`
- **Schema:** Curated markdown with header (`## Snapshot from {time_range_start} to {time_range_end}`), metadata (`token_count`, `dedup_count`, `service_filter`, `anomaly_markers` like "⚠ latency spike" / "🔴 error cluster"), aggregated metrics (p50/p95/p99/max per service), critical-path top-slow-spans, trace IDs for drill-down. Deduped (identical span trees counted once with emission count). NOT raw OTLP JSON dump (per tests excerpt P2 + creator brief Section 6)
- **Trigger:** TauRPC `snapshot.generate({time_range, token_budget: 10000 | 25000 | 50000})` from webview; span `session.snapshot` wraps the pipeline; child spans emit token-budget telemetry (Section 5 perf-budget-instruments)
- **MCP tools (hand-rolled JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio; rmcp 3.x declared-but-unused):** nine (`ALL_TOOL_NAMES`) — `query_traces`, `query_metrics`, `query_logs`, `generate_snapshot` are the JSON-RPC 2.0 interface to the same external-OTLP query pipeline; `query_incident_list`, `retrieve_report`, `retrieve_telemetry_slice`, `mark_incident_resolved` (chunk #94) and `retrieve_incident_events` (chunk `2026-10-02-incident-events-readable-through-mcp`) read the incident corpus. Every tool emits `mcp.tools.call.request` (parent) → `mcp.tools.call.response` (result metadata only — `result_type` + `result_count`, NOT result_content per security plan vector 4) through the single `dispatch_tool` emission site; the `duckdb.query.{traces|metrics|logs}` child belongs to the telemetry tools only

**Self-observation paste-to-AI** (the product's debug surface — the thing developers/agents read):
- **Path:** `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/agent-latest.jsonl` (the same JSON log file from Logging stack above)
- **Format:** JSON-per-line, immediately greppable / `jq`-able / paste-to-LLM-able
- **No separate snapshot needed** — the JSON log file IS the self-observation snapshot

The two surfaces NEVER intersect: external client OTLP data lives in DuckDB and is curated into the markdown snapshot; the product's own runtime telemetry lives in the JSON log file. By separating them, no recursion is possible.

title: Trace context propagation
body:
### Trace context propagation

- **HTTP boundaries (`:4318` OTLP/HTTP receiver on axum 0.8):** W3C `traceparent` header extracted at request entry via manual `tower::Layer` (or `tower-http::TraceLayer` for plain `tracing` spans, NOT OTel-flavored); attached as a regular field on the inner `#[tracing::instrument]` span (`fields(traceparent = %tp)`) — downstream calls inherit via `tracing::Span::current()`
- **gRPC boundaries (`:4317` OTLP/gRPC receiver on tonic 0.14):** gRPC metadata (`grpc-trace-bin` header) extracted at gRPC service method handler entry via manual interceptor; attached as a `traceparent` field on the local `#[tracing::instrument]` span; same propagation pattern as HTTP
- **IPC boundaries (TauRPC):** TauRPC router handlers manually extract optional `traceparent` field from IPC envelope; initialize the local span with `fields(traceparent = %tp)` so downstream `tracing::Span::current()` calls inherit
- **Internal async boundaries:** `tokio::spawn` calls use `.in_current_span()` extension trait (from `tracing` 0.1) to propagate span context into spawned tasks
- **Real-time push streams:** `pulse://stream/spans` etc. carry trace context in Arrow metadata column (`_trace_context` schema field) for end-to-end correlation. NOTE: `traceparent` value is treated as an opaque string in `tracing` events, not bound to any OTel SDK trace context

title: Heartbeat ticks
body:
### Heartbeat ticks

- **Tick interval:** 15s for long-running subsystems (ingest, buffer, viz, plugins) via `tokio::time::interval(Duration::from_secs(15))`; 100ms for the realtime throughput counter (separate high-frequency ticker for animation smoothness per creator brief)
- **Tick event format:** `tracing::info!(target: "{module}.tick", span_count=N, buffer_capacity_pct=M, broadcast_subscribers=X, "heartbeat")` — ride the same JSON file sink as the rest of the app
- **Stall detection (two signals — liveness AND progress):** (a) LIVENESS — agent reads recent ticks via tail of JSON file or CLI `logs` command; missing tick for >45s = stall signal; `health` IPC command exposes the same fields synchronously for active liveness probing per arch Standard Contracts. (b) PROGRESS — tick presence does not certify that work is moving: a wedged buffer consumer keeps ticking while `rows_ingested` stays frozen, which every liveness check reads as healthy (measured 2026-08-26). The companion signal is `rows_ingested_delta` remaining 0 across consecutive `buffer.tick`s while the ingest channel still holds queued work, announced once per transition on `buffer.consumer.stalled` and asserted by `cargo xtask check:ingest-progress`

**Complementarity with the `health` command:** Heartbeat ticks (asynchronous, 15s emission to the JSON log) and the TauRPC `health` command (synchronous status polling) serve different purposes and must not be conflated. Heartbeat ticks enable retroactive log analysis ("was the subsystem alive during this interval?"); the `health` command enables active liveness probing during boot (the test harness polls synchronously until status ok) and at runtime. Implementations emit tick events independent of `health` invocations, and return synchronous `health` status independent of tick history; both mechanisms remain and operate in parallel.

title: 1. A11y Scope Summary

body: **A11y tier:** Standard (1)

**Justification:** Andromeda Pulse is a cross-platform desktop application (Windows / macOS / Linux via Tauri 2.x) with 2 primary UI surfaces (desktop-webview React SPA + desktop-native tray menu) plus an OS notification surface, spanning 8 assertable entities with 7 must-be-accessible flows (Critical Paths P1–P7). The security tier is Minimal (local-first, zero infrastructure, no user accounts, loopback-only OTLP), but tests tier = Standard (cross-platform, multi-surface coordination, 7 critical paths, persistent in-memory data) and obs tier = Standard (8 instrumentable modules, 9 major surfaces — 8 until chunk 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process, when obs-plan §1 counted the console engine's door, which adds no UI surface —, real-time push, security-sensitive logging vectors). Creator brief explicit rigor signals include WCAG color discipline ("Status colors not-color-alone (paired with iconography per WCAG)"), reduced-motion respect ("respects `prefers-reduced-motion`"), typography legibility ("Glance-readable from 2 meters"), and motion-as-data principle (motion conveys state, not decoration). **Standard WCAG 2.1 AA** with a **motion-sensitive AAA escalation** (SC 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions).
**A11y scope (entities needing assertions):**
| Entity | Source | Assertability | Reason if not fully assertable |

| **desktop-webview (React 19 + Tailwind CSS + WebGPU canvas)** | Arch Excerpt Stack + Surfaces + Design Excerpt Surfaces | Assertable | Primary web UI surface: compact-widget, full-dashboard, settings-modal, investigation-modal layouts |

| **desktop-native (Tauri 2 tray icon)** | Arch Excerpt Stack + Surfaces + Design Excerpt Surfaces | Assertable | System tray menu surface (Windows NotifyIcon / macOS NSStatusItem / Linux AppIndicator) — keyboard navigation via arrow keys / Return; OS-native a11y APIs apply |

| **WebGPU canvas visualization** | Arch Excerpt Stack | Assertable | GPU-accelerated chart rendering within webview; depends on semantic labels, interactive controls, and ARIA markup from design layer — no built-in accessibility; relies on wrapper element semantics |

| **Tauri IPC bridge (TauRPC)** | Arch Excerpt Stack + A11y-Relevant Conventions | Not-assertable | No UI surface; IPC mechanics affect error serialization and focus state during async operations but not a11y-testable surface itself |
| **OTLP/gRPC receiver (tonic)** | Arch Excerpt Stack | Not-assertable | Backend service surface; non-UI, no a11y testing scope |
| **OTLP/HTTP receiver (axum + hyper + tower)** | Arch Excerpt Stack | Not-assertable | Backend service surface; non-UI, no a11y testing scope |
| **DuckDB columnar storage** | Arch Excerpt Stack | Not-assertable | Backend-only; no UI surface, no a11y testing scope |

| **WASM plugin runtime (wasmtime)** | Arch Excerpt Stack | Boundary-only | Plugins can extend UI surfaces if granted WIT imports; a11y testing of plugin-provided UI is plugin-author responsibility; boundary assertion covers capability gating only |
| **Tray icon status display** | Design Excerpt Surfaces + Layout Templates | Assertable | Traffic-light status indicator within tray-icon surface; keyboard-navigable via OS menu system |

| **Notification (OS toast)** | Creator Brief Excerpt must-work scenarios | Assertable | "Snapshot ready ({N} tokens)" notification; content must be screen-reader accessible via OS notification API; OS-native a11y |

| **Settings modal form** | Layout Templates + Creator Brief | Assertable | Theme selector, widget snap position, retention input, MCP toggle, snapshot preset, plugin manager — form controls require label association and keyboard navigation |
| **Investigation modal** | Layout Templates | Assertable | Modal with close button (Esc escape path); focus management required |
| **File picker (native)** | Layout Templates | Boundary-only | OS-native file dialog; a11y boundary is Tauri modal wrapper, not picker internals |
**A11y surfaces & assistive tech reach:**
| Surface | Automated Tool Reach | Manual Verification (supplemental) | ARIA Roles Inventory | Service Identity Tagging | Notes |

title: WCAG Criteria Mapping

body: **Tier:** **Standard (1)** — mapped to **WCAG 2.1 AA** full (~50 SCs) as baseline.
**Trigger-driven AAA escalation:**

- **motion-sensitive trigger** → **ADD WCAG 2.1 AAA SC 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions** alongside Standard AA list. All motion tokens (`--duration-fast`, `--duration-standard`, `--duration-investigation-collapse`, `--easing-out`, `--easing-in-out`) must emit reduced-motion override assertions.

- **visual-discrimination trigger** → **WCAG 2.1 AA SC 1.4.1 Use of Color** (already part of Standard AA; no AAA escalation). Paired iconography supplement verified per token (--color-accent + icon/label, --color-feedback-success + icon/label, etc.).
**WCAG 2.1 AA core criteria list (50 SCs):**

- **Perceivable:** SC 1.1.1 Non-text Content / SC 1.2.1 Audio-only and Video-only / SC 1.2.2 Captions / SC 1.2.3 Audio Description / SC 1.3.1 Info and Relationships / SC 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence / SC 1.3.3 Sensory Characteristics / SC 1.4.1 Use of Color / SC 1.4.2 Audio Control / SC 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) / SC 1.4.4 Resize Text / SC 1.4.5 Images of Text / SC 1.4.10 Reflow / SC 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast / SC 1.4.12 Text Spacing / SC 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus

- **Operable:** SC 2.1.1 Keyboard / SC 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap / SC 2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts / SC 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable / SC 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide / SC 2.3.1 Three Flashes / SC 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks / SC 2.4.2 Page Titled / SC 2.4.3 Focus Order / SC 2.4.4 Link Purpose / SC 2.4.7 Focus Visible

- **Understandable:** SC 3.1.1 Language of Page / SC 3.2.1 On Focus / SC 3.2.2 On Input / SC 3.3.1 Error Identification / SC 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions / SC 3.3.3 Error Suggestion / SC 3.3.4 Error Prevention / SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value / SC 4.1.3 Status Messages
- **Robust:** SC 4.1.1 Parsing (deprecated in WCAG 2.2; retain for AA baseline)
**WCAG 2.1 AA SCs explicitly not applicable to andromeda-pulse (justify omission from critical paths P1–P7):**
- **SC 1.2.1 Audio-only and Video-only** — app has no audio/video-only content; telemetry is data-visualized via WebGPU canvas (visual-only)
- **SC 1.2.2 Captions / SC 1.2.3 Audio Description / SC 1.4.2 Audio Control** — no synchronized video, no audio component; not applicable
- **SC 1.4.4 Resize Text / SC 1.4.5 Images of Text** — semantic HTML buttons / form inputs only (no text-as-image); browser zoom accommodates resizing
- **SC 1.4.10 Reflow** — desktop-only Tauri app; viewport stable; no responsive mobile reflow requirement

- **SC 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus** — no interactive hover/focus-revealed content requiring dismissal; the header connection-dot tooltip is a decorative `aria-hidden` summary on a non-interactive `role="img"` element (SC 1.4.13 N/A — recorded so audits do not re-flag); focus testing covered in P5/P7
- **SC 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable / SC 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide** — no time-dependent content; WebGPU animations respect prefers-reduced-motion (SC 2.3.3 AAA covers)
- **SC 2.4.4 Link Purpose** — verified via SC 4.1.2 name-role-value across critical paths (link text clarity rolled into Section 11 Anti-patterns)
- **SC 3.1.1 Language of Page** — single-language English; `lang="en"` on root element; no multi-language requirement
- **SC 3.2.1 On Focus / SC 3.2.2 On Input** — covered in P7 form interaction (no unexpected context change on focus / change events trigger explicit submission only)
- **SC 3.3.3 Error Suggestion / SC 3.3.4 Error Prevention** — covered via P2 token budget bounds + P7 form pre-submit validation (axe-core form rules cross these SCs)
- **SC 4.1.1 Parsing** — React 19 + TypeScript + ESLint enforce well-formed DOM at compile time; deprecated in WCAG 2.2 (retained for AA baseline)
**Trigger-pulled AAA SCs (WCAG 2.1 AAA only):**
- **SC 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions** (motion-sensitive trigger) — machine-verifiable via reduced-motion media query assertion + Lighthouse a11y audit
